note.html:
The Equipment Hub lists the devices, and the top bar colours only a failure

Goal

On Android, the Equipment Hub stops drawing four large tiles and becomes a list with one row per device, like iOS already has. On both platforms the list groups the trainer with the power and cadence it supplies, a tap on a row opens a device picker or that device's details as a sheet, and signal strength is three bars instead of a dBm number. The top bar draws all four equipment icons on every screen, first run included, and only a failed connection is drawn in red.

The design is the ISS-0519 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/K1LPrFBG4Kn7ShhSuFS3nP), approved by Edwin on 2026-09-28, and the state table in DES-0002-WorkoutSelectionNavigationAndChrome § 2.

Why this is allowed during the Android feature freeze

This redesigns two surfaces that FEAT-0125-TheChromeReportsEveryBoundDeviceAndTheHubIsBehindIt built inside PHASE-025-NavigationStructure. That phase carries the third named exception to the PHASE-019 freeze (Edwin, 2026-09-22), and the phase is still active. So this feature sits under that exception rather than asking for a new one. It adds no new capability a rider did not have: every action in the new Hub exists today behind a long-press, a ⋮ menu or a dialog. The one new reading is the connected device's signal strength.

The exception's three conditions apply unchanged (PHASE-025-NavigationStructure.md, "Freeze exception"): Android and iOS land together, the PARITY_MATRIX rows for the Hub and the top bar are updated, and the screen gallery is regenerated for every screen this changes.

Why a new feature and not FEAT-0125 reopened

FEAT-0125 is done, passed an independent review on 2026-09-23, and its requirements REQ-0214 and REQ-0215 are implemented with evidence against the code as it stands. Reopening it would turn that evidence into claims about code that is about to change. A new feature keeps FEAT-0125's record true for the shipped Hub and gives this redesign its own review.

Scope

In scope

  • The Hub as a list on both platforms. A "YOUR BIKE" card holds the Smart Trainer row with Power and Cadence as indented child rows joined by a connector line, and a caption under it. A "YOU" card holds Heart Rate, with its own caption. A LIVE READINGS strip shows power, cadence and heart rate.
  • Row actions. A failed or disconnected row carries a Reconnect button, an empty row a Connect button, and a connecting row a spinner.
  • Two sheets. An empty row opens a device picker as a bottom sheet. A set-up row opens that device's details as a bottom sheet, which replaces the long-press, the ⋮ menu and the Device info dialog.
  • The Hub during a ride, as a sheet with no chevrons: only Reconnect and cadence's Change source work.
  • Signal strength as three bars in the picker and in the details sheet, and reading the connected device's signal on both platforms, which neither app does today.
  • Colour scheme A ("colour only when something needs you") in the Hub rows and the top-bar icons.
  • The top-bar icons drawn on every screen, first run included, with the bike's three icons in one shaded group.

Out of scope

  • The cockpit's own cadence button and per-device controls: ISS-0494-CadenceIsChangedFromTheTopBarWhileEveryOtherDeviceIsHandledOnItsTile. The cockpit's cadence button is left as it is.
  • The start gate, the attention bar and the one-tap reconnect after a ride (REQ-0216, REQ-0217). Their colours follow the shared tint the top bar uses, and nothing else about them changes.
  • The compatibility test itself. The details sheet only opens it; its Settings entry stays.

Acceptance

  • On both platforms the top bar draws all four equipment icons on every screen that carries it, first run included, and tapping them opens the Hub. (Symbols: EquipmentIndicators without its anyBound early return; EquipmentIndicatorsButton without its if equipment.anyBound guard.)
  • The top-bar icons follow DES-0002's state table: connected in the bar's text colour, connecting in the accent, set up but not connected in grey, not set up in a fainter grey that is still legible, and a failure in red with a filled dot. No green, no amber, no hollow dot. (Symbols: linkTint on Android, EquipmentLabels.tint and SlotIndicatorGlyph on iOS.)
  • The Hub is a list on both platforms: YOUR BIKE with the trainer and its two child rows, YOU with heart rate, each with its caption, and the live readings strip. (Symbols: EquipmentList and EquipmentRow on Android, replacing EquipmentGrid; EquipmentHubView with EquipmentRowView on iOS.)
  • A failed or disconnected row offers Reconnect on the row, an empty row offers Connect, and a connecting row shows a spinner.
  • An empty row opens a picker sheet in which a device used in another slot is greyed, says where it is used, and cannot be chosen. (Symbols: DevicePickerSheet on both platforms.)
  • A set-up row opens a details sheet with Resistance, Sends and Signal rows and the actions Change device, Run the compatibility test (trainer only) and Forget this trainer, which asks once. When the device is not connected, Reconnect leads the actions and Signal is left out. (Symbols: DeviceDetailsSheet on both platforms.)
  • No long-press, no ⋮ or ellipsis menu and no Device info dialog remain on either platform's Hub. (Grep: SlotOverflow, SlotInfoDialog, showMenuOnLongPress on Android; ellipsis.circle and overflowActions in EquipmentSlotRow.swift on iOS.)
  • During a running ride the Hub is a sheet with no chevrons, where only Reconnect and cadence's Change source work; the timer keeps counting.
  • Signal strength is three bars in the picker and the details sheet, with no visible word; a screen reader hears the strength (REQ-0227), and no screen prints dBm. (Symbols: SignalBars and signalBarsFor on both platforms; ScannerModal.kt:125 and ScannerSheet.swift:44 no longer print dBm.)
  • Every new rider-facing string is translated into the eight Tier-1 locales, and :app:lint passes without a new MissingTranslation marker.
  • PARITY_MATRIX rows A0 and A2 describe the new Hub and top bar, and both screen galleries are regenerated for the Hub, its sheets and every screen with the top bar.

Verification

Full runs on 2026-09-28, on the tree committed as 47c1aa81 (Android) and 3d74948d (iOS):

  • Android cd android && ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug: 1,488 tests, 0 failures, 6 skipped; lint clean of MissingTranslation.
  • Android ./gradlew :app:check: passed (debug and release unit tests, lint, verifyGsonKeepRules).
  • Android ./run-instrumentation-tests.sh on Test_Phone_API_35: 336 tests, 0 failures. After the in-ride caption change, EquipmentHubTest 15 of 15; after the 360 dp tests were added, YourTrainerTopBarTest 17 of 17.
  • iOS xcodebuild test -scheme YourTrainer -only-testing:YourTrainerTests on iPad Pro 13-inch (M5): 956 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped.
  • iOS UI tests run: CadenceScannerUITests testClosingCadenceSearchLeavesTheNextTrainerSelectionInTrainer, testRunningRideReconnectsOnlyAndCadenceChangesWhilePaused, testMockSensorPowerMeterAndTrainerShowEachCadenceFallback: passed. Not run: testEquipmentTitlesFollowEachSupportedLanguage and testMockCadenceSensorHoldsItsRpmThroughOneMinuteOfCrankWraps (long-running).
  • After the round-one review fixes, 2026-09-29: Android testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug :app:compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin passed; connectedDebugAndroidTest for com.yourtrainer.ui.equipment 26 passed on Test_Phone_API_35, including the new SignalBarsTest. iOS YourTrainerTests 957 passed, 0 failed; the new testTheIndicatorsAreDrawnOnFirstRun passes as built and fails with the icons hidden.
  • Not yet walked: the manual checks TST-0674 and TST-0675 on hardware.

Review

Round 2, 2026-09-29: approved. One reviewer, clean context, on review-packet.py FEAT-0130 --round 2 --since 3d74948d. All three refuted claims are fixed: the signal criterion and REQ-0227 say "no visible word"; SignalBars carries "No signal reading" when there is none; and the iOS strings have all eight languages (46 catalog entries checked). The reviewer also ran testTheIndicatorsAreDrawnOnFirstRun and ScanViewModelSignalReadingsTest and read the other fixes in the diff. Its one observation, seven older strings in the iOS Hub and picker with no translations (the slot-rejection alerts, "OK" and "Looking for nearby devices"), was fixed in the same close-out because the Hub file is code this feature changed.

Round 1, 2026-09-28: changes requested. The diff was 7,780 lines, so the review was split by platform: two reviewers on review-packet.py FEAT-0130 --range 7823310e..47c1aa81 (Android) and two on --range 47c1aa81..3d74948d (iOS), each in a clean context. Most claims hold on both platforms. Guards broken and caught: the control-write skip in BluetoothManager.readRealSignal, the ride guard in ScanViewModel.startSignalReadings, the no-dot rule for a disconnected slot in IndicatorStyle, the running-ride tap rule in rowTapFor, and on iOS the rideRunning stop and the late-answer check in onSignalStrength.

Refuted claims, all fixed in code this feature changed: - Signal criterion "with a word" (all four reviewers). The criterion contradicted REQ-0227 and the code; the criterion and REQ-0227's title now say "no visible word". - "No signal reading" was never heard (Android, both reviewers). SignalBars returned before setting any label. It now keeps the bars' place and carries the label; SignalBarsTest pins it. - Two iOS strings untranslated ("Equipment Hub", and "Smart Trainer" in six languages), plus French "Cadence" and the picker's empty state. All eight languages are filled, using Android's words.

Other findings, fixed: - No automated test caught the first-run top bar going blank on iOS. EquipmentHubTests.testTheIndicatorsAreDrawnOnFirstRun renders the button with nothing set up and counts visible pixels; it fails with the icons hidden and passes as built. - On iOS the compatibility test, pushed inside the details sheet, left signal reads running while it drives the trainer. The reads now start and stop with the sheet's own list, so pushing the test stops them. - On iOS a Reconnect that could not start (the system no longer remembers the peripheral) opened the picker only after a failure, so a plain disconnect did nothing visible. It opens the picker in both cases again, as the old Hub did, from the row and from the details sheet. - A broken ride guard hung ScanViewModelSignalReadingsTest instead of failing it. Each test now stops its readings inside runTest; with the guard broken the run fails in 3 s. - Stale comments: the 360 dp note (now the emulator measurement), the details sheet's "until TASK-0992", the write counter's "same connection", and the read's claim never to delay a write. - An outdated iOS test name (testSignalHooksStayNilUntilTask0992) and an uncalled EquipmentLabels.tint.

Recorded, not changed: - A write that starts after a signal read was queued waits behind that read, at most BleTimeouts.rssiRead. Reads never run during a ride or, on iOS, during the compatibility test (REQ-0227, "Found in review"). - The Resistance row shows only while the trainer is connected (REQ-0226, "Found in review"); the running ride's sheet leaves out the captions and the strip (REQ-0225). - The app-level wiring that tells the view models a ride is running (MainActivity.kt:705, YourTrainerApp.swift:153) has no test. The details sheet cannot be opened during a running ride, which rowTapFor and EquipmentRow.make pin, so this is a second guard. - On iOS in light mode, "set up, not connected" and "not set up" greys differ by lightness alone (1.44:1); the dashed tile and the Hub's words tell them apart. - The trainer picker does not grey a power meter bound as the power source: the bike's roles may share one device by design (TASK-0855, TASK-0860), and a meter that cannot be a trainer is refused for its missing service. - The screen galleries are regenerated but gitignored, which contradicts AGENT_RULES.md's "commit the updated images". Edwin's call.

items.key: TST-0015 PRO seat selection and hidden riders — the warned, irreversible choice, and what stays reachable afterwards
items.name: PRO seat selection and hidden riders — the warned, irreversible choice, and what stays reachable afterwards
items.text:
## Purpose

The seat choice cannot be undone, so the warning surface is the only thing standing between a rider and a decision they will live with. This test exists to catch the failure where the logic is correct and the communication is not — which is the likely failure, since this half is copy and confirmation rather than code.

Manual because it is a judgement about whether a person understands what is about to happen. An instrumentation test can prove the dialog rendered; it cannot prove it was clear.

## Setup

Debug build. Use the tier override chips in Developer Settings (`dev_tier_override`) to move between FREE, PRO and FAMILY without Play. Real Play Billing rows are called out separately below and need the Play Console test track.

## Steps

1. **FREE, five riders.** On FREE, add riders until the cap. Verify each has its own history, PBs and FTP/HR settings, and that competitive sort chips, household ghosts and the leaderboard all still show locks. Verify the add-rider card at five shows a plain maximum-reached state and **not** an upgrade prompt — FAMILY grants no extra seats and offering one would be false. On iOS the Add Rider button disappears at five riders, and the Activate Family Leaderboard card that stays is not an upgrade prompt, because it offers no seats (accepted by Edwin, 2026-09-25).
2. **The warning.** With three riders, begin a PRO purchase. Before the purchase completes, verify the rider count, that PRO keeps one, that the others become inaccessible, and that nothing is deleted are all stated. Verify FAMILY is the presented default and PRO is still selectable.
3. **The chooser.** Verify each rider shows ride count, hours and last-ride date. Verify **nothing is pre-selected**. Verify the confirm step **names** the riders that will become inaccessible.
4. **After.** Verify the other riders are gone from the picker, sorts, ghosts, leaderboard and PB comparison — absent, not greyed. Verify the seat cannot be re-chosen anywhere in the app.
5. **Reachable data.** Settings → verify hidden riders can be exported and deleted, and that this is the only place they appear.
6. **Restore.** Upgrade via `pro_to_family` (real SKU, Play test track) and verify every hidden rider returns with history intact.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: each rider keeps their own history, PBs and FTP/HR. Sort chips, ghosts and leaderboard show locks. At five, a plain maximum-reached card, not an upgrade prompt.
- [ios] Step 1: each rider keeps their own history, PBs and FTP/HR. Sort chips, ghosts and leaderboard show locks. At five, Add Rider disappears; no card offers seats.
- Step 2: before paying, it plainly states the rider count, that PRO keeps one, the rest become inaccessible, nothing is deleted. FAMILY default; PRO selectable.
- Step 3: each rider shows ride count, hours and last-ride date. **Nothing is pre-selected.** The confirm step **names** the riders who become inaccessible.
- Step 4: the other riders are absent, not greyed, from picker, sorts, ghosts, leaderboard and PB comparison. The seat cannot be chosen again anywhere.
- Step 5: hidden riders can be exported and deleted here, and appear nowhere else.
- Step 6: every hidden rider returns with history intact.

## Pass criteria

A rider who has not read this document can state, before paying, how many riders they are about to lose and that they are recoverable. If that is not true the test fails regardless of whether the software behaved correctly.

## Levelled 2026-08-19 — `system` → `acceptance` (ISS-0213 / TASK-0507)

`level:` decides where a test appears, and this one said `system` while the note describes a person verifying rider-facing behaviour. The seat choice cannot be undone, so this verifies a warning surface — copy and confirmation, checked by a person looking at a screen.

`status:` goes to `active` and the verdict moves to `mark:` in the same edit — ADR-0031: an acceptance test rests at `active` and a runner-written `passing`/`ready` is not its verdict. The validator caught the half-migration immediately, which is the rule doing its job.

Safe to relevel because this note is **one procedure**, which is the shape ADR-0030 requires: one note, one check. `TST-0011`, `TST-0012` and `TST-0013` are the same kind of test in the *old* shape — 18, 15 and 107 checklist rows in one note each — and are left alone pending migration.

items.key: TST-0019 First Run
items.name: First Run
items.text:
## Setup

A fresh install, or the test install with its app data cleared on Android or the app deleted and reinstalled on iOS.

## Steps

1. **The empty state.** On a fresh install, or after clearing app data, open the app. It opens on the Riders list.
2. **The card opens the dialog.** Tap the "Add Rider" card.
3. **The first rider is FREE.** Create the first rider.

## Expect

- Step 1: only an "Add Rider" card, the navigation bar (the rail on a tablet), and four faint-grey equipment icons.
- [android] Step 2: the **RiderSetupDialog** opens, modal on tablet and full-screen on phone, with a `Create new` / `Import from file` toggle.
- [ios] Step 2: an Add Rider sheet opens, with an `Import from file…` button instead of the toggle.
- Step 3: the first rider has a "FREE" tier licence.

## What is automated

*(partially automated: `UserRepositoryTest.empty_db_has_no_users` covers the empty state and `LicensingManagerTest` the default tier; the dialog UI stays manual.)*

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0434]], which asked for the same card and the same tap on the same screen. Its one addition was the second way to reach the empty state — clearing app data rather than reinstalling — and step 1 carries that.

One tick no longer separates an empty state that renders nothing from a card that fails to open the dialog. Both leave a new rider unable to start, so name the step.

## Rewritten 2026-09-28

Step 1 used to expect no equipment icons on first run. Since FEAT-0130 the top bar draws all four on every screen, faint grey while nothing is set up, because they are the only way into the Equipment Hub ([[REQ-0224-TheTopBarDrawsAllFourEquipmentIconsAndOnlyAFailureIsInColour]]). [[TST-0675-TheTopBarIconsFromFirstRunToAFailedConnect]] tests their colours in depth.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0020 Profile Accuracy
items.name: Profile Accuracy
items.text:
Create a profile with specific weight (kg/lbs) and FTP. Verify that W/kg calculations in the cockpit are correct based on these values. *(Weight / unit-conversion math covered by `UnitConverterTest`; W/kg is simple division. Cockpit rendering with live data still manual.)*

## Expect

- The cockpit's W/kg is correct for the rider's weight and FTP.

items.key: TST-0021 Settings — Unit + Energy
items.name: Settings — Unit + Energy
items.text:
In Profile → Preferences (on iOS, the Units and Energy pickers in the Profile section of the rider's Profile screen), change the "Energy Unit" (kcal/kj) and "Measurement System" (metric/imperial). Verify the changes reflect across the app. *(Metric/imperial conversion round-trips covered by `UnitConverterTest`; end-to-end screen refresh still manual.)*

## Expect

- The new energy unit and measurement system show across the app.

items.key: TST-0022 Profile Master/Detail Layout
items.name: Profile Master/Detail Layout
items.text:
(TASK-0383)

## Setup

Any rider, on a tablet and on a phone, on each platform.

## Steps

1. On tablet, tap the rider's name in the navigation rail, then the **Profile** button under the current rider's card. Read the chips at the top.
2. Select each category in turn.
3. On phone, tap the rider's name in the bottom bar, then the **Profile** button under the current rider's card.

## On iOS

On iOS the rider's profile is its own screen since PHASE-025, reached from the rider's name in the tab bar or rail, then **Profile**, which is next to **Switch rider**. It is one scrolling list of sections rather than a category rail; Edwin accepted the list layout on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]), when it still lived in Settings. On iOS test these steps in place of the Android steps above; the step numbers match. Test each one on the tablet and on the phone.

1. Tap the rider's name in the tab bar or rail, then **Profile**, and read the **Profile** section at the top.
2. Scroll the same list through that rider's connected services (Strava, intervals.icu) and **Data** sections.
3. Change a value in one section and scroll to another.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: a strip of chips at the top: Profile, Preferences, Connected, Data, each with an icon. No second rail beside the navigation rail.
- [ios] Step 1: the **Profile** section at the top of the Profile screen belongs to the current rider.
- [android] Step 2: the section below the chips changes, and the rider-card header stays.
- [ios] Step 2: one scrolling list reaches Strava, intervals.icu and **Data**, with no category rail or chip strip. Appearance and other app settings are not here.
- [android] Step 3: on the phone, the same chip strip at the top.
- [ios] Step 3: the same rider stays selected.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one paragraph of prose on Android and one bulleted list on iOS, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

## Changed 2026-09-27

The Android lines described a category rail of the profile's own on a tablet. TASK-0959 replaced it with the chip strip at every width, which `UserProfileScreen.kt` draws, so the check now asks for the chip strip on both sizes ([[ISS-0518-TST0022StillExpectsASecondRailOnATabletProfile|ISS-0518]]). The check was already owed on Android for REL-0017, with no result since its invalidation on 2026-09-22, so no result is lost.

items.key: TST-0023 FTP Estimator — gate and questionnaire
items.name: FTP Estimator — gate and questionnaire
items.text:
In Profile → Profile, test the FTP estimator from locked to written value. (TASK-0386)

## Steps

1. **Gated on weight.** Clear the Weight field.
2. **The gate opens.** Enter a weight.
3. **The questionnaire.** Tap `Estimate…` and answer the three radio questions (Experience / Weekly hours / Self-rated level).
4. **The value is written.** Tap `Use X W`.

## Expect

- Step 1: `Estimate…` next to FTP is disabled, and the FTP subtitle says *"set weight to enable estimate"*.
- Step 2: `Estimate…` is enabled.
- Step 3: the estimate updates live and reads `"X W (Y W/kg)"`.
- Step 4: the value lands in the FTP field.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0024]] (steps 3 and 4). The gate and the dialog behind it are one control on one screen, and step 2 is the setup step 3 needs anyway.

One tick no longer separates a gate that fails to open from an estimator that opens but computes or writes the wrong number.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps under `## Steps` with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0026 Per-Rider Display Smoothing
items.name: Per-Rider Display Smoothing
items.text:
## Setup

Family tier with two riders, A and B, and a trainer connected. Tier Override in Developer Options sets FAMILY without a purchase; on iOS, Override: FAMILY under Settings → Developer · Tier override.

On Family tier with 2+ riders, set Power Smoothing to 3s for Rider A and 10s for Rider B. The setting is on the rider's Profile: tap the rider's name in the bottom bar or rail, then **Profile**. On Android, **Profile** is the button under the current rider's card, and the setting is under Preferences. On iOS, **Profile** is next to **Switch rider**, and the setting is in the Profile section of that screen. Switch riders and verify the cockpit's power display smoothing reflects the active rider's setting. To switch on Android, tap the rider's name, then the other rider's card. On iOS, tap the rider's name, then **Switch rider**, and pick the other rider. (TASK-0384)

## Expect

- The cockpit's power smoothing follows the selected rider's setting.

items.key: TST-0027 Rider Color — Family Exclusive
items.name: Rider Color — Family Exclusive
items.text:
## Setup

On Family tier with 2+ riders. (TASK-0385 / TASK-0386 follow-ups)

## Steps

1. Open the current rider's profile (the rider's name in the bottom bar or rail, then **Profile**), then its Rider Color picker, and look at the colours other riders use. On Android, **Profile** is the button under the current rider's card. On iOS it is next to **Switch rider**, and the picker is in the Profile section of that screen.
2. Look at the current rider's own colour in the same picker.
3. Open the New Rider dialog's palette.

## Expect

- Step 1: colours other riders use are greyed out and can't be tapped.
- Step 2: the rider's own colour can still be picked.
- Step 3: the New Rider palette greys out other riders' colours the same way.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one paragraph of prose, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0028 Trainer Pairing
items.name: Trainer Pairing
items.text:
## Setup

A trainer to connect, or the fake trainer from Developer Options, with no trainer set up yet. Open the Equipment Hub from the equipment icons in the top bar.

## Steps

Tap Connect on the Smart Trainer row and choose a smart trainer (FTMS) in the sheet that opens. Start a ride, then discard it.

## Expect

- Power and Speed show data.

## What is automated

*(Partially automated: `DevicePickerSheetTest` covers the picker sheet and the device tap; `EquipmentSlotTest` covers the row's state after connecting; the Bluetooth and FTMS link stays hardware-dependent.)*

## Where to find the rows, and who checks their layout

The devices are rows in the **Equipment Hub** on both platforms. Open it by tapping any of the equipment icons at the end of the top bar: a screen on Android, a sheet on iOS. The Workouts screen carries no equipment panel, and iOS Settings has no Equipment Hub row. That is all this check needs. It is here so the check can be tested, and TASK-0853 added its first version after Edwin marked this row `question` on 2026-09-08 with *"I don't see a third slot on the equipment screen"*. He was right: the slot was on a screen nothing navigated to ([[ISS-0417-TheEquipmentHubIsUnreachable]]).

**The Hub's contents and layout are [[TST-0657]]'s and [[TST-0674-TheEquipmentHubListSetsUpInspectsAndForgetsADevice]]'s, not this check's.** Since FEAT-0130 the Hub is one list on both platforms: a YOUR BIKE card with Smart Trainer, and Power and Cadence indented beneath it, then a YOU card with Heart Rate (`EquipmentList.kt`, `EquipmentHubView.swift`). Keeping a second description here would only give the checks a chance to disagree.

The empty-slot decision survives the redesign and is worth reading before testing: **the Power row is always there**, even with nothing bound to it. With a trainer set up it reads *From the trainer*; with no trainer it reads *Not set up* with a Connect button. Edwin settled that on 2026-09-08 ([[ISS-0416-ThePowerSlotAlwaysShowsAndItsCommentSaysItDoesNot]]): a rider who owns pedals has to be able to find the row without being told it exists.

items.key: TST-0029 HRM Pairing
items.name: HRM Pairing
items.text:
## Setup

A heart-rate strap, charged, and a trainer connected in Smart Trainer. No heart-rate monitor set up yet. Open the Equipment Hub from the equipment icons in the top bar.

## Steps

Tap Connect on the Heart Rate row and choose the strap in the sheet that opens. Start a ride, then discard it.

## Expect

- The heart-rate tile updates live.

## What is automated

*(Partially automated: `DevicePickerSheetTest` and `EquipmentSlotTest` cover the picker and the row's state; live heart-rate reception stays hardware-dependent.)*

## Rewritten 2026-09-28

The step used to scan from the Heart Rate slot. Since FEAT-0130 an empty row carries a Connect button that opens a picker sheet ([[REQ-0226-ARowOpensTheDevicePickerOrTheDevicesDetailsAsASheet]]). The expected result is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0030 Stability
items.name: Stability
items.text:
## Steps

Background the app for 30 seconds during a connection, then return to it.

## Expect

- The connection remains active.

## Original wording

Background the app for 30 seconds during a connection and return; verify the connection remains active.

items.key: TST-0031 Workflow Continuity
items.name: Workflow Continuity
items.text:
## Setup

A FREE rider with no trainer bound: open the Equipment Hub from the equipment icons at the end of the top bar and tap Forget on the trainer slot. A trainer to connect, or the fake trainer from Developer Options. A trainer that is bound but switched off takes a different path, the *Connecting…* bar, which [[TST-0667-FromAFinishedRideToTheNextStart]] tests.

Select a workout with no trainer bound. The start gate opens the Equipment Hub, not the bare *Choose a smart trainer* picker. Read the line at the top of the Hub. Tap Connect on the Smart Trainer row and choose the trainer. Read the line again, then wait without tapping anything.

## Expect

- Selecting the workout opens the Equipment Hub, with no picker on top of it.
- The Hub's top line names the workout: "Choose your trainer. <workout> opens once it connects."
- After choosing the trainer the line reads "<workout> opens when your equipment connects."
- When the trainer connects, the Hub closes by itself and the workout you picked opens, after the heart-rate prompt, without picking it again.

## Rewritten 2026-09-30

The start gate used to open the trainer scanner. Edwin decided that a rider with no trainer set up gets the Equipment Hub instead ([[ISS-0530-ANewRiderIsSentToABarePickerInsteadOfTheEquipmentHub]]), built by [[TASK-1025-OnAndroidTappingAWorkoutWithNoTrainerOpensTheEquipmentHub]] on Android and [[TASK-1026-OniOSTappingAWorkoutWithNoTrainerOpensTheEquipmentHub]] on iOS. Until then this check fails on both platforms. Edwin then confirmed that it starts by itself, and asked for the wait to be visible: *"yes it should then open ideally showing enough info to the user that he/she is waiting for the connection before opening."* The Hub names the waiting workout and closes by itself when the trainer connects ([[TASK-1027-OnAndroidAWaitingWorkoutSaysWhatItIsWaitingFor]], [[TASK-1028-OniOSAWaitingWorkoutSaysWhatItIsWaitingFor]]). This check was already reopened for REL-0017 and has no pass to invalidate.

items.key: TST-0032 HRM Prompt — Connect
items.name: HRM Prompt — Connect
items.text:
Tap "Connect" on the HRM prompt, then select an HRM device.

## Steps

1. Tap "Connect" on the HRM prompt.
2. Select an HRM device.

## Expect

- Step 1: the HRM scanner opens.
- Step 2: the workout proceeds automatically after connection.

## What is automated

*(partially automated: HrmPromptTest.connectCallbackFired — full flow requires BLE)*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0033 HRM Prompt — Dismiss Scanner
items.name: HRM Prompt — Dismiss Scanner
items.text:
## Setup

A rider with a trainer connected and no heart-rate monitor connected. Pick a Power workout so the prompt offers Connect and Skip.

## Steps

1. On a Power workout, tap "Connect" on the prompt, then dismiss the HRM scanner without selecting a device.
2. Tap Skip on the "Connect Heart Rate Monitor?" prompt.

## Expect

- Step 1: the workout starts without an HRM, as it does after Skip. The prompt does not come back.
- Step 2: tapping Skip starts the workout without an HRM.

## Not this check

On an HR-Zone workout the prompt has no Skip, so dismissing the scanner leaves the ride waiting; [[TST-0179-HR-Zone-Start-Requires-HRM]] tests that.

## Corrected to the apps, 2026-09-25

Step 1 now asserts what both apps do: closing the heart-rate scanner on a Power, Route or free ride without choosing a device starts the ride without the strap, the same as Skip. On Android, `EquipmentBinderHost.onDismissed` in `WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt` calls `skipHeartRateAndContinue`; on iOS, `scannerDismissed` in `WorkoutSelectionView.swift` does the same. Both carry the comment "goes on without the strap where Skip was allowed, as it always has".

PHASE-025 had rewritten this step on 2026-09-22 to say the prompt comes back. Edwin chose the apps' behaviour on 2026-09-25 (decision 6 in [[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit]], applied by [[TASK-0961-ApplyEdwins20260925DecisionsToTheWalk]]). REQ-0216's open question, whether the strap keeps its Connect or Skip prompt on Power and Route rides at all, is separate and unchanged by this correction. The steps were numbered on 2026-09-24 so the two results take separate marks (FEAT-0122, A7).

items.key: TST-0034 ERG Mode
items.name: ERG Mode
items.text:
Start a structured workout. Verify that the trainer's resistance changes automatically at interval transitions.

## Expect

- The trainer's resistance changes by itself at each interval transition.

items.key: TST-0035 Simulation Mode
items.name: Simulation Mode
items.text:
## Steps

1. On the Workouts screen, choose **Route** in the ride-mode strip and tap the Free Ride card. Verify the session starts in SIMULATION.
2. Adjust slope with +/- buttons through 0.5% steps from -15% to 20%. Verify trainer resistance changes with slope.

## Expect

- Step 1: the session starts in SIMULATION.
- Step 2: the slope moves in 0.5 % steps from −15 % to 20 %, and the trainer resistance changes with it.

## Coverage

`WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.startFreeRide_default_is_SIMULATION_for_Route_tab` covers the mode dispatch. The slope +/- UI and trainer resistance stay hardware dependent.

## Path corrected 2026-09-24

Step 1 named the Route tab that PHASE-025 replaced with the ride-mode strip. The expectation is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0036 Simulation Gear Shifting
items.name: Simulation Gear Shifting
items.text:
In simulation free ride, check the gear controls, shift gears, and read the gear label.

## Steps

1. In simulation free ride, look at the gear controls.
2. Shift gears.
3. Read the `GEAR N of M` label, on the rider's preset and again after changing the preset.

## Expect

- Step 1: gear up and down buttons sit below the slope controls.
- Step 2: resistance changes on the trainer.
- Step 3: the `GEAR N of M` label renders, and its `M` follows the rider's preset.

## Narrowed 2026-09-12 — the counts moved to a note CI runs

This row is now the rendering half only: the buttons are where they should be, the label draws, and a shift is felt. The numbers behind the label — 26 for Linear, 22 for Road, 12 for MTB — are asserted on every build by [[TST-0660]], which runs `VirtualGearTablesTest`.

The row keeps `automation: manual` and no `command:` on purpose. A `command:` would take it out of the release test entirely (`tools/instructions/TESTING.md` § "Release gating"), and the layout half would stop being asked for — which matters here, because this row also carries an `invalidated_by` from TASK-0460 about the cockpit's slope Row moving inside a Column.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0037 ERG Free Ride Watts
items.name: ERG Free Ride Watts
items.text:
Toggle to ERG mode in free ride.

## Steps

1. Toggle to ERG mode in free ride and read the display.
2. Adjust with +/-.
3. Keep pressing minus.

## Expect

- Step 1: the display shows watts, such as "150W", not a percentage.
- Step 2: the +/- buttons move the target in 5 W steps.
- Step 3: the minimum is 30 W.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0038 Screen Continuity
items.name: Screen Continuity
items.text:
Ensure the tablet screen does not dim or turn off while a workout is active.

## Expect

- The screen does not dim or turn off while the workout runs.

items.key: TST-0039 Interval Controls
items.name: Interval Controls
items.text:
Test the "Skip Next" and "Previous" buttons. Verify the timer and target power update immediately.

## Expect

items.key: TST-0040 Completion — Save
items.name: Completion — Save
items.text:
## Setup

Any rider and a trainer that accepts control, or the fake trainer.

## Steps

Ride a workout to its end, tap Save ride, then tap Done on the celebration.

## Expect

- The ride is in History with its time, distance and power.

## Not this check

- The dialog's buttons: [[TST-0684-WhenARideEndsADialogAsksOnlyWhetherToSaveItKeepRidingOrDiscardIt]].
- The celebration between Save ride and Done: [[TST-0685-AfterSaveTheCelebrationLeadsWithTheHeadlineThenTheNumbersAndDoneGoesToHistory]].

## Provenance

Partially automated: `RideEndDecisionDialogTest` (Android) and `RideEndDecisionTests` (iOS) check that Save ride saves; the full flow needs the database. Rewritten on 2026-10-10 for [[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]]: Save ride now opens the celebration, and its Done goes to History, on both platforms.

items.key: TST-0041 Completion — Discard
items.name: Completion — Discard
items.text:
## Setup

Any rider and a trainer that accepts control, or the fake trainer.

## Steps

Ride a workout to its end, tap Discard ride, then open History.

## Expect

- The ride is not in History.

## Not this check

- That Discard ride asks nothing further: [[TST-0684-WhenARideEndsADialogAsksOnlyWhetherToSaveItKeepRidingOrDiscardIt]].

## Provenance

Partially automated: `RideEndDecisionDialogTest` (Android) and `RideEndDecisionTests` (iOS) check that Discard ride discards. Rewritten on 2026-10-10 for [[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]]: the button is Discard ride in the new decision dialog.

items.key: TST-0042 Completion — Keep riding (Free Ride)
items.name: Completion — Keep riding (Free Ride)
items.text:
## Setup

Any rider and a trainer that accepts control, or the fake trainer.

## Steps

Start a free ride, end it by hand with FINISH, read the dialog, then tap Keep riding.

## Expect

- The dialog offers Keep riding, and Keep riding returns to the free ride, which carries on.

## Not this check

- The dialog's eyebrow for a free ride: [[TST-0684-WhenARideEndsADialogAsksOnlyWhetherToSaveItKeepRidingOrDiscardIt]].

## Provenance

Partially automated: `RideEndDecisionDialogTest` (Android) and `RideEndDecisionTests` (iOS) check when Keep riding is offered; the free ride's own state stays manual. Rewritten on 2026-10-10 for [[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]]: the button that was Resume Workout is Keep riding.

items.key: TST-0043 Paid generation — one deliberately complex prompt per provider
items.name: Paid generation — one deliberately complex prompt per provider
items.text:
Three paid API calls, one per provider, on a Pro or Family rider with a key configured. Use the **same deliberately complex prompt every time**: *"90-minute pyramid with 12 zone changes, cadence targets on every interval, 3 cues per body interval"*. A prompt that size exercises the long-request path as well as the generation, so these three calls are the whole paid-API cost of this row. Start from the **Power** editor's AI builder. On iOS, choose each provider in Settings → AI Coach before its call, and open the builder from Workouts → Power → + → Build with AI with Mode on Power; it shows the result as a preview with Save workout.

## Procedure

1. **OpenAI.** Select OpenAI, paste the prompt, tap Generate. The generation **completes** rather than failing with a timeout, and the editor fills with a valid workout matching what the prompt asked for. The shared OkHttpClient gives a 90 s read; before that fix this prompt routinely hit the 10 s default and threw `SocketTimeoutException`.
2. **Gemini.** Same prompt, Gemini selected, same result. *(A standing release exception applies here: the Gemini API key has been unavailable for testing. If that is still true, record this tick as **not run** and say so — do not tick the row on two providers and call it done.)*
3. **Claude.** Same prompt, Claude selected, same result.
4. **Save and find it again.** Save one of the three generated workouts. It appears in the Workout Library with the correct profile graph.
5. **The Power editor stays Power-shaped.** Because the generation started from the Power editor, the result carries `targetPowerPercent` per interval and the terrain draws watt bars — no HR zone bands anywhere. This is the check that the Power and HR-Zone builders do not cross-contaminate.

## Expect

- Step 1: OpenAI returns a complete workout matching the prompt, with no timeout.
- Step 2: Gemini returns a complete workout matching the prompt, with no timeout.
- Step 3: Claude returns a complete workout matching the prompt, with no timeout.
- Step 4: the saved workout appears in the Workout Library with its profile graph.
- Step 5: every interval is Power-shaped: the terrain draws watt bars, with no HR zone bands anywhere.

3. **Coaching cues.** Prompt: *"VO2max intervals with coaching motivation"*. The generated workout carries coaching cues, and they appear as banners during the ride.

## Expect

- Step 1: the warmup and cooldown are diagonal ramps on the terrain graph, not stepped blocks.
- Step 2: the intervals carry cadence targets, shown as TARGET RPM in the cockpit.

The result is **still HR-Zone shaped**: the editor's calling context dictates the type, not the prompt's wording. If the model returns a Power-shaped workout with no recoverable zone tags, a clear toast appears (`"AI returned a Power-shaped workout for an HR-Zone request…"`) — never a silent miscast and never a crash.

items.key: TST-0054 AI error messages are actionable and dismissable, on both providers
items.name: AI error messages are actionable and dismissable, on both providers
items.text:
Two deliberately invalid keys, two error lines, one container. The two provider message strings differ and each keeps its own tick; the widget they render in is the same and is checked once.

## Procedure

1. **Claude's message.** Enter an invalid Anthropic key (e.g. `sk-ant-invalid`) and tap Generate. The error line reads `"Claude Error 401 at https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages: authentication_error — invalid x-api-key"` or close to it, not an opaque generic exception. This is ClaudePartner mirroring OpenAiPartner's error-body parsing.
2. **Gemini's message.** Switch to Gemini, enter an invalid key (e.g. `AIzaSy-invalid`), tap Generate. The error reads `"Gemini Error 400: INVALID_ARGUMENT — API key not valid…"` or a similarly short message. Before the fix Gemini dumped its whole multi-kB response body, echoed system prompt included, into the editor.
3. **The container, checked once.** On either provider the error is **not a toast**. It is an inline `Text` in the AI builder card, in the error colour, capped at four lines with an ellipsis, with a Close (×) icon button to its right and a troubleshooting link below (`WorkoutEditorScreen.kt:1922-1948`, ISS-0203 / TASK-0432). It stays on screen until the rider taps Close, so the copy can be read at leisure rather than caught in a three-second window. Tap the × — the error disappears immediately and the input is usable again.

## Expect

- Step 1: the error reads close to "Claude Error 401 … authentication_error — invalid x-api-key", not a generic exception.
- Step 2: the error reads close to "Gemini Error 400: INVALID_ARGUMENT — API key not valid…", in one short line.
- Step 3: the error stays inline, at most four lines, never a toast, until Close (×) removes it.

items.key: TST-0056 While a generation runs: the counter, Cancel, and the recent-prompt strip
items.name: While a generation runs: the counter, Cancel, and the recent-prompt strip
items.text:
Everything the AI builder card does around a generation, in one go at the card. Steps 1 and 2 share a single generation; step 3 needs three short ones.

## Procedure

1. **The counter and the rotating status.** Tap Generate on a long prompt. Within 1–2 s the card replaces the empty input with a `"Generating… Ns · <status>"` line where N ticks each second. The status rotates every 5 s through "Drafting intervals…", "Choosing power targets…", "Adding coaching cues…", "Almost there…". A Cancel TextButton sits to the right of the status.
2. **Cancel mid-flight.** Five to ten seconds in, tap **Cancel**. The card returns to the idle textbox immediately, with no error toast, and the elapsed counter resets to 0. Tap Generate again with a fresh prompt — it works normally, with no stuck state.
3. **The recent-prompt strip.** Generate three different prompts in succession. After each, a `Recent` label and a horizontal chip strip appear below the input, newest first, capped at 10 and ellipsised when long. Tap a chip — the textbox refills with that prompt. Re-submit an existing prompt — it moves to the front with no duplicate. Cancel out of the editor or navigate away and back — the strip is empty, because it is per-session memory only.

## Expected results

- The elapsed counter ticks and the status rotates on the five-second cadence.
- Cancel returns the card to idle with no residue, and a second generation still works.
- The chip strip is newest-first, de-duplicating, tappable, and gone after leaving the editor.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |

| [[TST-0058-AI-Builder-Recent-Prompts-Chip-Strip]] | the recent-prompt chip strip and its per-session lifetime | step 3 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

items.key: TST-0062 Free Tier Locks
items.name: Free Tier Locks
items.text:
Verify the FREE lock inventory is **exactly** the following, on a FREE rider. Both halves matter: a lock that is missing is a leak, and a lock that should not be there is a paywall in front of something we decided to give away.

**1. Locked — routes to the paywall:**

- **New Workout** (the FAB, per workout type) — hard gate, no editor glimpse and no read-only mode (`MainActivity.kt` `onAddWorkout`).
- **Edit** (kebab → Edit, on any workout) — the same hard gate (`onEditWorkout`).
- **Import** (`.ytw` / `.zwo` / share-sheet receipt) — `WorkoutViewModel.importWorkout` emits `_importPaywallRequired` and **does not parse the file**.
- **Bundled workouts outside the free allowlist** — a Lock icon on the card itself, per workout, from `FreeBundledCatalog`. This is where the FREE/PRO line now lives for content.

**2. NOT locked — and each of these was, once:**

- **The favourite star.** Open to FREE (`FEAT-0096` item 4). `onToggleFavorite` carries no tier check.
- **Riding bundled workouts.** No monthly cap; the 3-ERG-sessions counter, its consume call and its paywall route are all gone (`FEAT-0096` item 3).
- **The competitive layer** — sort chips, household leaderboard, ghosts (`ADR-0010`).
- **Multiple riders**, up to five (`FEAT-0104`).

**3. External-source sections are absent, not lock-carded.** On Workout Selection, the Strava routes, Strava starred segments, intervals.icu library and intervals.icu Planned sections are gone in their entirety — no section header, no rows, and no lock-card placeholder. This is deliberately different from the bundled-workout lock cards in step 1, which do render on FREE (`ISS-0299`).

**4. Hiding them does not hide the offer.** Profile → Connected still lists the integrations, each with an Upgrade button, and the paywall's benefit list names them. That is the discoverability path the hiding in step 3 relies on.

**5. Last, because it ends the FREE test: upgrade to PRO.** The four external-source sections appear on Workout Selection.

*(partially automated: `WorkoutRepositoryTierLimitTest` and `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` cover the import gate and the custom-workout cap; the lock-icon rendering, the per-card allowlist locks and the paywall navigation stay manual.)*

## Expect

- New Workout, Edit, Import and the bundled cards outside the free allowlist each open the paywall.
- The favourite star, riding bundled workouts, sort chips, leaderboard, ghosts and up to five riders are not locked.
- The Strava and intervals.icu sections are absent: no header, no rows, no lock card.
- The rider's Profile lists those services with Upgrade buttons, and the paywall's benefit list names them.
- On PRO the four sections appear.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0613]] (steps 3, 4 and 5). The absence in step 3 was already a bullet in this row's locked-inventory list, so the two rows overlapped. TST-0613 added two things this row did not have: the discoverability path on Profile → Connected, and the sections coming back after an upgrade. Both are carried over rather than dropped.

Step 5 changes the tier, so it goes last. Everything above it must be tested on FREE first, and re-running the row means putting the device back on FREE.

One tick no longer separates a leaking lock from a hidden section that reappears wrongly, and no longer separates "the sections are hidden" from "the sections are hidden and unreachable". Write down the step number.

## Release test history

**2026-08-30 — `incomplete`.** *"This check should be updated, wildcarding is no longer locked. Instead some workouts have been locked."* Correct, and the check was the thing at fault: it still described the pre-`FEAT-0096` inventory, in which the star was locked and bundled content was not. Rewritten against the code on the same day — the four gates above were each read at their call site rather than inferred from the feature note. The `invalidated_by` on this check named `ADR-0010`'s sort chips alone, which was too narrow; `FEAT-0096` moved considerably more.

items.name: The debug-workout toggle hides and shows the [Debug] workouts
items.text:
One toggle, flipped once, with the library checked either side of it.

On iOS, open Settings → About and tap Version three times to reveal the inline Developer · Workouts section. Its Show debug workouts toggle is the control for these two observations. On Android, use the Developer Settings screen.

## Procedure

1. **Off — hidden.** With "Show debug workouts" off in Developer Settings, no workout with the `[Debug]` prefix appears anywhere in the library.
2. **On — visible.** Turn "Show debug workouts" on. The debug workouts appear.

*(Partially automated: `WorkoutRepositoryLibraryTest` exercises the `isDevShowTestWorkouts()` gating on both sides. The Developer Settings toggle itself stays manual.)*

## Expected results

- Step 1: with the toggle off, no workout with the `[Debug]` prefix appears anywhere in the library.
- Step 2: with the toggle on, the debug workouts appear.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0097-Debug-Workouts-Visible]] | debug workouts appear once the toggle is on | step 2 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0097** — a toggle stuck in one position fails this row whichever position it is stuck in, and shipping debug workouts to riders is the worse of the two failures.

## Evidence (fill after running)

items.key: TST-0102 One completed ride carries the whole Strava upload path
items.name: One completed ride carries the whole Strava upload path
items.text:
Nobody would set this up five times. One ride, with Strava linked, tested from the pill before upload to the backlog row after it.

**Setup.** Strava linked, and at least one older session in history that has **not** uploaded — a session recorded before linking is the easiest way to have one. Step 1 reads that session; steps 2 onward use a fresh ride.

## Procedure

1. **The outline pill, before any upload.** On a session with `stravaUploadStatus` unset and Strava linked, the history row shows a white pill with an orange border: `[☁ CloudUpload] Strava`. Tap it — the status flips to `uploading`.
2. **Auto-upload after a completed workout.** Complete a workout. The upload starts on its own, with no tap, and the activity appears on Strava.
3. **The uploading pill.** While either upload is in flight, the pill is the solid-orange `Uploading…` variant with a white spinner.
4. **The activity id reaches the database.** Within about 60 s of upload success — the worker polls — this returns a non-null long: `adb shell "run-as com.yourtrainer sqlite3 databases/your_trainer_database 'SELECT stravaActivityId FROM workout_sessions WHERE sessionId=?'"`. This is the only step that needs a terminal rather than the screen, so it is named on its own.
5. **View on Strava.** With `stravaActivityId` stored, the pill reads `View on Strava`, solid orange. Tap it — `strava.com/activities/{id}` opens in the Strava app, falling back to the browser.
6. **The backlog row disappears once nothing is pending.** With every session now uploaded, the Strava subsection's `Backlog` row is **not rendered at all** — not empty, absent.

## On iOS

Steps 1 to 3, 5 and 6 are tested as written. Step 4 has no terminal query on iOS. Instead, close the app completely, reopen it and open the same ride: its pill still reads `View on Strava`, and tapping it opens the same activity as before. Only a stored activity id survives the relaunch, so this is the iOS evidence for step 4. Edwin chose this evidence on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]).

## Expect

- Step 1: the older session shows a white pill with an orange border reading "Strava". Tapping it starts the upload.
- Step 2: the upload starts on its own, with no tap, and the activity appears on Strava.
- Step 3: while uploading, the pill is solid orange and reads "Uploading…" with a white spinner.
- [android] Step 4: the query returns a non-null activity id.
- [ios] Step 4: after the relaunch the pill still reads "View on Strava" and opens the same activity.
- Step 5: the pill reads "View on Strava", solid orange, and opens that activity in Strava or the browser.
- Step 6: the Strava subsection has no Backlog row at all, not an empty one.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0472-Upload-Pill-Not-Uploaded-Linked]] | the outline pill, and the tap that starts an upload | steps 1 and 3 |
| [[TST-0473-View-Strava-Pill-Known-Activity-Id]] | the `View on Strava` pill and its deep link | step 5 |
| [[TST-0481-StravaActivityId-Capture-Upload-Happy-Path]] | the `stravaActivityId` column populated after upload | step 4 |
| [[TST-0476-Backlog-Row-Hidden-When-Empty]] | the backlog row absent when nothing is pending | step 6 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0472** — the manual tap-to-upload path and the automatic one are different entry points, and a broken tap now hides behind a working auto-upload.
- **TST-0473** — a deep link that opens the wrong activity, or nothing, records as the same failure as an upload that never happened.
- **TST-0481** — this is the only database assertion in the set, and it can fail while every pill on screen looks right; that is why it stays its own numbered step with its query written out.
- **TST-0476** — a backlog row rendered empty is a cosmetic defect sharing a verdict with five functional ones.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- The pill's appearance at each stage, the `adb` query's output, and whether the backlog row was present.

items.key: TST-0105 Multi-User Link (Family)
items.name: Multi-User Link (Family)
items.text:
## Steps

1. Rider A links to strava_a. Switch to Rider B.
2. Rider B links to strava_b.

- [ios] Step 1: rider B's Strava section shows the Connect with Strava button, not Connected.

*(partially automated: per-rider token storage is scoped by `userId`; Strava OAuth flow stays manual.)*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0106 Two riders upload to their own Strava accounts, and the uploaded data is right

Two rides on one device, two Strava accounts, then one visit to strava.com to read both.

## Procedure

1. **Each rider's ride goes to their own account.** Rider A completes a workout — it uploads to A's Strava. Rider B completes a workout — it uploads to B's Strava. Neither appears on the other's account.
2. **The uploaded activities carry the right data.** Open strava.com for both riders. Each activity has the correct name, duration, power and HR data.

*(Partially automated: `WorkoutSessionRepositoryTest` covers the per-user session scoping that drives dispatch; the Strava upload and everything read on strava.com stay manual.)*

- Step 1: each ride is on its own rider's Strava account, and not on the other's.
- Step 2: each activity is titled with the ride's workout or route name, and has the right duration, power and heart rate.

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

## Evidence (fill after running)

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] sends a title and a description with each upload. Before, Strava named the activity itself, such as "Evening Ride". items.key: TST-0108 Unlink is per-rider and leaves other riders connected

They now sit under `## Steps`, with one expectation each under `## Expect`, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

Edwin decided on 2026-09-17 to accept the iOS layout where it differs from Android, and to give each check an iOS variant that names the iOS screen and the same underlying result (ADR-0007; [[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]). Since PHASE-025 the iOS app keeps Strava in the current rider's Profile, reached from the rider item in the bar or rail (`RiderProfileView`, `SettingsView.stravaSection`; [[TASK-0949-ProfileLivesUnderTheRider]]). Settings has no Strava section. It has no Switch: an unlinked rider sees the official Connect with Strava button, and a linked rider sees Connected with an Unlink button. items.key: TST-0110 Strava-detail subsection — full localisation (CHG-20260502 Strava L10n gap fix)
items.name: Strava-detail subsection — full localisation (CHG-20260502 Strava L10n gap fix)
items.text:
With Strava linked on the active rider, switch device language to German. Open Profile → the Strava section expands to show the "Connected" subsection with three rows: **Backlog** (count of pending uploads with retry button), **Reconnect for read access** (only when the rider authorised the legacy write-only scope), **Refresh now** (force-pull historical activities). Verify every label, subtitle, button text, and plural form (e.g. `1 Workout in Warteschlange` vs `7 Workouts in Warteschlange`) renders in German — no English literals slip through. Spot-check French and Japanese for the same three rows. **Pre-fix:** seven hardcoded EN literals in `StravaDetailRow.kt` (body / actionLabel / message / hint / errorText) leaked through even when device locale was non-EN; the new `HardcodedComposeTextTest` regex set (named-arg literals + body / subtitle / actionLabel / message / hint / errorText / prompt / confirmText / dismissText) catches this class of regression at unit-test time.

On iOS the Strava section of the rider's Profile has no Backlog, Reconnect for read access or Refresh now row. It shows Connected with Unlink, a **Refresh Strava status** button and, while rides wait, an **Upload N pending rides** button (`SettingsView.swift`). Edwin accepted these as the iOS equivalent on 2026-09-25 ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]], decision 19), so on iOS check that those labels render in German, French and Japanese.

## Expect

- [android] Backlog, Refresh now and, where shown, Reconnect for read access: every label, subtitle, button and plural is translated, with no English.
- [ios] Connected, Unlink, Refresh Strava status and Upload N pending rides are translated in each language, with no English.

items.key: TST-0111 Dark/Light Mode

Toggle theme in settings. Verify all screens are legible in both modes.

On Android the theme is in Settings → Appearance. On iOS it is the Theme control in the Appearance section of Settings.

items.key: TST-0114 Share Diagnostics
items.name: Share Diagnostics
items.text:
In Settings → Hardware → Diagnostics row, tap "Share Diagnostics". Moved from About → Hardware on 2026-05-14.

## Steps

1. In Settings → Hardware → Diagnostics row, tap "Share Diagnostics", and open the text file.
2. After connecting a trainer, read the FTMS entries in the file.
3. Find the `[DIS]` section in the same file.
4. Save the file to Google Drive and read the name it lands with.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: the share sheet opens a text file: app version and install UUID in the header, timestamped BLE entries, MACs anonymised (device_1, device_2).
- [ios] Step 1: the share sheet opens the log: app version and install UUID in the header, timestamped BLE entries, MACs anonymised (device_1, device_2).
- Step 2: FTMS entries show "Control Point discovered", "Request Control", and "Control GRANTED" or error details.
- Step 3: a `[DIS]` section holds Manufacturer, Model and Firmware.
- [android] Step 4: the saved name is `your-trainer-diagnostics.txt`.
- [ios] Step 4: the saved name ends `.txt`.

## Why step 4 reads the saved name

**Why step 4 confirms the saved filename (ADR-0013, 2026-09-05).** The share subject used to be `Your Trainer Diagnostics`, and Google Drive names the saved file from the subject, so the log arrived with no `.txt` and opened in nothing.

## On iOS

iOS shares diagnostics from Settings → About → About Your Trainer → **Share Diagnostics**, not from a Hardware row. Check the same log contents there. Then save the shared log to Google Drive through the share sheet and read the name Drive gives it: it must end `.txt`. The Android name `your-trainer-diagnostics.txt` is not required on iOS. Edwin chose the share sheet's name as the iOS evidence on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]).

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0116 Slope control — range, limits, and where the number is shown
items.name: Slope control — range, limits, and where the number is shown
items.text:
In simulation mode, work the slope control through its range and then read the cockpit.

## Steps

1. **Range and step size.** Slope adjusts from −15 % to 20 % in 0.5 % steps.
2. **It stops at both limits.** Pushing past −15 % or past 20 % does nothing.
3. **The slope percentage is shown in the intensity control area.**
4. **The slope number is not duplicated anywhere else in the cockpit.** With Slope behaviour set to something other than `Auto` on a SIM-capable trainer, a chip renders directly under the slope `%` (TASK-0460). Confirm there is still no second slope number elsewhere on the screen.
5. **Elevation gain sits next to distance in the header.**

## Expect

- Step 1: the slope adjusts from −15 % to 20 % in 0.5 % steps.
- Step 2: pushing past −15 % or past 20 % does nothing.
- Step 3: the slope percentage shows in the intensity control area.
- Step 4: a chip renders directly under the slope `%`, and no second slope number shows elsewhere.
- Step 5: elevation gain sits next to distance in the header.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0117` | 3, 4, 5 | Where the slope number is shown now shares a result with what values it can take, so a control that reaches 20 % but prints the figure twice records as the same failure as one that stops at 15 %. Step 4 stays a named step because it is the negative — a duplicate slope number passes every other step here. |

items.key: TST-0119 Gear Power Range (LINEAR 26-gear retune)
items.name: Gear Power Range (LINEAR 26-gear retune)
items.text:
## Steps

At 80 rpm on flat (0 %) with the LINEAR preset, ride gears 1, 9, 18 and 26. Pre-TASK-0459 figures (gear 5 ≈ 135 W, gear 22 ≈ 380 W) no longer apply.

## Expect

- The watt steps between gears 1, 9, 18 and 26 feel even.

## Original wording

At 80 RPM on flat (0 % slope) with the default LINEAR preset, ride gear 1, gear 9, gear 18 and gear 26 and judge whether the watt deltas feel evenly stepped. Pre-TASK-0459 figures (gear 5 ≈ 135 W, gear 22 ≈ 380 W) no longer apply.

## Narrowed 2026-09-12 — the four resistances are already frozen, and the even-step judgement is the sweep's

The percentages this row used to spot-check — 5 %, 30 %, 57 % and 82 % at gears 1, 9, 18 and 26 — are not sampled by hand any more. `resistanceForGear_each_step_matches_baseline_table` in `PhysicsUtilsLinearSnapshotTest` freezes all 26 LINEAR values on every build, and [[TST-0129-Virtual-Gear-Presets-LINEAR-Retuned-Baseline]] is the acceptance row that carries that command.

What is left is the judgement the numbers cannot make: whether the watts a rider produces step evenly from gear to gear. [[TST-0658]] measures exactly that. Its step 6 reports the delta between adjacent gears across the climb and flags a gear that jumps twice as far as its neighbours, which is the finding this row was asking a rider to feel. Run the sweep and read its scorecard rather than sampling four gears by hand; this row stays in the release test as the place that records the judgement.

items.key: TST-0120 Slope + Gears
items.name: Slope + Gears
items.text:
## Steps

In the Free Ride cockpit, set the slope to 5 % and shift gears.

## Expect

- The slope row and its chip sit inside one column, with the gear row beneath it.
- Every tap target still works at the size it had before TASK-0460.
- A gear shift gives the same resistance step whether or not the chip is showing.

## Original wording

In the Free Ride cockpit, set slope to 5 % and shift gears. Confirm the slope Row and its chip sit inside their Column with the gear Row as a sibling beneath, that every tap target still works at the size it did before TASK-0460, and that a gear shift produces the same resistance step whether or not the chip is showing.

## Narrowed 2026-09-12 — the arithmetic moved to a note CI runs, the layout stayed here

[[TST-0663]] asserts what the slope and the gear each do to resistance, on every build, via `PhysicsUtilsLinearSnapshotTest`. The sibling row [[TST-0430-Slope-Gears-Together]] makes the same arithmetic claim under ISS-0130 and took that command directly, because it carries no layout remainder.

This row does carry one. Its `invalidated_by` from TASK-0460 asks for the cockpit's tap targets after the slope Row moved inside a Column, and no unit test looks at a layout. That is why the row keeps `automation: manual` and no `command:` — a `command:` would take it out of the release test and the layout check would never be asked for again (`tools/instructions/TESTING.md` § "Release gating").

items.key: TST-0121 Elevation Terrain View
items.name: Elevation Terrain View

In simulation mode, ride for 2+ minutes with varying slopes: flat, a climb, a descent.

## Expect

- Zone-coloured power fills under the elevation curve.

## Original wording

In simulation mode, ride for 2+ minutes with varying slopes (flat, climb, descent). Verify the terrain view shows a cumulative mountain profile. Verify zone-colored power fills under the elevation curve.

items.key: TST-0122 ERG Target Terrain
items.name: ERG Target Terrain

items.key: TST-0123 Structured Workout Simulation
items.name: Structured Workout Simulation
items.text:
## Steps

1. On a trainer that supports FTMS simulation parameters, start a Route ride — `route_flat_10k` or `route_rolling_medium`. Read the top of the control block.
2. Read the grade below the gear control.
3. Pedal and read the terrain view.

## Expect

- Step 1: the gear row sits on top of the control block: a small GEAR beside large numbers, such as `GEAR 9 / 26`, between − and + buttons.
- Step 2: the grade sits below it, smaller and grey, read-only (`GRADE  N.N%`), with no +/− of its own.
- Step 3: the terrain view shows the route's gradient profile, with the rider's marker moving along it.

## A Route ride is the only way to reach this layout

The row used to open "Start a structured workout. Toggle to SIMULATION." There is no such toggle, because FEAT-0051 removed it, and no code path would honour one. `WorkoutViewModel.selectWorkout` sends every structured workout that is not a Route to `FreeRideMode.ERG` unconditionally. It sets `SIMULATION` for a selected workout only in its Route branches.

The layout claim itself is live. In `ActiveWorkoutScreen`, the control block's `isStructuredSimulation` reads `selectedWorkout != null && (isSimulationMode || isRouteWorkout)`. The `isRouteWorkout` half is the one a rider can reach, so a Route ride draws the block the row describes: the `isStructuredSimulation` branch puts the gears first in a `CockpitStepperRow` with `GearReadout`, and the grade under it as read-only `workout_grade_label` text.

Two sentences the old row carried do not survive the move. The grade is not a `+/-` control on a Route: it is read-only text, because the profile drives it. And "terrain still shows planned intervals" is wrong for a Route. The interval-timer card, the cockpit's "PROGRESS ZONE", is drawn only when `selectedWorkout != null && !isRouteWorkout`, and the visualisation is `RouteTerrainView`, the gradient profile, not a planned-interval strip.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

## Step 1 rewritten for FEAT-0131, 2026-09-29

Step 1 used to ask for `GEAR N / <total>` in large type with 72 dp buttons. FEAT-0131 split the readout into a small GEAR label beside large numbers (`GearReadout` on Android, `GearReadoutView` on iOS), and the buttons now shrink to 56 dp on a phone, so the line names what the rider sees instead of a size ([[CHG-20260929-The-Cockpit-Fits-Every-Screen-And-The-Terrain-Keeps-Its-Share]]).
