items.key: TST-0211 Export HR Workout
items.name: Export HR Workout
items.text:
## Steps

1. Name an HR-Zone workout `Sweet Spot: 2x20`. Tap Share on it and save the shared file to Drive.
2. Import the saved file back into Your Trainer.

## Expect

- Step 1: the name that lands in Drive ends `.ytw`.
- Step 2: the file imports back into Your Trainer.

## Notes

*(partially automated: `BackupFileSerializationTest` covers `.ytw` JSON round-trip for HR_ZONE workoutType; Share intent + SAF save stay manual.)*

**Check the file that lands, not the one that is produced (ADR-0013, 2026-09-05).** "A `.ytw` file is produced" was true of the cache file and false of what the rider ended up with: the share subject was `Your Trainer Workout: <name>`, Google Drive names the saved file from the subject, and the `.ytw` was lost. Save the shared file to Drive and confirm the landed name ends `.ytw`, then import it back into Your Trainer — `WorkoutSelectionScreen` refuses an import whose name has no known extension, so a lost extension breaks the round trip into our own app. Name the workout `Sweet Spot: 2x20` first; the colon is the character that caused ISS-0387. Full test: [[TST-0646-SharedFileSurvivesADriveRoundTrip]].

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0212 Import on the Heart Rate tab — a .ytw lands, a .zwo is refused
items.name: Import on the Heart Rate tab — a .ytw lands, a .zwo is refused
items.text:
## Setup

A PRO rider. A previously exported `.ytw` and a `.zwo` file on the device or in Drive.

On Workouts, pick **Heart Rate** in the ride-mode strip. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS. Tap Import twice and feed the picker a different file each time.

**A .ytw imports.** Pick a previously exported `.ytw`. It imports and appears in the Heart Rate library with its zones intact.

**A .zwo is refused.** Tap Import again and pick a `.zwo` file. A snackbar reads "Unsupported file type — please select a .ytw file" and carries a Retry action that re-opens the picker. The workout does not import.

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` covers the tier gate; `IntervalDeserializerTest` covers the `targetHrZone` round trip through Gson; `ZwoParserTest` covers `.zwo` parsing. The SAF picker, the snackbar copy and the per-tab extension allowlist stay manual.)*

The allowlist is per tab: the Heart Rate tab accepts `.ytw` only, while the Power tab also takes `.zwo` (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:938-942`). That is why the refusal has to be tested on this tab specifically — the same `.zwo` would import happily one tab over.

## Expect

- The `.ytw` imports into the Heart Rate library with its zones intact.
- The `.zwo` is refused: "Unsupported file type — please select a .ytw file", with Retry, and nothing imports.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0213` (ZWO Blocked on HR Tab) — picking a `.zwo` on the Heart Rate tab and reading the refusal message. It is the **A .zwo is refused** step, and it keeps its own named step because it is the negative half of the same Import button.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates a `.ytw` that fails to import from a `.zwo` that imports when it should not. Those are opposite failures of the same allowlist, so a rider must write down which named step failed.

`TST-0213` said "toast". The message is a snackbar with a Retry action (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:944-951`); a toast is only the fallback when no scaffold snackbar host is available. The copy itself was and remains exact. Corrected here on 2026-09-12 rather than carried into a freshly authored body.

items.key: TST-0214 The Heart Rate tab's action buttons — red accent and the right import arrow
items.name: The Heart Rate tab's action buttons — red accent and the right import arrow
items.text:
## Setup

Any rider on Workouts.

Open Workouts and pick **Heart Rate** in the ride-mode strip. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS. All three steps are one glance at the button row.

**New button fill.** Red-filled.

**Import button fill.** Soft red.

**Import icon direction.** The Import button's icon is a downward arrow (`FileDownload`), not an upward arrow.

## Expect

- New is red-filled, Import is soft red, and the Import icon is a downward arrow.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0215` (Import Icon) — the Import button's arrow pointing down rather than up. It is the **Import icon direction** step, on the same button this row was already looking at.

## What this row handed off

The red favourite star moved to [[TST-0194-Favorites]] on 2026-09-12. `TST-0194` already taps a star, watches it turn red, and then leaves and returns to check the colour survives. Asserting the colour here as well meant two rows owned it and only one of them proved it persisted.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates a wrong button fill from a wrong icon direction. A rider must write down which of the three named steps was wrong.

items.key: TST-0216 HR Free Ride Unconstrained
items.name: HR Free Ride Unconstrained
items.text:
## Setup

A trainer and a heart-rate strap connected. On Android, set Tier Override (Debug) to Free in Developer Options. On iOS, Tier override has no FREE choice: in Settings → Developer · Tier override tap Reset to real entitlements while signed in to a sandbox account that holds no Your Trainer purchase, then fully close and reopen the app.

## Steps

1. On FREE tier, start Zone Ride (HR Free Ride), end it, and start it again.
2. **Re-verify:** ISS-0170 fix removed the leftover cockpit START-button paywall. Read the START button.

## Expect

- Step 1: it starts, and starts again, without limit.
- Step 2: the START button shows no "PRO" lock.

## What is automated

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.startFreeRide_HR_ZONE_for_HR_tab` covers the dispatch path; `LicensingManagerTest` confirms Free-Ride dispatch never touches the structured-workout counter; cockpit START-button rendering on FREE tier stays manual.)*

## Corrected 2026-09-12 — "no token is consumed" named a counter that no longer exists

The original wording asked a rider to confirm a token was *not* consumed. FEAT-0096 deleted the token counter entirely (`LicensingManager.kt:148-155`), so there was nothing to watch not happening — a negative check against an absent mechanism reads as passing whatever the app does.

What is still worth testing is the outcome: a FREE rider can start a Zone Ride as many times as they like. That is now what the row asks for.

The FREE line moved to per-workout content gating via `FreeBundledCatalog`; [[TST-0062-Free-Tier-Locks]] holds that inventory. [[TST-0217-HR-Structured-Consumes-Token-Start]] was retired by the same removal.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0218 HR Library Accessible on Free
items.name: HR Library Accessible on Free
items.text:
On FREE tier, verify the Heart Rate library is visible; bundled workouts listed without a lock. *(partially automated: `WorkoutRepositoryLibraryTest` — bundled library is not tier-gated at the repo level; library-tab rendering stays manual.)*

## Expect

- The Heart Rate library is listed, and its bundled workouts carry no lock.

items.key: TST-0219 The Heart Rate tab on FREE — New, Import and Share are all gated
items.name: The Heart Rate tab on FREE — New, Import and Share are all gated
items.text:
## Setup

A FREE rider. Tier Override in Developer Options sets FREE without a purchase.

On FREE tier, open Workouts and pick **Heart Rate** in the ride-mode strip. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS. All three steps are on that one screen, on that one tier.

**New.** Tap the "New" button. It carries a lock icon, and the tap goes to the paywall.

**Import.** Tap "Import". It carries a lock icon, and the tap goes to the paywall.

**Share.** Open an HR-Zone workout's context menu and look for Share. It is either absent or locked with a paywall redirect.

*(partially automated: `LicensingManagerTest` covers tier resolution; `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` covers the view-model import gate that triggers the paywall; `ImportPaywallNavigationTest` covers the paywall navigation dispatch. The per-button lock-icon rendering on this specific tab stays visual.)*

The gate itself is shared with the Power tab. What this row checks is that the Heart Rate tab is wired into it too, which is a per-tab render rather than a per-tier rule.

## Expect

- New and Import each carry a lock and open the paywall. Share is absent, or locked and opens the paywall.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0220` (HR Import Pro Only) — the Import button's lock and paywall redirect on the HR tab. It is the **Import** step.
- `TST-0221` (HR Export Pro Only) — Share being unavailable or locked in an HR-Zone workout's context menu. It is the **Share** step.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates three independently rendered gates. A New button that lost its lock, an Import button that lets a FREE rider through, and a Share action that is still live in the context menu all record as one failure now, so a rider must write down which named step was open.

items.key: TST-0222 Route library — one glance at the Route tab
items.name: Route library — one glance at the Route tab
items.text:
Open Workouts, pick **Route** in the ride-mode strip, and read the whole screen once. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS. Nothing in this row needs a trainer, a ride or a connection. Two routes must already be in the library for step 4: one flat, total ascent under 100 m (*Endurance Flats*), and one mountain, total ascent over 1000 m (*Alpe d'Huez*). Turn the developer toggle on so the `[Debug]` routes draw.

## Setup

A PRO rider with the two routes step 4 names already imported, and Show debug workouts on in Developer Options. A tablet for steps 1 to 7, and a phone in portrait for step 8.

## Steps

1. **The list is populated.** At least 15 bundled routes are listed, plus the `[Debug]` routes while the developer toggle is on.
2. **No "coming soon" card.** The placeholder card that once stood in for an empty library must not appear anywhere in the list.
3. **Card silhouette.** Each Route card draws a monochrome elevation silhouette, not a power-bar waveform.
4. **The silhouette scales with the climb.** The flat route's silhouette is a visibly thin band at the bottom of its card, its ~50 m of relief drawn against a 200 m baseline. The mountain route's fills the card height and shows full relief. Before ISS-0193 both filled the card, which made difficulty impossible to compare at a glance.
5. **Card metadata.** A Route card subtitle reads its distance, ascent, steepest grade and difficulty, such as `12.4 km • 310m ↑ • 6% max • Diff: 3` (`ws_card_route_summary_with_grade_format`).
6. **A Route card carries no duration.** The minutes figure belongs to Power and HR-Zone cards only (`ws_card_power_summary_format`, "45 min • Diff: 3"), so read a Power card in the same list to see the difference.
7. **Max-grade segment.** On the tablet, read the two routes' subtitles. The steepest grade comes after the ascent, the number first, as `12% max`. It is the steepest grade over the route's 50 m windows, not the raw per-segment peak (ISS-0309). The flat route shows a single digit and the climb a double digit.
8. **The same segment on a phone.** Repeat step 7 on a phone in portrait. Since FEAT-0131 a phone and a tablet show the same subtitle; a narrow card wraps the line instead of dropping the segment (ISS-0505). Only a route whose computed max grade rounds to 0 % drops it, with no empty separator left behind.
9. **Free Ride card.** The Route mode's primary card reads "Free Ride", subtitle "Slope + virtual gears", in the green accent.
10. **Import button.** The library header's Import button reads "Import (.gpx .fit .tcx)", in the same green accent.
11. **The library lists on FREE.** Switch the tier to FREE in Developer Settings and reopen Workouts with **Route** picked. The bundled library is still listed; listing is not tier-gated.

## Expect

- Step 1: at least 15 bundled routes, plus the `[Debug]` routes while the developer toggle is on.
- Step 2: no "coming soon" card anywhere in the list.
- Step 3: each Route card draws a monochrome elevation silhouette, not a power-bar waveform.
- Step 4: the flat route's silhouette is a thin band at the bottom; the mountain route's fills the card.
- Step 5: a Route card subtitle reads like `12.4 km • 310m ↑ • 6% max • Diff: 3`.
- Step 6: a Route card shows no minutes; the Power card does.
- Step 7: the subtitle reads `<dist> km • <ascent>m ↑ • <N>% max • Diff: <n>`: one digit on the flat route, two on the climb.
- Step 8: the phone shows the same subtitles as the tablet, `<N>% max` included.
- Step 9: the primary card reads "Free Ride", subtitle "Slope + virtual gears", in the green accent.
- Step 10: the Import button reads "Import (.gpx .fit .tcx)", in the same green accent.
- Step 11: on FREE the bundled route library is still listed.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0223` | 3 | A card drawing a power waveform where a silhouette belongs now shares its result with every other card defect on the screen. |
| `TST-0224` | 5, 6 | A wrong subtitle format and a duration that should not be there land on one tick. The missing-profile fallback it also asked for is a unit test now; see below. |
| `TST-0225` | 4 | A silhouette that ignores absolute relief no longer records apart from a silhouette that is the wrong shape entirely. |
| `TST-0226` | 7, 8 | The segment on a phone and on a tablet share one result, so a failure names the device only if the tester writes it down. |
| `TST-0227` | 9 | A missing Free Ride card no longer records apart from a missing Import button. |
| `TST-0240` | 10 | A wrong Import button label no longer records apart from a wrong Free Ride subtitle. |
| `TST-0275` | 11 | A FREE rider losing the library reads as the same failure as a PRO rider losing it. |

*(partially automated: `WorkoutRepositoryLibraryTest` covers the bundled-asset catalogue surface and that listing is not tier-gated; `RouteGpxImporterTest` covers distance and ascent computation from the route profile; `FreeRideCardTest.route_tab_renders_free_ride_with_slope_subtitle` covers the Free Ride title and subtitle; `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` exercises the per-tab extension allowlist behind the Import button's copy. Every rendering claim above stays visual.)*

## Step 7 retired, 2026-09-25

Step 7 used to read: *"A route with a missing profile falls back to the difficulty alone. Fewer than two stored profile points renders `Diff: n` and nothing else."* No rider can reach that card through the app. The GPX, FIT and TCX importers refuse a track with fewer than two points (`RouteImportOutcome.Failure.TooFewPoints`), and every point they keep becomes one profile point. `WorkoutValidator` refuses a `.ytw` route with a shorter profile, and every bundled route has at least five profile points. Only an Android `.ytwpack` install skips the validator. Edwin decided on 2026-09-25 to retire the step and cover the fallback with a unit test instead ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]], decision 7). On Android that test is [[TASK-0965-RetireTheUnreachableRouteCardStepAndUnitTestTheFallback|TASK-0965]]; the fallback is at `WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:2426-2428`, inside `WorkoutItem`, reached when `profile.size >= 2` fails at `:2392`. The step used to cite `:2839`, which is a `LibraryUiState` declaration. On iOS it is [[TASK-0963-TheIosRouteCardWithNoProfileIsUnitTested|TASK-0963]]. Steps 8 to 12 became steps 7 to 11.

## Steps 5, 7 and 8 rewritten for FEAT-0131, 2026-09-29

Step 8 used to say the steepest grade was absent below 600 dp, and that this was correct. ADR-0018 forbids a screen that changes its content by width, so [[TASK-1006-TheTwoIss0505SitesTheAmendmentDoesNotAllow]] made the route card show the grade at every width and removed `isWideRow`. Step 5's example changed with it ([[CHG-20260929-The-Cockpit-Fits-Every-Screen-And-The-Terrain-Keeps-Its-Share]]).

items.key: TST-0228 Cockpit Title in Top Bar
items.name: Cockpit Title in Top Bar
items.text:
Start any Route ride. Verify the workout name appears in the cockpit top bar and is not duplicated elsewhere in the cockpit body.

## Expect

- The workout name is in the cockpit top bar, and not repeated in the cockpit body.

items.key: TST-0229 Terrain Fills Vertical Space
items.name: Terrain Fills Vertical Space
items.text:
In the Route cockpit, verify the terrain view expands to fill the available vertical space between the metrics row and the controls row — no large unused gap.

## Expect

- The terrain view fills the space between the metrics row and the controls row, with no large gap.

items.key: TST-0230 Route ride — the cockpit through one bundled route
items.name: Route ride — the cockpit through one bundled route
items.text:
Tap a bundled Route on a SIM-capable trainer and ride it. Do not set repeats; step 5 depends on the ride being single-lap. One ride answers all five steps.

## Steps

1. **The ride starts in SIM.** Trainer resistance is driven by terrain grade. Watts are measured, not a target — the rider controls power through effort and gearing.
2. **The rider marker advances.** The 2D elevation profile shows a marker moving left to right as the rider pedals, and distance covered increases smoothly.
3. **Power is the hero metric.** The cockpit renders power large and speed as the secondary figure.
4. **No ERG watt controls.** The `+` / `−` watt buttons must not appear anywhere in the Route cockpit. On a Route, watts are measured from the rider's effort rather than set.
5. **No LAP | RIDE sub-values.** With no repeats set, the cockpit shows today's `AVG | MAX` everywhere. The `LAP | RIDE` variant must not appear.

## Expect

- Step 1: the ride is in SIM: grade drives resistance, and watts are measured, not a target.
- Step 2: the marker moves left to right, and distance covered rises smoothly.
- Step 3: power is the large figure; speed is the smaller one.
- Step 4: no `+` / `−` watt buttons anywhere in the Route cockpit.
- Step 5: `AVG | MAX` everywhere; `LAP | RIDE` never appears.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0231` | 2 | A marker that never moves no longer records apart from a ride that never entered SIM. |
| `TST-0233` | 3, 4 | The hero-metric layout and the absent ERG controls share one result, so a cockpit that shows speed large and a cockpit that offers watt buttons read the same. |
| `TST-0270` | 5 | Lap sub-values leaking onto a single-lap ride now fails the same tick as the wrong hero metric. |

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.selectWorkout_ROUTE_with_sim_capable_trainer_uses_SIMULATION` and `.selectWorkout_ROUTE_populates_initial_grade_from_profile` cover mode dispatch, the initial grade and distance-driven profile indexing; BLE resistance and every on-screen figure stay manual.)*

items.key: TST-0232 Grade drives resistance, and it changes continuously
items.name: Grade drives resistance, and it changes continuously
items.text:
Ride a route with varied but smoothly varying terrain — no stepped intervals. One ride answers both steps.

## Steps

1. **Resistance follows the terrain.** Trainer resistance increases on climbs and decreases on descents, and speed changes follow from physics given the rider's weight and power.
2. **No abrupt jumps between grade samples.** Resistance changes smoothly across sample boundaries. The engine interpolates grade rather than stepping it.

## Expect

- Step 1: resistance rises on climbs and falls on descents, and speed follows from weight and power.
- Step 2: resistance changes smoothly, with no jumps between grade samples.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0234` | 2 | A stepped, jumpy resistance curve now records the same result as resistance that does not respond to grade at all. |

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.selectWorkout_ROUTE_populates_initial_grade_from_profile` covers grade computation from the profile and the interpolation path between samples; the trainer's physical response stays hardware-dependent.)*

items.key: TST-0235 ERG fallback on a trainer with no SIM support
items.name: ERG fallback on a trainer with no SIM support
items.text:
Start a bundled Route ride on a trainer that does not support FTMS SIM — an older direct-drive unit or a basic smart trainer. On any trainer, pinning Slope behaviour to `ERG` in Settings → Hardware exercises the same dispatch path. One ride answers both steps; step 2 is about the first five seconds, so watch the target from the moment the ride starts.

## Steps

1. **Targets are computed from grade and weight.** Target watts follow grade plus rider weight and are sent as ERG targets, and the trainer's resistance changes with them.
2. **The first five seconds ramp rather than jump.** Target watts are not artificially inflated at the start. They ramp with actual speed instead of being clamped to a value that assumed 10 km/h, so the target feels proportional to the rider's effort from the first pedal stroke.

## Expect

- Step 1: target watts follow grade and rider weight, are sent as ERG targets, and the resistance changes with them.
- Step 2: the target ramps with actual speed from the first stroke; it is not inflated at the start.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0455` | 2 | The ride-start ramp and the steady-state computation now share one result, so a fallback that is right after ten seconds and wrong at t=0 reads as a pass unless the rider watches the opening. |

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.selectWorkout_ROUTE_without_sim_support_falls_back_to_ERG` covers the fallback dispatch; the trainer's response and the opening ramp stay hardware-dependent.)*

items.key: TST-0236 Auto-Zoom Window
items.name: Auto-Zoom Window
items.text:
Ride **Alpe d'Huez (YT)**, a bundled route 15.6 km long, and verify the terrain view auto-zooms around the rider's current position instead of squashing the whole route end to end. The window holds 1 km behind the rider and 4 km ahead, and it scrolls with the rider (`RouteTerrainView.kt:240-243`).

**Pick a route longer than 5 km, or the check reads as a failure that is not one.** The zoom applies only above a 5,000 m route length; below it the view shows the route whole, which is correct. On the Velodrome (250 m) or the Time Trial Course (exactly 5,000 m, so under the strict threshold) there is nothing to auto-zoom. Mont Ventoux (YT), Passo dello Stelvio (YT) and Sa Calobra (YT) are the other bundled routes that qualify.

## Expect

- The terrain view shows about 1 km behind and 4 km ahead and scrolls with the rider, not the whole route squashed.

items.key: TST-0237 Route Free Ride Terrain Style
items.name: Route Free Ride Terrain Style
items.text:
## Steps

On the Workouts screen, choose Route in the ride-mode strip, tap the Free Ride card and start. Ride for 2+ minutes with varying slope.

## Expect

- A cumulative elevation profile with power-zone-coloured fill under the curve, matching the TASK-0351 restyle.

## Original wording

On the Workouts screen, choose Route in the ride-mode strip and tap the Free Ride card (the Route tab before PHASE-025). Start. Ride for 2+ minutes with varying slope. Verify the terrain view shows a cumulative elevation profile with power-zone-colored fill under the curve — matching the restyled look of TASK-0351.

items.key: TST-0238 Multi-Lap Loop
items.name: Multi-Lap Loop
items.text:
## Steps

1. Start a Route with the repeat button set to 1, which rides the route twice. Ride past the end of lap 1.
2. Ride to the end of lap 2.

## Expect

- Step 1: the rider marker resets to km 0 at the lap boundary.
- Step 2: session distance adds up across both laps: a 5 km route ridden twice records 10 km.

## Notes

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.toggleLoop_cycles_off_1_2_3_off` + `WorkoutLoopTest` cover the loop-count state machine and boundary logic that drive the rider-marker reset; distance accumulation stays visual.)*

## Corrected 2026-09-17

This check used to set the repeat button to 2 and expect a route ridden twice. The button counts extra laps after the first, so 2 rides the route three times ([[TST-0188-Loop-Label-Uniform-Across-Paradigms]]). Edwin chose repeat 1 on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]), the shortest ride that still crosses a lap boundary.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0239 Loop Bracket on Terrain
items.name: Loop Bracket on Terrain
items.text:
With repeat active on a Route, verify the terrain view shows a bracket (┣━┫) over the route body and a repeat-count badge. *(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.toggleLoop_cycles_off_1_2_3_off` covers the `targetLoops` state that drives the bracket-render branch; terrain drawing stays visual.)*

## Expect

- The terrain view shows a bracket (┣━┫) over the route body and a repeat-count badge.

items.key: TST-0241 Import a route through the picker — GPX, FIT and TCX
items.name: Import a route through the picker — GPX, FIT and TCX
items.text:
On Workouts, pick **Route** in the ride-mode strip, tap Import and run the same flow three times, once per file format. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS. The SAF picker is the part no test reaches.

## Setup

A PRO rider. A valid `.gpx`, `.fit` course and `.tcx` file on the device or in Drive.

## Steps

1. **GPX.** Pick a valid `.gpx`. The summary dialog shows distance, total ascent, elevation-point count, and a name field pre-filled with the file name and still editable.
2. **FIT.** Same flow with a valid `.fit` course file, same summary dialog.
3. **TCX.** Same flow with a valid `.tcx`, same summary dialog.

## Expect

- Step 1: the summary shows distance, total ascent, elevation-point count, and an editable name filled with the file name.
- Step 2: the same summary dialog, for the `.fit` course.
- Step 3: the same summary dialog, for the `.tcx`.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0242` | 2 | A FIT course that no longer parses records the same result as a GPX that no longer parses, so the release test cannot say which format broke. |
| `TST-0243` | 3 | The same for TCX. Write the failing format next to the tick when one of the three fails. |

*(partially automated: `RouteGpxImporterTest`, `RouteFitImporterTest` and `RouteTcxImporterTest` cover parsing and the distance / ascent / point-count figures per format; `RouteImportSummaryDialogTest` covers dialog rendering. The SAF picker stays manual.)*

items.key: TST-0244 Import summary dialog — Save writes the route, Cancel writes nothing
items.name: Import summary dialog — Save writes the route, Cancel writes nothing
items.text:
Trigger the import summary dialog twice from the same file and take a different exit each time.

## Steps

1. **Save.** Edit the name, tap Save. The workout appears in the Route library under the edited name, and a **snackbar** reads "Imported: \<edited name\>". The feedback is the scaffold's snackbar, not a toast (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:961-968`); a toast appears only on a screen with no scaffold snackbar host.
2. **Cancel writes nothing.** Trigger the dialog again and tap Cancel. No workout is saved.
3. **Cancel says nothing either.** No import feedback appears on the Cancel path — no snackbar, no toast. This is the negative the merge keeps as its own step, because a Cancel that silently saves and a Cancel that silently confirms are different defects.

## Expect

- Step 1: the route is in the Route library under the edited name, and a snackbar, not a toast, reads "Imported: \<edited name\>".
- Step 2: no workout is saved.
- Step 3: no snackbar and no toast.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0245` | 2, 3 | A Cancel that saves the route anyway now fails the same tick as a Save that writes the wrong name. |

*(partially automated: `RouteImportSummaryDialogTest.save_fires_onConfirm_with_edited_name` and `.cancel_fires_onCancel_not_onConfirm` cover the dialog's two exits; library persistence and the snackbar copy stay manual.)*

items.key: TST-0246 Share sheet — Your Trainer opens a route sent from another app
items.area: Opening a file from another app
items.name: Share sheet — Your Trainer opens a route sent from another app
items.text:
With Your Trainer installed, hand it a route file from outside the app three times, once per format. Open the file from a Gmail attachment, from Drive, or from a file manager.

This is the Android incoming-share path registered with `ACTION_SEND`. The iOS app has an in-app Files importer but no incoming document or URL handler in the current project. Its ledger still owes this check; decide iOS applicability or add the receiving path before recording an iOS result.

## Steps

1. **GPX.** Share a `.gpx`. Your Trainer appears in the share-sheet chooser; picking it opens the import summary dialog.
2. **FIT.** Same with a `.fit` attachment.
3. **TCX.** Same with a `.tcx` attachment.

## Expect

- Step 1: Your Trainer is in the share sheet, and picking it opens the import summary.
- Step 2: the same for the `.fit`.
- Step 3: the same for the `.tcx`.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0247` | 2 | A manifest that stopped claiming FIT now records the same result as one that stopped claiming GPX, so the tick cannot say which MIME type was dropped. |
| `TST-0248` | 3 | The same for TCX. Write the failing format next to the tick. |

*(partially automated: `RouteGpxImporterTest`, `RouteFitImporterTest`, `RouteTcxImporterTest` and `WorkoutViewModelPendingImportTest` cover per-format parsing and the pending-import dispatch through the view model; the `ACTION_SEND` manifest registration that puts the app in the chooser stays manual.)*

items.key: TST-0249 External Share — FREE Tier Redirects to Paywall
items.area: Opening a file from another app
items.name: External Share — FREE Tier Redirects to Paywall
items.text:
On FREE tier, share a `.gpx` into Your Trainer from Gmail / Drive / a file manager. Verify the paywall screen opens immediately — no file parse, no summary dialog, no toast. Same check for `.fit`, `.tcx`, `.ytw`, and `.zwo`.. *(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` covers the VM choke-point — FREE-tier import of any extension short-circuits to a paywall signal before parsing; share-sheet + navigation stays manual.)*

## Expect

- The paywall opens at once for every format: no file parse, no summary dialog, no toast.

items.key: TST-0250 Open-With (file manager Open-With) — GPX/FIT/TCX/ZWO/YTW
items.area: Opening a file from another app
items.name: Open-With (file manager Open-With) — GPX/FIT/TCX/ZWO/YTW
items.text:
Open a system file manager (Files by Google + one third-party such as Solid Explorer or X-plore).

## Steps

1. For each of `.gpx`, `.fit`, `.tcx`, `.zwo`, `.ytw`, **tap the file** (or long-press → Open with…).
2. Pick Your Trainer for a Route format (`.gpx`, `.fit`, `.tcx`).
3. Pick Your Trainer for a workout format (`.zwo`, `.ytw`).
4. Repeat for a downloaded copy (`file://`) and a SAF / Drive copy (`content://`).

## Expect

- Step 1: "Your Trainer" is in the chooser.
- Step 2: picking it opens the route summary dialog.
- Step 3: picking it imports the workout directly.
- Step 4: downloaded (`file://`) and Drive (`content://`) copies both open.

## Notes

This is an Android Open-With and URI-handling check. The current iOS app imports files from its own Files picker and has no registered incoming document or URL handler. Its ledger still owes this check; settle iOS scope or supply that handler before attempting an iOS verdict.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0251 Open-With cold-launch with NO rider yet (TASK-0426 / ISS-0197)
items.area: Opening a file from another app
items.name: Open-With cold-launch with NO rider yet (TASK-0426 / ISS-0197)
items.text:
## Steps

1. Force-stop Your Trainer. From the file manager Open-With a `.gpx`, `.fit`, or `.tcx`. App opens at the rider-selection screen.
2. Pick / create a rider.
3. Confirm the import, then open the matching tab.

## Expect

- Step 1: the file is held: no toast and no dialog yet.
- Step 2: once the rider is picked, the route summary dialog appears (an `Imported: ...` toast for `.ytw` or `.zwo`).
- Step 3: the workout is in the matching ride mode.

## Notes

Pre-fix: the URI was consumed against the stale `currentUserTier = "FREE"` initial value before the rider loaded; either the paywall fired (without nav resolution) or the import was silently dropped, and the file appeared to vanish.

This is the Android external Open-With cold-start path. The current iOS app has no incoming document or URL handler, so its Files picker cannot reproduce this rider-selection handoff. Keep the iOS result unresolved until its scope or receiving path is decided.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0252 Open-With from outside the app, and only one app instance (TASK-0426 / ISS-0197)
items.area: Opening a file from another app
items.name: Open-With from outside the app, and only one app instance (TASK-0426 / ISS-0197)
items.text:
Open Your Trainer to any rider and navigate somewhere other than Workout Selection — Settings, Active Workout or History. Background the app. Then Open-With a `.gpx` from the file manager. One Open-With answers all three steps.

This is the Android external Open-With and task-reuse path. The current iOS app has no incoming document or URL handler, and its app switcher does not test Android's `singleTask` behavior. Keep the iOS result unresolved until its scope or an iOS equivalent is decided.

## Steps

1. **The dialog comes to the front.** The Route Import Summary dialog appears on top of the screen the app was left on, not silently in the background.
2. **The saved route lands in the library.** Save the route, then visit the Route tab and find it there.
3. **Exactly one app instance.** Open the recent-apps switcher. There is exactly **one** Your Trainer entry, not two. Before the fix, `launchMode="singleTop"` let the file-manager task spawn a separate MainActivity in a new task; `singleTask` now brings the existing instance forward and fires `onNewIntent`.

## Expect

- Step 1: the route summary dialog opens on top of the screen the app was left on.
- Step 2: the saved route is in the Route library.
- Step 3: exactly one Your Trainer entry, not two.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0253` | 3 | A second app task in the switcher now fails the same tick as a dialog that never appeared, even though one is a manifest regression and the other a navigation one. The duplicate-instance check is kept as its own named step for that reason — note it separately when it is the half that failed. |

items.key: TST-0254 Import failures — three bad files, three snackbar messages
items.name: Import failures — three bad files, three snackbar messages
items.text:
Import three deliberately broken `.gpx` files in one go and read the message each produces. Every message is the scaffold's snackbar, not a toast (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:961-968`); a toast appears only on a screen with no scaffold snackbar host.

## Steps

1. **Malformed file.** Import a truncated or broken `.gpx`. The snackbar reads "Import failed — File is malformed or not a valid route file."
2. **No elevation.** Import a `.gpx` whose trackpoints carry no `<ele>` tags. The snackbar reads "Import failed — Track points have no elevation data — route needs elevation to ride."
3. **Empty track.** Import a `.gpx` containing `<trk><trkseg></trkseg></trk>`. The snackbar reads "Import failed — No track points found in the file."

## Expect

- Step 1: the snackbar reads "Import failed — File is malformed or not a valid route file."
- Step 2: the snackbar reads "Import failed — Track points have no elevation data — route needs elevation to ride."
- Step 3: the snackbar reads "Import failed — No track points found in the file."

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0255` | 2 | The three rejection reasons collapse to one result, so a no-elevation file that is reported as malformed reads as a pass unless the rider notes the wrong message. |
| `TST-0256` | 3 | The same for the empty-track message. Note which of the three messages was wrong next to the tick. |

*(partially automated: `RouteGpxImporterTest` covers all three reject paths and the typed failure each produces; the snackbar copy stays manual.)*

items.key: TST-0257 Wrong-Tab File Filter
items.name: Wrong-Tab File Filter
items.text:
## Setup

A PRO rider and a `.gpx` file on the device or in Drive. The ride-mode strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS.

## Steps

1. On Workouts, pick **Heart Rate** in the ride-mode strip. Tap Import and pick a `.gpx`.
2. The snackbar carries a **Retry** action; tap it.

## Expect

- Step 1: a snackbar reads "Unsupported file type — please select a .ytw file", and nothing imports.
- Step 2: the file picker opens again.

## Notes

The feedback is the scaffold's snackbar, not a toast; a toast appears only on a screen with no scaffold snackbar host.

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` covers the dispatch rejection for an unsupported extension; the per-tab copy and the Retry action stay manual.)*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0258 Free Tier Import Lock
items.name: Free Tier Import Lock
items.text:
## Setup

A FREE rider. Tier Override in Developer Options sets FREE without a purchase.

On FREE tier, open Workouts, pick **Route** in the ride-mode strip, and tap Import. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS. Verify the button shows a lock icon and tapping navigates to the paywall — no SAF picker. *(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` covers the VM tier gate + `ImportPaywallNavigationTest` covers the paywall nav dispatch; button lock-icon rendering stays manual.)*

items.key: TST-0259 Pro Tier Import Success
items.name: Pro Tier Import Success
items.text:
On Pro/Family tier, run the full Import flow end-to-end (SAF → summary dialog → Save). Verify the imported route is rideable (trainer resistance responds to grade). *(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` covers Pro-tier bypass of the import gate; `RouteImportSummaryDialogTest` covers the summary dialog; end-to-end SAF + rideability stays hardware-dependent.)*

## Expect

- The imported route is rideable: trainer resistance responds to grade.

items.key: TST-0260 History shows the route ride, and the Route filter finds it
items.name: History shows the route ride, and the Route filter finds it
items.text:
Complete a Route ride, then open History. One completed ride answers both steps.

## Setup

Any rider with a trainer connected. Complete one Route ride, and have at least one Power session in History to filter out.

## Steps

1. **The session row is labelled.** The row shows a "Route" label and the Route-tab icon (bike / location).
2. **The Route filter chip works.** Tap the "Route" chip. On Android the filters are in a row under the **Past Sessions** heading in History. On iOS they are in the History strip, which sits above the bottom bar on a phone and under History in the rail on a tablet. Only Route sessions remain in the list.

## Expect

- Step 1: the row shows a "Route" label and the Route icon (bike / location).
- Step 2: only Route sessions remain in the list.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0261` | 2 | A filter chip that lets a Power session through now fails the same tick as a session row missing its Route label, though only one of the two involves the filter predicate. |

*(partially automated: `WorkoutSessionRepositoryTest` covers session persistence and the `workoutType` round-trip; `WorkoutHistoryViewModelTest` covers the chip state driving the session predicate. Both renderings stay manual.)*

items.key: TST-0263 Lap-times strip on a velodrome ride — overflow, personal-best deltas, and the rollover banner
items.name: Lap-times strip on a velodrome ride — overflow, personal-best deltas, and the rollover banner
items.text:
Run a velodrome (∞) ride past 6 laps on a course where you already hold a personal best. One ride answers all four steps.

## Steps

1. **Every closed lap is shown.** The strip lists each closed lap with no truncation and no leading ellipsis.
2. **The newest lap is pinned right.** Older laps push left and overflow off-screen as new ones land; swipe left and the older laps pan back into view. The strip auto-scrolls to the new lap on each rollover, via `LaunchedEffect(laps.size)`.
3. **Personal-best delta suffix.** Each strip entry shows `(−m:ss)` in green or `(+m:ss)` in muted grey. Lower is better, so a minus sign is the faster lap.
4. **The lap-rollover banner does not swallow touches.** While the banner is on screen after a rollover, tap STOP. The tap is processed and the session ends.

## Expect

- Step 1: every closed lap is shown, with no truncation and no leading ellipsis.
- Step 2: the newest lap is on the right; older laps scroll off left and swipe back; each rollover scrolls to the new lap.
- Step 3: each lap shows `(−m:ss)` in green or `(+m:ss)` in muted grey against the personal best.
- Step 4: the tap is processed and the session ends.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0264` | 3 | A delta with the wrong sign now records the same result as a strip that truncates its laps, though one is a formatting bug and the other a layout one. |
| `TST-0266` | 4 | A banner that eats the STOP tap now fails the same tick as a mis-anchored strip, so note which half failed — a swallowed STOP is the one that traps a rider mid-ride. |

items.key: TST-0267 Strip Hidden on Power / HR-Zone
items.name: Strip Hidden on Power / HR-Zone
items.text:
Start a Power or HR-Zone workout. Verify the lap-times strip never renders regardless of interval transitions.

## Expect

- The lap-times strip never shows, at any interval transition.

items.key: TST-0269 LAP | RIDE sub-values on hero metrics
items.name: LAP | RIDE sub-values on hero metrics
items.text:
## Steps

1. On a multi-lap Route ride past at least one rollover, read the HR / POWER / CADENCE hero sub-values.
2. Ride through the next rollover and read them again.

## Expect

- Step 1: each reads `LAP n | AVG n | MAX n`, not `AVG | MAX`. Where one line is too narrow, `LAP n` sits above `AVG n | MAX n`.
- Step 2: `LAP` restarts with the new lap's running average, while `AVG` and `MAX` carry on over the whole ride.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

## Expect lines corrected 2026-09-30

The Expect lines named the lap line `LAP X | RIDE Y`. The app draws `LAP n | AVG n | MAX n`, and has done since the strings were extracted in PHASE-014, so the lines now name what is drawn. Since [[TASK-1011-EdwinsAnswersTheLapLineWrapsAndTheRidingAsLabelMovesLeft]] the line breaks into two lines between its groups where it does not fit, which step 1 now allows. What the check asks for is otherwise unchanged ([[CHG-20260929-The-Cockpit-Fits-Every-Screen-And-The-Terrain-Keeps-Its-Share]]).

items.key: TST-0271 Lap sub-values silent on Power / HR-Zone
items.name: Lap sub-values silent on Power / HR-Zone
items.text:
Start a Power and then an HR-Zone structured workout. Verify the cockpit sub-values remain `AVG | MAX` even if the workout has interval repeats active.

## Expect

- The sub-values stay `AVG | MAX` on the Power and the HR-Zone workout, even with repeats on.

items.key: TST-0272 Cadence TARGET line preserved
items.name: Cadence TARGET line preserved
items.text:
On a structured Power workout with a cadence target, verify the CADENCE sub-line still reads `TARGET: N | AVG: X` (the TARGET takes precedence over the `LAP | RIDE` fallback).

## Expect

- The CADENCE sub-line reads `TARGET: N | AVG: X`, not the `LAP | RIDE` fallback.

items.key: TST-0273 Route Free Ride Unconstrained
items.name: Route Free Ride Unconstrained
items.text:
## Steps

On FREE tier, start Route Free Ride.

## Expect

- The ride runs to completion and can be started again, without limit.

## Original wording

On FREE tier, start Route Free Ride. Verify the ride runs to completion and can be started again, without limit. *(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.startFreeRide_default_is_SIMULATION_for_Route_tab` + `LicensingManagerTest` — Free-Ride dispatch reaches SIMULATION on the Route tab.)*

## Corrected 2026-09-12 — "no token is consumed" named a counter that no longer exists

The original asked a rider to confirm a token was *not* consumed, and FEAT-0096 deleted the counter in June (`LicensingManager.kt:148-155`). A negative check against an absent mechanism reads as passing whatever the app does, so it was worth nothing.

The outcome is still worth testing: a FREE rider can start a Route Free Ride as often as they like. That is what the row asks for now.

The FREE line moved to per-workout content gating through `FreeBundledCatalog`; [[TST-0062-Free-Tier-Locks]] holds the inventory. [[TST-0274-Route-Structured-Consumes-Token-Start]] was retired by the same removal, as were [[TST-0217-HR-Structured-Consumes-Token-Start]] and the run plan's whole Phase 3.

items.key: TST-0276 Per-rider export — location, tier gate and default filename
items.name: Per-rider export — location, tier gate and default filename
items.text:
## Setup

**PRO or FAMILY tier, with at least two riders, one of them named something like "Sarah Jones".**

## Steps

1. **The row lives on the rider profile.** Open the current rider's profile → Data: tap the rider's name in the bottom bar or rail, then **Profile**. On Android, **Profile** is the button under the current rider's card. On iOS it is next to **Switch rider**, and Data is a section of the same Profile screen.
2. **It is per-rider.** Switch to a different rider, then open their Profile. To switch on Android, tap the rider's name, then the other rider's card. On iOS, tap the rider's name, then **Switch rider**, and pick the other rider.
3. **PRO and FAMILY are not gated.** With a rider selected, run the Export row.
4. **The default filename is pre-filled.** Read the filename in the SAF "Save As" dialog. On iOS, read the filename the Files save sheet offers.

## Expect

- Step 1: an "Export My Data" row, with the rider's name in the default filename.
- Step 2: the same row, carrying this rider's name.
- [android] Step 3: the row is enabled, and it saves a `.ytrider.json.gz` file through the Save As dialog (SAF).
- [ios] Step 3: the row is enabled, and it saves a `.ytrider.json.gz` file through the Files save sheet.
- [android] Step 4: the Save As dialog offers `Sarah-Jones-YYYY-MM-DD.ytrider.json.gz`.
- [ios] Step 4: the Files save sheet offers `Sarah-Jones-YYYY-MM-DD.ytrider.json.gz`.

## Notes

The export was previously surfaced in Settings; it lives on the rider profile so the rider context is unambiguous.

The full sanitisation and date contract is pinned in `RiderFilenameTest` (12 tests); step 4 exists only because Compose-test cannot drive the system SAF dialog.

*(partially automated: `UserRepositoryTest.empty_db_has_no_users` + `insert_persists_user_and_surfaces_in_allUsers_flow` cover the visibility data condition, `LicensingManagerTest` covers tier resolution, and `RiderFileSerializationTest` covers the produced file's shape; the Profile-screen rendering, the button enable-state and the SAF dialog stay manual.)*

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0278]] (step 3) and [[TST-0279]] (step 4). One screen, one rider, one SAF invocation — nobody would set this up three times.

[[TST-0277]] stays separate. It tests the FREE tier's export gate, and a leaking export gate is a revenue defect rather than another reading of this screen.

One tick no longer separates a missing row from a disabled button from a wrong filename. The three fail for different reasons in different files, so write down the step number.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps under `## Steps` with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0277 Export Gating — Free Tier
items.name: Export Gating — Free Tier
items.text:
Set tier to FREE. Verify the Export My Data row (`up_data_export_title`) shows a lock icon and tapping it opens the paywall. No file is produced. *(partially automated: `LicensingManagerTest` tier resolution; navigation pattern covered in `ImportPaywallNavigationTest`; button visual + SAF negative-case stay manual.)*

## Expect

- The Export My Data row shows a lock, and tapping it opens the paywall.
- No file is produced.

items.key: TST-0280 Dispatch on Import — rider file vs device file
items.name: Dispatch on Import — rider file vs device file
items.text:
Two imports back to back, from Import Backup. The sequence is the point: running them one after the other is what proves the sniffer does not confuse the two formats.

On iOS, use **Restore from Backup** in Settings → Data for both files. That picker detects a full device backup as well as a single-rider file. On Android, use Import Backup.

## Setup

A PRO or FAMILY rider. A `.ytrider.json.gz` rider file and a `.ytbackup.json.gz` device backup, pinned offline in Drive.

## Steps

1. **A rider file opens the rider dialog.** Pick a `.ytrider.json.gz` — a freshly exported one or a `demo/riders/` fixture. The **detection-driven rider-import dialog** appears, offering "Add as new rider / Merge into existing". The device-level Merge/Overwrite dialog does not.
2. **A device backup opens the device dialog.** Immediately after, pick a `.ytbackup.json.gz`. The device-level Merge/Overwrite dialog appears instead.

*(partially automated: `BackupImporterParseTest` classifies the two file shapes deterministically, so dispatch cannot leak; the dialog rendering stays manual.)*

## Expect

- Step 1: the rider-import dialog opens, offering "Add as new rider / Merge into existing". The device Merge/Overwrite dialog does not.
- Step 2: the device-level Merge/Overwrite dialog opens instead.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0440]] (step 1) and [[TST-0441]] (step 2). The three rows were the same two imports written out three times — this one already carried both halves.

One tick no longer says which direction the sniffer got wrong. A rider file opening the device dialog risks an overwrite of everything; a device backup opening the rider dialog only fails. Write down which file you had picked.

## Steps heading added 2026-09-17

The numbered items had no `## Steps` heading, so the release test counted the whole check as one part and gave it one mark. With the heading each numbered item is its own part, and a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The items themselves are unchanged.

items.key: TST-0281 Rider import — detection None, on a clean device
items.name: Rider import — detection None, on a clean device
items.text:
On a clean device, import the demo fixture once and read three things off that one import.

**Stage the fixture.** `adb push demo/riders/demo-sarah.ytrider.json.gz /sdcard/Download/`, then import it from Import Backup. On iOS, put the file in Files and import it from Settings → Data → Restore from Backup.

## Steps

1. **Detection finds no overlap.** Read the import dialog.
2. **Add creates the rider.** Tap Add.
3. **Her Strava connection reads disconnected.** Open Sarah's profile → Connected.

## Expect

- Step 1: *"Add Sarah as a new rider?"* with [Cancel] [Add], and **no** "Add as new vs Merge" choice.
- Step 2: Sarah is in the rider list with her full data.
- Step 3: Strava is not connected.

## Notes

A rider file carries no credentials, and an imported rider must not inherit the exporting device's Strava link.

The data invariants (25 sessions, 195 W FTP / 65 kg / 178 max HR, no credentials in the raw JSON) are pinned in `PerRiderImportRoundTripTest` (9 tests). *(partially automated: `RiderImportConflictDetectionTest.empty_db_returns_None` + `PerRiderRestoreTest.first_ADD_NEW_import_creates_rider_with_full_data` cover the detection branch and data correctness; the SAF flow and the dialog rendering stay manual.)*

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0289]] (the staging line and step 3). Both rows imported the same fixture on the same clean device and read the same dialog; the only thing TST-0289 asserted that this row did not was the disconnected Strava state, which is now step 3.

One tick no longer separates a detection branch that picks the wrong dialog from an import that carries credentials across devices. The second is a privacy defect and the first is not, so name the step if the tick fails.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps under `## Steps` with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is otherwise unchanged. Staging the fixture was step 1 and produced no result of its own, so it is now the setup line above `## Steps`, and the three results are steps 1 to 3. The Absorbed section's step numbers follow that change.

items.key: TST-0282 Detection — Source-id Full Overlap (re-import)
items.name: Detection — Source-id Full Overlap (re-import)
items.text:
With Sarah already imported, import the same file again. Detection finds full overlap → dialog reads *"Already up to date — all sessions in this file are already on Sarah. No new data to merge."* / [OK]. **No "Add as duplicate" / "Merge anyway" buttons exist.** Tap OK → no change to the database (Sarah's session count unchanged). (TASK-0437 / ISS-0206) *(partially automated: `RiderImportConflictDetectionTest.full_source_id_overlap_returns_FullOverlap_with_owner_name`; the missing-button invariant must be eyeballed in the dialog.)*

## Expect

- *"Already up to date — all sessions in this file are already on Sarah. No new data to merge."* with [OK].
- **No "Add as duplicate" or "Merge anyway" button.**
- After OK, Sarah's session count is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0283 Detection — Source-id Partial Overlap (incremental sync)
items.name: Detection — Source-id Partial Overlap (incremental sync)
items.text:
Re-export Sarah from another device that has 5 additional rides on top of the previously-merged set. Import the new file. Detection finds 25 of 30 sessions present → dialog reads *"This file extends Sarah. 5 new sessions can be merged in; 25 already present will be skipped. Existing rider's FTP, weight, name, and colour are kept; only sessions and favourites are merged in."* / [Cancel] [Merge]. Tap Merge → Sarah now has 30 sessions; her profile fields unchanged. (TASK-0437 / ISS-0206) *(partially automated: `RiderImportConflictDetectionTest.partial_source_id_overlap_returns_PartialOverlap_with_counts` + `PerRiderRestoreTest.merge_same_file_into_two_different_riders_lands_full_data_on_both` covers the merge path data correctness; auto-skip behaviour stays manual.)*

## Expect

- *"This file extends Sarah. 5 new sessions can be merged in; 25 already present will be skipped."*
- *"Existing rider's FTP, weight, name, and colour are kept; only sessions and favourites are merged in."* [Cancel] [Merge].
- After Merge, Sarah has 30 sessions and her profile fields are unchanged.

items.key: TST-0284 Rider import — name collision, both answers
items.name: Rider import — name collision, both answers
items.text:
**Setup, used twice: an existing Sarah on the device, plus a rider file for a *different* Sarah with the same display name.** Detection finds zero source-id overlap and a name match. (TASK-0437 / ISS-0206)

## Steps

1. **The dialog asks the question.** Import the file and read the import dialog. Tap outside the dialog or press Back, then import the file again.
2. **No — add with different name.** Tap **No**.
3. **A name already in use is refused.** In that second dialog, type a name that already exists (the original Sarah's, for instance).
4. **The renamed rider is added.** Put back `"Sarah (2)"` and tap Add. Delete `Sarah (2)` before the next step.
5. **Yes — merge.** Import the same file again and tap **Yes**.

## Expect

- Step 1: *"There's already a rider named Sarah on this device. Is this the same person?"* [Yes — merge] [No — add with different name]. Back or outside-tap cancels.
- Step 2: a second dialog opens, its name pre-filled `"Sarah (2)"`.
- Step 3: an inline error reads *"Name already in use — try …"*.
- Step 4: `Sarah (2)` joins the rider list with full data. The original Sarah is unchanged.
- Step 5: the file's sessions merge into Sarah. Her FTP, weight, max HR, name and rider colour are unchanged.

## Notes

*(partially automated: `RiderImportConflictDetectionTest.no_source_overlap_with_single_name_match_returns_NameCollisionSingle` + `suggestUniqueRiderName_*` cover the detection branch and the suggestion bumping; the dialog rendering stays manual.)*

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0285]] (the rename steps).

The No and Yes answers are exclusive branches of one dialog, so each needs its own import. No is tested first because Yes merges the rides into the existing Sarah. The saving here is the setup, not the tap: building a second same-named Sarah file and putting an existing Sarah on the device is the expensive part, and it is now done once for both answers.

One tick no longer separates a merge that overwrites profile fields it should have left alone from a rename path that suggests or accepts the wrong name.

## Corrected 2026-09-17

Edwin decided on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]) that the dialog has two buttons, as [[TST-0490-Two-Action-Dialog-No-Stacked-Cancel]] and the app say. The steps now test No before Yes, because the old Yes-first order merged the rides before the rename branch could be tried. Step 5 names the five profile fields that [[TST-0443-Merge-Preserves-Target-Profile]] used to check; that check is retired into this one.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps under `## Steps` with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0287 Re-import after delete is fresh
items.name: Re-import after delete is fresh
items.text:
Import Sarah → delete Sarah on Rider selection (long-press her card, then Delete, on Android; touch and hold, then Delete, on iOS) → re-import same file. With B-light's cascade (TASK-0436) Sarah's sessions and source-id tags went with her, so detection sees no overlap → "Add Sarah as a new rider?" prompt → confirm → Sarah re-imported with full data. Pre-fix this would silently create an empty rider. (TASK-0436 / ISS-0206) *(partially automated: `UserRepositoryTest.delete_cascades_to_sessions_metrics_favorites_laps` + `PerRiderRestoreTest.second_ADD_NEW_import_of_same_file_creates_distinct_rider_with_full_data`.)*

## Expect

- The prompt reads *"Add Sarah as a new rider?"*.
- After confirming, Sarah is back with her full data, not as an empty rider.

items.key: TST-0288 Import Not Gated by Tier
items.name: Import Not Gated by Tier
items.text:
## Setup

A FREE-tier device and a `.ytrider` rider file. Tier Override in Developer Options sets FREE.

On a FREE tier device, verify Import flow works unchanged — receiving a rider file is free. *(partially automated: `BackupImporterParseTest` covers the per-rider file parse; tier-free behaviour is a policy assertion, covered conceptually by there being no tier check on the import path.)*

On iOS, use Rider Selection → Add Rider → Import from file… with a `.ytrider` file. This is the single-rider import route. Import Rider Data in the Data section of the rider's Profile is gated on a FREE rider. TST-0296's device-backup import is Restore from Backup in Settings → Data, which is not gated.

## Expect

- On FREE, importing a rider file works unchanged: receiving a rider file is free.

items.key: TST-0290 Settings → Data — Android Backup section and the export rows below it
items.name: Settings → Data — Android Backup section and the export rows below it
items.text:
Open Settings → Data.

On iOS, this Android-specific section is absent. The iOS release test keeps the check owed and asks for a platform scope decision before a verdict.

## Steps

1. **Header and primary copy.** An "Android Backup" header, followed by the always-accurate primary copy *"If Android backup is enabled on this device, your profiles and workout history ride along…"*.
2. **The per-OEM hint.** A navigation hint listing the Samsung and Stock Android paths.
3. **The settings link resolves.** An `Open Android Settings →` link opens a backup-related Android settings page, or falls back to root Settings.
4. **No detected state.** The section does **not** branch on a detected Auto Backup state. Third-party apps cannot query `BackupManager.isBackupEnabled()` (REQ-0109 § "API constraint"), so any copy claiming to know whether backup is on is the defect.
5. **The rows below.** Under the section sit Export Device Backup (CloudUpload icon) and Import Backup (CloudDownload icon), as SettingsRow entries with right-anchored buttons.

*(partially automated: `BackupController.kt:21-24` documents the no-query design and the static copy lives in `SettingsScreen.kt:517-535`; the intent resolution and the visual copy stay manual.)*

## Expect

- Step 1: an **Android Backup** header, then copy starting *"If Android backup is enabled on this device, your profiles and workout history ride along…"*.
- Step 2: a hint lists the Samsung and Stock Android paths.
- Step 3: `Open Android Settings →` opens a backup settings page, or falls back to root Settings.
- Step 4: no copy claims to know whether Auto Backup is on.
- Step 5: below it, Export Device Backup (cloud-upload icon) and Import Backup (cloud-download icon) rows, each with its button on the right.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0460]], which tested the same pane top to bottom. The only thing it asserted that this row did not is the pair of export rows below the section, now step 5.

One tick no longer separates wrong Android Backup copy from a missing Export or Import row. They sit in the same pane but come from different code, so name the step.

## Steps heading added 2026-09-17

The numbered items had no `## Steps` heading, so the release test counted the whole check as one part and gave it one mark. With the heading each numbered item is its own part, and a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The items themselves are unchanged.

items.key: TST-0291 Export Backup enables only once there is something to export
items.name: Export Backup enables only once there is something to export
items.text:
On iOS the household backup is in Settings → Data: **Back Up All Riders**, disabled until a rider exists, and **Restore from Backup**, available on a fresh install. Each rider's own export and import are in the Data section of that rider's Profile.

## Setup

A fresh install with zero riders and zero sessions: clear the Android app data, or delete and reinstall the iOS app.

## Steps

1. **Nothing to export.** On a **fresh install with zero riders and zero sessions**, Export Backup is **disabled** with the caption *"Nothing to export yet — complete a workout or add a rider first, then come back"*. Import Backup is **enabled**. On iOS, Back Up All Riders is disabled with no caption, and Restore from Backup is enabled; the missing caption is accepted (Edwin, 2026-09-25).
2. **One rider is enough.** Create the first rider. Export Backup becomes enabled even with zero sessions — `hasExportableData() = hasProfile || hasSession` (`BackupController.kt:46-49`).

*(partially automated: `BackupRoomDbTest.H1_hasExistingData_false_when_empty` covers empty-db detection; the button text and the transition after the first rider stay manual.)*

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: Export Backup is disabled, captioned *"Nothing to export yet — complete a workout or add a rider first, then come back"*. Import Backup is enabled.
- [ios] Step 1: Back Up All Riders is disabled, with no caption. Restore from Backup is enabled.
- [android] Step 2: Export Backup is enabled, even with zero sessions.
- [ios] Step 2: Back Up All Riders is enabled, even with zero sessions.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0292]], which asserted step 2 alone and was already a subset of this row's second sentence.

One tick no longer separates a button that is enabled when it should not be from one that stays disabled after the first rider is created. The first leaks an empty file, the second blocks a real export.

## Steps heading added 2026-09-17

The numbered items had no `## Steps` heading, so the release test counted the whole check as one part and gave it one mark. With the heading each numbered item is its own part, and a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The items themselves are unchanged.

items.key: TST-0293 Export Round-Trip
items.name: Export Round-Trip
items.text:
## Setup

At least one profile and one completed session. Test this third in the destructive backup sequence below.

On iOS, **Back Up All Riders**, in Settings → Data, opens the Files exporter. That path does not show the Android snackbar with row counts, so the iOS verdict needs a platform expectation.

With ≥1 profile and ≥1 completed session, tap Export Backup. Save as `your-trainer-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.ytbackup.json` to Downloads. Verify completion snackbar shows correct row counts. *(partially automated: `BackupRoomDbTest` C-series tests cover exporter row-count + structure; SAF save + snackbar rendering stays manual.)*

## Expect

- A completion snackbar shows the correct row counts.

## Test this third, in the destructive backup sequence

**These four rows do not merge; the saving is in running them in order.** Each needs a different install state, and two of them destroy the state the others need, so the order is the whole economy of this group.

1. Fresh install → [[TST-0291-Export-Button-Gating]]
2. Create a rider
3. **[[TST-0293-Export-Round-Trip]] — this row.** It produces the backup file every later step consumes, so nothing after it can run until it has.
4. [[TST-0298-Merge-Vs-Overwrite-Prompt]] — import over existing data
5. [[TST-0437-Auto-Backup-Does-Not-Carry-Credentials]] — uninstall and reinstall
6. [[TST-0295-Import-After-Wipe]] — Clear Data

**Anything that needs the pre-wipe state must finish before step 6.** TST-0295 clears app data, and nothing before it can be re-tested without rebuilding the install from step 1.

items.key: TST-0295 Import After Wipe
items.name: Import After Wipe
items.text:
Deleting and reinstalling the iOS test app produces an empty rider state. Its full-backup importer is **Restore from Backup**, in Settings → Data, which is there on a fresh install before any rider exists.

## Setup

A device backup exported once the install holds riders, sessions, favourites, a custom workout and a chosen theme and accent, such as the three-rider file [[TST-0438-Multi-Rider-Export]] step 1 exports. The backup made in [[TST-0293-Export-Round-Trip]] also works when the install held those things. Strava must be linked and a bring-your-own AI key set before the wipe, so step 2 has something to lose.

## Steps

1. Clear app data (Android Settings → Apps → Your Trainer → Storage → Clear Data). Reopen the app. Tap Import Backup, pick the saved file, and look through the restored install.
2. Open the Strava connection and the bring-your-own AI key slot.

*(partially automated: `BackupRoomDbTest` F-series + `BackupCredentialExclusionTest` cover the full-restore round-trip + the empty-credentials invariant; app-data wipe + reopen stays manual.)*

## Expect

- Step 1: profiles, sessions, metric points, favorites, custom workouts, and theme/accent are all restored.
- Step 2: Strava is disconnected and the bring-your-own AI key slot is empty; the rider signs in again.

## Test this last, in the destructive backup sequence

**These four rows do not merge; the saving is in running them in order.** Each needs a different install state, and two of them destroy the state the others need, so the order is the whole economy of this group.

1. Fresh install → [[TST-0291-Export-Button-Gating]]
2. Create a rider
3. [[TST-0293-Export-Round-Trip]] — export, producing the file this row imports
4. [[TST-0298-Merge-Vs-Overwrite-Prompt]] — import over existing data
5. [[TST-0437-Auto-Backup-Does-Not-Carry-Credentials]] — uninstall and reinstall
6. **[[TST-0295-Import-After-Wipe]] — this row, and it goes last.** Clearing app data destroys the state every row above it needs. **Anything that needs the pre-wipe state must finish before this row runs**, because recovering it means rebuilding the install from step 1.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The steps were one paragraph, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered with one expectation each, so a failure in one result no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0296 Backup import and export are both open to a FREE rider
items.name: Backup import and export are both open to a FREE rider
items.text:
One FREE-tier install, with at least one profile and one completed session, answers both halves.

On iOS, with the FREE rider selected, open Settings → Data. **Back Up All Riders** and **Restore from Backup** are both available with no lock, which is the FREE backup policy. The per-rider Import Rider Data, in the Data section of the rider's Profile, is a PRO feature and carries a lock; it is not this check's subject.

## Setup

A FREE-tier install with at least one profile and one completed session. Tier Override in Developer Options sets FREE.

## Procedure

1. **Import Backup is enabled and works.** On FREE tier, Import Backup is enabled and restores. A FREE rider must be able to get their data back.
2. **Export Backup is enabled, with no lock and no paywall.** On the same install, Export Backup is enabled — **no lock icon, no paywall redirect**. Device backup is the sole data-safety exception to REQ-0124's Pro/Family import and export gate.

*(Partially automated: `BackupImporterParseTest` covers the parse path on any tier, since the importer carries no tier check; `LicensingManagerTest` covers FREE-tier resolution and `BackupRoomDbTest.C1_export_with_existing_data` confirms the exporter bypasses the import gate. The Compose button states stay manual.)*

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: on FREE, Import Backup is enabled, with no paywall, and restores the file.
- [ios] Step 1: on FREE, Restore from Backup is available, with no lock or paywall, and restores the file.
- [android] Step 2: on FREE, Export Backup is enabled, with no lock icon and no paywall.
- [ios] Step 2: on FREE, Back Up All Riders is available, with no lock and no paywall.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0297-Export-Not-Gated-By-Tier]] | Export enabled on FREE, with no lock icon and no paywall redirect | step 2 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0297** — import and export are gated by different code, and export regressing behind the paywall would trap a FREE rider's data on the device; that now records as the same verdict as import being gated.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- The state of both buttons on the FREE install, and whether either routed to the paywall.

items.key: TST-0298 Merge vs Overwrite Prompt
items.name: Merge vs Overwrite Prompt
items.text:
On iOS, start with a selected PRO or FAMILY rider and existing data. Open Settings → Data → **Restore from Backup**, and pick the full device backup. The iOS importer opens the Merge/Overwrite choice for a populated install. On Android, use Import Backup.

## Setup

Existing data on the device, and a device backup that includes a profile with the same `userId`, such as the one [[TST-0293-Export-Round-Trip]] saved.

## Steps

1. With existing data, import a file that includes a profile with the same `userId`.
2. Tap **Merge**, then look at the existing data.
3. Import the same file again and tap **Overwrite**, then look at the data.

Both paths run atomically, with no partial state when a write fails. `BackupRoomDbTest`'s G-series forces that failure; the release test cannot, so it is not a tested step.

*(partially automated: `BackupRoomDbTest` E/F/G-series tests cover merge / overwrite / transaction atomicity; prompt rendering + user-tap dispatch stay manual.)*

## Expect

- Step 1: the Merge/Overwrite prompt appears.
- Step 2: Merge keeps the existing data and adds only what is new.
- Step 3: Overwrite replaces the existing data with the file's.

## Test this fourth, in the destructive backup sequence

**These four rows do not merge; the saving is in running them in order.** Each needs a different install state, and two of them destroy the state the others need, so the order is the whole economy of this group.

1. Fresh install → [[TST-0291-Export-Button-Gating]]
2. Create a rider
3. [[TST-0293-Export-Round-Trip]] — export, producing the file the rest consume
4. **[[TST-0298-Merge-Vs-Overwrite-Prompt]] — this row.** It is the only step that needs data already present **and** a backup file to import over it, so it has to run after the export and before anything that empties the install.
5. [[TST-0437-Auto-Backup-Does-Not-Carry-Credentials]] — uninstall and reinstall
6. [[TST-0295-Import-After-Wipe]] — Clear Data

**Anything that needs the pre-wipe state must finish before step 6.** TST-0295 clears app data, and nothing before it can be re-tested without rebuilding the install from step 1.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The steps were one paragraph, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered with one expectation each, so a failure in one result no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0299 Ghosts on a second ride — personal best, today, and both at once
items.name: Ghosts on a second ride — personal best, today, and both at once
items.text:
Complete a Route workout including at least one full lap, then start the same workout again and produce a lap faster than the stored personal best. One repeat ride answers all three steps.

## Steps

1. **Personal-best ghost.** A small bike icon (20 dp, 40 % alpha) renders in the **rider's accent colour** with a **trophy glyph above it** (10 dp, 75 % alpha — the personal-best shape-coded marker). The ghost line and icon advance during the ride.
2. **Today ghost.** The session-best ghost renders in **grey**, not the rider's colour, with a **dashed line** (5 dp on / 3 dp off, 0.75 dp wide) and a **⟳ refresh glyph above the bike icon** (10 dp, 75 % alpha). The refresh glyph replaced the earlier "TODAY" text label.
