3. **Both together.** After the faster lap, both ghosts render on the same y-row and stay legible: personal best in the accent colour with a solid line and trophy glyph, today in grey with the dashed line and refresh glyph. The earlier "adjacent y-rows" design was replaced by these shape-coded markers (`RouteTerrainView.kt:326-335`).

## Expect

- Step 1: a small bike in the rider's accent colour with a trophy above it; the line and bike advance.
- Step 2: the today ghost is grey, with a dashed line and a ⟳ refresh glyph above the bike.
- Step 3: both ghosts share one row and stay legible: accent, solid line and trophy; grey, dashed line and ⟳.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0310` | 2 | The today ghost's colour, line style and glyph now share a result with the personal-best ghost's, so a marker regression that hits only one of them reads the same as one that hits both. |
| `TST-0311` | 3 | Coexistence is no longer ticked apart from the two ghosts existing at all. Write down which of the three steps failed, since "neither drew" and "they drew on top of each other" have different causes. |

*(partially automated: `GhostRepositoryTest` covers the reconstruction path from session, lap and metric points into a distance series; on-device marker visibility stays manual.)*

items.key: TST-0300 Ghost Freezes On Pause
items.name: Ghost Freezes On Pause
items.text:
## Steps

1. While racing a Best Lap ghost, pause the ride.
2. Resume.

## Expect

- Step 1: the ghost marker stops at the exact pixel position.
- Step 2: it continues from the same position, with no jump ahead.

## Notes

*(partially automated: the pause-freeze mechanism relies on `lapElapsedSeconds` being derived from the paused timer; live visual freeze stays manual.)*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0301 Ghost Rewinds On Lap Rollover
items.name: Ghost Rewinds On Lap Rollover
items.text:
On a multi-lap ride, observe the ghost's position at the instant lap 1 rolls over to lap 2. Verify the ghost marker snaps back to the start of the terrain and begins racing lap 2. *(partially automated: `lapElapsedSeconds` reset happens via the existing `_currentLapStartSec` flow used for PB lap bookkeeping; visual snap-back stays manual.)*

## Expect

- At the rollover the ghost marker snaps back to the start of the terrain and races lap 2.

items.key: TST-0303 Family Ghost Colors + Labels (Family tier)
items.name: Family Ghost Colors + Labels (Family tier)
items.text:
With ≥2 riders who have each completed the same course, ride it on a third rider. Verify each family ghost has a distinct colour and is labelled with the rider's **first initial inside a coloured circle** above the bike icon (10dp, white text, 75 % alpha). Replaces the prior "rider name" text label per `RouteTerrainView.kt:326-335`. *(partially automated: `GhostRepositoryTest.getFamilyBestLaps picks one fastest lap per other rider`; colour stability + initial markers stay manual.)*

## Expect

- Each family ghost has its own colour, and the rider's first initial in a coloured circle above the bike.

items.key: TST-0305 Own ghosts always render and family ghosts stay behind the chip, on FREE and on PRO
items.name: Own ghosts always render and family ghosts stay behind the chip, on FREE and on PRO
items.text:
Ride a course that carries both your own ghost data and another rider's. That needs an account that was once FAMILY and has been downgraded, since neither FREE nor PRO writes another rider's ghosts. Ride it once on FREE, then flip the tier in Developer Settings and ride it again on PRO.

## Steps

1. **FREE — own personal best renders.** The trophy glyph in your accent colour draws on the terrain.
2. **FREE — the today ghost renders too.** After lap 1 the grey dashed line with the ⟳ refresh glyph appears alongside the personal best. Own data is never gated (ISS-0171).
3. **FREE — family ghosts do not render.** No other rider's ghost line or marker may appear anywhere on the terrain.
4. **FREE — the lock chip appears and leads to the paywall.** A "🔒 Family ghosts" chip sits top-left; tapping it opens the paywall.
5. **PRO — own personal best and today ghost both render.** Flip the tier to PRO in Developer Settings and ride the course again. Steps 1 and 2 must hold unchanged.
6. **PRO — family ghosts do not render.** Same negative as step 3, at the higher tier.
7. **PRO — the lock chip appears and leads to the paywall.** Same as step 4.

## Expect

- Step 1: FREE: your personal best, a trophy in your accent colour, draws on the terrain.
- Step 2: FREE: after lap 1 the grey dashed today ghost with ⟳ appears beside the personal best.
- Step 3: FREE: no other rider's ghost line or marker anywhere on the terrain.
- Step 4: FREE: a "🔒 Family ghosts" chip sits top-left, and tapping it opens the paywall.
- Step 5: PRO: your personal best and the today ghost both draw, as on FREE.
- Step 6: PRO: no other rider's ghost line or marker anywhere on the terrain.
- Step 7: PRO: the chip sits top-left, and tapping it opens the paywall.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0307` | 5, 6, 7 | FREE and PRO now share one result, so a gate that leaks family ghosts at exactly one tier reads as a plain failure without saying which tier leaked. Write the tier next to the tick. |
| `TST-0312` | 5 | The today ghost at PRO no longer records apart from the personal-best ghost at PRO. |
| `TST-0313` | 2 | The today ghost at FREE no longer records apart from the personal-best ghost at FREE. |

The negatives — steps 3 and 6 — stay named steps of their own at both tiers, because a leak of another rider's data is the failure this row exists to catch and it would otherwise pass silently under "my own ghost drew".

**This merge still costs two rides.** The tier flip cannot be done mid-ride, so steps 5 to 7 mean restarting. What the merge saves is the expensive part: building the downgraded-FAMILY ghost data once instead of four times.

*(partially automated: the tier filter and the `ghostLock` decision live in `ActiveWorkoutScreen`; chip rendering and paywall navigation stay manual.)*

items.key: TST-0306 No lock chip when the course carries no family ghosts, on FREE and on PRO
items.name: No lock chip when the course carries no family ghosts, on FREE and on PRO
items.text:
Ride a course that carries only your own ghost data — the ordinary case on both tiers. Ride it on FREE, then flip the tier in Developer Settings and ride it again on PRO.

## Steps

1. **FREE — own personal best renders.**
2. **FREE — no lock chip appears.** With nothing of another rider's to gate, there is nothing to upsell and the "🔒 Family ghosts" chip must not draw.
3. **PRO — own personal best renders.**
4. **PRO — no lock chip appears.** Same negative at the higher tier.

## Expect

- Step 1: FREE: your own personal best draws.
- Step 2: FREE: no "🔒 Family ghosts" chip.
- Step 3: PRO: your own personal best draws.
- Step 4: PRO: no "🔒 Family ghosts" chip.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0308` | 3, 4 | A stray chip at exactly one tier now records the same result as a stray chip at both. Write the tier next to the tick. |

Steps 2 and 4 are the negatives and each keeps its own named step, because a chip that appears with nothing behind it is a paywall pitch shown to a rider who has nothing locked.

*(partially automated: `ghostLock` is null when no other-rider ghosts exist; the on-device absence of the chip stays manual.)*

items.key: TST-0309 FAMILY Tier Shows All Ghosts
items.name: FAMILY Tier Shows All Ghosts
items.text:
On FAMILY tier, ride a course with multiple riders' ghost data. Verify all ghosts appear and no lock chip is shown. *(partially automated: tier filter returns the full ghost list.)*

## Expect

- Every rider's ghost appears, and no lock chip is shown.

items.key: TST-0314 Setting a power PB — the celebration's headline, and the chip it leaves on the library
items.name: Setting a power PB — the celebration's headline, and the chip it leaves on the library
items.text:
## Setup

A heart-rate strap connected for at least 80 % of each ride. A Power workout this rider has never ridden, such as [Debug] ERG Verify (Show debug workouts on). A second rider in the household.

## Steps

1. Ride the workout to its programmed end, tap Save ride, and read the celebration's headline.
2. Ride it to its end again with a lower average heart rate, save, and read the headline.
3. Open Workouts and find that workout's card.
4. Switch to the second rider, then back.

## Expect

- Step 1: `First time on <workout>` is the headline, or one of the Also this ride chips under a higher-ranked fact.
- Step 2: the headline reads `New best on <workout>`, with the heart-rate cost in bpm and `<n> bpm lower than the best from <date>`.
- Step 3: the card carries a `🏆 PB: <n> bpm` chip.
- Step 4: the chip hides for the second rider, and shows again on the way back.

## Not this check

- The trophy in History and the PBs filter: [[TST-0321-History-Trophy-Filter]], which builds a three-ride history of its own.
- The rest of the celebration: [[TST-0685-AfterSaveTheCelebrationLeadsWithTheHeadlineThenTheNumbersAndDoneGoesToHistory]].

## What is automated

*(mostly automated: `PbCalculatorTest` covers the average-HR formula and the validity gate; `PersonalBestServiceTest` covers the FIRST and BETTER transitions; `CelebrationRankerTest` (Android) and `CelebrationRankerTests` (iOS) pick `first` and `best` from the same case table; `CelebrationTextTest` and `CelebrationTextTests` word them; `PbChipTest` covers chip-label rendering for all four domain formats. The end-to-end rides, the rider-switch atomicity and the chip's position on `WorkoutItem` stay manual.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the personal-best card from the end of a ride. The best is now the celebration's headline after Save, as [[REQ-0131-SessionEndComparison]] was amended to say. Step 1 allows a higher-ranked fact, such as a peak power, to take the headline, because a rider who has ridden other workouts that day can earn one; the first time then shows as a chip. The four steps are numbered so each gets its own result.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0320` (Library PB Chip) — the `🏆 PB:` chip on the library card, and its disappearance and return across a rider switch. It is steps 3 and 4.

items.key: TST-0315 Power PB Adherence Fallback (no HRM)
items.name: Power PB Adherence Fallback (no HRM)
items.text:
## Setup

No heart-rate strap. Show debug workouts on. The rider has ridden [Debug] Mini Ramp to its end once without a strap, stopping pedalling for 30 seconds in the middle, and saved it.

## Steps

1. Ride [Debug] Mini Ramp to its end again without a strap, pedalling throughout. Save, and read the headline.

## Expect

- Step 1: the headline reads `New best on [Debug] Mini Ramp`, with an adherence percentage such as `94 %` and `<n> points better than the best from <date>`.

## Not this check

- The heart-rate cost a strap gives: [[TST-0314-Power-PB-Happy-Path-With-HRM]].

## What is automated

*(mostly automated: `PbCalculatorTest.power falls back to adherence when hrm uptime below 80 percent`; the celebration words a `percent` best with `celebration_comparison_best_points` on Android and the same sentence on iOS, covered by `CelebrationTextTest` and `CelebrationTextTests`. An HRM drop mid-ride stays hardware.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the personal-best card and its footer. The adherence figure now shows as the large number under a `New best on` headline, so the check rides the workout twice: the first ride is setup, and only a better second ride has a best to state ([[REQ-0131-SessionEndComparison]]).

items.key: TST-0316 Route PB Happy Path
items.name: Route PB Happy Path
items.text:
## Setup

A trainer that accepts control. A circuit route that rolls over at the end of each lap, such as Velodrome, with no personal best for this rider in the current physics version.

## Steps

1. Ride the route through at least one full lap, then tap FINISH, Save ride, and read the headline.
2. Ride it again with a faster lap, to the end, save, and read the headline.

## Expect

- Step 1: `First time on <route>` is the headline, or one of the Also this ride chips under a higher-ranked fact.
- Step 2: the headline reads `New best on <route>`, with the lap time, such as `24:06`, and `<delta> faster than the best from <date>`.

## Not this check

- That a route best from before 2026-06-18 does not compete: [[TST-0636-Physics-Constants-And-PB-Lineage-ISS-0335]].
- The household best on a route, which needs FAMILY and a second rider: the ranking unit tests, `CelebrationRankerTest` and `CelebrationRankerTests`.

## What is automated

*(mostly automated: `PbCalculatorTest` covers per-lap attempt generation and tolerance; `PersonalBestServiceTest.route multi-lap picks the best news for the outcome`; `route lap exactly 1 second faster than pb reports BETTER not EQUAL`; `CelebrationTextTest` and `CelebrationTextTests` word a route best with its delta. The ride stays manual.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the personal-best card. A route best is now the celebration's headline after Save, with the lap time as its large number and the comparison under it ([[REQ-0131-SessionEndComparison]]). Step 1 used to read `Time: 24:18` on the card; a first time has no previous best to compare with.

items.key: TST-0317 HR-Zone PB Happy Path
items.name: HR-Zone PB Happy Path
items.text:
## Setup

A heart-rate strap connected for at least 80 % of each ride. An HR-Zone workout this rider has never ridden, such as [Debug] Single Z3.

## Steps

1. Ride the workout to its programmed end, tap Save ride, and read the headline.
2. Ride it again to its end with a better result, save, and read the headline.

## Expect

- Step 1: `First time on <workout>` is the headline, or one of the Also this ride chips under a higher-ranked fact.
- Step 2: the headline reads `New best on <workout>`, with the efficiency in W/bpm, such as `1.82 W/bpm`, and how much better than the previous best.

## Not this check

- The headline for a ride held in its zone: [[TST-0686-TheCelebrationsHeadlineNamesTheRidesMostNotableFact]].

## What is automated

*(partially automated: `PbCalculatorTest.hr zone primary is efficiency factor np over avg hr`, `PersonalBestServiceTest.first power attempt writes FIRST and upserts pb` (same evaluation path), and the `W/bpm` best in `CelebrationRankerTest` and `CelebrationRankerTests`.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the personal-best card. The best is now the celebration's headline after Save ([[REQ-0131-SessionEndComparison]]). A first ride held mostly in its zone can take the zone headline instead, which is why step 1 also accepts First time on as a chip.

items.key: TST-0318 Manual Stop Disqualifies PB
items.name: Manual Stop Disqualifies PB
items.text:
## Setup

A heart-rate strap. A Power or HR-Zone workout this rider has ridden to its end before.

## Steps

Start the workout with repeat off. At about 80 % of its duration, tap FINISH, then Save ride, and read the headline and the chips under it.

## Expect

- Neither the headline nor a chip reads `New best on` or `First time on`: a ride stopped early never counts as a personal best.

## Not this check

- What the headline does say, which depends on the rider's other rides: [[TST-0686-TheCelebrationsHeadlineNamesTheRidesMostNotableFact]].

## What is automated

*(mostly automated: `PbCalculatorTest.power rejects session manually ended at 98 percent of target duration` and `PersonalBestServiceTest.session manually stopped below 99 percent natural completion gate is not qualifying`; the rankers leave `best` and `first` out for an incomplete ride, in `CelebrationRankerTest` and `CelebrationRankerTests`.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the personal-best card and its "Session too short to compare" line. An incomplete ride can still take other headlines, such as a peak power or the week's ride count (DES-0005 section 3), so the check asserts what must be absent.

items.key: TST-0319 A free ride never takes a personal-best headline
items.name: A free ride never takes a personal-best headline
items.text:
## Setup

Any rider and a trainer that accepts control.

## Steps

Start a free ride in any mode, end it by hand, tap Save ride, and read the headline and the chips under it.

## Expect

- Neither the headline nor a chip reads `New best on` or `First time on`; a free ride has no target to compare.

## Not this check

- The headlines a free ride can take, such as a distance milestone: [[TST-0686-TheCelebrationsHeadlineNamesTheRidesMostNotableFact]].

## What is automated

*(mostly automated: `PersonalBestServiceTest` free-ride fallback returns NOT_QUALIFYING, and the rankers' free-ride cases in `CelebrationRankerTest` and `CelebrationRankerTests`.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the personal-best card from the end of a ride, so "no card" became "no personal-best headline" on the celebration after Save.

items.key: TST-0321 Three PB rides — the trophy, the PBs filter, and what happens when the holder is deleted
items.name: Three PB rides — the trophy, the PBs filter, and what happens when the holder is deleted
items.text:
## Setup

A rider with no personal best yet on one workout. Ride that workout three times, each ride beating the one before.

Complete three rides of the same workout, each one beating the previous PB. Open History. The steps run in the order below, because the last one destroys the state the others need.

**Trophy on the latest row.** The first row — the latest ride — shows a trophy icon.

**PBs filter.** Tap the "PBs" chip. On Android the filters are in a row under the **Past Sessions** heading in History. On iOS they are in the History strip, which sits above the bottom bar on a phone and under History in the rail on a tablet. All three rows appear, because each was a PB at save time even though only the last is still the current PB.

**Delete promotes the next best.** Test this last. Delete the ride that holds the current PB. Reopen the library: the PB chip now shows the next-best qualifying attempt's metric, or disappears if no qualifying attempt remains.

*(mostly automated: `PersonalBestServiceTest` covers the `PbState` transitions, the promotion on deleting a PB holder, and the row clearing when the last qualifying attempt goes; `HistoryTypeFilterRowTest.pbs_chip_displayed_alongside_type_chips` and `tapping_pbs_chip_fires_toggle` cover the chip UI and its dispatch. The trophy on real history rows, the filter's effect on a real list, and the delete flow stay manual.)*

## Expect

- The latest row shows a trophy icon.
- The PBs filter shows all three rows.
- After the delete, the PB chip shows the next-best qualifying attempt's metric, or disappears if none remains.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0322` (Session Delete Promotes Next-Best PB) — deleting a PB-holding ride and checking that the library chip promotes or clears. It is the **Delete promotes the next best** step. It needed a history with a PB in it, which is exactly what this row's three rides build.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates a missing trophy from a PBs filter that shows the wrong rows, nor either from a delete that fails to promote the next-best attempt. A rider must write down which named step failed.

**Order matters more than usual here.** The delete step removes one of the three PB rows, so testing it before the **PBs filter** step would leave the filter with two rows to find instead of three. Test the three steps in the order written.

## Why this did not merge into TST-0314

`TST-0321`'s three-ride setup strictly contains `TST-0314`'s two-ride one, so folding `TST-0314` in here would have looked free. It is not. The first-attempt and improved-attempt card copy is the feature `TST-0314` exists to check, and it is checked at session end on the ride itself. The trophy and the filter are a different screen entirely. Merging would put a session-end overlay assertion and a History-screen assertion under one tick, and they fail for unrelated reasons.

items.key: TST-0323 Rider Restore Rebuilds PBs
items.name: Rider Restore Rebuilds PBs
items.text:
Export a `.ytrider.json.gz` for a rider with ≥1 PB. Delete the rider. Import the file as a new rider. Verify the PB chip appears on the library card for the imported rider (PB was rebuilt from session history, not read from the file). *(partially automated: `PersonalBestServiceTest.recompute for rider rebuilds pb from history` + `RiderFileSerializationTest` covers the export/import round-trip of the underlying session rows.)*

## Expect

- The imported rider's library card shows the PB chip, rebuilt from session history, not read from the file.

items.key: TST-0324 Backfill on Upgrade
items.name: Backfill on Upgrade
items.text:
Install the v22-migration build on a device with pre-v22 Power / HR workout history. Open the app. Verify the Library PB chips appear on previously-completed workouts (historical naturally-completed rides become PBs via the one-shot backfill worker). *(partially automated: `PersonalBestBackfillWorker` enqueues idempotently in `YourTrainerApplication`; evaluate() idempotence covered by `PersonalBestServiceTest.backfill is idempotent across repeat runs`; on-device first-launch behaviour stays manual.)*

## Expect

- Personal-best chips show on workouts completed before the upgrade.

## Not applicable on iOS, 2026-09-25

iOS has never shipped a build from before personal-best chips, and it has no personal-best backfill, so there is nothing to upgrade from. Edwin decided on 2026-09-25 that this check is not applicable on iOS ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]], decision 20).

items.key: TST-0325 Split-screen — a structured workout renders, and resizing while it runs does not break it
items.name: Split-screen — a structured workout renders, and resizing while it runs does not break it
items.text:
One structured workout, started beside another app and resized while it is running. Use Android split-screen on an Android tablet or Split View on an iPad.

## Procedure

1. **The structured workout renders.** Put Your Trainer beside another app such as a browser using the tablet's split view. Start a structured workout. The terrain graph renders correctly, the watts labels are readable, coaching cues display within the terrain bounds, the cockpit metrics are not clipped, and the timeline ruler ticks are visible.
2. **Resize while it runs.** With the workout still active, drag the split-screen divider. The UI adapts without crashing and without layout corruption. Then re-check the five items from step 1 at the new size.

## Expect

- Step 1: terrain, watts labels, cues inside the terrain, cockpit metrics and ruler ticks all show, none clipped.
- Step 2: no crash or broken layout, and the same five things still show.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0327-Resize-During-Workout]] | resizing the divider mid-workout without crash or corruption | step 2 |

**[[TST-0326-Split-Screen-Free-Ride]] was deliberately left standing.** Its three free-ride modes — Simulation, ERG and HR Zone — are already three sub-checks inside one row, and folding them under a structured-workout row would make four modes one tick. It stays a separate row.

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0327** — a crash on resize is a much harder failure than a clipped label, and the two now share a verdict; step 2 asks for the step-1 items to be re-read after the resize so the evidence can say which it was.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- Screenshots at the initial split and after the resize.

items.key: TST-0326 Split-Screen Free Ride
items.name: Split-Screen Free Ride
items.text:
Same setup in split-screen. Start a free ride in all three modes.

## Steps

1. Start a free ride in Simulation mode.
2. Start a free ride in ERG mode.
3. Start a free ride in HR Zone mode.

## Expect

- Step 1: elevation terrain and slope controls show. Ruler visible; power, HR and cadence readable.
- Step 2: the growing profile and target silhouette show. Ruler visible; power, HR and cadence readable.
- Step 3: zone bands and the HR line show. Ruler visible; power, HR and cadence readable.

## Invalidation history

`invalidated_by:` is a single record and this check has two. The current one is in the frontmatter; the one it displaced is here, because a field that holds one fact cannot hold the second and dropping it was the defect [[ISS-0380]] exists to fix:

- **`FEAT-0044` — "HR Zone mode added".** Restored from `0535db82` on 2026-08-29 and overwritten within the same commit by this release's `targetSdk 36` invalidation. Recovered again 2026-08-30 after independent review ([[ISS-0383-InvalidationRestoreLostOneRecord]]) caught it; it is the one note of the 54 whose restore was not byte-identical.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0328 Ramp Test FTP Calculation
items.name: Ramp Test FTP Calculation
items.text:
## Setup

Show debug workouts on (Android Developer Options; iOS Settings → Developer · Workouts). A trainer that accepts control. Note the rider's FTP before starting.

## Steps

1. Run `[Debug] FTP Ramp` to completion.
2. Tap Save and update FTP, then read the profile FTP.

## Expect

- Step 1: the dialog reads `New FTP detected: <n> W`, about 90 % of the profile FTP, and offers Save and update FTP.
- Step 2: the profile FTP updates.

## Not this check

- The dialog's other cases: [[TST-0684-WhenARideEndsADialogAsksOnlyWhetherToSaveItKeepRidingOrDiscardIt]].

## What is automated

*(partially automated: `RideEndDecisionDialogTest` checks the new-FTP line and Save and update FTP on Android, and `RideEndDecisionTests` on iOS.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] replaced the ride-end summary with a decision dialog. The detected FTP is now a line in that dialog, and UPDATE PROFILE & FINISH is Save and update FTP, which updates the FTP and saves the ride.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0329 The locale picker end to end, the feedback row below it, and a Japanese pass for CJK rendering
items.name: The locale picker end to end, the feedback row below it, and a Japanese pass for CJK rendering
items.text:
One pass through Settings → Language, with two locale switches: German for steps 1–3, then Japanese for step 4.

## Procedure

1. **The picker and the switch.** Settings → Language. The row shows the current effective locale on its right. Tap it — a picker dialog opens with `System default` and the eight Tier-1 locales. Pick `Deutsch`: the activity recreates and the Settings panel re-renders in German, titles, subtitles and buttons alike.
2. **The rest of the app follows.** Tap back and visit Profile, Workouts, History and the Active Workout screen. All are localised too.
3. **The language-feedback row.** Still on Settings → Language, directly below the auto-translate toggle and the bulk-translate row, a row reads *"Spotted a translation issue?"* with a `Report it` TextButton on the right — no `→` arrow, matching the Export and Import rows above it. Tap it: the device email composer opens with `support@your-applications.com` in `To:` and the subject prefilled `Your Trainer — Language feedback (<locale>) — v<version>`. The body is **hybrid**: the rider-facing prompts (`What I saw:`, `What I expected:`, `Where in the app:`) render in the rider's language so they can be filled in naturally, while the trailing `Locale: …` and `Version: …` diagnostics stay English so the support reader does not have to translate them. In German the row prompt reads `Übersetzungsfehler entdeckt?` with `Melden`, and the body prompts are German while the diagnostics stay English.
4. **The Japanese CJK pass.** Switch the device to Japanese and repeat step 3. The row prompt, the picker and the email body prompts all render in Japanese, with **no missing glyphs, no tofu boxes and no clipped characters**. This is the only step that exercises a non-Latin script, so it keeps its own tick — a font or measurement regression shows in Japanese and in nothing else.
5. **System default returns the device locale.** Reopen the picker and choose `System default`. The UI returns to the device's own language.

## Expected results

- [android] Step 1: the picker lists `System default` and eight languages. Picking `Deutsch` redraws Settings in German: titles, subtitles and buttons.
- [ios] Step 1: the picker lists System Default and eight languages. After the restart Settings is in German: titles, subtitles and buttons.
- Step 2: Profile, Workouts, History and the Active Workout screen are in German too.
- Step 3: `Übersetzungsfehler entdeckt?` with `Melden`, no arrow. The email to `support@your-applications.com`: German prompts, English Locale and Version lines, subject `Your Trainer — Language feedback (<locale>) — v<version>`.
- Step 4: Japanese renders everywhere the German pass touched, with no missing glyphs, tofu boxes or clipped characters.
- Step 5: the app returns to the device's own language, English.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0334-Language-Feedback-Row-TASK-0461-Relocated]] | the feedback row's placement, styling and hybrid email body, plus a Japanese CJK check | steps 3 and 4 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0334** — the feedback row is the rider's only route for reporting a bad translation, and a broken mail intent now records the same as a picker that will not switch; the CJK pass is split out as step 4 because it fails for reasons unrelated to either.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- The email composer's subject and body as generated in German and in Japanese.

items.key: TST-0330 The manual links — the About card, the locale segment, the stub redirect, and the four contextual links
items.name: The manual links — the About card, the locale segment, the stub redirect, and the four contextual links
items.text:
Every link out of the app to the manual, tested in one pass. Steps 1–3 and 5 are in the app; step 4 is in a desktop browser with the app closed.

## Procedure

1. **The Manual & Guides card.** Settings → About. The **Manual & Guides** card uses the same shape as the Privacy Policy and Email Support cards above and below it: a surface-variant Card with a title, a subtitle paragraph, and a final tappable inline TextButton line that renders the URL itself in primary tint — no "Open" word, no OutlinedButton. Tap it, and the system browser opens `https://www.your-applications.com/your-trainer/manual.html`, whose page carries the four sub-page links (workouts / ai-skills / workout-schema / troubleshooting).
2. **German URLs carry the locale segment.** Switch the device language to German and tap the same card. The browser opens `https://www.your-applications.com/your-trainer/de/manual.html`, and the DE stub auto-redirects — meta-refresh with a JS fallback — to the EN page. Repeat for each contextual link from step 5: all four URLs include `/de/`.
3. **English URLs drop it again.** Switch back to English. The URLs go back to bare paths (`…/manual.html`), with no locale segment.
4. **The stub redirects on its own, in a desktop browser.** Separately from the app, open `https://www.your-applications.com/your-trainer/de/manual.html` directly in a desktop browser. It lands on the EN page. This is the only step that tests the hosted stub rather than the app, so it keeps its own tick.
5. **The four contextual learn-more links.** Each opens the right URL via `Intent.ACTION_VIEW`. (a) Workout Editor → AI builder card, on both the Power and HR-Zone start screens → "Prompt tips →" → `…/ai-skills.html`. (b) History → AI Coach card, expanded → same link, same URL. (c) Workout Editor → start screen, Power and HR-Zone → "Workout schema docs →" below the preset list → `…/workout-schema.html`. (d) Workout Editor → AI builder card with a corrupted API key → "Troubleshoot →" below the error text → `…/troubleshooting.html`. In cases (a) and (b) the "Prompt tips →" link sits **right-aligned directly under the multi-line goal-input field**, flush with the field's right edge, not under the Generate button. None of these links appear on Settings → AI Coach, on the main Workout Selection screen, or in the active workout cockpit.

## Expected results

- Step 1: the card is shaped like Privacy Policy and Email Support, and opens `https://www.your-applications.com/your-trainer/manual.html`, linking four sub-pages.
- Step 2: the manual opens `…/de/manual.html`, which redirects to the English page, and all four contextual URLs include `/de/`.
- Step 3: every URL is a bare path such as `…/manual.html`, with no locale segment.
- Step 4: the DE stub redirects to EN from a plain browser.
- Step 5: Prompt tips, right-aligned under the goal field, opens `…/ai-skills.html`, schema docs `…/workout-schema.html`, Troubleshoot `…/troubleshooting.html`. Not on AI Coach, Workout Selection or the ride screen.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0331-Manual-Guides-Link-TASK-0463-Privacy]] | the Manual & Guides card's shape and its tap target | step 1 |
| [[TST-0332-Contextual-Learn-More-Links-TASK-0463]] | the four contextual links, their URLs and their placement | step 5 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0331** — a card that has reverted to the OutlinedButton style still opens the right URL, so a styling regression and a broken link now share one verdict.
- **TST-0332** — four separate links collapse into one step, so a single dead link, or one that has drifted back under the Generate button, records as "step 5 failed" and must be named in the evidence.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- The URL opened by each of the five link paths, in both languages, and whether the desktop stub redirected.

items.key: TST-0333 Locale fallback banner — non-Tier-1 device locale (TASK-0462)
items.name: Locale fallback banner — non-Tier-1 device locale (TASK-0462)
items.text:
On a tablet with device language set to a non-Tier-1 locale (Korean / Polish / Swedish — anything outside `de, fr, es, it, nl, ja, pt-BR, zh-TW, en`), fresh-install the app. After granting Bluetooth permissions, on the rider-selection screen (or workout-selection if a rider already exists), a tertiary-coloured banner appears at the top reading `Your language isn't fully supported yet.` + `Available: Deutsch · Français · 日本語 · …` with a `Choose` button and a `✕` dismiss icon. Tap `Choose` → locale picker dialog opens → pick `日本語` → activity recreates → banner gone, UI in Japanese. Force-stop + reopen → banner stays gone (sticky-dismiss persisted). On a German device → no banner (effective = DE, not EN-via-fallback). On an English device → no banner (EN-match, not EN-fallback).

## Expect

- A tertiary-coloured banner reads `Your language isn't fully supported yet.` and `Available: Deutsch · Français · 日本語 · …`, with `Choose` and `✕`.
- `Choose`, then `日本語`: the banner goes and the app is in Japanese.
- After a force-stop and reopen, the banner stays gone.
- A German device shows no banner, and nor does an English one.

items.key: TST-0339 Auto-translate on import — the blocking wait dialog, and the failure dialog behind it
items.name: Auto-translate on import — the blocking wait dialog, and the failure dialog behind it
items.text:
Same file, same setup, imported twice: once with a working key and once with a corrupted one.

**Setup.** Auto-translate toggle ON, AI configured, device language Dutch. The file is `test-fixtures/workouts/ytw/good.ytw` — four custom-labelled intervals, no IDs in the source.

## Procedure

1. **The happy path, behind a wait dialog.** Share the file to the app. A modal AlertDialog appears **immediately**, reading *"Workout vertalen…"* with the body *"\"Ramp Warmup Demo\" wordt naar het Nederlands vertaald. Dit duurt meestal ongeveer 10 seconden."* It is non-dismissable. After roughly 5–10 s it dismisses and the workout appears in the list **already translated**, with a Dutch name on the card. Open it: name, description and all four interval labels are Dutch. The list never shows an intermediate source-language version.
2. **The failure path.** Corrupt the AI key and import the same file again. The wait dialog appears, then dismisses, and an error dialog reads *"Vertaling mislukt"*, the locale-aware service error message, and *"De workout is in de oorspronkelijke taal geïmporteerd. Open hem om het opnieuw te proberen."*, with an OK button. Tap OK: the workout is in the list in English. Open it — the editor banner is showing. Restore the key, tap `Vertalen`, and it succeeds.

## Expect

- Step 1: the list and the editor never show the source language, even briefly.
- Step 2: the workout is still imported, the failure is explained in Dutch, and `Vertalen` works once the key is back.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0340-Auto-Translate-Failure-Dialog-TASK-0488]] | the failure dialog, its copy, and recovery through the banner | step 2 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0340** — the failure path is where a rider can lose a workout entirely if the import is abandoned along with the translation, and it now records under the same verdict as the happy path's dialog timing.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- Both dialogs' exact copy, and the state of the imported workout after each run.

items.key: TST-0341 A route import never calls the translator
items.name: A route import never calls the translator
items.text:
Routes carry no rider-facing prose to translate — a GPX is coordinates and elevations — so the auto-translate path that runs on workout imports must not run on route imports (ADR-0003).

## Setup

- **Settings → Language → "Auto-translate imported workouts" switched ON.** The toggle is the thing being tested, so it must be on.
- **An AI key configured** (Settings → AI Coach). Without a key nothing could translate anyway, so the check would pass for the wrong reason and prove nothing. This precondition is the whole reason it is stated here.
- A `.gpx` route file on the device, or shared to it from another app.
- The device **offline**, which is the cheap way to observe the negative: a translation attempt needs the network, so if one fires it fails visibly. Watching logcat for the translate service is the alternative if you would rather stay online.

## Steps

1. Share or open the `.gpx` file into Your Trainer.
2. The route import summary dialog appears. Save it.

## Expect

- Step 1: no translation banner, no "Translating…" state and no translation error.
- Step 2: the route saves offline with no error and no translation, under its own name.

## Not this check

- That a *workout* arriving in another language **is** translated when the toggle is on — that is the positive case and it is a different check.
- Whether the translation is any good. This check only asserts that no call is made.

## Provenance

Covers [[FEAT-0066]] and [[TASK-0453]], which introduced the toggle. Rewritten 2026-09-06 into the Setup / Steps / Expect shape; the AI-key precondition was added because without it the check could not fail.

items.key: TST-0342 Bulk translate — the run, and cancelling it mid-flight
items.name: Bulk translate — the run, and cancelling it mid-flight
items.text:
Both steps start from Settings → Language with at least five user-created workouts missing the rider's locale. Run the cancel first if you want the second run to have something left to do.

## Procedure

1. **The run.** A "Translate all my workouts" row appears with a count badge. Tap it → a confirmation dialog → Continue → a progress dialog with a per-workout counter (`Translating workout 3 of 7…`). On completion the dialog reads `7 of 7 workouts translated to Français.` Open any of those workouts — it renders in French.
2. **Cancel mid-flight.** Start a bulk translate with at least five pending workouts. While the progress dialog is showing, tap Cancel. The workout currently in flight **finishes and is saved**; the ones after it are skipped. Re-running the bulk action picks up the remaining ones.

## Expected results

- Step 1: the count badge, the per-workout counter and the completion line all agree with what translated. A translated workout opens in the new language.
- Step 2: Cancel stops the queue without discarding the in-flight result, and the action is resumable.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0343-Bulk-Action-Cancel-Mid-Flight]] | Cancel keeps the in-flight result and leaves the rest resumable | step 2 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0343** — a Cancel that throws away a paid translation already in flight now records as the same failure as a bulk action that will not start, and the wasted API call is invisible in the verdict.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- The counts shown at each stage, and how many workouts were translated after the cancel.

items.key: TST-0346 Trainer compatibility check — entry row and disclosure dialog
items.name: Trainer compatibility check — entry row and disclosure dialog
items.text:
## Steps

1. **The row is in Settings → Hardware.** Open Settings → Hardware. On iOS, open Settings and read the Equipment section.
2. **About no longer carries one.** Open Settings → About.
3. **Check opens the disclosure dialog.** Tap `Check`. On iOS, tap the Check Trainer Compatibility row.
4. **Cancel returns where you came from, without fetching.** Tap `Cancel`.
5. **The same from the paywall banner.** Reach the dialog from the paywall banner instead and tap `Cancel`. The iOS paywall has no such banner yet; see "On iOS" below.
6. **Tapping outside does what Cancel does.** Open the dialog again and tap outside it. On iOS the check is a screen, not a dialog: open it again and leave it with Back or a swipe from the left edge.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: a `Trainer compatibility check` row after Diagnostics: Verified icon, `Check` button, subtitle FREE "…one-time free Pro upgrade", PRO/FAMILY "…community-supported trainer list".
- [ios] Step 1: Settings → Equipment has a `Check Trainer Compatibility` row with a seal icon, above Bluetooth Diagnostics. No subtitle or Check button; the row opens the check.
- Step 2: Settings → About has no compatibility check row.
- [android] Step 3: a dialog `Fetch the compatibility list?`: the fetch goes to your-applications.com, no rider data is sent, a 7-minute test is optional after. `Check now` (filled) and `Cancel`.
- [ios] Step 3: a `Trainer Compatibility` screen headed `Check your trainer`: a one-time network lookup, no ride data shared. `Check now` (filled) and `Cancel`.
- [android] Step 4: back on Settings → Hardware, and nothing was fetched.
- [ios] Step 4: back on Settings, and nothing was fetched.
- Step 5: back on the paywall.
- [android] Step 6: tapping outside does what Cancel does.
- [ios] Step 6: Back or a swipe does what Cancel does: back in Settings, nothing fetched.

## Where Cancel lands

Cancel has no fixed destination: `CompatibilityCheckScreen.kt:144` wires `onCancel` to the screen's `onBack`, and `MainActivity.kt:945` supplies `onBack = { navController.popBackStack() }`, so it pops the back stack and the rider lands wherever they started. ISS-0258 is why this matters — the screen is popped before the 7-minute test launches, so returning from the test does not land on a stale dialog.

Tapping outside the dialog calls the same `onCancel` as Cancel: `onDismissRequest` is wired to it (`:172`). TASK-0530 moved the row out of Settings → About on 2026-05-14.

## On iOS

Edwin decided on 2026-09-18 that the iOS compatibility cards get their own expected text, naming the iOS screen and the same underlying result ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]], "Decided, 2026-09-18"). The "on iOS" lines above are that text, written from `SettingsView.swift` and `CompatibilityCheckView.swift` on 2026-09-24. The iOS check has no tier-aware subtitle, because the Pro grant it would promise needs Submit for review, which iOS does not have yet ([[ISS-0458-IosCompatibilityTestCannotBeSubmittedOrLaunchedFromDeveloperOptions]], deferred).

Step 5 has no iOS path: the iOS paywall shows no compatibility banner. Edwin decided on 2026-09-25 that the banner belongs to ISS-0458's deferred grant flow, because it advertises the Pro grant that only Submit for review delivers. The release test shows step 5 on iOS as waiting for ISS-0458, which is deferred to the first iOS release.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0347]] (steps 3 to 6). The entry row and the dialog it opens are one tap apart, and TST-0347's own correction on 2026-09-12 tied its Cancel behaviour to the entry point this row asserts.

One tick no longer separates a row in the wrong place from a dialog with the wrong copy or a Cancel that goes somewhere else. Step 5's two entry points are the part most likely to regress on their own, so name the entry point you used.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test read them as one part and could give the whole check only one mark. They now sit under `## Steps`, with one expectation each under `## Expect`, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0348 Online list fetched on Check now (TASK-0526 — no cache)
items.name: Online list fetched on Check now (TASK-0526 — no cache)
items.text:
Tap `Check now`, and watch the request with logcat or charles-proxy.

## Steps

1. Tap `Check now`. On iOS, open Settings → Equipment → Check Trainer Compatibility and tap `Check now`.
2. With logcat or charles-proxy, watch the request each Check makes.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: a `Checking compatibility…` spinner, then a result card within ~2 s on Wi-Fi.
- [ios] Step 1: a `Checking your trainer…` spinner, then a result card within ~2 s on Wi-Fi.
- Step 2: each Check requests `https://www.your-applications.com/your-trainer/compatibility.json` exactly once. Nothing is cached.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

## Corrected 2026-09-24

Step 2's address gained `www.`: both apps request `https://www.your-applications.com/your-trainer/compatibility.json` (`CompatibilityListService.DEFAULT_URL` on Android, `CompatibilityListService.defaultURL` on iOS), so a proxy shows that host. The "on iOS" line is Edwin's 2026-09-18 decision that the iOS cards get their own expected text ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]). Step 2 holds on iOS as written: each `Check now` or `Retry` fetches once, with no cache. On Android, the bundled test list in Developer Options makes no request at all, so it must be off for this check ([[TASK-0924-AndroidDebugControlsForTheOwedChecks]]).

items.key: TST-0349 Verified variant — KICKR / KICKR CORE / Direto
items.name: Verified variant — KICKR / KICKR CORE / Direto
items.text:
## Setup

One of the seeded-verified trainers connected (Wahoo KICKR V5/V6, KICKR CORE, or Elite Direto X/XR). On Android, the bundled test list in Developer Options is off, so the published list is read.

## Steps

With the trainer connected, tap Check. On Android the check is the `Trainer compatibility check` row in Settings → Hardware; on iOS it is Settings → Equipment → Check Trainer Compatibility, then `Check now`.

## Expect

- [android] Header `Trainer verified` (green), body `Your trainer (<manufacturer> <model>) is verified to work. No action needed.`
- [ios] Header `Verified ✓` (green), body `<trainer name> is verified to work with Your Trainer. No action needed.`
- A single `Done` button, and no `Run compatibility test`.

## Original wording

With one of the seeded-verified trainers paired (Wahoo KICKR V5/V6, KICKR CORE, or Elite Direto X/XR), tap Check. Verify card header `Trainer verified` (green), body `Your trainer (<manufacturer> <model>) is verified to work. No action needed.`, and a single `Done` button — no `Run compatibility test` button.

## Headings added 2026-09-24

The procedure already quoted the three results above; the headings let the release test check those quotes against this note. The check is still one part. The "On iOS" lines are Edwin's 2026-09-18 decision that the iOS cards get their own expected text, naming the iOS screen and the same underlying result ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]), written from `CompatibilityCheckView.swift`.

items.key: TST-0350 NotListed result — the copy changes with the tier
items.name: NotListed result — the copy changes with the tier
items.text:
**Precondition: a trainer whose manufacturer and model are not in `compatibility.json`.** The Check is a fetch, not a ride, so it can be re-run cheaply after a tier change.

## Steps

1. **FREE rider — the card.** With rider tier FREE, tap Check, and read the card's title and buttons. On Android the bench KICKR stands in for an unlisted trainer once Developer Options → Compatibility List Source (Debug) → Use the bundled test list is on ([[TASK-0924-AndroidDebugControlsForTheOwedChecks]]).
2. **FREE rider — Pro-grant copy.** Read the card's body.
3. **PRO or FAMILY rider — community copy.** Change the tier to PRO or FAMILY and run Check again on the same trainer.

## Expect

- Step 1: `New trainer detected` (orange), with `Run compatibility test` as the primary button, plus `Done`.
- Step 2: the body reads *"if it passes and the submission is accepted by review, you may qualify for a one-time free Pro upgrade"*.
- [android] Step 3: no free-Pro wording anywhere. Body: *"if it passes, your scorecard helps verify this trainer for the community-supported list"*. `Run compatibility test` stays primary.
- [ios] Step 3: the `Should work` card (orange), no Pro-grant wording anywhere, and `Run compatibility test` still primary.

## On iOS

Open Settings → Equipment → Check Trainer Compatibility and tap `Check now`. iOS shows the same `Should work` card for a trainer that is not listed and one that is expected to work, on every tier. Step 2's iOS line is Edwin's 2026-09-18 decision that the iOS cards get their own expected text ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]).

Step 1 cannot be tested on iOS yet, for two reasons. iOS has no Pro-grant copy, because the grant needs Submit for review, which iOS does not have ([[ISS-0458-IosCompatibilityTestCannotBeSubmittedOrLaunchedFromDeveloperOptions]], deferred to the iOS version). And iOS has no bundled test list, so it needs a real trainer that is not on the published list, and none is on the bench; ISS-0458 adds the iOS test list after its launcher.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0351]] (step 2). The tier flip between them is affordable here in a way it is not for [[TST-0358]] and [[TST-0359]]: this screen is produced by a network fetch that takes seconds to repeat, while the scorecard those two read is produced by a seven-minute ride that the trip to Developer Settings destroys.

One tick no longer separates the Pro-grant copy leaking onto a paid rider from the community copy leaking onto a FREE one. The first is the one that matters — it promises a paid rider an upgrade they already hold — so write down the tier you were on.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test read them as one part and could give the whole check only one mark. They now sit under `## Steps`, with one expectation each under `## Expect`, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

## Split 2026-09-27

Step 1 was one expected line of 30 words: the card's title and buttons, and its body quoted word for word. It is now two steps, the card and then its body, so each line fits the release test's 25-word limit and the copy is still quoted in full ([[PHASE-0010]] in project-os-dev). What the check asks for is unchanged; the old step 2 is step 3.

items.key: TST-0352 ExpectedToWork variant — seeded but unverified trainer
items.name: ExpectedToWork variant — seeded but unverified trainer
items.text:
If a tester has access to one of the 8 expected-to-work trainers (Tacx Neo / Flux, Saris H3, Elite Suito, JetBlack VOLT, Zwift Hub, Magene T100, Wahoo KICKR Bike), pair it and tap Check. The body is conditional on tier, so the check is read once on each tier.

## Steps

1. As a PRO or FAMILY rider, pair the trainer and tap Check.
2. As a FREE rider, tap Check on the same trainer.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: `Help verify your trainer` (orange), the PRO/FAMILY community-contribution framing, primary `Run compatibility test`.
- [ios] Step 1: header `Should work` (orange). The body says not verified yet but should work, and asks for the test. Primary: `Run compatibility test`.
- Step 2: on FREE, the body carries the Pro-grant hook.

## Without the hardware

*(Release exception if no expected_to_work hardware on hand.)*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

## On iOS

Open Settings → Equipment → Check Trainer Compatibility and tap `Check now`. Step 1's iOS line is Edwin's 2026-09-18 decision that the iOS cards get their own expected text ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]), written from `CompatibilityCheckView.swift` on 2026-09-24. Step 2 cannot be tested on iOS yet: iOS shows the same `Should work` card on every tier and has no Pro-grant hook, because the grant needs Submit for review ([[ISS-0458-IosCompatibilityTestCannotBeSubmittedOrLaunchedFromDeveloperOptions]], deferred to the iOS version).

The bundled Android test list lists Tacx Flux S as expected to work, but that needs a Flux S on the bench too. Without one of the eight trainers, this check is still a release exception on both platforms.

items.key: TST-0353 NoTrainerConnected variant — no trainer bound (ISS-0257 / TASK-0531)
items.name: NoTrainerConnected variant — no trainer bound (ISS-0257 / TASK-0531)
items.text:
## Setup

Open the Equipment Hub from the equipment icons at the end of the top bar, tap the Smart Trainer row, tap Forget this trainer and confirm. Or use a fresh install with nothing connected. Return to the compatibility check and tap Check. On iOS the check is Settings → Equipment → Check Trainer Compatibility, then `Check now`.

## Steps

1. Tap Check with no trainer connected, and read the card's title and buttons.
2. Read the card's body.
3. Read the body text for what it must not say.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: `No trainer connected` (orange), with a single `Done`.
- [ios] Step 1: `No trainer connected` (orange), with a single `Done`.
- [android] Step 2: the body reads `Connect a trainer in the Equipment Hub, opened from the equipment icons in the top bar, then come back to check compatibility.`
- [ios] Step 2: the body reads `Connect a smart trainer from the Equipment Hub first, then run this check.`
- Step 3: the body never says "pair" or "paired", and does not mention Settings → Hardware.

## Setup rewritten 2026-09-28

The setup used to tap Forget on the trainer's slot. Since FEAT-0130 Forget is in the trainer's details sheet, opened by tapping its row, and asks once ([[REQ-0226-ARowOpensTheDevicePickerOrTheDevicesDetailsAsASheet]]). The steps and expected results are unchanged.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

## On iOS, added 2026-09-24

Step 1's iOS line is Edwin's 2026-09-18 decision that the iOS cards get their own expected text ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]), written from `CompatibilityCheckView.swift`. Step 2 holds on iOS as written.

## Split 2026-09-27

Step 1 was one expected line of 32 words on Android: the card's title and button, and its body quoted word for word. It is now two steps, the card and then its body, so each line fits the release test's 25-word limit and the copy is still quoted in full. What the check asks for is unchanged; the old step 2 is step 3.

items.key: TST-0354 TrainerUnidentified variant — trainer connected but no DIS (ISS-0257 / TASK-0531)
items.name: TrainerUnidentified variant — trainer connected but no DIS (ISS-0257 / TASK-0531)
items.text:
## Setup

A trainer that reports no Device Information Service model number **and** advertises no Bluetooth name. A trainer that only lacks Device Information Service (0x180A) is not enough: since ISS-0257 both apps look such a trainer up by its advertised name, so it reads as verified, not listed or expected to work instead. No trainer on the current bench does this, and no debug control produces it.

## Steps

Connect that trainer and tap Check. On Android the check is the `Trainer compatibility check` row in Settings → Hardware; on iOS it is Settings → Equipment → Check Trainer Compatibility, then `Check now`.

## Expect

- [android] Header `Trainer connected — couldn't identify` (orange).
- [ios] Header `Trainer connected` (orange).
- [android] The body says the model wasn't reported: run the test on the live connection, and fill in the trainer on submission.
- [ios] Body `Connected trainer didn't report a model, so it can't be looked up — but you can still run the compatibility test against the live connection.`
- Both `Run compatibility test` (primary) and `Done`.

## Why it matters

The rider must still have a path to the test screen.

## Original wording

Connect a trainer that does **not** expose BLE Device Information Service (0x180A) — many budget / older trainers fall into this bucket. Tap Check. Verify header `Trainer connected — couldn't identify` (orange) and body explaining the manufacturer/model wasn't reported, with an instruction to run the test against the live connection and fill in the trainer details on submission. Verify BOTH `Run compatibility test` (primary) AND `Done` buttons appear — the rider must still have a path to the test screen.

## Corrected 2026-09-24

The setup named any trainer without Device Information Service. `CompatibilityCheckScreen.kt` (the ISS-0257 fingerprint order) and `CompatibilityCheckView.swift` fall back to the advertised name, so this card appears only when the trainer reports neither a model nor a name. The expected results are unchanged, and the check is still one part. The "On iOS" lines are Edwin's 2026-09-18 decision that the iOS cards get their own expected text ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]). The iOS card mentions no submission, because iOS cannot submit a scorecard yet ([[ISS-0458-IosCompatibilityTestCannotBeSubmittedOrLaunchedFromDeveloperOptions]]).

items.key: TST-0355 Offline variant — airplane mode (5 s timeout)
items.name: Offline variant — airplane mode (5 s timeout)
items.text:
## Setup

A trainer connected. On Android, the bundled test list in Developer Options is off: the test list is read from the app and makes no request, so it never reaches the offline card.

## Steps

Enable airplane mode (or disable WiFi + mobile data). Tap Check; on iOS, open Settings → Equipment → Check Trainer Compatibility and tap `Check now`. Re-enable the network and tap Retry.

## Expect

- After the 5 s timeout, header `Couldn't reach the list` (red), with two buttons: `Retry` and `Done`.
- [android] Body `Network unavailable. Try again with internet.`
- [ios] Body `Your Trainer couldn't load the compatibility list. Check your connection and try again.`
- After Retry, the result resolves correctly without leaving the screen.

## Original wording

Enable airplane mode (or disable WiFi + mobile data). Tap Check. After the 5 s OkHttp timeout, verify header `Couldn't reach the list` (red), body `Network unavailable. Try again with internet.`, and two buttons: `Retry` + `Done`. Re-enable network, tap Retry → resolves correctly without leaving the screen.

## Headings added 2026-09-24

The procedure already quoted the results above; the headings let the release test check those quotes against this note. The check is still one part. The iOS header, the 5 s request timeout and the two buttons match Android (`CompatibilityListService.swift`, `CompatibilityCheckView.swift`); only the body differs, and its "On iOS" line is Edwin's 2026-09-18 decision that the iOS cards get their own expected text ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]).

items.key: TST-0356 Compatibility test — the run and the scorecard it produces
items.name: Compatibility test — the run and the scorecard it produces
items.text:
**One seven-minute run on a known-good trainer (KICKR CORE / KICKR / Direto), started from the NotListed or ExpectedToWork result.**

## Steps

1. **The test launches.** Tap `Run compatibility test`.
2. **The sequence runs.** Watch the test as it runs.
3. **A scorecard renders at completion.** Let the run finish cleanly rather than stopping it early.
4. **The status text is tier-aware.** Read the green status text.
5. **The actions below the scorecard.** Look below the per-row scorecard.

## Expect

- Step 1: the compatibility test screen opens, the same one Developer Settings → Trainer Compat Test reaches.
- Step 2: it runs ERG 100 W → ERG 150 W → SIM 4 % → SIM mid-ride mode switch → Resistance 30 % → Resistance 70 % → ERG return.
- Step 3: a scorecard renders at completion.
- Step 4: the green status reads `Eligible to submit for review` on FREE, `Ready to submit — thank you for helping verify` on PRO or FAMILY.
- Step 5: `Submit for review →` beside `Copy JSON`, below the scorecard. Submit shows only when the run qualifies for the grant (`qualifiesForGrant`).

## Not this check

[[TST-0358]] and [[TST-0359]] test the Submit tap itself and stay separate — `eligibleForGrant` is computed at composition, so leaving this screen to change tier destroys the scorecard.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0357]] (steps 3 to 5). The scorecard only exists at the end of the run this row starts, so the two were never independently testable — a scorecard tick always cost a seven-minute ride.

One tick no longer separates a test that fails to launch or stalls mid-sequence from a scorecard that renders with the wrong status text or the wrong buttons. The run is long enough that you will know which; write down the step.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test read them as one part and could give the whole check only one mark. They now sit under `## Steps`, with one expectation each under `## Expect`, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0358 Submit for review opens pre-filled GitHub Issue — FREE rider (TASK-0528)
items.name: Submit for review opens pre-filled GitHub Issue — FREE rider (TASK-0528)
items.text:
## Steps

As a FREE-tier rider, tap `Submit for review →`. Do not submit during testing; close the tab.

## Expect

- The system browser opens `https://github.com/edankert/yourtrainer-community/issues/new?…`.
- The title reads `Verification: <manufacturer> <model>`.
- The labels `trainer-verification` and `unreviewed` are applied.
- The body has the Pro-grant disclosure: *"A one-time Pro upgrade is granted only for the first verified scorecard…subject to maintainer review"*.
- The body asks for a contact for the Pro code (Discord, GitHub username or Email), and has the scorecard JSON in a fenced json block.
- The footer reads `install ID prefix: <first-8-chars>`, not the full UUID.

## Original wording

As a FREE-tier rider, tap `Submit for review →`. Verify the system browser opens to `https://github.com/edankert/yourtrainer-community/issues/new?…` with: (a) title `Verification: <manufacturer> <model>`; (b) labels `trainer-verification` + `unreviewed` applied; (c) body containing the Pro-grant disclosure quote-block (*"A one-time Pro upgrade is granted only for the first verified scorecard…subject to maintainer review"*), Contact-for-Pro-code-delivery prompts (Discord / GitHub username / Email), the scorecard JSON in a fenced ```json block, and a footer line `install ID prefix: <first-8-chars>` — **NOT** the full UUID. Do NOT actually submit during testing; close the tab.

3. Look for contact fields in the body. Close the tab.

## Expect

items.key: TST-0364 Compat-test abort scorecard on unexpected failure (FEAT-0085 / TASK-0591)
items.name: Compat-test abort scorecard on unexpected failure (FEAT-0085 / TASK-0591)
items.text:
## Setup

A known-good trainer (KICKR CORE) that accepts control. **If your trainer is on the verified list and Settings → Hardware → Trainer compatibility check therefore hides the Run-test button:** unlock Developer Settings (Settings → About → tap Version 7 times), tap `Run trainer compatibility test` to launch the test directly against your real trainer. iOS has no such launcher yet ([[ISS-0458-IosCompatibilityTestCannotBeSubmittedOrLaunchedFromDeveloperOptions]], deferred).

## Steps

1. Run the compatibility test and let it complete cleanly.
2. Re-run the test and intentionally power off / unplug the trainer mid-test (during the ERG warmup).
3. Start the test once more and tap the compat-test cancel button once.

## Expect

- Step 1: the first scorecard renders normally, with no "Test couldn't complete" abort banner.
- Step 2: no freeze on the running view: within ~6 s the scorecard shows per-phase FAIL rows and no abort banner.
- Step 3: the test's cancel button responds to a single tap, whatever the trainer's state.

## What the fix handles

`BleResult.Failed.Disconnected` is handled gracefully, not thrown. See TST-0010 for the regression-coverage details.

## Original wording

Run the compatibility test on a known-good trainer (KICKR CORE) and let it complete cleanly. Scorecard renders normally with NO "Test couldn't complete" abort banner. Then re-run the test and intentionally power off / unplug the trainer mid-test (during the ERG warmup). Verify the test screen does NOT freeze on the RunningView — within ~6 s of the disconnect, the scorecard appears with per-phase FAIL rows AND no abort banner (BleResult.Failed.Disconnected is handled gracefully, not thrown). The compat-test cancel button responds within a single tap regardless of trainer state. See TST-0010 for the regression-coverage details. **If your trainer is on the verified list and Settings → Hardware → Trainer compatibility check therefore hides the Run-test button:** unlock Developer Settings (Settings → About → tap Version 7 times), tap `Run trainer compatibility test` to launch the test directly against your real trainer.

## Headings added 2026-09-24

ISS-0444 listed this check as one very long part with no `## Steps`. The headings let the release test check the procedure's quotes against this note. The steps were left unnumbered at first, so the check was one part and one mark; they were numbered on 2026-09-25 (below).

## Steps numbered, 2026-09-25

The three results are now numbered steps, so each takes its own mark in the release test. Edwin chose this on 2026-09-25 (decision 25 in [[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit]], applied by [[TASK-0961-ApplyEdwins20260925DecisionsToTheWalk]]). Step 3 was "in a run of your choice"; it is now its own run, so tapping cancel cannot cut short the run step 1 or 2 is judged on.

items.key: TST-0598 Route view modes, the inset, and the docked elevation strip
items.name: Route view modes, the inset, and the docked elevation strip
items.text:
Start a Route ride and work through the view modes. Step 7 wants ghost data on the course and decorations enabled, so ride a route you have completed before.

## Steps

1. **The layers button cycles four states.** Terrain with map inset, map with terrain inset, terrain only, map only.
2. **The inset moves and resizes.** Put it in each of the four corners and set each size — S, M, L. On Android, also drag the grip in the inset's corner, then tap it.
3. **The inset stays in overview.** While the primary view follows the rider, the corner inset keeps showing the whole route.
4. **The mode persists per rider.** End the ride, force-stop the app, reopen and start the same route on the same rider. The mode and inset size come back as they were left.
5. **A second rider has their own mode.** Switch riders and confirm that rider's mode is their own, not the first rider's.
6. **Defaults by width.** A compact width defaults to terrain only; a regular width defaults to terrain with map inset.
7. **The docked overview elevation strip is always there.** Cycle every view mode again, terrain-primary included. The docked strip under the route visual shows in all of them, carries the rider glyph at the current position, and — with decorations enabled and ghost data present — carries the personal-best, today and family-initial ghosts at their own positions, each coloured by the grade beneath it. This is the strip under the route visual, not the lap-times strip covered by `TST-0262` and `TST-0263`.

## Expect

- Step 1: the layers button cycles terrain with map inset, map with terrain inset, terrain only, map only.
- [android] Step 2: the inset moves to each corner and takes each size. The grip faces the screen's middle; dragging it resizes, tapping it steps the size.
- [ios] Step 2: the inset moves to each corner and takes each size.
- Step 3: while the main view follows the rider, the inset still shows the whole route.
- Step 4: the rider's view mode and inset size come back as they were left.
- Step 5: the second rider has their own view mode, not the first rider's.
- Step 6: a compact width opens in terrain only; a regular width in terrain with map inset.
- Step 7: the docked strip shows in every mode, with the rider and the personal-best, today and family ghosts, each grade-coloured.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0601` | 7 | The docked strip disappearing in one view mode now records the same result as the layers button failing to cycle, so note which of the seven steps failed. |

That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This row and the row it absorbed were both among the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

items.name: HR zones display Z1–Z7 and derive from Max HR / LTHR
items.text:
With a Max HR set, open the current rider's profile: tap the rider's name in the bottom bar on a phone or in the rail on a tablet, then **Profile**. On Android, **Profile** is the button under the current rider's card. On iOS it is next to **Switch rider**, and these fields are in the Profile section of that screen; they are no longer in Settings. Everything below happens on that one screen. (TASK-0386 for the estimator dialog)

## Setup

Any rider with a Max HR set. Know the rider's birth year, or an age to enter, for step 3.

## Steps

1. **Seven zones render.** Read the HR zones.
2. **Typing Max HR re-derives LTHR.** Change Max HR by typing.
3. **The Max HR estimator shows both formulas.** Tap `Estimate…` next to Max HR and enter an age.
4. **The estimator writes Tanaka.** Tap `Use X bpm`.
5. **A manual LTHR survives a screen re-entry.** Edit LTHR by hand, leave the screen and come back.
6. **A manual LTHR gives way on the next Max HR change.** Change Max HR again.

## Expect

- Step 1: seven zones with bpm ranges: Recovery, Aerobic, Tempo, SubThreshold, SuperThreshold, Aerobic Capacity, Anaerobic.
- Step 2: LTHR re-derives to 88 % of Max HR, for a Max HR of 100–220 bpm.
- Step 3: both estimates show live: Simple (220 − age) and Tanaka (208 − 0.7 × age). Age pre-fills from a stored birth year.
- Step 4: the **Tanaka** value, not the Simple one, lands in Max HR, and LTHR re-derives from it as in step 2.
- Step 5: the manual LTHR is still there.
- Step 6: LTHR re-derives and replaces the manual value.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0025]] (steps 3 and 4). The estimator dialog was already the second half of step 2's derivation path, so the two rows opened the same dialog for different reasons.

Step 3's two-formula display is carried over deliberately. Showing both and writing Tanaka is the whole behaviour, and a version that shows one formula or writes the Simple value would pass a looser step.

One tick no longer separates a zone table that renders wrong from an estimator that computes or writes the wrong bpm. It also no longer separates the estimator's display from what it writes.

items.key: TST-0610 ERG ramp duration is a per-rider preference
items.name: ERG ramp duration is a per-rider preference
items.text:
## Setup

Two riders, a trainer that accepts control, and a structured ERG workout with intervals of at least 30 s.

## Steps

1. Open the current rider's profile: tap the rider's name in the bottom bar or rail, then **Profile**. On Android, **Profile** is the button under the current rider's card, and the row titled **ERG Ramp Duration** is under Preferences. On iOS, **Profile** is next to **Switch rider**, and the ERG Ramp control is in the Profile section of that screen.
2. Drag it to 30, start a structured ERG workout and cross an interval boundary.
3. Drag it to 0 and cross the next boundary.
4. Restart the app and read the value.
5. Switch to a second rider, open their Profile and read theirs. To switch on Android, tap the rider's name, then the second rider's card. On iOS, tap the rider's name, then **Switch rider**, and pick the second rider.

## Expect

- Step 1: a 0–30 s slider in whole seconds, reading **5s** for a rider who never changed it.
- Step 2: the target ramps across each boundary, 15 s either side, instead of stepping instantly.
- Step 3: the target steps instantly at the next boundary.
- Step 4: the value survives the restart.
- Step 5: the second rider has their own value.

## Notes

The control is a `Slider` with `valueRange = 0f..30f` and `steps = 29` (`UserProfileScreen.kt:852-857`), not a stepper, and the default is 5 rather than 20 (`UserProfile.kt:28`, `WorkoutViewModel.kt:258`, and the Room migration's column default at `AppDatabase.kt:114`). Zero means no ramp: `WorkoutMath.kt:29` returns the biased target unchanged. The ramp is also skipped when either the current or the adjacent interval is shorter than the ramp itself (`WorkoutMath.kt:38`, `:48`), so pick a workout with intervals of at least 30 s when the slider is at its maximum.
