items.key: TST-0619 The History stats card — the 28-day chart and the training overview above it
items.name: The History stats card — the 28-day chart and the training overview above it
items.text:
Both halves live in the same expanded stats card, so one expansion reads both. Steps 1–3 need a rider with sessions spread across the last four weeks; steps 4 and 5 need riders with sparser histories, so plan which accounts to use before starting.

## Procedure

1. **The 28-day chart.** Open History and **expand** the stats card. The chart is in the expanded half, under the heading *Last 4 Weeks*. It has 28 day slots, each carrying **two bars side by side**: duration in minutes in the theme's primary colour, and energy in orange. The colour says which measure the bar is, not what type of workout it was. The left axis is ticked in minutes and the right in the rider's energy unit; the top-left axis label reads `min` and the top-right reads `kJ` or `kcal` to match Settings. A Monday marker line falls every seven slots, and the most recent day is drawn in the tertiary colour. Tap a slot — a detail line appears under the chart with that day's date, ride count, minutes and energy (`:1068-1080`). There is no metric selector; duration and energy are always both drawn and distance is not in the chart at all.
2. **A rider with no sessions sees no chart.** Not an empty one — `:627` wraps the heading and the chart together in `if (stats.dailyActivity.isNotEmpty())`, and the canvas returns early on an empty list at `:916`. Absent is the shipped behaviour.
3. **The This Week block.** Also in the expanded card, on a rider who rode in at least two of the last four completed weeks: a **This Week** block with one stat card each for rides, hours, distance, energy (kJ or kcal, following Settings), average power and best power. The first four show this week's figure large with the all-time figure beneath. Collapsed, the card carries the activity heatmap instead.
4. **The comparison line and the sign of the deltas.** The line under the heading reads *"compared to your 4-week average"*, and the deltas are signed the right way round — more training this week reads as positive.
5. **Suppression below the threshold.** On a rider who rode in **fewer than two** of the last four completed weeks, the *"compared to your 4-week average"* line is absent and every card renders its figure with no delta at all. `WorkoutHistoryScreen.kt:650-653` and `:670-715` both key off `stats.hasFourWeeks`, and `WorkoutHistoryViewModel.kt:690-698` defines it: the four complete weeks before this one, summed and **always divided by four**, with `hasFourWeeks` true when at least two of those weeks contain any ride.

## Expect

- Step 1: every slot draws a minutes bar and an energy bar against two axes. Tapping a slot shows that day.
- Step 2: with no sessions there is no Last 4 Weeks chart at all, not an empty one.
- Step 3: This Week shows cards for rides, hours, distance, energy, average power and best power.
- Step 4: the line reads "compared to your 4-week average", and more training this week reads as positive.
- Step 5: with fewer than two weeks of riding there is no comparison line and no deltas.

## Two things raised rather than asserted

**The average-power card's halves disagree.** Its hero value is `stats.avgPower`, the all-time average (`:710`), while its delta is `thisWeek.avgPower - fourWeekAvg.avgPower` — a this-week number under an all-time headline. The best-power card is all-time in both halves. Whether that is intended is Edwin's call, so this row does not claim either reading is correct.

**TSS is not on this card.** It appears in History per session, in the session detail's training-metric row (`:1825`), alongside IF and VI.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0620-History-Training-Overview-Card]] | the This Week block, the four-week comparison line, and the suppression case | steps 3–5 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0620** — the chart and the overview are different computations in one card, and the suppression threshold in step 5 is the subtle one; a delta shown to a rider with one week of data now fails the same row as a chart with the wrong axis label.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- Screenshots of the expanded card for each rider used, and the delta values read off step 4.

items.key: TST-0621 Session detail — the HR-zone bars, the lap splits, and what is absent when the data is
items.name: Session detail — the HR-zone bars, the lap splits, and what is absent when the data is
items.text:
Steps 1–2 read one session: a completed multi-lap route ride taken with an HRM. Steps 3 and 4 each need a different session, so pick them before starting.

## Procedure

1. **The HR-zone bars.** Find the **HR Zones** column in the session detail. Five horizontal bars, labelled Z1 to Z5, one per zone, each in that zone's muted colour from `ZoneColorUtils.getHrZoneColor`. Each bar carries **whole minutes**, suffixed `m`. The bars are **not stacked and carry no percentages**: each bar's length is its own time as a fraction of the largest zone's time, so the longest zone always fills its row. The minutes across the five bars account for the session's HR-covered time. Five zones is correct and not an oversight — FEAT-0090 makes Z6 and Z7 display-only, and the drivable Z5 already merges icu's Z5 and Z6 into 100–105 % LTHR.
2. **The lap splits.** A lap-splits table lists one row per completed lap, with its time.
3. **A single-lap session shows no lap-splits table.** Not an empty table — no table. Open a single-lap session and confirm the table is absent.
4. **A session with no HR data shows no HR Zones column.** Not five empty bars, and not an empty axis — the column is not rendered. `:1846` computes `hasHrZones` as "any zone has non-zero time" and `:1887` renders the column only when that holds, so a power-only session shows Peak Power with nothing beside it.

Steps 3 and 4 are the two absent-data cases and are numbered separately: they are different conditions on different widgets, and each is the kind of check that passes by accident when the widget above it is broken.

The NP/TSS/IF/VI grid is covered by TST-0414 and the peak-power row by TST-0416. TST-0557 covers the zone calculation as a unit test; nothing automated looks at the rendering.

## Expect

- Step 1: HR Zones shows five bars, Z1 to Z5, in whole minutes, unstacked and with no percentages.
- Step 2: a lap table with one row per completed lap, with its time.
- Step 3: a single-lap session shows no lap table at all.
- Step 4: a session with no HR data shows no HR Zones column at all.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0622-HR-Time-In-Zone-Bars-Render]] | the five zone-coloured bars, their minutes, and the absent column without HR | steps 1 and 4 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0622** — the zone chart and the lap table are independent widgets that happen to share a screen, so a zone chart drawn with the wrong unit now records as the same failure as a missing lap table; the two absent-data cases are kept as steps 3 and 4 for the same reason.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- The five bar labels and values, and a note for each of steps 3 and 4 saying what was present or absent.

items.key: TST-0623 Coach answers cite the MCP training-load figures, not invented numbers
items.name: Coach answers cite the MCP training-load figures, not invented numbers
items.text:
**The app does not compute CTL, ATL or TSB, so there is no local figure to compare the coach's answer with.** The app sends the rider's per-day TSS totals for the last 90 days to the `training_load` tool on the MCP server and renders the `ctl`, `atl` and `tsb` it gets back into one line of the coach's context (`WorkoutAiService.fetchTrainingLoadSummary:902`, `buildDatedTssArray:492`, `formatTrainingLoadSummary:555`). The Training Overview card on History shows rides, duration, distance and energy — no training load at all (`WorkoutHistoryScreen.kt:545-615`), so it is not a cross-check. Whether the server's arithmetic is right belongs to the sibling `yourtrainer-mcp` repo, not to this row.

What this row still catches is the failure that matters: the coach making figures up. Test it as four checks.

**Preconditions.** A BYOK key configured, a PRO or Family seat, at least six weeks of history whose sessions carry a TSS, and the MCP toggle left on in Settings (`SettingsScreen.kt:560`). Open a session's detail and confirm the Training metrics row shows a TSS value (`WorkoutHistoryScreen.kt:1824`); a session with no TSS contributes nothing to the input.

## Steps

1. **The coach cites the three figures.** Ask the History coach about current form.
2. **The figures are self-consistent.** Read the CTL, ATL and TSB in that answer, and the form-state word the app appends.
3. **The figures disappear when the grounding does.** Turn the MCP toggle off in Settings and ask the same question again.
4. **The figures move with the work.** Ride a hard session, confirm its TSS in the session detail, then ask again.

## Expect

- Step 1: the answer gives CTL, ATL and TSB as numbers, not form in the abstract.
- Step 2: TSB is CTL minus ATL, within rounding. Form word: very fresh at 25+, fresh 10+, neutral above −10, fatigued above −25, else very fatigued.
- Step 3: the answer stops giving CTL, ATL and TSB as figures. **A confident number here is invented, and the check fails.**
- Step 4: ATL rises and TSB falls.

## Provenance

items.key: TST-0624 The structured-intent path generates reproducibly, and its toggle switches paths
items.name: The structured-intent path generates reproducibly, and its toggle switches paths
items.text:
With a BYOK key configured, one pass through the AI settings screen and the AI builder covers both the structured-intent (MCP) route and the toggle that chooses between it and direct generation.

## Procedure

1. **The structured path produces a real workout.** With the MCP path enabled, give the AI builder a prompt describing a workout. It returns a structured workout that saves to the library, opens in the editor, and rides with the intervals the prompt asked for.
2. **The structured path is reproducible in shape.** Re-run the **same prompt** and compare: the same interval structure and the same durations, rather than a different workout each time. This is the property that distinguishes the structured path from direct generation, so it is asserted on its own and not folded into step 1.
3. **The toggle is there and selects the path.** In AI settings, a toggle selects between structured intent and direct generation: Use our MCP server in Settings — AI Coach on Android, Use MCP for workout authoring in Settings → AI Coach on iOS. With it on, generate and confirm the structured path ran.
4. **Turning it off leaves generation working.** Turn the toggle off and generate again — generation still succeeds, through the direct path. Turning MCP off must not disable AI generation altogether.
5. **The setting persists.** Restart the app and confirm the toggle is where it was left.

TST-0043 covers the direct generation path on all three providers, which is a different route to the same screen.

## Expect

- Step 1: the workout saves, opens in the editor and rides with the intervals the prompt asked for.
- Step 2: the same interval structure and the same durations as the first result.
- Step 3: the toggle is there, and with it on the structured path runs.
- Step 4: generation still succeeds, through the direct path.
- Step 5: after the restart the toggle is where it was left.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0625-AI-MCP-Opt-Out-Toggle]] | the toggle selects the path, direct generation still works with it off, and the setting persists | steps 3–5 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0625** — a toggle that fails to persist and a structured path that produces nothing now share one verdict, and the more damaging of the two — MCP off disabling generation entirely — is the one at risk of being read as "the AI row failed again".

## Evidence (fill after running)

- The prompt used, both generated shapes for the reproducibility step, and the toggle state after restart.

items.key: TST-0626 No network call fires without a rider tap, except to an account the rider connected
items.name: No network call fires without a rider tap, except to an account the rider connected
items.text:
With AI, Strava and intervals.icu all connected for the current rider, put a proxy or packet capture in front of the device. Traffic to an account the rider connected is allowed without a tap: connecting it is the rider's standing consent to upload their rides and read their own data back (AGENT_RULES.md, "No silent network calls", as Edwin corrected it on 2026-09-26). Today that means the ride upload after saving (TST-0102), and the Strava ride-link check when the app comes back or a rider is picked ([[TST-0480-Auto-Reconcile-App-Foreground|TST-0480]]). Everything else still waits for a tap, including the Online Library, update checks and the AI coach.

## Steps

1. Cold-launch the app and leave it idle on each of rider selection, Workout Selection, History and Settings for two minutes each.
2. Tap each explicit action — refresh, check for updates, browse the online library, ask the coach, upload a session.

## Expect

- Step 1: only Strava and intervals.icu requests leave, for the picked rider who connected them. Nothing goes to the Online Library, the AI provider or other hosts.
- Step 2: each action, and only that one, produces traffic.

## Provenance

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

## Rewritten 2026-09-26

Step 1 used to expect no request at all on launch, on screen entry or on a timer. Edwin corrected the network rule on 2026-09-26: an account the rider connected is standing consent, so traffic to it is allowed without a tap. Step 1 now allows that traffic and still forbids everything else. When [[FEAT-0128-IntervalsIcuAsTheHouseholdsRideStore|FEAT-0128]] ships its automatic read from intervals.icu, it falls under the same allowance.

items.key: TST-0628 There is no bulk-publish entry point to third-party services
items.name: There is no bulk-publish entry point to third-party services
items.text:
## Setup

Strava and intervals.icu both linked for the current rider, and at least one saved ride. On both platforms the connected services are on the rider's Profile: the rider's name in the bottom bar (tab bar on iPhone) or the rail, then **Profile**. On Android, **Profile** is the button under the current rider's card. On iOS it is next to **Switch rider**.

With Strava and intervals.icu linked, sweep the workout library, the route library, the celebration after Save, with its upload chips, and History. On Android, also open the rider profile's Connected section. On iOS, open the rider's Profile: tap the rider's name in the tab bar or rail, then **Profile**, and read its Strava and intervals.icu sections. Verify there is no affordance that sends the whole library, mirrors it, or syncs everything to a third-party service. Per-item send and per-item history are expected and correct. Note before testing this that Android's Strava section carries an **Upload all** button for the pending-upload backlog (TST-0477) — that is a retry of rides already queued, not a library publish; confirm the distinction holds on the build under test before recording a verdict.

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Expect

- Nothing sends, mirrors or syncs the whole library to a third-party service.
- Per-item send and per-item history are there.
- [android] Strava's `Upload all` only retries rides already queued; it does not publish the library.

## Reworded 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] replaced the post-ride summary with a decision dialog and a celebration after Save, whose upload chips offer a Retry for that one ride. The sweep now names the celebration.

items.key: TST-0629 intervals.icu links and unlinks
items.name: intervals.icu links and unlinks
items.text:
## Setup

A PRO rider and an intervals.icu account with at least one workout.

## Steps

1. On Android, open the current rider's profile (the rider's name in the bottom bar or rail, then the **Profile** button under the current rider's card) → Connected. On iOS, open the rider's Profile (the rider's name in the tab bar or rail, then **Profile**) and find its intervals.icu section. Tap Link for intervals.icu and complete the OAuth flow in the system browser.
2. Force-stop and reopen.
3. Tap disconnect, then browse the intervals.icu library.

## Expect

- Step 1: back in the app, intervals.icu reads **Linked**, names the athlete, and offers disconnect.
- Step 2: the link survived.
- Step 3: it reads unlinked, and the library asks to link again instead of loading.

## Notes

That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

items.key: TST-0632 intervals.icu library browses and adds
items.name: intervals.icu library browses and adds
items.text:
With intervals.icu linked on a PRO or Family seat, open Workout Selection and find the **My intervals.icu Library** section. Test the four things only a rider can see.

## Setup

A PRO or Family rider with intervals.icu linked to an account holding at least one power workout and one HR-zone workout. A trainer connected, and a heart-rate strap for an HR-zone row. The ride modes are picked in the ride-mode strip. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS.

## Steps

1. **The section loads on a tap, never on its own.** Read the section on first arrival, then tap it. Tap the refresh control in the section header.
2. **The ride mode routes the rows.** The same section appears with **Power** and with **Heart Rate** picked in the ride-mode strip. Find an HR-zone workout in each.
3. **The duration chip filters the rows.** Set the duration filter to a band.
4. **Tapping a row rides it.** Tap a row and ride.

## Expect

- Step 1: first "Tap to load your intervals.icu workouts"; then rows with name, minutes and folder. The header's refresh pulls again.
- Step 2: each mode shows only its own workouts: the HR-zone workout is under Heart Rate, not Power.
- Step 3: intervals.icu rows narrow with the local ones; a row with no moving time stays.
- Step 4: once the gate has trainer, power source and (HR-zone) strap, it rides the workout's durations, targets and order, without a library copy.

## Notes

**There is no search field, no preview step and no add-to-library step on this screen.** The earlier wording asked for all three. Browse, filter and tap-to-ride is the whole flow (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:2030-2125`, `openIntervalsIcuWorkout:620`).

**The two parser assertions this row used to carry have moved to unit tests and should not be tested by hand.** `IntervalsIcuDslParserTest` asserts that an HR-zone token produces an `HR_ZONE` workout (`HR zone token Z2 HR produces an HR_ZONE workout`, and `mixed Z power and Z HR — presence of any HR token flips workoutType`) and that icu Z6 and Z7 clamp to YT Z5 (`Z6 HR token on pull clamps to Z5 with soft notice (FEAT-0090)`, and the Z7 case). Authoring a Z6 workout on intervals.icu by hand to confirm the clamp would show the rider nothing anyway: the clamp notice is deliberately not surfaced, because the policy is fixed and a message on every pull is noise (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:630-634`).

That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

items.name: Rider-facing copy says connect, never pair

- Step 2: the surface is named **Equipment Hub** wherever it is named.

items.name: Rider-facing copy holds the product-as-subject register
items.text:
Read the rider-facing copy on the paywall, About, the onboarding and empty states, and any integration or upgrade prompt. Sign-offs on correspondence are outside this check and are fine as they are.

## Steps

1. Read the copy for who its subject is.
2. Read the copy for how it opens and how it addresses the rider.
3. Read the copy for its English cadence.

- Step 1: it is written with the product as the subject, not the developer — no *I built*, no *I'll send*.
- Step 2: there are no motivational-imperative openers and no second-person stacking.
- Step 3: British-English cadence — *household* rather than *whole family*, *one-time purchase* rather than *buy once*.

items.key: TST-0641 Restore recovers an entitlement after a reinstall
items.name: Restore recovers an entitlement after a reinstall
items.text:
A purchase lives on the store account, not on the device. After a reinstall, or on a second device signed into the same account, the app asks the store for purchases as soon as it starts. The paid tier returns with no tap. Restore Purchase is the manual fallback, and it must still give a clear answer.

## Setup

- A store account holding a **real PRO or FAMILY purchase**: a Play test account on Android, a sandbox account on iOS. The debug tier override bypasses billing and would prove nothing here.
- Either uninstall and reinstall Your Trainer, or install it on a second device signed into that same account.
- A second store account with **no** purchase, for the last step.

## Steps

1. Launch the reinstalled app. Wait up to ten seconds, then read the tier in **Settings → About**.
2. Open the paywall from the **Upgrade to Family** button in Settings → About.
3. Tap **Restore Purchase**.
4. Force-stop the app and cold start it.
5. Sign in with the account that has no purchase, reinstall, open the paywall and tap **Restore Purchase** there.

## Expect

- Step 1: the paid tier, **PRO** or **FAMILY**, shows with no tap. A tier that stays FREE is a fail.
- Step 2: the paywall opens.
- Step 3: **"Purchase restored!"** appears, and the tier stays PRO or FAMILY.
- Step 4: the tier **survives the restart**. Reverting to FREE is a fail.
- Step 5: the app says plainly there is nothing to restore. It does not look failed or hang.

## Not this check

- Whether PRO survives the store being *unreachable*, and whether the app waits for the store before guessing: [[TST-0018-EntitlementResolution]].
- Whether the purchase completes: [[TST-0074-Purchase-Flow]].
- Which rider holds the seat after a reinstall: [[TST-0016-SeatResolutionAndArrivalStates]].

## Provenance

Covers [[FEAT-0011]].

Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20, one of the 44 rows that audit found uncovered. Written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms.

Rewritten 2026-09-06 into the Setup / Steps / Expect shape. The previous text sent the tester to "Settings → Subscription → Restore", which does not exist on Android — the control is **Restore Purchase** on the paywall screen (`PaywallScreen.kt:527`), and that error alone could have failed the check.

Corrected 2026-09-17 after Edwin's decision in [[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]. Step 1 used to expect FREE until Restore was tapped, which contradicted TST-0018. Android queries Play as soon as billing connects (`BillingManager.startConnection`), and iOS reads `Transaction.currentEntitlements` at launch, so a reinstall returns the paid tier with no tap. On iOS, Restore Purchase currently calls `AppStore.sync()` and shows no confirmation or "nothing to restore" message (`PaywallSheet.swift`); steps 3 and 5 record that as a fail if it persists.

items.key: TST-0648 A trainer that refuses control is recognised, written to no more, described once, and listed in its own bucket
items.name: A trainer that refuses control is recognised, written to no more, described once, and listed in its own bucket
items.text:
Test on **both platforms**. No Schwinn 800IC is needed and none is available: the fake trainer with its capability override set to "Refuses control" reproduces the bike's behaviour, and the KICKR leg proves nothing changed for a trainer that works.

## Setup

Developer Options on Android: under "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)", turn on "Fake a connected trainer", then fully quit and reopen the app. Set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to "Refuses control — every target write answered Control Not Permitted". It acts on writes, so it applies at once. This is the whole data-only state; no bike is needed.

On Android, do not use "Failure mode:" for this. That list only reaches the compatibility test's own mock (the "Run this test against a mock trainer (no hardware; ~15 s, not remembered)" checkbox), not the fake trainer the rest of the app connects to.

**Both platforms can now test every step.** Steps 8 and 10 used to say Android had no whole-app control for *refuses once* or *feature read timeout*, and told the tester to record `question` against [[ISS-0441-TheFakeTrainerCannotRefuseOnceOrTimeOutItsFeatureRead]]. That issue is **fixed as of 2026-09-17** ([[TASK-0924-AndroidDebugControlsForTheOwedChecks]]): both values are in "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)", beside the three that were already there. Test them and expect a verdict.

Step 8 is this check's own negative test for the three-strike latch — the case that must end `drivable` — so the version of this check that forbade testing it on Android was withholding the most valuable step it has.

On iOS, turn on Use mock trainer in Settings → Developer · Trainer and restart. Set Mock trainer capability to Off and Mock failure mode to Refuses control, then restart and connect the mock for the main leg. For step 8, choose Refuses once in Mock failure mode; for step 10, choose Feature read timeout in Mock trainer capability and set Mock failure mode to None. Each change needs a full app restart and a new mock connection. The iOS controls drive the whole-app mock, not the compatibility test's private mock.

A KICKR, or another trainer that accepts control, for the KICKR leg (steps 12 to 15). Android's capability override affects the KICKR too, so set it to Off before each KICKR connection. On iOS, turn Use mock trainer off and restart before connecting the real KICKR.

A heart-rate strap, or the mock HRM, for step 5.

A `data_only` entry in the trainer compatibility list, for step 7. On Android, turn on **Use the bundled test list** in Developer Options → Compatibility List Source (Debug); its Nautilus Schwinn 800IC entry is data-only ([[TASK-0924-AndroidDebugControlsForTheOwedChecks]]). iOS has no bundled test list, so step 7 there depends on the published list carrying a data-only entry.

The iOS build on a second device. Every step is tested on both platforms.

## Steps

### The mock leg — a bike that says no

1. Connect the fake trainer with the override set to "Refuses control", and start a Power workout so the app writes a target.
2. On both platforms, open the Equipment Hub by tapping any of the equipment icons at the end of the top bar, and read the Smart Trainer row. Tap the row and read its Resistance row. Then read both again in one non-English locale.
3. Open Bluetooth diagnostics and read the log.
4. Start a Power workout, then read the log again.
5. With a heart-rate strap or the mock HRM connected, start an HR-Zone workout and look at the delta pill. Without a monitor the start gate holds an HR-Zone ride at Connect or Cancel. Take a screenshot to compare with the same screen on a KICKR.
6. Run the in-app compatibility test and read its scorecard.
7. Open Settings, trainer compatibility check, against a list with a `data_only` entry. On Android, Developer Options → Compatibility List Source (Debug) → Use the bundled test list supplies one. iOS has no test list, so it reads the published list, which must carry a `data_only` entry (Edwin, 2026-09-25).

### The latch guard — one refusal is not a verdict

8. A trainer that refuses once, during a Power workout. On Android set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to **Refuses once — first target write refused, the rest succeed**; it acts on writes, so it needs no reconnect. On iOS, select Mock failure mode **Refuses once** and restart before connecting the mock.
9. Back on the fake trainer with the override still "Refuses control", disconnect and reconnect.

### The unknown states

10. Connect a trainer whose feature read times out. On Android set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to **Feature read timeout — 0x2ACC never answers, capability stays unknown**, then disconnect and reconnect, because it acts on the read. On iOS, select Mock trainer capability **Feature read timeout** and restart before connecting the mock.
11. Set the override to "No Control Point — 0x2AD9 treated as absent". Disconnect and reconnect the fake trainer.

### The KICKR leg — nothing changed for a trainer that works

12. Set the capability override to Off, disconnect the fake trainer, connect a KICKR on each platform and look at the cockpit. Compare the HR-Zone screen with the screenshot from step 5.
13. Run the compatibility test once on the KICKR and read its dispatch rows.
14. On iOS, read the Bluetooth log.
15. On Android, set the override back to "Refuses control", reconnect the fake trainer and start a Power workout until it latches `data-only`. Switch the override to Off before disconnecting the fake trainer and connecting the KICKR. On iOS, set Mock trainer capability Off and Mock failure mode Refuses control, restart and latch the mock; then turn Use mock trainer off and restart before connecting the KICKR. Confirm the KICKR is driven. Disconnect it, restore the normal mock and reconnect to check that the verdict is derived again.

## Expect

- Step 1: the Power workout starts on the refusing fake trainer.
- Step 2: the row shows the hand mark and *Resistance by hand* **once**; its Resistance row reads *Set by hand*. Both read correctly translated.
- Step 3: the log shows `Control capability: unknown → data-only` with its source, after two refusal votes, each followed by a re-issued Request Control.
- Step 4: **no control write appears in the log after the latch**, and exactly one line says writes are suppressed.
- Step 5: the row reads `TARGET n W` with the arrow and delta beside it, and never pulses. No `SUGGEST` pill. It looks different from a KICKR's.
- Step 6: the ERG, Simulation and resistance rows read N/A with a reason. The verdict does not blame the bike, and no control write is attempted.
- Step 7: the entry renders as its own bucket, not as *not listed*.
- Step 8: the capability never leaves `drivable`, and control writes continue after the one refusal.
- Step 9: the capability starts at `unknown` again.
- Step 10: the capability stays `unknown`, writes continue, and the trainer row carries no hand mark.
- Step 11: the capability is `data-only` immediately, before any write.
- Step 12: no manual-resistance line, no data-only `TARGET` readout, and the gear and slope-mode controls are present.
- Step 13: nothing in the scorecard has changed for a trainer that works.
- Step 14: the log carries a Control Point response line and a Start/Resume.
- Step 15: the KICKR is driven: gear and slope-mode controls are back, and no manual-resistance line. The reconnected fake trainer's verdict is derived again, not remembered.

## Not this check

- What the cockpit shows a data-only rider instead of the controls it removed: [[TST-0649-RidingByHandInEveryMode]].
- The fields the parser reads: [[TST-0650-IndoorBikeDataFieldsAndASurvivingLog]].
- The gear calibration rows TST-0143 to TST-0158. A compatibility-test run is **not** evidence for them. It writes an ERG target, a slope or a resistance level straight at the trainer and never consults the gear table. Those rows are the gear sweep, [[TST-0658-TheGearSweepRidesTheGearTable]], and separate rides.
- Whether a data-only scorecard earns the Pro grant, or can be submitted: [[TST-0656-DataOnlyScorecardEarnsNoProGrant]].

## What a failure means

Step 8 is the only step that catches the critical defect the design review found: a capability that latches on the first refusal. Without that guard, a KICKR that briefly loses control would be silenced for the rest of the ride. A `SUGGEST` pill on a KICKR means the gate is inverted. A missing line in step 3, with correct behaviour everywhere else, means the diagnostics are lying. That is the class of defect this whole phase exists to close.

## History of this check

- **Step 2** was untestable as first written. TASK-0853 moved the manual-resistance line onto the equipment panel on the Workouts screen. It had shipped onto an Equipment Hub screen that nothing navigated to ([[ISS-0417-TheEquipmentHubIsUnreachable]]). Edwin's `question` mark on TST-0028 is what found that. Since PHASE-025 (2026-09-22) the line is in the Equipment Hub on both platforms, opened from the equipment icons in the top bar.
- **Step 10**: four different failures produce no feature bits, and none of them is evidence that the bike cannot be driven. That is why `no read` must leave the capability `unknown`.
- **Step 15** was added by TASK-0850's sweep. TST-0451 asserts the same reset for the SIM-capability flag, and TASK-0823 extended that reset to carry this capability too. But TST-0451 is a regression test, so nothing reopens it. The risk is real and belongs in a check that is actually owed, which is this one.
- **Step 13** was corrected on 2026-09-13 by [[TASK-0896-SetupStepsExpectOnTheOwedChecks]]. It used to say "this one run is the evidence for TST-0143 to TST-0158". FEAT-0117 showed that the compatibility test never reaches the gear table, and five of those rows were retired into TST-0658.
- **Steps 2 and 10 were rewritten on 2026-09-28** for FEAT-0130. The manual-resistance line under the trainer's name became the hand mark and *Resistance by hand* on the trainer's row in the Hub list, and the details sheet opened from that row gained a Resistance row reading *Set by hand: this bike does not let the app change it* ([[REQ-0225-TheEquipmentHubIsAListGroupedByBikeAndRider]], [[REQ-0226-ARowOpensTheDevicePickerOrTheDevicesDetailsAsASheet]]). What the steps assert is unchanged: the app says it once, in the rider's language.
- **The Expect lines were shortened on 2026-09-27** ([[TASK-0977-ShortenTheExpectLinesOfTheOwedChecks]]) so the release test prints one short line per step. Step 1 gained a line that asserts nothing, so the lines pair with the steps. Step 4 lost its explanation: one log line per write is the ISS-0409 defect returning. Steps 5 and 12 lost their history: the `SUGGEST` pill is gone on both platforms ([[TASK-0877-TheHrZonePillDropsTheWord]], [[TASK-0935-TheIosHrZoneRowGetsTheSharedReadout]]), an earlier version of step 5 expected it, and in step 12 the data-only row that must be absent on the KICKR is the shared readout that replaced the pill.

items.key: TST-0649 A number to reach and a direction to turn, in Power, HR-Zone and Route alike
items.name: A number to reach and a direction to turn, in Power, HR-Zone and Route alike
items.text:
Test on **both platforms**.

## Setup

Developer Options on Android: under "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)", turn on "Fake a connected trainer", then fully quit and reopen the app. Set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to "Data-only — feature word reports no target bits"; it applies on the next connect.

On Android, do not use "Failure mode:" for this. That list only reaches the compatibility test's own mock (the "Run this test against a mock trainer (no hardware; ~15 s, not remembered)" checkbox), not the fake trainer the rest of the app connects to.

On iOS, turn on Use mock trainer in Settings → Developer · Trainer, set Mock trainer capability to Data-only and Mock failure mode to None, fully close and reopen the app, then connect the mock. The iOS mock capability picker changes the feature word the whole-app mock reports; it is separate from Mock failure mode.

Pedal the fake trainer through its power range, so the cue has something to react to.

A KICKR, or another trainer that accepts control, for the drivable leg (step 13). On iOS turn Use mock trainer off and restart before connecting it. Have the parity gallery captures open for comparison.

The iOS build on a second device.

## Steps

### Power workout

1. Start a structured Power workout and read the intensity row.
2. Ride under the target, then over it, and hold power on a boundary for a moment.
3. Read the centre column.
4. Start Quick Ride, the ERG free ride, and read the intensity row.

### HR-Zone workout

5. Start an HR-Zone workout and read the large number and the row beneath it.
6. Hold a power well away from the suggestion for two minutes, watching the suggestion.
7. Stop pedalling until power reads 0.
8. Time how often the suggestion changes, going up and going down.
9. Start Zone Ride, the HR-Zone free ride.

### Route and free-ride SIM

10. Start a route.
11. Start a free ride in SIM.
12. Look across every screen above for anything that suggests a speed.

### The drivable leg

13. Set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to "Off — the trainer's real answer", disconnect the fake trainer, connect the KICKR and repeat steps 1 to 12. Compare each screen against the gallery captures rather than from memory.

### The manual

14. Open the sibling site's *riding a bike the app cannot control* page, in English and in one other locale.

## Expect

- Step 1: the intensity row reads `TARGET 210 W` with an up, down or on-target cue. There is no `− 100% +` control.
- Step 2: the cue changes at ±5% and again at ±10%, without flickering on a boundary. The power number keeps its normal colour throughout.
- Step 3: the centre column is unchanged: current watts, w/kg, `AVG | MAX`, `TARGET: N W`.
- Step 4: Quick Ride is unchanged, with watts ± still there.
- Step 5: the large number is the rider's own power. The suggestion sits where the intensity row was, as a wattage with an arrow.
- Step 6: the suggestion stays near what the rider is doing. It does not walk down 309, 299, 289… as the controller's own target does.
- Step 7: the suggestion holds its last value rather than collapsing toward zero.
- Step 8: the suggestion changes no more often than every 20 s upward and every 10 s downward.
- Step 9: Zone Ride has the same design, and the zone selector is still present.
- Step 10: no gear control and no slope-mode chip, and the grade is still displayed. The rider's speed still responds to the gradient.
- Step 11: SLOPE ± is still present. The gear control and the chip are gone.
- Step 12: nothing anywhere suggests a speed.
- Step 13: on the KICKR the cockpit is as before this phase: gear control, slope chip, intensity percentage, and the pill's Applied and Predicted states.
- Step 14: the page describes what the data-only cockpits showed, and says plainly that the bike's wattage is an estimate.

## Not this check

- The pacer and the segment line: [[TST-0651-PacerGhostOnAndOff]]. A route on a data-only trainer has the pacer forced on, so the target in step 10 is the pacer's.
- How the app decides a trainer cannot be driven, and what the log says about it: [[TST-0648-DataOnlyDetectionOnAMockRefusingTrainer]].
- The same screens tested in one pass for consistency: [[TST-0653-DataOnlySixScreenWalk]].

## What a failure means

A suggestion in step 6 that drifts away from the rider's power means the transform is anchored to the controller rather than to measured power. That is the option-A design the review rejected. A cue that flickers in step 2 means the cause of the flicker that removed REQ-0072's bands was never found, only re-introduced.

## Notes

- Step 3: the target was deliberately not promoted to the large number, because the wattage is already on the profile bars.
- Step 7: the 800IC reports 0 W below about 100 W, so a rider stopping or easing off is the real case, not an edge case.
- Step 8: 20 s up and 10 s down is the controller's own cadence.
- The Expect lines were shortened on 2026-09-27 ([[TASK-0977-ShortenTheExpectLinesOfTheOwedChecks]]). Step 2's two lines became one, so the lines pair with the steps; neither assertion changed.

items.key: TST-0650 The parser keeps what the bike sends, and a 40-minute ride still exports its connect-time block
items.name: The parser keeps what the bike sends, and a 40-minute ride still exports its connect-time block
items.text:
Test on **both platforms**. The fake trainer supplies the packets. The KICKR leg confirms nothing changed on real hardware.

## Setup

Developer Options on Android: "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)" on. The repeated-status mode is **Send a Machine Status every second**, under "Fake Trainer — what it puts on the wire (Debug)" ([[TASK-0924-AndroidDebugControlsForTheOwedChecks]]).

One **forty-minute** ride on the fake trainer. This is not a spot check: the defect only appears once the 500-line log has wrapped round several times.

The packets steps 5 to 9 name come from the packet menu in the same section: "Heart rate relayed — bit 9" for steps 5 and 6, "Heart rate zero — bit 9 set, value 0" for step 7, "Bits 7, 8 and 9 — average power, energy, heart rate" for step 8, and "Speed, total distance, resistance level" for step 9. Both controls apply within a second, with no reconnect. Set the packet back to Default and the repeated status off when done.

**iOS has neither control.** Settings → Developer · Trainer offers no repeated-status mode and no choice of packet, so steps 1 to 9 cannot be produced on iOS. Edwin decided on 2026-09-25 to build both, mirroring Android, in [[TASK-0962-IosDebugControlsForTheFirstIosReleaseWalk|TASK-0962]], deferred to the first iOS release.

A heart-rate strap, for step 6.

A KICKR, or another trainer that accepts control, for step 10.

The iOS build on a second device.

## Steps

### The log

1. Connect the fake trainer in the repeated-status mode.
2. Ride for forty minutes.
3. Open Settings, Equipment, Bluetooth Diagnostics, and share the log. Read the export.
4. Disconnect and reconnect mid-ride, then export the log again.

### The fields

5. With **no heart-rate strap connected**, feed a packet carrying a non-zero heart rate in bit 9. Look at the cockpit.
6. Connect a strap and watch the heart-rate tile across several notifications.
7. Disconnect the strap. Feed a bit-9 heart rate of zero.
8. Feed a flags word with bits 7 and 8 set as well as bit 9.
9. Feed a packet with speed, total distance and resistance level present. Read the log, then look at every screen.

### The KICKR leg

10. Ride a KICKR for ten minutes and export the log.

## Expect

- Step 1: the export's connect-time block is at the top and complete: characteristic table, 0x2ACC feature and target bits, Request Control and Start/Resume responses.
- Step 2: **a repeated line appears once, with a count**, such as `[FTMS] Status notification: [4] (x2400)`, not hundreds of times.
- Step 3: the Indoor Bike Data flags word appears exactly once, with its field names decoded. MAC addresses still read `device_1`, `device_2`.
- Step 4: the pinned block describes the current connection, and the counts start again.
- Step 5: the cockpit shows the bike's heart rate.
- Step 6: **the strap's value wins** at every notification, and the bike's is ignored.
- Step 7: no heart rate is shown. Zero means no strap on the console, not a stopped heart.
- Step 8: the heart rate is still correct.
- Step 9: the log shows all three fields were read, and **nothing new appears on any screen**.
- Step 10: cadence, power and the displayed speed are exactly what they were. The export's format for a line that is not repeated is unchanged.

## Not this check

- Where the trainer's own speed should be shown. That is ADR-0011 and ISS-0388, and this phase deliberately leaves it untouched.
- How the app decides a trainer cannot be driven: [[TST-0648-DataOnlyDetectionOnAMockRefusingTrainer]].

## What a failure means

An export in step 3 whose earliest line is minutes old means the pinned block is not protected from being pushed out of the log. A heart rate in step 6 that flickers between two values means the strap-wins rule is a preference rather than a gate, and the bike is still writing into the same place.

## Notes

- Step 8 proves the parser walks the offsets field by field rather than reading heart rate from a hard-coded position.
- Step 9: this phase supplies the fields and does not decide where they are displayed.
- On 2026-09-27 the four Expect lines that step 3 carried were given to steps 1, 2 and 3, so the lines pair with the steps ([[TASK-0977-ShortenTheExpectLinesOfTheOwedChecks]]). All four are still read in the export at step 3; the connect-time block comes from connecting, and the repeated line from the ride.

items.key: TST-0651 The pacer rides the route the way a rider would, draws for every tier, and leaves the cockpit untouched when it is off
items.name: The pacer rides the route the way a rider would, draws for every tier, and leaves the cockpit untouched when it is off
items.text:
Test on **both platforms**. The engine's arithmetic is covered by unit tests: the Alpe d'Huez times against the ZwiftPower table are asserted in code, not here. This check is for what a rider sees.

## Setup

A KICKR, or another trainer that accepts control, for steps 1 to 13. Have the parity gallery captures open for step 1.

A route with climbs and bends, and an out-and-back route with a turn, for step 10.

Developer Options: "Tier Override (Debug)", to switch between Free, Pro and Family in step 9. Restart the app after each change.

A phone in portrait, for step 13.

Developer Options on Android: under "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)", turn on "Fake a connected trainer", then fully quit and reopen the app. For steps 14 and 16, set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to "Data-only — feature word reports no target bits" and reconnect; set it back to "Off — the trainer's real answer" afterwards.

The iOS build on a second device.

## Steps

### Off, which is the default on a trainer that works

1. On the KICKR, start a route without touching the pacer row. Compare the cockpit with the gallery captures.
2. Start a free ride in SIM without touching the pacer row.

### On, on a drivable trainer

3. Start the same route with the pacer set to **Steady**.
4. Read the control row.
5. Look at the terrain view ahead of the rider.
6. Ride a steep pitch, then shallow ground, then a climb with hairpins. Watch the CADENCE tile and the power target.
7. Tap the preset chip up to **Hard**, watching the pacer on the terrain.
8. Ride under the pacer's number, then over it, watching the power tile.

### Every tier sees it

9. Repeat step 3 as a **FREE** rider, then a **PRO** rider, then a **FAMILY** rider.
10. On the out-and-back route, ride past the turn onto a **reversed lap**.

### Free-ride SIM

11. Start a free ride in SIM with the pacer on, and change the slope.
12. Read the growing profile while changing power.

### The phone

13. On a phone in portrait, with the pacer on, read the control row.

### Data-only

14. Connect the data-only fake trainer and start a route. Try to switch the pacer off.

### A cockpit entered part-way through

15. With the pacer on, on the KICKR, ride ten minutes of a route. Leave the cockpit and come back to it.
16. Repeat step 15 on the data-only fake trainer, where the verdict can arrive after the ride has begun.

## Expect

- Step 1: as before this phase: gear control and slope-mode chip; no segment line, preset chip, `PACER` ghost or power-tile cue.
- Step 2: the free ride is as before this phase too: gear control; no segment line, preset chip, `PACER` ghost or power-tile cue.
- Step 3: a `PACER` ghost draws on the terrain, on the elevation strip and on the map.
- Step 4: the row shows the segment and distance left on one side, **`PACER 230 W ▲`** on the other; `PACER`, not `TARGET`.
- Step 5: the next segment is marked with its target as a chip, and the profile is tinted by segment target zone.
- Step 6: CADENCE reads `AIM 75` on a steep pitch and higher on shallow ground. **The power target holds through the hairpins**, with a slight negative split.
- Step 7: the target rises, and **the pacer's drawn position does not jump**.
- Step 8: the cue on the power tile responds at ±5% and ±10%.
- Step 9: the pacer draws for all three tiers, and **the "Family ghosts" lock chip never appears because of it**.
- Step 10: every other ghost is hidden on the reversed lap, and **the pacer still draws**.
- Step 11: **the target moves within a tick**, and the cadence hint follows.
- Step 12: the profile carries `PACER +120 m` or `−120 m`, and it changes as the rider's power does.
- Step 13: nothing is clipped or wrapped, and there is no per-device layout.
- Step 14: **the pacer is on and cannot be switched off**, and the row reads `TARGET`, not `PACER`.
- Step 15: **the pacer is beside the rider**, where its plan puts it for the elapsed time; not on the start line or kilometres behind.
- Step 16: the pacer is beside the rider, at its planned position for the elapsed time; not on the start line or far behind.

## Not this check

- Whether the pacer choice belongs to the rider and survives a restart, a rider switch and a backup: [[TST-0654-PacerAndPowerSourceBelongToTheRider]].
- The rest of the data-only cockpit: [[TST-0649-RidingByHandInEveryMode]].
- The pacer engine's arithmetic, which unit tests assert.

## What a failure means

A lock chip in step 9 means the pacer's sentinel id is in the visibility filter but not in the lock predicate, which is half the fix. A pacer that vanishes in step 10 means it is being filtered with the ghosts that ignore direction, which it does not resemble. A pacer sitting at the start line in step 15 means its position is still a side effect of the per-second tick rather than a property of the plan.

## Notes

- Step 6: a target that jumps on every bend is the pacing the climb-pacing evidence rejects.
- Step 9 is the second critical finding of the design review, and it is invisible unless the check is tested at each tier.
- Step 10: the pacer was generated for the direction being ridden, which is why it survives the reversed lap.

## History of this check

Steps 15 and 16 were added by TASK-0851. The defect they describe was real, and it was fixed on both platforms while the gallery was being built: only the per-second tick moved the pacer, so a cockpit entered part-way through drew it where the ride started. Nothing asserted it, and leaving and re-entering the cockpit is an ordinary thing a rider does.

items.key: TST-0652 Power meter pedals supply real wattage, and adding a power slot does not un-pair the rider's trainer
items.name: Power meter pedals supply real wattage, and adding a power slot does not un-pair the rider's trainer
items.text:
Nobody on the project owns power meter pedals. On Android, **a physical KICKR in Power Source with the fake trainer in Smart Trainer** exercises the Cycling Power connection, parser, slot rules and source preference. On iOS, **Mock Power Meter in Power Source with Mock Wahoo KICKR in Smart Trainer** exercises the parser and source behavior in the isolated debug app. The iOS mock replaces the whole Bluetooth provider, so it cannot connect the physical KICKR at the same time. Record the iOS result as simulated source behavior; it is not proof of a physical Bluetooth connection. The dual-sided pairing rule still needs real pedals and carries an acceptance exception until a pair is available.

## Setup

Developer Options: "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)" on, as the trainer.

On Android, an awake KICKR, which advertises both FTMS and Cycling Power, stands in for pedals. On iOS, enable **Use mock trainer** and fully restart; its Mock Power Meter supplies Cycling Power packets beside the Mock Wahoo KICKR trainer. The mock trainer advertises both FTMS and Cycling Power for the unplaced-device rule, but a mock cannot prove the physical KICKR's advertisement.

A Cycling-Power-only device, or a stored preference for one, for step 5.

A heart-rate strap on Android, or Mock HRM Strap in iOS mock mode, so all three slots can be filled in step 7.

Garmin Connect signed in on a browser, for step 9.

A ride saved before this release, for step 10.

On both platforms the devices are rows in the **Equipment Hub**. Open it by tapping any of the equipment icons at the end of the top bar: a screen on Android, a sheet on iOS. The power slot is the row titled **Power**, beneath Smart Trainer. Tapping a row with a device of its own opens its details sheet, which holds Change device and Forget; tapping an empty row, or one that reads *From the trainer*, opens the device picker. While a ride runs, rows open nothing and only Reconnect works.

## Steps

### The parser

1. Connect the platform's fake or mock trainer. Tap the **Power** row and choose its separate power source. Look at the cockpit's power.
2. With both the power-slot device and trainer reporting cadence, read the cadence tile. Then stop the power-slot device's cadence and watch the tile. On Android, stop pedalling the KICKR in the power slot; the fake trainer keeps sending its own cadence. On iOS, turn on **Stop the Mock Power Meter's cadence** in Settings → Developer · Trainer ([[TASK-0925-IosDebugControlsForTheOwedChecks]]); its power keeps arriving and the Mock Wahoo KICKR's cadence is untouched.

### The slot rules

3. Connect the dual-service KICKR on Android, or Mock Wahoo KICKR on iOS, with no explicit placement.
4. With the platform's separate power source in the Power row, look at the Smart Trainer row and at the fake or mock trainer's control.
5. Store a preference for a Cycling-Power-only device, then present that device where it no longer satisfies the trainer slot.
6. In the Equipment Hub, open the device picker for Smart Trainer, then Power, then Heart Rate: tap the row, and on a row with a device tap Change device. Swipe each picker away before opening the next.
7. Fill all three rows. Tap each one to open its details sheet. On Power, tap Forget this power source and confirm, then relaunch the app.

### The choice, and the record

8. End the ride. With both still connected, tap the Hub's Power row, then Change device, and choose the trainer. Start a ride and watch the cockpit's power for a minute. End it, choose the separate power source again in the Power row, and start another ride.
9. Save that second ride. Open its session detail. Export the FIT file and import it into Garmin Connect.
10. Open a ride saved before this release.

### What needs real pedals

11. Dual-sided pedals connecting as one device, and left-right behaviour. **Do not test this step on the KICKR.** Record the acceptance exception instead of a pass.

## Expect

- Step 1: live watts, not zero.
- Step 2: the power source's cadence wins. The tile does not flicker when it stops.
- [android] Step 3: the KICKR goes to Smart Trainer only, not also to Power Source.
- [ios] Step 3: the mock KICKR goes to Smart Trainer only. This covers slot choice, not the real KICKR.
- [android] Step 4: Smart Trainer still holds the fake trainer, and it is still driven.
- [ios] Step 4: Smart Trainer still holds the mock KICKR, and it is still driven.
- Step 5: the rider sees a message. The preference is not cleared in silence.
- Step 6: each picker lists only its own kind of device.
- Step 7: each details sheet offers Change device and Forget. After the relaunch, Power reads *From the trainer*.
- Step 8: the watts follow the chosen source and never switch mid-ride.
- Step 9: the ride names its power source. Garmin Connect accepts the file.
- Step 10: the power source reads `unknown`.
- Step 11: left and right pedal power behave correctly.

## Not this check

- Whether the power source stays with the tablet across riders: [[TST-0654-PacerAndPowerSourceBelongToTheRider]].
- What History and personal bests show about where power was measured: [[TST-0655-WherePowerCameFromInHistoryAndPersonalBests]].
- A dedicated cadence sensor in the fourth slot: [[TST-0657-ACadenceSensorFillsTheFourthSlot]].

## What a failure means

Step 4 failing, with the fake trainer losing the trainer slot when the KICKR joins the power slot, is the un-pairing hazard the design review found. It is the reason this feature reopens five pairing checks.

## Notes

- Step 2: crank cadence is measured at the crank, which is why the power source's cadence wins. The precedence is a first value, and Edwin can change it.
- FEAT-0110's priority is open and is Edwin's call. This check is written so it is ready when he schedules it.

## History of this check

- **Step 2** was sharpened by TASK-0851. It used to read "does not fight the mock trainer's own cadence", which does not say which one wins.
- **Step 6a** was added by TASK-0850's sweep. TST-0633 asserts inline Change and Forget on a connected slot. TASK-0826 added a line to that slot and TASK-0848 added a third slot, but TST-0633 is a regression test, so nothing reopens it. A third slot is exactly the kind of change that pushes a control behind an overflow menu, so the assertion belongs in a check that is owed.
- On 2026-09-17, step 8 stopped asking for a power-source change during a ride. Android's ride screen has no route to Power Source, and Edwin decided not to add one ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]). The source is now chosen in the Equipment Hub before each ride starts; the expectation is unchanged.
- On 2026-09-28, steps 1, 4 and 6 to 8 were rewritten for FEAT-0130. The Hub is a list, the scanners are picker sheets, and Change device and Forget moved from each slot's ⋮ or ellipsis menu into the details sheet a row opens ([[REQ-0226-ARowOpensTheDevicePickerOrTheDevicesDetailsAsASheet]]). Step 7's two platform lines became one, because both platforms now draw the same sheet. An unbound power row reads *From the trainer*, which is what "stays empty" meant.
- On 2026-09-16, the old step 6a became numeric step 7 so the release test can give it an independent mark. The former steps 7–10 are now steps 8–11; this changes no expected behavior or ledger verdict.

items.key: TST-0653 The six-screen data-only test on the mock trainer: every screen a knob rider meets, in one pass
items.name: The six-screen data-only test on the mock trainer: every screen a knob rider meets, in one pass
items.text:
The three feature checks each test one feature deeply. This one tests the **rider's path** end to end on a bike the app cannot drive, in a single session. It is the check that catches a phase that works feature by feature and does not hang together.

## Setup

Developer Options on Android: under "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)", turn on "Fake a connected trainer", then fully quit and reopen the app. Set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to "Data-only — feature word reports no target bits"; it applies on the next connect.

On Android, do not use "Failure mode:" for this. That list only reaches the compatibility test's own mock (the "Run this test against a mock trainer (no hardware; ~15 s, not remembered)" checkbox), not the fake trainer the rest of the app connects to.

On iOS, turn on Use mock trainer in Settings → Developer · Trainer, set Mock trainer capability to Data-only and Mock failure mode to None, fully close and reopen the app, then connect the mock. The iOS mock capability picker changes the feature word the whole-app mock reports; it is separate from Mock failure mode.

A rider with an FTP and a weight set, and an LTHR that is not a round fraction of Max HR.

A heart-rate strap, or the mock HRM, for step 3. An HR-Zone ride does not start without one.

The iOS build on a second device, for step 8. Screenshots of every screen from both platforms.

The gallery keys from TASK-0843, where a parity difference is recorded.

## Steps

### The six screens

1. **The Equipment Hub.** Connect the fake trainer, open the Equipment Hub by tapping any of the equipment icons at the end of the top bar, and read the Smart Trainer row. It is the same list on both platforms: a screen on Android, a sheet on iOS.
2. **Power cockpit.** Start a structured Power workout and read the control row.
3. **HR-Zone cockpit.** With a heart-rate strap or the mock HRM connected, start an HR-Zone workout and read the large number, the suggestion and the pill.
4. **Route cockpit, terrain primary.** Start a route with the terrain view primary and read the whole cockpit.
5. **Route cockpit, map primary.** Switch the map to primary.
6. **Free-ride SIM cockpit.** Start a free ride in SIM.

### Then, in the same session

7. **Diagnostics.** Export the Bluetooth log.

### Both platforms, side by side

8. Repeat steps 1 to 7 on the other platform. Read the two sets of screenshots together.

## Expect

- Step 1: the trainer connects, and its row shows the hand mark and *Resistance by hand*, once, in neutral colour, not amber.
- Step 2: `TARGET N W`, with a cue where the intensity percentage was.
- Step 3: the row reads `TARGET n W` with the arrow and delta beside it, in the deviation band's colour. No `SUGGEST` pill.
- Step 4: grade shown; no gear control or slope chip. Pacer on, not dismissible. Row: segment line, `TARGET N W`. Profile: next-segment marker. Cadence: `AIM 75`.
- Step 5: the pacer draws on the map too, and the control row reads as it did with the terrain primary.
- Step 6: SLOPE ± is present, the gear control is gone, the row reads `TARGET N W`, and the pacer gap line is on the growing profile.
- Step 7: the log carries the capability transition, the suppressed-writes line once, and the flags word.
- Step 8: both platforms match in wording, position and presence. On every cockpit the target sits in one place and is never called `PACER`.

## Not this check

- Each feature in depth: detection in [[TST-0648-DataOnlyDetectionOnAMockRefusingTrainer]], the cockpit in [[TST-0649-RidingByHandInEveryMode]], the pacer in [[TST-0651-PacerGhostOnAndOff]].

## Why this check exists

A rider who reaches screen 4 and finds the target in a different place than on screen 2 has been given two instruments to learn instead of one. A rider whose HR-Zone screen says `SUGGEST` and whose Route screen says `PACER`, on the same bike, is being told that the same number means two things. Consistency across the six screens is the claim here, and no single-feature check makes it.

## History of this check

- Step 1 was rewritten on 2026-09-28 for FEAT-0130. The manual-resistance line under the trainer's name became the hand mark and *Resistance by hand* on the trainer's row, and both platforms now draw the same list, so the old advice to compare facts rather than layout was dropped ([[REQ-0225-TheEquipmentHubIsAListGroupedByBikeAndRider]]).

- The Expect lines were shortened on 2026-09-27 ([[TASK-0977-ShortenTheExpectLinesOfTheOwedChecks]]). The line "Across steps 2 to 6" joined step 8, so the lines pair with the steps. Step 8 still means that any difference between the platforms is a parity defect, recorded against the TASK-0843 gallery keys. Step 3 lost its history: [[TASK-0877-TheHrZonePillDropsTheWord]] replaced the `SUGGEST` pill with the shared readout on Android, [[TASK-0935-TheIosHrZoneRowGetsTheSharedReadout]] brought iOS to match, and an earlier version of the line expected the pill.

items.key: TST-0654 The pacer choice belongs to the rider and the power source to the tablet, and both survive a restart, a rider switch and a backup
items.name: The pacer choice belongs to the rider and the power source to the tablet, and both survive a restart, a rider switch and a backup
items.text:
PHASE-021 added two settings. One is whether the pacer comes along and how hard it rides; that belongs to the **rider**. The other is which device the ride's power is read from; since 2026-09-30 that belongs to the **tablet**, beside the trainer, because the pedals stay on the bike whoever rides it ([[ISS-0532-ThePowerPedalsAndCadenceSensorAreSavedPerRiderButBelongToTheBike]]). This check tests both claims.

Test on **both platforms**.

## Setup

A FAMILY household with two riders, A and B. Cheapest: Developer Options, "Tier Override (Debug)" set to Family, then restart the app and add rider B.

A **drivable** fake trainer. Developer Options on Android: under "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)", turn on "Fake a connected trainer", then fully quit and reopen the app. "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" must read "Off — the trainer's real answer": a data-only trainer forces the pacer on and hides the answer, and the override stays set from earlier sections until it is changed.

A KICKR, for the power slot in steps 9 to 11.

A rider file written **before this release**, which carries no pacer fields, for step 8.

The iOS build on a second device. On iOS, FAMILY is Override: FAMILY under Settings → Developer · Tier override, and the drivable trainer is Use mock trainer under Settings → Developer · Trainer, with Mock trainer capability Off, followed by a full restart.

## Steps

### The pacer choice, within one rider

1. As rider A, open Profile — Preferences and read the Pacer row. Switch the pacer on and pick **Race**, then start a route and abandon it.
2. Reopen Profile — Preferences.
3. Force-stop the app and relaunch it. Open Profile — Preferences again.

### The pacer choice, between riders

4. Switch to rider B and open B's Profile — Preferences.
5. Set B's pacer to **Easy**. Switch back to A and open A's Profile — Preferences.

### The backup round trip

6. Export rider A. Import that file **over the existing rider A** (the merge path). Open A's Profile — Preferences.
7. Import the same file as a **new** rider. Open that rider's Profile — Preferences.
8. Import the rider file written before this release. Open that rider's Profile — Preferences.

### The power source

9. As rider A, open the Equipment Hub from the equipment icons at the end of the top bar, tap the Power row and choose the KICKR. Switch to rider B and open the Equipment Hub again. To switch on Android, tap the rider's name in the bottom bar or rail, then B's card. On iOS, tap the rider's name, then **Switch rider**, and pick B.
10. Still as rider B, relaunch the app and open the Equipment Hub.
11. As rider B, tap the Power row, then Forget this power source, and confirm. Switch to rider A, relaunch, and open the Equipment Hub.

## Expect

- Step 1: before any change, the pacer reads **on** for a rider created in this release, **off** for one from an older install or backup.
- Step 2: still **Race**.
- Step 3: still **Race** after the relaunch.
- Step 4: B's pacer reads **on with its default preset**, not Race.
- Step 5: A's pacer reads **Race**. Each rider keeps their own answer.
- Step 6: A keeps the preset stored on the device, not the one in the file.
- Step 7: the new rider has the file's preset.
- Step 8: **pacer off, preset Steady**.
- Step 9: B's Power row names the KICKR and reads *Connected*. The KICKR did not disconnect during the switch.
- Step 10: B's Power row reconnects to the KICKR without being asked.
- Step 11: A's Power row reads *From the trainer*. Forgetting it as one rider forgot it for the tablet.

## On iOS

iOS asks for the pacer on the **Ride with a pacer?** sheet that opens when a Route card is selected; there is no Pacer row on the rider's Profile screen. On iOS, every step that opens Profile — Preferences opens a Route card instead, reads the sheet's pacer switch and preset, and cancels the sheet. Setting a choice means choosing it on the sheet and tapping **Start route**, then abandoning the ride. The expectations are the same: each rider keeps their own saved choice.

For steps 9 to 11 on iOS, the Mock Power Meter stands in for the KICKR in the Power row. The whole-app mock cannot connect a real Bluetooth device beside it, and the tablet-wide preference is the same either way.

## Rewritten 2026-09-30: the power source belongs to the tablet

Steps 9 to 11 used to expect each rider to have their own power source. Edwin decided on 2026-09-30 that the power source and the cadence source are saved for the tablet, beside the trainer ([[ISS-0532-ThePowerPedalsAndCadenceSensorAreSavedPerRiderButBelongToTheBike]]). Built by [[TASK-1022]] (Android) and [[TASK-1023]] (iOS); until then, steps 9 to 11 fail on both platforms. Steps 1 to 8, the pacer, are unchanged.

## Corrected 2026-09-17: a new rider starts with the pacer on

Edwin decided on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]) that the app keeps TASK-0875's behaviour: a rider created after 2026-09-13 starts with the pacer on, while existing riders and older backups read off (`MainViewModel.addRider` on Android). Steps 1 and 4 now say which rider reads which. The iOS sheet is accepted as the iOS equivalent of the profile row. The iOS app does not yet start new riders with the pacer on (`MainViewModel.addUser` keeps the `false` default), so step 4 on iOS records a fail until that is ported.

## Corrected 2026-09-14: the pacer lives on the rider profile

This check was written while the pacer was asked on a pre-ride sheet. TASK-0873 retired that sheet and moved the switch and the effort to Profile — Preferences, so the steps and Expect lines now name that row. What they assert is unchanged. Found by TASK-0906.

The 2026-09-17 iOS code still opens `PacerPreRideSheet` when a Route card is selected and had no Pacer row in Settings → Profile, and the rider's Profile screen that took over that section on 2026-09-22 has none either. The iOS release test names that sheet for steps 1 to 8; the On iOS section above records that it is the accepted equivalent.

## Rewritten 2026-09-28: the power slot is the Power row

Since FEAT-0130 the power slot is the Hub row titled *Power*, and Forget is in the details sheet that row opens. An empty power slot reads *From the trainer* while a trainer is connected, which is what "empty" meant in steps 9 and 11 ([[REQ-0225-TheEquipmentHubIsAListGroupedByBikeAndRider]]).

## Not this check

- What the pacer draws: [[TST-0651-PacerGhostOnAndOff]].
- What the power slot accepts and rejects: [[TST-0652-PedalsInThePowerSlot]].
- The cadence source across a rider switch: [[TST-0657-ACadenceSensorFillsTheFourthSlot]] step 14.
- What a ride records about where its power came from: [[TST-0655-WherePowerCameFromInHistoryAndPersonalBests]].
- The older profile fields on the merge path: TST-0008.

## What a failure means

Step 4 showing Race is the failure that matters most, and it is silent. A preference stored for the whole device instead of per rider gives a second rider a pacer they never asked for. That is precisely the default change the phase avoided, to keep the seventy-one route checks valid. iOS is the platform to watch: it already keeps the active gear preset device-wide, and TASK-0836 was written to avoid repeating that.

Step 6 failing means the merge path writes profile fields from the file. That is the discard hazard TASK-0836 names, and TST-0008 tests it for the older fields.

## Notes

- No other check tests this. TST-0651 asks what the pacer draws and TST-0652 asks what the power slot accepts. Neither leaves the ride, and inside one ride a preference that belongs to the tablet looks the same as one that belongs to the rider.
- Step 6 is ISS-0392's rule, that the target profile wins, applied to a field that did not exist when the rule was decided.
- Step 8: a file from last month must not switch the pacer on for somebody, because that would change every route ride they take.

items.key: TST-0655 A ride says where its power was measured, and a best set on the pedals still ranks beside one set on the trainer
items.name: A ride says where its power was measured, and a best set on the pedals still ranks beside one set on the trainer
items.text:
A ride now records whether its watts were measured at the pedals or at the trainer. The field exists to serve one decision: **a change of power source does not break personal-best lineage**, the way a change of physics version does. A rider who buys pedals keeps one list of bests rather than gaining a second one, and the marker on the ride lets them judge the comparison for themselves.

That is a first value, and it is Edwin's to change. So it needs a check that shows what the current answer looks like on screen.

Test on **both platforms**.

## Setup

Developer Options: "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)" on, as the trainer. "Show debug workouts" on, for the two-minute **[Debug] ERG Verify** workout used in steps 4 to 6.

On Android, use an awake KICKR in Power Source with the fake trainer in Smart Trainer. The KICKR only reports the watts you pedal; nothing controls it. On iOS, turn on **Use mock trainer** in Settings → Developer · Trainer, fully restart, then choose **Mock Power Meter** in Power Source beside **Mock Wahoo KICKR** in Smart Trainer. The iOS mock replaces the app's entire Bluetooth provider, so a physical KICKR cannot join that mock trainer. Neither fixture is a pair of physical pedals.

A ride saved **before this release**, for step 3.

A rider with FTP set to 200 W and no personal best yet on [Debug] ERG Verify. No heart-rate strap connected during steps 4 to 6, so the workout's best is target adherence: the share of the ride spent within 5 % of the target watts (REQ-0130).

The iOS build on a second device.

## Steps

### The marker in History

1. Ride ten minutes with the platform's separate power source in Power Source and save the ride. In History, expand it.
2. Open the Equipment Hub from the equipment icons at the end of the top bar, tap the Power row, then Forget this power source, and confirm. Ride ten minutes on the fake trainer alone and save. Expand that ride.
3. Expand a ride saved before this release.

### One best across power sources

4. With the separate power source in Power Source, ride [Debug] ERG Verify to its end and save it. On Android, pedal the KICKR at least 20 % above every target, so almost none of the ride is within 5 %.
5. Forget the power source from the Power row in the Equipment Hub. Ride the same workout to its end on the fake trainer alone and save it. Read the personal-best result on the completion screen.
6. Put the separate power source back in the Power row in the Equipment Hub. Ride the same workout to its end and save it. On Android, hold each target within 5 % on the KICKR. Read the personal-best result.
7. Open Personal Bests. Open the workout's best, then tap **View session**.

### Both platforms

8. Repeat on the other platform, and read the two History screens together.

The iOS mock proves that a separately bound Cycling Power source stamps the History marker and shares personal-best lineage with trainer power. It does not prove a physical KICKR's Bluetooth connection or real pedal behavior; those remain with TST-0652's hardware checks and exception. On iOS the mock's watts cannot be steered, so steps 5 and 6 may rank either way; the expectations below hold regardless.

## Expect

- Step 1: the ride reads **"Power measured at the pedals"**, in the rider's language.
- Step 2: **no source line at all**. That is the design, not a miss.
- Step 3: no source line. The app does not guess what measured it.
- Step 4: the ride runs to its end and saves.
- Step 5: the completion screen reports better, equal or worse against the separate-source best, **never a first best**.
- Step 6: compared with the existing best the same way, never as a first best. The rule has no direction.
- Step 7: **one best for this workout**, not split by source, none retired. Its session shows the pedals line, or none for trainer power.
- Step 8: the same sentence, translated, and the marker in the same place.

## Not this check

- That the source is recorded, and that the FIT export's second device record still imports: [[TST-0652-PedalsInThePowerSlot]].
- The physics-version lineage rule: TST-0636.
- The History trophy, PBs filter and delete promotion over three improving rides: [[TST-0321]]. On Android, steps 4 to 6 produce those three rides.

## What a failure means

A step 5 or step 6 ride reported as a first best means somebody made the power source part of the lineage key. That is the opposite of the decision. It is also the shape TST-0636 asserts for the physics version: the two cases look alike in the code and were deliberately answered differently.

A missing "View session" path in step 7 leaves the rider a shared list and no way to see why one entry is not comparable. That is worse than either clean answer.

## Notes

- Step 2: a source line on every ride would be noise.
- Step 7: the path from best, to ride, to marker is the whole of what makes the shared ranking judgeable. If any link in it is missing, the decision becomes a silent lineage break rather than a visible one.
- Steps 4 to 6 on Android: the fake trainer reports random power between 100 and 250 W whatever the target (`BluetoothManager.observeMockIndoorBikeData`), so its adherence lands a few percent above zero. Pedalling far off target sets a lower first best, and holding target sets a higher last one, so each ride beats the one before.

## Provenance

Steps 2, 5 and 6 were reworded on 2026-09-28 for FEAT-0130, which made the power slot the Hub row titled *Power* and moved Forget into the details sheet the row opens. What the check asserts is unchanged, so it was not reopened.

Corrected 2026-09-17 after Edwin's decision in [[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]. The earlier steps asked for a "five-minute power best", which the app does not have: a Power workout's best is average heart rate, or target adherence without a strap (REQ-0130). The rewrite uses one workout's real best and checks that rides on either source are compared with it. Step 9 became step 8.

items.key: TST-0656 A scorecard from a bike the app cannot drive earns no Pro upgrade, and says so without telling the rider to fix it
items.name: A scorecard from a bike the app cannot drive earns no Pro upgrade, and says so without telling the rider to fix it
items.text:
A FREE rider who runs the compatibility test on an unlisted trainer can earn a one-time Pro upgrade for the scorecard.
