The release candidate on the smallest supported phone, and on Android a tablet for step 11. Both platforms have all six modes.

- On Android, use any phone or emulator and run `adb shell wm size 720x1280` and `adb shell wm density 320`, which gives a 360 × 640 dp screen. Undo it after step 10 with `adb shell wm size reset` and `adb shell wm density reset`.
- On iOS, use the iPhone SE (3rd generation) simulator, which is 375 × 667 pt.
- A trainer that accepts control, so every mode starts and Free Ride and Route show their gear row. On Android turn on **Fake a connected trainer** in Developer Options; on iOS turn on **Use mock trainer** in Settings → Developer · Trainer. Restart after either.
- A heart-rate strap for steps 3, 7 and 8: a real one on Android, **Mock HRM Strap** on iOS.
- Default text size for steps 1 to 8. For steps 9 and 10, the largest text: on Android, Settings → Display → Font size at its largest; on iOS, Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → Larger Text at the largest size. Set it back afterwards.
- For step 11 on Android, before the tablet gets the release candidate, start a structured Power workout on the build it already has and take a screenshot of the cockpit. That build is v2.1.8 from the Play Store; use the SM-X910 if it is on the bench.
- For step 11 on iOS, nothing to prepare. iOS has never shipped, so there is no earlier build to compare with.

## Steps

1. Start a structured Power workout and look at the whole cockpit.
2. Read the power, heart-rate and cadence numbers.
3. Start a structured HR-Zone workout and look at the terrain.
4. Start a Route ride and look at the terrain.
5. Start a Free Ride. Tap − and + on the slope, then on the gear row under it, several times each.
6. Start a Quick Ride and tap − and + on the target watts several times.
7. Start a Zone Ride and look at the terrain.
8. Start a Route ride with the repeat button set to 1, which rides the route twice. Read the small line under heart rate, power and cadence.
9. With the largest text, start the Power workout again and look at the whole cockpit.
10. With the largest text, start a Route ride and read the gear row.
11. On Android, start the same Power workout on the tablet and compare the cockpit with the screenshot from the earlier build. On iOS, open the latest CI run of the candidate's commit and find the result of TST-0679's grid.

## Expect

- Step 1: the profile takes about a third of the space above the bottom bar or more. The bar shows the rider and START whole.
- Step 2: each number sits whole on one line. Heart rate and cadence are the same size, and power is the largest.
- Step 3: the HR-Zone profile is visible, about as tall as the Power workout's.
- Step 4: the route's terrain is at least as tall as the Power workout's profile.
- Step 5: each tap lands on the button aimed at. The slope stays on one line, and the gear row reads a small GEAR beside larger numbers.
- Step 6: each tap lands on the button aimed at, and the target watts, such as `124W`, stay whole on one line.
- Step 7: the Zone Ride terrain is visible.
- Step 8: each shows LAP, AVG and MAX. Where one line is too narrow, LAP n sits above AVG n | MAX n. Nothing split or cut.
- Step 9: the terrain is still visible, and no number is cut off or broken across lines.
- Step 10: GEAR and its numbers stay on one line, and nothing is cut off.
- [android] Step 11: the numbers are the same size as in the screenshot, the terrain about as tall. The bottom bar replaces the old buttons.
- [ios] Step 11: TST-0679's `CockpitLayoutRulesTests` passed. Its scale rule fails if an iPad that fitted before FEAT-0131 draws the cockpit below scale 1.0 (`tabletsThatFit`).

## Not this check

- The ride-end summary and the other screens on the smallest phone: [[TST-0677-OnTheSmallestPhoneTheRideEndAndThreeOtherScreensShowEverything]].
- Every size, font scale and language in turn: the automated grids [[TST-0678-AndroidCockpitLayoutRulesAtEverySupportedSize]] and [[TST-0679-IosCockpitLayoutRulesAtEverySupportedSize]].
- Phone landscape: out of scope ([[ISS-0334-IphoneLandscapeCockpitOverlap]]).
- What each cockpit mode's numbers mean: the mode's own checks, such as [[TST-0649-RidingByHandInEveryMode]].

## Provenance

Rewritten on 2026-09-30 by [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]] for FEAT-0132. The cockpit's action row became a bottom bar of fixed size, outside the cockpit scale, on phones and tablets alike ([[REQ-0236-TheCockpitsActionsAndTheRiderSitInABottomBarShapedLikeTheNavigationBar]]). So step 1 measures the terrain against the space above the bar and asks for the bar whole, and the tablet's step 11 no longer expects the bottom of the cockpit to look as before ([[REQ-0231-ATabletCockpitThatFitsTodayDrawsExactlyAsToday]], amendment of 2026-09-30). Steps 2 to 10 are read again against the bar; their words still hold.

Written on 2026-09-29 with FEAT-0131's planning, from Edwin's decision that 360 × 640 dp and 375 × 667 pt must look right. It sat at `level: system` until the feature was built, so the v2.2.0 release test did not owe it early. [[TASK-1009-TheChecksTheFittedCockpitReopens]] moved it into the release test on 2026-09-29 and corrected two steps to what was built. Quick Ride has a target-watts row, not a gear row, so the gear readout is read on Free Ride's second row instead. Heart rate is a side tile in a Power workout, so it is compared with cadence, not with power. The v2.1.8 gallery holds no cockpit picture, so the tablet step, now step 11, compares against a screenshot taken before the tablet is updated. iOS has no earlier build at all, so on iOS that step reads the result of TST-0679's automated iPad check instead of comparing by eye. On 2026-09-30 step 8 was added, and the three steps after it were renumbered 9 to 11. It reads the Route lap line, which breaks into two lines where it does not fit, as Edwin chose on 2026-09-29 ([[TASK-1011-EdwinsAnswersTheLapLineWrapsAndTheRidingAsLabelMovesLeft]], answer 2B). Before that, a Route ride with laps was left out of this check while the question was open.

items.key: TST-0677 On the smallest phone the ride-end dialog, the celebration, Workouts, History and the rider screen show everything and every action is reachable
items.name: On the smallest phone the ride-end dialog, the celebration, Workouts, History and the rider screen show everything and every action is reachable
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies that the ride-end dialog and the celebration after Save, Workouts, History and the rider selection screen show all their content and keep every action reachable on the smallest supported phone at the largest text size.

## Setup

The release candidate on the smallest supported phone, with the largest text.

- On Android, run `adb shell wm size 720x1280` and `adb shell wm density 320` for a 360 × 640 dp screen, and set Settings → Display → Font size to its largest. Undo both afterwards with `adb shell wm size reset`, `adb shell wm density reset` and the font size.
- On iOS, use the iPhone SE (3rd generation) simulator, 375 × 667 pt, with Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → Larger Text at the largest size.
- A trainer so a ride starts: **Fake a connected trainer** in Android Developer Options, or **Use mock trainer** in iOS Settings → Developer · Trainer, then restart.
- Three riders in the household, one with at least five saved rides. Importing `demo-dave` from Demo Data as a new rider gives one with 18 saved rides.

## Steps

1. Ride any workout for a minute, then tap FINISH, and look at the dialog.
2. Scroll the dialog to its end.
3. Tap Keep riding, finish again, tap Save ride, and scroll the celebration to its end.
4. Open Workouts, pick Heart Rate in the ride-mode strip, and look at the header above the list.
5. As the rider with saved rides, open History, expand the stats card, then expand a ride and scroll through its charts.
6. Open the rider screen and scroll to the last rider.

## Expect

- Step 1: the dialog is a sheet at the bottom; its eyebrow, title and totals are readable, and nothing is cut off at the sides.
- Step 2: Save ride, Keep riding and Discard ride are all visible.
- Step 3: Keep riding returns to the ride; after Save ride, the celebration's numbers, zones and Done can all be reached.
- Step 4: the title and every header button are whole, and at least one workout row is visible.
- Step 5: the This Week cards and every chart are whole, and no chart hides another or the text under it.
- Step 6: every rider and every rider's actions can be reached.

## Not this check

- The cockpit itself: [[TST-0676-OnTheSmallestPhoneEveryCockpitShowsItsTerrainAndWholeNumbers]].
- What the dialog and the celebration say: [[TST-0684-WhenARideEndsADialogAsksOnlyWhetherToSaveItKeepRidingOrDiscardIt]] and [[TST-0685-AfterSaveTheCelebrationLeadsWithTheHeadlineThenTheNumbersAndDoneGoesToHistory]].
- Every size and font scale in turn: the automated grid, `ScreenLayoutRulesTest` and `CelebrationLayoutRulesTest` on Android, `CockpitLayoutRulesTests` (`testRideEndDialog`, `testCelebration`) on iOS.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-09-29 with FEAT-0131's planning. It sat at `level: system` until the feature was built, so the v2.2.0 release test did not owe it early. [[TASK-1009-TheChecksTheFittedCockpitReopens]] moved it into the release test on 2026-09-29. Step 4 now names the Heart Rate library, whose title is the longest, and step 5 names the stats card, whose This Week cards changed.

Steps 1 to 3 rewritten on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]]: [[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] replaced the ride-end summary with a decision dialog, a bottom sheet on a phone, and put the numbers on the celebration after Save. On a phone at the largest text the upload chips move into the celebration's scrolling page and its bottom bar keeps Done.

items.key: TST-0680 Not-connected devices are slashed, and the cockpit's bottom bar shows the rider and the actions
items.name: Not-connected devices are slashed, and the cockpit's bottom bar shows the rider and the actions
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies FEAT-0132 on a phone in dark theme, where connected and not-connected icons were hardest to tell apart. The top bar and the Hub rows must use one drawing, and the cockpit must end in a bar with the rider in every ride state.

## Setup

A phone under 600 dp wide on the release candidate, in dark theme, with one rider. No heart-rate strap set up. A bundled Power workout and Free Ride.

- On Android, turn on **Fake a connected trainer** in Developer Options and restart, with Mock Wahoo KICKR as the Smart Trainer. Discarding a ride disconnects every device, which step 6 uses.
- On iOS, use the real KICKR as the Smart Trainer, with **Use mock trainer** off in Settings → Developer · Trainer. A mock device cannot be switched off, and iOS keeps its devices connected after a ride, so step 6 switches the KICKR off instead.

## Steps

1. With the trainer connected, read the four icons in the top bar on Workouts.
2. Open the Equipment Hub from the icons and read each row's icon. Close it.
3. Open the Power workout and read the bottom of the cockpit before START.
4. Tap START and read the bottom bar while riding.
5. Tap PAUSE and read the bottom bar.
6. Tap FINISH, then Discard. On iOS, also switch the trainer off. Read the top bar, then open the Hub and read it.
7. Switch the trainer back on if it is off. Tap Reconnect on its row and watch its icon and row until it is connected.
8. Open Free Ride, tap START and read the bottom bar.
9. Tap the rider in the bottom bar.

## Expect

- Step 1: trainer, power and cadence are plain, in the bar's text colour. Heart rate is faint grey with a diagonal slash.
- Step 2: row icons match the top bar; no tile is in the accent colour. Heart rate: slashed, on a dashed tile, *Not set up*.
- Step 3: a full-width bar like the Workouts navigation bar. Left: the rider's mark in their colour, name under it. Middle: START. Right: empty.
- Step 4: the rider, then PAUSE and FINISH, each an icon in a tinted pill with its label under it.
- Step 5: the rider, RESUME and FINISH.
- Step 6: trainer, power and cadence are faint grey and slashed, in the top bar and in their rows. The trainer row reads *Disconnected*.
- Step 7: while connecting, the icon is in the accent colour with no slash, and the row shows a spinner. Then it is plain.
- Step 8: the rider stays on the left while Free Ride runs, beside PAUSE and FINISH.
- Step 9: nothing happens. The rider is not a button.

## Not this check

- Every state of the top bar from first run to a failed connect: [[TST-0675-TheTopBarIconsFromFirstRunToAFailedConnect]].
- Setting up, inspecting and forgetting a device in the Hub: [[TST-0674-TheEquipmentHubListSetsUpInspectsAndForgetsADevice]].
- The rider's colour on the terrain: [[TST-0668-TheRiderIsIdentifiableInEveryCockpit]].
- The cockpit fitting the smallest phone: [[TST-0676-OnTheSmallestPhoneEveryCockpitShowsItsTerrainAndWholeNumbers]] and the layout grids.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-09-30 with FEAT-0132's planning, and held at `level: system` until the feature was built, the way TST-0676 was held for FEAT-0131.

- 2026-09-30, [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]]: checked against the build, given `level: acceptance` and moved to `active`, so the v2.2.0 release test owes it. Three things were corrected. A paused ride shows FINISH beside RESUME on both platforms, not an empty right slot. The details sheet has no Disconnect action, so step 6 reaches *Disconnected* by discarding a ride on Android and by switching the real trainer off on iOS. "Tapping the rider does nothing" became step 9, so each step has one expected line.

items.key: TST-0684 When a ride ends, a dialog asks only whether to save it, keep riding or discard it
items.name: When a ride ends, a dialog asks only whether to save it, keep riding or discard it
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies the decision dialog that replaced the ride-end summary on both platforms (DES-0005 section 1): its eyebrow and title for each way a ride ends, its one line of totals, and its three buttons. Steps 8 and 9 verify that a ride that has started cannot be left any other way (ISS-0545).

## Setup

A tablet with a trainer that accepts control. The fake trainer is the cheapest: **Fake a connected trainer** in Android Developer Options, or **Use mock trainer** in iOS Settings → Developer · Trainer, then restart. Any rider. A Power workout with time to spare, such as Sweet Spot Base, and any bundled route.

## Steps

1. Start a Power workout, ride a minute, and tap FINISH.
2. Read the line under the title, and the buttons.
3. Tap Keep riding.
4. Ride the workout to its end.
5. Tap Discard ride.
6. Start a bundled Route ride, ride a minute, and tap FINISH.
7. Discard it. Pick Route, start a Free Ride, ride a minute, and tap FINISH.
8. Tap Keep riding, then PAUSE. Try to go back: the back gesture or key on Android, a back button at the top left on iOS.
9. With the dialog open (on iOS, tap FINISH to open it), try to go back again.

## Expect

- Step 1: eyebrow `<WORKOUT> · <elapsed> OF <planned>`, title Finish the ride?
- Step 2: `<time> · <distance> · <watts> W average`, then Save ride, Keep riding and Discard ride in muted red.
- Step 3: the dialog closes and the workout carries on from where it stopped.
- Step 4: eyebrow `<WORKOUT> · EVERY INTERVAL DONE`, title Ride complete, and only Save ride and Discard ride.
- Step 5: the dialog closes at once, with no second question.
- Step 6: the eyebrow gives the distance ridden of the route's length, such as `STELVIO · 0.6 km OF 24.3 km`.
- Step 7: the eyebrow reads `FREE RIDE · <elapsed>`, and Keep riding is offered.
- Step 8: on Android the dialog opens over the ride. On iOS there is no back button, and FINISH is in the bottom bar.
- Step 9: nothing changes. The dialog stays open and the ride does not start again.

## Not this check

- What Save ride does next, the celebration: [[TST-0685-AfterSaveTheCelebrationLeadsWithTheHeadlineThenTheNumbersAndDoneGoesToHistory]]. That a saved ride reaches History: [[TST-0040-Completion-Save]].
- That Discard ride saves nothing: [[TST-0041-Completion-Discard]].
- That Keep riding returns to a free ride: [[TST-0042-Completion-Resume-Free-Ride]].
- The ramp test's new FTP and Save and update FTP: [[TST-0328-Ramp-Test-FTP-Calculation]].
- The dialog as a bottom sheet on the smallest phone: [[TST-0677-OnTheSmallestPhoneTheRideEndAndThreeOtherScreensShowEverything]].
- The eyebrow of a Quick Ride or a Zone Ride. Android names the mode (`QUICK RIDE · 1:05`), iOS reads `FREE RIDE`; that difference is recorded in TASK-1041 for a decision.
- Every size and text scale: `ScreenLayoutRulesTest` (Android) and `CockpitLayoutRulesTests.testRideEndDialog` (iOS).

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the built dialog: Android `RideEndDecisionDialog` (`RIDE_END_SAVE_TAG`, `RIDE_END_KEEP_RIDING_TAG`, `RIDE_END_DISCARD_TAG`) and iOS `RideEndDecisionDialog` (`rideEnd.save`, `rideEnd.keepRiding`, `rideEnd.discard`). Both platforms upper-case the eyebrow.

items.key: TST-0685 After Save, the celebration leads with the ride's headline, then shows its numbers and zones, and Done goes to History
items.name: After Save, the celebration leads with the ride's headline, then shows its numbers and zones, and Done goes to History
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies layout B of DES-0005 section 2 on both platforms: the band with the headline, the six numbers for each kind of ride, the time in each heart-rate zone, and Done.

## Setup

A tablet with a trainer that accepts control, or the fake trainer (Android Developer Options → **Fake a connected trainer**; iOS Settings → Developer · Trainer → **Use mock trainer**; restart). A heart-rate strap for steps 4 to 7. Any rider, a Power workout, an HR-Zone workout and a bundled route.

## Steps

1. Without a strap, ride a Power workout to its end and tap Save ride.
2. Read the numbers under the band.
3. Tap Done.
4. With the strap connected, ride a Power workout to its end, save, and read the numbers.
5. Read the heart-rate zone bar under the numbers.
6. Ride an HR-Zone workout to its end, save, and read the numbers.
7. Ride a bundled route for at least one lap, save, and read the numbers.

## Expect

- Step 1: the celebration opens: eyebrow, headline, large number, comparison line, the ride's picture and a Saved to History chip.
- Step 2: time, average power, normalised power, TSS, average heart rate and energy; average heart rate reads `--`.
- Step 3: History opens, with this ride at the top.
- Step 4: the same six numbers, now with the average heart rate filled in.
- Step 5: a stacked bar under Time in heart-rate zone, and a legend for each zone with minutes, such as `Z2 Aerobic 14 min`.
- Step 6: time, average heart rate, average power, distance, TSS and energy.
- Step 7: time, distance, climbed, average power, normalised power and average heart rate.

## Not this check

- Which fact the headline states: [[TST-0686-TheCelebrationsHeadlineNamesTheRidesMostNotableFact]], and the personal-best checks [[TST-0314-Power-PB-Happy-Path-With-HRM]], [[TST-0316-Route-PB-Happy-Path]] and [[TST-0317-HR-Zone-PB-Happy-Path]].
- The upload chips in the bottom bar: [[TST-0687-TheCelebrationShowsEachConnectedAccountsUploadAndOnlyThose]].
- Share: [[TST-0689-TheCelebrationSharesTheRideAsAPictureInFourShapes]].
- The celebration on the smallest phone: [[TST-0677-OnTheSmallestPhoneTheRideEndAndThreeOtherScreensShowEverything]].
- A free ride's six numbers (time, distance, average power, normalised power, average heart rate, energy) are read in [[TST-0686-TheCelebrationsHeadlineNamesTheRidesMostNotableFact]]'s milestone ride, without a separate expectation.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the built screens: Android `CelebrationScreen` (`Routes.RIDE_CELEBRATION`, Done `CELEBRATION_DONE_TAG`) and iOS `CelebrationView` (Done `celebration.done`). Android labels the heart-rate number "Avg heart rate", iOS "Avg HR"; both are the average heart rate.

items.key: TST-0686 The celebration's headline names the ride's most notable fact: a peak power, the time held in a zone, or a distance milestone
items.name: The celebration's headline names the ride's most notable fact: a peak power, the time held in a zone, or a distance milestone
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies three of the headline kinds in DES-0005 section 3 from real rides, each set up so that no higher-ranked fact applies: a peak power (rank 3), the time held in a heart-rate zone (rank 6) and a lifetime distance milestone (rank 4). It also checks one "Also this ride" chip. The personal-best headlines are checked by the personal-best checks.

## Setup

A tablet with a trainer that accepts control and a heart-rate strap. Debug builds can use the fake trainer for steps 1 and 2 (Android **Fake a connected trainer**, iOS **Use mock trainer**); steps 3 and 4 need heart rate and distance from a real ride or the mock strap.

- A new rider with no rides, added for this check. As that rider, ride a Quick Ride for six minutes at about 150 W and save it, the same week as step 1.
- Demo Data's `demo-jack` rider file (`demo/riders/demo-jack.ytrider.json.gz`), offline in Drive. Its 12 rides add up to 95.0 km, the last on 19 April 2026, so one ride of 5 km or more crosses 100 km and no earlier ride in the last 90 days competes. Import it again to test this a second time.

## Steps

1. As the new rider, ride a Quick Ride for six minutes at about 200 W, and save.
2. Read Also this ride, below the numbers.
3. Connect the strap. Ride a Zone Ride in zone 2 for ten minutes, holding zone 2, and save.
4. Import `demo-jack` as a new rider. As demo-jack, ride a Free Ride of at least 6 km, and save.

## Expect

- Step 1: `Best 5 minutes since <month>`, the watts as the large number, and `<n> W above the best from <date>`.
- Step 2: a chip reads Second ride this week.
- Step 3: `<minutes> minutes held in zone 2`, a percentage, and `of the ride inside the target zone`.
- Step 4: `100 km indoors since <first ride's date>`, `100 km`, and `13 rides on this trainer. Today is the gold dot.`

## Not this check

- New best on and First time on: [[TST-0314-Power-PB-Happy-Path-With-HRM]], [[TST-0315-Power-PB-Adherence-Fallback-No-HRM]], [[TST-0316-Route-PB-Happy-Path]] and [[TST-0317-HR-Zone-PB-Happy-Path]].
- The household, pacer, laps, week and longest headlines, and the full rank order: the unit tests `CelebrationRankerTest` (Android) and `CelebrationRankerTests` (iOS), which share one case table.
- The same headline after reopening the ride from History: [[TST-0690-HistorysShareOpensAPastRidesCelebration]].
- Each kind's colours. The pictures in DES-0005 show them; the release test does not judge colour.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]]. The setups follow the ranking rules both platforms built (TASK-1031, TASK-1032): a peak power needs an earlier ride in the last 90 days with a lower peak; a free ride never takes a personal-best headline; the longest peak duration wins. `demo-jack`'s distance was summed from the file on 2026-10-10.

items.key: TST-0687 The celebration shows how each connected account's upload is going, and nothing for an account that is not connected
items.name: The celebration shows how each connected account's upload is going, and nothing for an account that is not connected
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies the upload chips in the celebration's bottom bar (DES-0005, "Upload chips") on both platforms, and that iOS now uploads a saved ride to each connected account by itself ([[ISS-0534-OniOSASavedRideIsNotUploadedToAConnectedAccount]]).

## Setup

PRO, so the Strava upload is not gated. The rider has Strava and intervals.icu connected: Android Profile → Connected, iOS the rider's Profile. A trainer that accepts control, or the fake trainer. Airplane mode off.

## Steps

1. Save a ride, and watch the bottom bar of the celebration.
2. Tap View on Strava.
3. Return to the app, and tap Open on the intervals.icu chip.
4. Turn airplane mode on. Save another ride, and read the chips.
5. Turn airplane mode off, and watch the chips without tapping.
6. Tap Retry on a chip that reads Upload failed.
7. Disconnect intervals.icu. Save a ride, and read the bottom bar.
8. Disconnect Strava too. Save a ride, and read the bottom bar.

## Expect

- Step 1: one chip for Strava and one for intervals.icu, each reading Uploading…, then Uploaded with a green tick.
- Step 2: Strava opens on this ride's activity.
- Step 3: intervals.icu opens on this ride's activity.
- [android] Step 4: the Strava chip reads Waiting for the network; the intervals.icu chip reads Upload failed, with Retry.
- [ios] Step 4: both chips read Waiting for the network.
- [android] Step 5: the Strava chip turns to Uploaded by itself; the intervals.icu chip still reads Upload failed.
- [ios] Step 5: both chips turn to Uploaded by themselves.
- Step 6: the chip reads Uploading…, then Uploaded.
- Step 7: only the Strava chip shows.
- Step 8: no upload chip shows; the bottom bar holds only its buttons.

## Not this check

- What the upload is called on Strava and intervals.icu: [[TST-0688-EachUploadIsTitledWithTheRidesNameAndDescribedByItsHeadline]].
- History's upload pills and Retry: [[TST-0102-Auto-Upload-After-Workout]].
- Which rider's account a ride goes to: [[TST-0106-Auto-Upload-Per-User]].
- A FREE rider's Strava gate: the Strava checks in the PRO Route section.

## Platform readiness

On iOS an upload made offline waits for the network instead of failing, and nothing on the iOS debug menu makes an upload fail. So step 6 has no failed chip to retry on iOS unless the account's access is revoked; the release test marks it.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the built chips: Android `UploadStatusChip` (`UPLOAD_CHIP_STRAVA_TAG`, `UPLOAD_CHIP_INTERVALS_ICU_TAG`, `UPLOAD_CHIP_RETRY_TAG`) with uploads from `RideUploads` (Strava queued by WorkManager until the network returns; intervals.icu sent at once), and iOS `UploadChip` (`celebration.uploadRetry`) with uploads from `RideUploader`, which keeps an offline ride pending until `NWPathMonitor` sees the network. On iOS a failed chip also names a short reason, `Upload failed · <reason>`.

items.key: TST-0688 Each upload to Strava and intervals.icu is titled with the ride's name and described by its headline
items.name: Each upload to Strava and intervals.icu is titled with the ride's name and described by its headline
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies DES-0005 section 5 on both platforms: what a saved ride is called on Strava and intervals.icu, and that the place where the rider connects each account says so.

## Setup

PRO. The rider has Strava and intervals.icu connected, and a browser signed in to both accounts. A workout ride saved on this build has uploaded to both, such as the first ride of [[TST-0687-TheCelebrationShowsEachConnectedAccountsUploadAndOnlyThose]].

## Steps

1. On strava.com, open that ride's activity and read its title.
2. Read the activity's description.
3. On intervals.icu, open the same ride and read its name and description.
4. Save a Quick Ride, and open it on strava.com.
5. In the app, read the Strava and intervals.icu lines where the accounts are connected.

## Expect

- Step 1: the title is the workout's name, with no app name in front.
- Step 2: `<headline>: <large number>, <comparison>. Ridden indoors with Your Trainer.`, such as `First time on Sweet Spot Base: 1:00:00, the time to beat next time.`
- Step 3: the same title and the same description as on Strava.
- Step 4: the title is Quick Ride, not Strava's own name such as Evening Ride.
- Step 5: each line says Connected, then `finished rides upload automatically, with their name and a short description`.

## Not this check

- The chips on the celebration while the upload runs: [[TST-0687-TheCelebrationShowsEachConnectedAccountsUploadAndOnlyThose]].
- That the activity's duration, power and heart rate are right, and on the right rider's account: [[TST-0106-Auto-Upload-Per-User]].
- The description in another language. It follows the app's language, and the unit tests `UploadTextTest` (Android) and `UploadTextTests` (iOS) cover German.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the built text: Android `UploadText.forSession` and iOS `UploadText`, used by every upload path. Strava receives `name`, `description` and `trainer = 1`; intervals.icu receives `name` and `description`. On intervals.icu the connected line keeps the athlete's name when it is known: `Connected as <name> — finished rides upload automatically, with their name and a short description`.

items.key: TST-0689 The celebration shares the ride as a picture: four shapes, a card for each fact, two switches, a photo behind the sticker, Share… and Save to Photos
items.name: The celebration shares the ride as a picture: four shapes, a card for each fact, two switches, a photo behind the sticker, Share… and Save to Photos
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies the share picker of DES-0005 section 4: the four shapes, the cards a ride earns, the two switches, a photo behind the sticker, Share… and Save to Photos, and the note about Strava. Sharing is free on every tier, so this is tested on a FREE rider.

## Setup

A tablet, a FREE rider and a heart-rate strap. The celebration of a ride saved with heart rate is open, such as the Zone Ride of [[TST-0686-TheCelebrationsHeadlineNamesTheRidesMostNotableFact]]. A photo in the device's library. On iOS, allow Your Trainer to add to Photos when asked.

## Steps

1. Tap Share.
2. Pick Story, Square post, Sticker over a photo and Wide post in turn.
3. Pick Story, and swipe through the pictures.
4. Turn Heart-rate zones off.
5. Turn My name on. Close the picker and open it again.
6. Pick Sticker over a photo, and pick a photo.
7. Tap Share…, and read the share sheet.
8. Close the share sheet. Tap Save to Photos, then open the photo library.
9. Read the note under the buttons.

## Expect

- Step 1: the share picker opens full screen: Shape, the picture, On the picture, Share… and Save to Photos.
- Step 2: the picture is redrawn in each shape, and each carries Your Trainer and `Indoor · <date>` at its foot.
- Step 3: the headline card comes first, then The numbers, then Heart-rate zones and each other card this ride earned.
- Step 4: the thin heart-rate zone strip leaves the picture.
- Step 5: My name is still on, and the rider's name sits above the date on the picture.
- Step 6: the photo fills the picture behind white text with a soft shadow.
- Step 7: the system share sheet offers the picture as an image to other apps.
- Step 8: the picture is in the photo library.
- Step 9: `Strava does not take pictures from other apps. To add this one to the activity, save it and add it in the Strava app.`

## Not this check

- Sharing a ride from History: [[TST-0690-HistorysShareOpensAPastRidesCelebration]].
- Sharing the rider card: [[TST-0691-TheRiderCardIsSharedAsAPictureWithTheWeightHiddenUnlessTurnedOn]].
- The picker as a sheet on a phone, and each card's exact drawing: the snapshot references `ShareCardTests` (iOS) and the Android references TASK-1037 adds.
- A household rival's name on the Household board card, which needs two riders who both allow names: not tested here.
- Whether the sticker stays transparent inside Instagram or Snapchat: the app hands over a PNG; what another app does with it is outside the release test.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the iOS build: Share `celebration.share`, `SharePickerView` with shape rows `share.shape.*`, the paged preview `share.preview`, switches `share.toggle.zones` and `share.toggle.name` (stored as `UserProfile.showNameOnPictures`), `share.photo`, Share… `share.share`, Save to Photos `share.saveToPhotos` and the note `share.stravaNote`. On Android the picker is [[TASK-1037-OnAndroidTheRideIsSharedAsAPicture]]: Share `CELEBRATION_SHARE_TAG` opens `SharePickerScreen`. It landed on 2026-10-10, and the `readiness_for` mark was removed.

items.key: TST-0690 History's Share opens a past ride's celebration with the headline it had, and shares it from there
items.name: History's Share opens a past ride's celebration with the headline it had, and shares it from there
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies the Share entry in each ride's menu in History (DES-0005 section 4): it reopens that ride's celebration with the same headline and colours, and its Share opens the share picker.

## Setup

Any tier. A ride saved on this build whose headline you noted when it was saved, and a ride saved before this release. Importing Demo Data's `demo-dave` rider gives rides from before.

## Steps

1. In History, open the menu of the ride saved on this build.
2. Tap Share.
3. Tap Share on the celebration.
4. Close the picker, and tap Done.
5. Open the menu of a ride saved before this release, and tap Share.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: the menu offers Share.
- [ios] Step 1: Share is the first entry in the menu.
- Step 2: that ride's celebration opens, with the same headline and colours as when it was saved.
- Step 3: the share picker opens for that ride.
- Step 4: History shows again, where it was.
- Step 5: the celebration opens with a headline worked out from the ride, such as `Second ride this week`, or the ride's name.

## Not this check

- The share picker itself: [[TST-0689-TheCelebrationSharesTheRideAsAPictureInFourShapes]].
- Export FIT in the same menu, which keeps its PRO check: [[TST-0092-FIT-Export]].

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the iOS build: `history.share`, offered first by `HistorySessionAction.offered`, also on rides inside a thread, presenting `CelebrationView`. A ride saved before the celebration existed works out the facts that can still be worked out when it opens (TASK-1032). On Android the entry is [[TASK-1039-OnAndroidHistoryCanShareAPastRide]]: Share (`HISTORY_SHARE_TAG`, `ws_dropdown_share`) is first in `SessionItem`'s menu. It landed on 2026-10-10, and the `readiness_for` mark was removed.

items.key: TST-0691 The rider card is shared as a picture, with the weight hidden unless the rider turns it on
items.name: The rider card is shared as a picture, with the weight hidden unless the rider turns it on
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies DES-0005 section 6 and [[FEAT-0078-ShareRiderCard]]: the rider card's Share opens the share picker with two shapes, the picture carries the full card with the weight hidden by default, and the weight setting is remembered for each rider.

## Setup

Any tier, with two riders whose weight is set. Neither has turned on weight for pictures yet.

## Steps

1. Open the first rider's card Share.
2. Read the picture.
3. Turn Weight on.
4. Close the picker, and open the same rider's Share again.
5. Open the second rider's card Share.
6. Tap Share…, and read the share sheet.

## Expect

- Step 1: the share picker opens with only Story and Square post, and one picture, the rider card.
- Step 2: the full rider card on the rider's colour, with FTP but no weight, and Your Trainer and `Indoor · <today>` at the foot.
- Step 3: the rider's weight appears on the card.
- Step 4: Weight is still on.
- Step 5: Weight is off for the second rider.
- Step 6: the system share sheet offers the rider card picture as an image.

## Not this check

- The rider card on the screen, which always shows the weight: [[TST-0417-Rider-Card-Profile]].
- Sharing a ride: [[TST-0689-TheCelebrationSharesTheRideAsAPictureInFourShapes]].
- A pre-filled caption: [[TASK-0547-RiderCardSharedCaption]] was cancelled on 2026-10-10, and neither platform sends one.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the iOS build: Share is the first entry of each rider card's long-press menu on the rider screen (`riders.share`), opening `SharePickerView` with `ShareSubject.riderCard`; the Weight switch is `share.toggle.weight`, stored as `UserProfile.showWeightOnPictures` for that rider. With Weight off, iOS also hides W/kg, because FTP and W/kg together give the weight away. On Android the action is [[TASK-0546-RiderCardShareAffordance]] (`RIDER_CARD_SHARE_TAG` in `RiderCardMenu`) and the switch [[TASK-0548-RiderCardWeightToggle]] (`showWeightOnPictures`), which also hides W/kg. They landed on 2026-10-10, and the `readiness_for` mark was removed.

items.key: TST-0366 Family tier resolves for a cold-started, never-used rider
items.name: Family tier resolves for a cold-started, never-used rider
items.text:
**Two preconditions in one run, because one rider can satisfy both:** a FAMILY licence on the device, and a rider who was created and has never ridden and is not the primary rider.

1. **Cold start.** Force-quit the app. Reopen it and immediately select that rider, before anything else has had a chance to resolve the tier.
2. **Ride.** Complete a workout as that rider, and tap Save ride.
3. **Premium features are there.** Tap Done on the celebration, and open the ride's menu in History.

*(partially automated: `LicensingManagerTest` covers device-wide tier resolution and the billing-priority logic, `UserRepositoryTest.multiple_riders_sorted_or_not_still_each_retrievable` the multi-rider path; the Play Billing purchase, the cold-start timing and the screens after Save stay manual.)*

## Expect

- The celebration opens with no paywall, and the ride's menu offers Export FIT without a lock.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0367]], which asked for the same completion overlay under a different precondition: a rider who had never been used, rather than a cold start. ISS-0108 was one defect that both preconditions exposed, and a rider who is both new and selected straight after a force-quit exercises them together in one workout.

One tick no longer separates "the tier resolves too late after a cold start" from "the tier resolves wrongly for a rider with no history". If it fails, run it again with the app already warm to tell the two apart.

## Expect rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the summary's FIT export and Strava upload buttons: a ride now uploads by itself to each connected account, and Export FIT is in History. The check still asks whether FAMILY has resolved for this rider, read from the PRO-gated Export FIT. It states how the product behaves now as well as the fixed defect, so it carries `kind: feature` (`TESTING.md`, "When to invalidate").

items.key: TST-0380 HRM disconnect and reconnect, in both cockpit layouts
items.name: HRM disconnect and reconnect, in both cockpit layouts
items.text:
**The disconnect is the expensive part, and the two cockpit layouts show it differently, so this needs one ride of each type.** Start with the HRM connected, then disconnect it mid-ride by moving out of range or turning it off.

## Steps

1. **HR-hero layout — "Heart-rate signal lost".** In an HR-Zone workout, heart rate is the centre hero. Disconnect the HRM mid-ride.
2. **Default layout — "tap to reconnect".** In a Power workout, heart rate is the left-hand metric. Disconnect the HRM mid-ride.
3. **Reconnect.** Tap that cell, then bring the HRM back.
4. **The ride does not notice.** Watch the workout timer, power and cadence through the whole disconnect and reconnect.

## Expect

- Step 1: HR reads "--", not frozen, over *Heart-rate signal lost* in red. The hero is not tappable; LINK HRM in the bottom bar reconnects.
- Step 2: the left metric reads *tap to reconnect*, underlined in the accent colour, and is tappable. Neither string shows in the other's layout.
- Step 3: it reads *reconnecting…* in amber, no longer underlined. Then HR updates again.
- Step 4: the workout timer, power and cadence keep running throughout.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0381]] (step 3) and [[TST-0382]] (step 4). Setting up an HRM and forcing it to drop is the costly part, and both absorbed rows hang off that one disconnect.

Both disconnect strings are kept. `ActiveWorkoutScreen.kt:1376` renders `workout_hrm_signal_lost` in the HR-hero layout and `:1448` renders `workout_hrm_tap_reconnect` in the default layout. Merging them into one expected string would let either layout render the other's copy and still pass.

One tick now covers two rides, one per layout. It no longer says which layout was at fault, nor whether the failure was the string, the tap target, or a ride that stalled while the HRM was away. Write down the step number and the workout type.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

## A feature check since 2026-09-29

This check came from a fixed defect, and its Expect lines also say how the cockpit looks now. FEAT-0131 redrew that part on phones, so it carries `kind: feature` and was reopened (`TESTING.md`, "When to invalidate"; [[CHG-20260929-The-Cockpit-Fits-Every-Screen-And-The-Terrain-Keeps-Its-Share]]).

## Reworded 2026-09-30

Since FEAT-0132 LINK HRM is an item in the cockpit's bottom bar, not a round button ([[REQ-0236-TheCockpitsActionsAndTheRiderSitInABottomBarShapedLikeTheNavigationBar]]). [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]] reworded step 1's button name; what the check asks is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0396 Coaching cues — display, auto-dismiss, and long-cue wrapping
items.name: Coaching cues — display, auto-dismiss, and long-cue wrapping
items.text:
One run of the "[Debug] Coaching Cues & Ramps" workout answers all three questions. Start it and watch the terrain graph.

## Procedure

1. **Display.** Coaching cues appear as a floating banner overlaid on the terrain graph, at the times the workout specifies.
2. **Auto-dismiss.** Each cue disappears after its duration — 5 s by default — without a tap.
3. **Long-cue wrapping.** At 20 s into the warmup, the long cue wraps to two lines and does not overflow the banner.

## Expect

- Step 1: cues appear as a banner over the terrain, at the times the workout sets.
- Step 2: each cue clears by itself after its duration, 5 s by default.
- Step 3: the long cue 20 s into the warm-up wraps to two lines inside its banner.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0397-Cue-Auto-Dismiss]] | cues disappear after their duration | step 2 |
| [[TST-0398-Long-Cue-Wrapping]] | the long warmup cue wraps to two lines | step 3 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0397** — a cue that shows but never clears now records the same as a cue that never shows, which is a difference a rider mid-ride cares about a great deal.
- **TST-0398** — a layout overflow on one long cue disappears into the same verdict as the cue system being broken.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- Which of the three observations held, named one by one.
