items.key: TST-0400 Workout import — one good file and three refusals
items.name: Workout import — one good file and three refusals
items.text:
Four trips through the same "Import (.ytw .zwo)" button and the same file picker. Have the four files ready before starting.

## Setup

A PRO rider on Workouts. Four files ready on the device or in Drive: a valid `.zwo`, a non-workout file such as a `.pdf`, a malformed `.zwo` and a malformed `.ytw`. The ride modes are picked in the ride-mode strip. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS.

## Procedure

1. **A good `.zwo` imports.** Tap "Import (.ytw .zwo)" and pick a valid `.zwo`. The snackbar reads "Imported: \<workout name\>", and the workout appears in the library with the right intervals and terrain graph.
2. **An unsupported file type is refused, per tab.** Pick a non-workout file such as a `.pdf` or `.png`. With **Power** picked in the ride-mode strip the snackbar reads "Unsupported file type — please select a .ytw or .zwo file" and carries a **Retry** action. Pick **Route**, then **Heart Rate**, in the ride-mode strip, repeat the same import in each, and confirm each shows **its own mode-specific variant** of that message rather than the Power wording. The per-tab variants are the part most likely to rot, so check them rather than sampling one. On iOS, Files greys out a file the importer does not accept, so the `.pdf` cannot be picked in any ride mode; that is the refusal on iOS (Edwin, 2026-09-25, [[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]] decision 17).
3. **A malformed `.zwo` is refused by name.** Pick a `.zwo` whose XML is broken. The snackbar reads "Import failed — File is malformed or not a valid .zwo file."
4. **A malformed `.ytw` is refused by name.** Pick a `.ytw` whose JSON is broken. The snackbar reads "Import failed — File is malformed or not a valid .ytw workout."

*(Partially automated: `ZwoParserTest` and `IntervalDeserializerTest` cover the ZWO and `.ytw` parses including their typed failures, and `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` covers the tier gate. The SAF picker, the library refresh, the per-tab snackbar copy and the extension filter all stay manual.)*

## Expect

- Step 1: a snackbar reads "Imported: \<workout name\>", and the workout is listed with the right intervals and graph.
- [android] Step 2: Power reads "Unsupported file type — please select a .ytw or .zwo file", with Retry. Route and Heart Rate each have their own wording.
- [ios] Step 2: Files greys out the `.pdf` in every ride mode, so it cannot be picked.
- Step 3: the snackbar reads "Import failed — File is malformed or not a valid .zwo file."
- Step 4: the snackbar reads "Import failed — File is malformed or not a valid .ytw workout."

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0401-Unsupported-File-Type]] | the unsupported-type message, and its per-tab variants | step 2 |
| [[TST-0402-Malformed-ZWO-Toast]] | the typed malformed-`.zwo` message | step 3 |
| [[TST-0403-Malformed-YTW-Toast]] | the typed malformed-`.ytw` message | step 4 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0401** — three or four tab variants collapse into one step, so a single tab that has reverted to the Power wording records as "step 2 failed" and must be named in the evidence.
- **TST-0402** — a typed parse failure regressing to the old generic "file format not recognised" message is exactly the thing TASK-0317 fixed, and it now shares a verdict with a working import.
- **TST-0403** — the `.ytw` and `.zwo` paths are different parsers reporting through one surface, and one of them regressing no longer fails a row of its own.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- The exact snackbar text for each of the four files, and for step 2 one line per tab.

## Corrected 2026-09-17

The steps used to name a toast. The Workouts screen shows import results in its snackbar, with a Retry action on the unsupported-type refusal (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt`, AR-14), as [[TST-0254-Import-Failure-Toast-Malformed]] and [[TST-0257-Wrong-Tab-File-Filter]] already say. Edwin confirmed the snackbar on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]). The message text is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0404 Cadence targets in the cockpit — display, nudges, arrows, and their absence
items.name: Cadence targets in the cockpit — display, nudges, arrows, and their absence
items.text:
One ride through a workout with cadence targets, "Easy Spin" (target 90) and a "Recovery" interval that has none.

## Steps

1. **The target shows.** During "Easy Spin", read the cadence metric's subtext.
2. **Colour nudges.** Pedal above 100 RPM.
3. **Arrows point the way.** Pedal below the target, then above it.
4. **Negative — an interval with no target wears no decoration.** Ride into the "Recovery" interval and read the cadence. This step keeps its own line because an absence folded under a positive is how a gate quietly stops checking it.

## Expect

- Step 1: the subtext reads "TARGET: 90".
- Step 2: the value turns orange 5–10 RPM off target, red more than 10 off.
- Step 3: ▲ shows below target, ▼ above it.
- Step 4: plain cadence: no TARGET subtext, no colour, no arrow.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0405]] (step 2), [[TST-0406]] (step 3) and [[TST-0407]] (step 4). All four read the same cadence metric during one ride on one trainer, and the expensive part is the ride.

Step 4 is the negative case and is named separately on purpose, per the rule TASK-0891 states: a workout that decorates an untargeted interval is a defect no positive step can see.

One tick no longer separates a missing target subtext from wrong nudge colours, wrong arrows, or decoration leaking into an interval that has no target. Write down the step number.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0408 Cadence coaching banner announces the next target
items.name: Cadence coaching banner announces the next target
items.text:
Ride a workout whose intervals carry different cadence targets.

## Steps

1. **The banner appears ahead of the change.** Watch the last 10 seconds before "Low Cadence Grind" starts.
2. **It appears for every change, not just the first.** Ride on.

## Expect

- Step 1: 10 s before, a banner reads "Next: Low Cadence Grind — 65 RPM".
- Step 2: a banner comes before every interval whose cadence target differs.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0409]] (step 2). Both rows watch the same banner during the same ride; TST-0409 asked for the general rule where this row named one instance of it.

One tick no longer separates a banner that never appears from one that appears once and then stops. The second is the more likely regression, so stay on the ride past the first interval change.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0410 Spiral of death — relief and recovery
items.name: Spiral of death — relief and recovery
items.text:
Ride the "Spiral Test" interval (120 % power, target 50 RPM) on a real trainer.

## Steps

1. **Relief.** Stop pedalling, or drop below 50 RPM, for 3 or more seconds.
2. **Recovery.** Resume pedalling above 70 RPM.

## Expect

- Step 1: the target power halves and a "Low cadence detected" cue appears.
- Step 2: the target power returns to normal within 10 seconds.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0411]] (step 2). Recovery cannot be tested without triggering relief first, so the two were always tested in one go on one trainer.

One tick no longer separates relief that never fires from relief that fires and never lets go. The second is the worse failure — the rider is left at half power for the rest of the interval — so note which step failed.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0414 The expanded session in History — training metrics, TSS colour, and the peak-power row
items.name: The expanded session in History — training metrics, TSS colour, and the peak-power row
items.text:
Complete a workout, open History, and expand the session. Every step below is one scroll down that expanded card.

**Training metrics.** NP, TSS, IF and VI are shown below the Workout Analysis graph.

**TSS colour.** The TSS colour matches the value shown: green below 150, amber between 150 and 300, red above 300.

**Peak power row.** The 5 s, 30 s, 1 min, 5 min and 20 min peak-power values are shown below the training metrics.

*(partially automated: `AnalyticsMathTest` covers the NP / TSS / IF / VI maths; `WorkoutSessionRepositoryTest` and `MetricRepositoryTest` cover session and metric persistence. The card rendering, the colour and the peak-power row stay visual.)*

## Expect

- NP, TSS, IF and VI show below the Workout Analysis graph.
- The TSS colour matches its value: green below 150, amber from 150 to 300, red above 300.
- The 5 s, 30 s, 1 min, 5 min and 20 min peak powers show below the training metrics.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0415` (TSS Color Coding) — the TSS value taking a colour from its band. It is the **TSS colour** step.
- `TST-0416` (Peak Power Row) — the five peak-power durations below the metrics. It is the **Peak power row** step.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates a missing metric from a wrong TSS colour or a missing peak-power row. All three render on the same expanded card, so a rider must write down which named step was wrong.

**Only one TSS band can be checked per session.** `TST-0415` listed three colours, but a single ride produces a single TSS, so a rider was never going to see green, amber and red in one ride. The step is worded as "the colour matches the value shown" for that reason. Checking the other two bands means riding a session that lands in them, and no row asks for that today.

items.key: TST-0417 Rider Card on Profile
items.name: Rider Card on Profile
items.text:
Switch to a rider with 5+ completed sessions, then open the current rider's profile: tap the rider's name in the bottom bar on a phone or in the rail on a tablet, then **Profile**. On Android, **Profile** is the button under the current rider's card. On iOS it is next to **Switch rider**. The whole check reads off that one card, without a trainer and without a ride.

## Setup

A rider with at least five completed sessions. Only the current rider's profile opens, so switch to that rider first.

## Steps

1. **The card renders.** Look at the top of the profile.
2. **Six attributes carry numbers.** Read the six attributes on the card.
3. **The overall rating carries a band.** Read the overall rating on the card.

## Expect

- Step 1: a rider card with a six-axis radar chart, at the top of the profile.
- Step 2: PWR, SPR, CLB, END, CON and REC each show a rating from 0 to 99.
- Step 3: an overall 0–99 rating with its band label, such as "Recreational" or "Competitive".

## Notes

*(partially automated: `RiderCardTest` + `RatingEngineTest` + `RiderAttributeCalculatorTest` — text render, clamp to 0–99, anchor interpolation, null-HRE redistribution, overall weighting and band thresholds are all covered; the radar chart's Canvas rendering stays visual.)*

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0418]] (step 2) and [[TST-0419]] (step 3). All three read the same card on the same screen, so a rider was being asked to open one profile three times.

One tick no longer separates a card that failed to render at all from a card that rendered with a missing attribute or a missing band label. If the tick fails, write down which of the three steps it was.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps under `## Steps` with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0420 Empty State
items.name: Empty State
items.text:
Create a new rider with 0 sessions. Verify a greyed-out card with "Ride more to unlock your stats" is shown. *(partially automated: `RiderCardTest.empty_state_renders_when_ratings_null` — null-ratings branch covered; "Ride more" copy + grey-out stay visual.)*

## Expect

- A greyed-out card reads "Ride more to unlock your stats".

items.key: TST-0421 Compact Card on Selection
items.name: Compact Card on Selection
items.text:
On the rider selection screen, verify each rider shows a compact rider card with radar chart and overall rating. *(partially automated: `RiderCardTest.compact_size_still_renders_name` — size variant renders; selection-screen layout stays manual.)*

## Expect

- Each rider shows a compact rider card with a radar chart and overall rating.

items.key: TST-0432 Interval transitions — the tablet buzzes and the app survives
items.name: Interval transitions — the tablet buzzes and the app survives
items.text:
Start a structured workout with at least four intervals and ride it to the end, so at least three interval transitions happen. Both steps are watched across those transitions.

**Vibration.** At each interval transition the tablet vibrates briefly.

**No freeze or crash.** The app does not freeze or crash at any transition, and the ride continues to the end.

These two were one bug. The missing `VIBRATE` permission was what crashed the app at a transition, so the buzz and the survival come from the same fix and fail together.

## Expect

- The tablet buzzes briefly at each interval transition.
- No freeze or crash at any transition. The ride reaches the end.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0433` (No Crash on Transition) — riding three or more transitions and confirming no freeze or crash. It is the **No freeze or crash** step, on the same ride.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates a transition that does not buzz from a transition that takes the app down. They shared a root cause once, but a regression could bring back either alone — a silent transition is a missing haptic call, a crash is a permission or effect problem. A rider must write down which named step failed.

items.key: TST-0435 Family Tier Add Rider
items.name: Family Tier Add Rider
items.text:
On Family tier with 1-4 riders, verify the "Add Rider" card appears after the last rider card. *(partially automated: `UserRepositoryTest.multiple_riders_sorted_or_not_still_each_retrievable` — multi-rider persistence covered; add-card rendering stays manual.)*

## Expect

- The "Add Rider" card appears after the last rider card.

items.key: TST-0437 Auto Backup Does Not Carry Credentials
items.name: Auto Backup Does Not Carry Credentials
items.text:
On a device with Auto Backup enabled and Strava connected, uninstall and reinstall. After Auto Backup restores, verify the app shows Strava as disconnected and the BYOK key slot is empty. (Credentials must not ride through Auto Backup either.) *(partially automated: `BackupCredentialExclusionTest` guards the Strava-token + API-key exclusion at the serialisation layer — which is the same scrubbing path Auto Backup uses via `android:allowBackup` attribute rules; uninstall/reinstall round-trip stays manual.)*

The iOS release test must not treat its reinstall or iCloud backup path as this Android Auto Backup result without a separate expectation and scope decision.

## Expect

- After Auto Backup restores, Strava shows as disconnected and the bring-your-own AI key slot is empty.

## Test this fifth, in the destructive backup sequence

**These four rows do not merge; the saving is in running them in order.** Each needs a different install state, and two of them destroy the state the others need, so the order is the whole economy of this group.

1. Fresh install → [[TST-0291-Export-Button-Gating]]
2. Create a rider
3. [[TST-0293-Export-Round-Trip]] — export, producing the file the rest consume
4. [[TST-0298-Merge-Vs-Overwrite-Prompt]] — import over existing data
5. **[[TST-0437-Auto-Backup-Does-Not-Carry-Credentials]] — this row.** The uninstall is destructive, so it comes after every row that needs the populated install, and before the Clear Data row. Strava must be connected when the uninstall happens, or the check has nothing to prove.
6. [[TST-0295-Import-After-Wipe]] — Clear Data

**Anything that needs the pre-wipe state must finish before step 6.** TST-0295 clears app data, and nothing before it can be re-tested without rebuilding the install from step 1.

items.key: TST-0438 Multi-rider backup — export and restore as one round trip
items.name: Multi-rider backup — export and restore as one round trip
items.text:
**Precondition: a FAMILY-tier install with three riders**, each with their own sessions and favourites.

On iOS, Back Up All Riders in Settings → Data creates the file. After the wipe, which on iOS is deleting and reinstalling the test app, Restore from Backup in the same Data section restores it before any rider exists.

## Steps

1. **Export.** Export a device backup. The file contains all three profiles, and each session's `userId` matches the rider who created it — no cross-rider data bleed.
2. **Restore.** Wipe the device. Import that same backup. All three riders reappear with their own sessions and favourites intact.

*(partially automated: `BackupRoomDbTest.C3_export_with_multiple_riders_and_sessions` covers the multi-rider export shape and the F-series overwrite tests cover multi-rider restore; whole-file inspection and the actual device-wipe flow stay manual.)*

## Expect

- Step 1: the file holds all three profiles, and each session's `userId` matches the rider who created it: no cross-rider bleed.
- Step 2: all three riders reappear with their own sessions and favourites intact.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0439]] (step 2). Export and restore of the same file are one round trip, and restoring a file this run did not produce tests less than restoring the one it did.

The wipe in step 2 is destructive. Anything that needs the pre-wipe state must finish before it.

One tick no longer separates an export that loses a rider from a restore that loses one. Open the exported file before wiping if the tick fails, because that tells you which half was at fault.

## Steps heading added 2026-09-17

The numbered items had no `## Steps` heading, so the release test counted the whole check as one part and gave it one mark. With the heading each numbered item is its own part, and a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The items themselves are unchanged.

items.key: TST-0444 HRM state follows the rider across a user switch
items.name: HRM state follows the rider across a user switch
items.text:
## Setup

**User A has an HRM connected, User B has none configured.** One switch sequence covers all three steps. Both riders use the same connected trainer. On a Power workout the prompt offers Connect and Skip; an HR-Zone workout would hold the ride instead, so step 2 uses a Power workout.

## Steps

1. **Switching away resets.** Switch from A to B. On Android, tap the rider's name in the bottom bar on a phone or in the rail on a tablet, then tap B's card. On iOS, tap the rider's name, then **Switch rider**, and pick B.
2. **B is prompted.** Start a Power workout as B.
3. **Switching back reconnects.** Switch back to A the same way.

## Expect

- Step 1: B's heart-rate icon is faint grey, B's Heart Rate row reads *Not set up*, and heart rate reads 0, not A's reading.
- Step 2: "Connect Heart Rate Monitor?" appears.
- Step 3: the monitor reconnects by itself; its icon turns the bar's text colour.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0445]] (step 2) and [[TST-0446]] (step 3). All three are one A → B → A sequence with one heart-rate monitor, and each absorbed row needed the switch this row already performs.

One tick no longer separates a stale reading carried across the switch from a missing prompt or a failed reconnect. The first is the data defect — B's session would record A's heart rate — so name the step if the tick fails.

## Rewritten 2026-09-28

Steps 1 and 3 used to expect an empty slot and a green icon. Since FEAT-0130 an empty row reads *Not set up*, a not-set-up icon is faint grey, and a connected icon is in the bar's text colour ([[REQ-0224-TheTopBarDrawsAllFourEquipmentIconsAndOnlyAFailureIsInColour]]).

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.key: TST-0456 One test over Settings — the six categories, About, Hardware, and Appearance
items.name: One test over Settings — the six categories, About, Hardware, and Appearance
items.text:
Open Settings once and visit three of its six categories. Every step below is on the same screen.

iOS lays Settings out differently. Edwin accepted the iOS layout on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]), so on iOS test the **On iOS** steps below in place of the Android procedure. The step numbers match.

## Setup

Any rider. Open Settings from the navigation bar at the bottom on a phone, or the rail on a tablet; the gear that used to open it from the top bar is gone. A trainer bound for step 4, then forgotten to read the empty state.

## Procedure

1. **Six categories, as chips.** On a tablet, beside the app's navigation rail with Settings selected, and on a phone, Settings lists Appearance, Language, Hardware, AI Coach, Data and About as a strip of chips at the top, above the detail pane.
2. **About renders inline.** Settings → About. The About content — the Bluetooth and location blurb, Data Sovereignty, the Privacy Policy card, the Support & Contact card, the Current License card and the Version text — all render **inside the category**, with no navigation to a separate screen. Share Diagnostics is not here; it moved to Hardware in 2026-05-14.
3. **The About footer and the word *developer*.** Still on About: the **Developed in Ireland** footer is present. Wherever the copy names the app's authorship — the support cards and the licence card included — it says *developer*, never *maker*. This is wording rather than structure, which is why it is its own step: the cards can all be present and correct while the vocabulary has drifted.
4. **Hardware — the Preferred Smart Trainer row.** Settings → Hardware. The **Preferred Smart Trainer** row shows the connected device's name in its subtitle, followed by *"· change it in the Equipment Hub"*. With no trainer bound, the name reads *"No device assigned"* and the rest of the subtitle is unchanged. The row's only control is a **Forget** `OutlinedButton` (`SettingsScreen.kt:301-309`), greyed out when no trainer is bound and enabled when one is. The row matches the shape of Profile → Connected → Preferred HRM. There is no trainer *chooser* in Settings — only a way to drop the one that is bound.
5. **Appearance — the accent dialog and the paywall route.** Settings → Appearance. Tap the Accent Color swatch: the palette dialog opens, with Pro-locked swatches carrying a 🔒 glyph. **Tap a locked swatch and confirm it routes to the paywall.** That route leaves Settings entirely, which is why it is worded as its own step rather than folded into the dialog's appearance.

## On iOS

1. **One scrolling list.** On a tablet and on a phone, Settings is one scrolling list of app-level sections, among them Equipment, Appearance, Subscription, Language and About. The rider's own sections — Profile, Strava, intervals.icu and Data — are on the rider's Profile screen instead. There is no category rail and no chip strip.
2. **About opens its own view.** Settings → About → **About Your Trainer** opens a separate About view with the Bluetooth and location blurb, Data Sovereignty, the Current License card and Share Diagnostics. Privacy Policy is a link in the About section of Settings.
3. **The About footer and the word *developer*.** The About view ends with the **Developed in Ireland** footer, and wherever its copy names the app's authorship it says *developer*, never *maker*.
4. **Equipment — no trainer row.** Settings → Equipment. The section holds Check Trainer Compatibility, Bluetooth Diagnostics and Slope behaviour, and no Equipment Hub row. The trainer is chosen and forgotten in the Equipment Hub, opened from the equipment icons at the end of the top bar.
5. **Appearance — locked accents and the paywall route.** Settings → Appearance, as a FREE rider. The accent swatches sit in one row, and premium swatches carry a lock. **Tap a locked swatch and confirm it opens the paywall.**

## Expected results

- [android] Step 1: six categories, Appearance, Language, Hardware, AI Coach, Data and About, as chips at the top on the tablet and the phone. No second rail.
- [ios] Step 1: one scrolling list of sections, among them Equipment, Appearance, Subscription, Language and About. No rail or chip strip.
- [android] Step 2: the About content shows inside the category, with no separate screen.
- [ios] Step 2: About Your Trainer opens its own view with the About content.
- Step 3: the footer reads Developed in Ireland, and the copy says *developer*, never *maker*.
- [android] Step 4: the row names the trainer or reads *No device assigned*, then *· change it in the Equipment Hub*, with a Forget button. No trainer chooser.
- [ios] Step 4: Settings has no trainer row, and no trainer chooser.
- Step 5: a locked accent swatch opens the paywall.

## The Language category, corrected 2026-09-24

This check said Android Settings had five categories and left out Language. Language has been a category of its own since PHASE-014 (2026-05-01, `SettingsCategory.LANGUAGE` in `SettingsScreen.kt`), so a tester counting five would have failed correct code. Step 1 and its expectation now name six ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit]]).

## The subtitle question, settled 2026-09-22

The Hardware subtitle used to point at "the Workouts screen", where the Android equipment panel lived, while `AGENT_RULES.md` fixes **Equipment Hub** as the rider-facing name. PHASE-025 settled it by moving the equipment into the Equipment Hub on both platforms, and the shipped string now reads `%1$s · change it in the Equipment Hub` (`settings_hardware_trainer_subtitle_format`). Step 4 quotes that string.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0457-About-Inlined]] | About renders inside the category, with its six pieces | step 2 |
| [[TST-0639-About-Footer-And-Developer-Wording]] | the Ireland footer and the *developer* wording | step 3 |
| [[TST-0459-Hardware-Trainer-Info-Only]] | the Preferred Smart Trainer row, its subtitle and its Forget button | step 4 |
| [[TST-0461-Appearance-Accent-Dialog]] | the accent palette dialog and the paywall route from a locked swatch | step 5 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0457** — About navigating to a separate screen again would be a structural regression, and it now shares a verdict with the rail's layout.
- **TST-0639** — this is a copy check among four structural ones. *Maker* creeping back into the licence card is invisible in a verdict that says "Settings failed", so step 3 is worded separately and should be recorded separately.
- **TST-0459** — the Forget button is the only destructive control in this row, and the open naming question above is carried here rather than in its own note.
- **TST-0461** — the paywall route is a monetisation path leaving Settings; a locked swatch that silently applies instead of routing would give away a Pro accent, and that failure now reads as "the Settings test failed".

## Evidence (fill after running)

- A line per step, and for step 4 the subtitle exactly as it rendered.

## Changed 2026-09-27

Step 1 on Android expected a Settings rail of its own on a tablet. TASK-0959 replaced it with the chip strip at every width, which `SettingsScreen.kt` draws, and CHG-20260923 records it. The line now asks for the chips on both sizes. Found while project-os-cockpit's TST-0092 was tested; the check had no Android result for REL-0017 since its invalidation.

items.key: TST-0458 Seven taps opens Developer Settings, and Debug Workouts is inside it
items.name: Seven taps opens Developer Settings, and Debug Workouts is inside it
items.text:
The second step is what the first step is for, so they are tested in one go.

iOS uses a different gesture and no separate screen. Edwin accepted the iOS behaviour on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]), so on iOS test the **On iOS** steps below in place of the Android procedure.

## Procedure

1. **Seven taps.** On the About category body, tap the `Version X.Y.Z` text seven times. Developer Settings opens.
2. **Debug Workouts is there.** In Developer Settings, the "Debug Workouts" section is present, with its toggle switch.

## On iOS

1. **Three taps.** In Settings → About, tap the **Version** row three times. Developer sections appear inline in Settings, below About.
2. **Show debug workouts is there.** Among them, the **Developer · Workouts** section carries the "Show debug workouts" toggle.

## Expected results

- [android] Step 1: seven taps open Developer Settings.
- [ios] Step 1: three taps show the Developer sections in Settings.
- Step 2: the debug-workout toggle is there.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0113-Developer-Options]] | the Debug Workouts section and its toggle exist in Developer Settings | step 2 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0113** — a Developer Settings screen that opens but has lost a section now records as the same failure as a gesture that no longer opens it, and only the second of those blocks a rider's own debugging.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- Whether the gesture opened the screen, and what sections it contained.

items.key: TST-0462 Rider Setup dialog — open, palette, validation and cancel
items.name: Rider Setup dialog — open, palette, validation and cancel
items.text:
**Precondition: FAMILY tier with at least two existing riders**, so the colour picker has taken colours to grey out. From the rider picker, tap "Add Rider".

## Steps

1. **The dialog opens with a mode toggle.** Switch to Import, then switch back to Create new for the rest of the release test.
2. **Taken colours are excluded.** Open the Rider Color picker.
3. **Save validates.** Leave Name blank (and / or set FTP to 0) and tap Save. Then type in the field.
4. **Cancel on a dirty form guards.** With a name typed, tap Cancel. Tap **Keep editing** to stay in the dialog, then tap Cancel again and **Discard** to leave.
5. **Cancel on a clean form does not.** Re-open the dialog, touch nothing, and tap Cancel.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: a `[ Create new | Import from file ]` toggle. Import hides the form and Save, and shows a CloudDownload icon and "Choose file…".
- [ios] Step 1: the Add Rider sheet has an `Import from file…` button at the bottom, not a mode toggle.
- [android] Step 2: taken colours show at 30 % with an outline, not tappable. Hint: *"Greyed-out colours are already in use by another rider."* Default skips them.
- [ios] Step 2: colours other riders use are dimmed and can't be tapped. No hint.
- [android] Step 3: the Name / FTP row shows the error in its subtitle, the input in its error state. Typing clears it.
- [ios] Step 3: Save stays disabled until Name and FTP are both valid.
- Step 4: *"Discard new rider?"* with Discard and Keep editing.
- Step 5: it closes at once, with no prompt.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0468]] (step 2), [[TST-0465]] (step 3), [[TST-0464]] (step 4) and [[TST-0463]] (step 5). All five are the same dialog, opened once, and none of them creates a rider.

The order is load-bearing. Step 5 closes the dialog for good, so it goes last, and step 4 leaves through Discard rather than through Save.

[[TST-0466]] and [[TST-0467]] stay separate on purpose: both end in a saved rider, which changes device state and invalidates the two-rider precondition this test depends on.

One tick no longer separates a dialog that fails to open from one that opens and then mis-handles the palette, the validation or either cancel path. Four of the five steps have their own failure mode, so name the step number when the tick fails.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The five steps were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test read them as one part and could give the whole check only one mark. They now sit under `## Steps`, with one expectation each under `## Expect`, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.key: TST-0466 Save Creates + Selects
items.name: Save Creates + Selects
items.text:
Enter valid Name + FTP + Weight, tap Save. Verify the new rider is created, auto-selected, and the dialog dismisses; the flow proceeds to the workout-selection screen.

## Expect

- The rider is created and selected, the dialog closes, and Workouts opens.

items.key: TST-0467 Import from File
items.name: Import from File
items.text:
Switch to Import mode, tap `Choose file…`, pick a `.ytrider.json.gz`. On iOS, tap Import from file… on the Add Rider sheet instead. Verify the rider is imported and a toast confirms sessions count.

## Expect

- The rider is imported, and a toast confirms the number of sessions.

items.key: TST-0469 One Strava round trip on one rider — link, survive a restart, unlink
items.name: One Strava round trip on one rider — link, survive a restart, unlink
items.text:
In Profile → Connected on Android, or the Strava section of the rider's Profile on iOS, on a **PRO or FAMILY** rider with no Strava link.

## Steps

1. **The control lives on the rider profile.** Look for a Strava connection in Settings, then on the rider profile.
2. **The unlinked render.** Read the Strava row.
3. **The Switch opens a browser, not the Strava app.** Tap the Switch. On iOS, tap the Connect with Strava button.
4. **On return.** Complete the flow.
5. **The link survives a restart.** Fully close the app and reopen it.
6. **Unlinking is the same Switch, going off.** Turn the Switch off. On iOS, tap Unlink.

## Expect

- Step 1: Strava link and unlink are on the rider's profile; nothing in Settings offers a Strava connection.
- [android] Step 2: the orange "Connect with Strava" image leads the row, with a Switch on the right, off.
- [ios] Step 2: the orange "Connect with Strava" button is the section's only control; there is no Switch.
- [android] Step 3: Strava sign-in opens in Chrome, not the Strava app.
- [ios] Step 3: Strava sign-in opens in a Safari sheet, not the Strava app.
- [android] Step 4: the Switch is on, the subtitle reads "Connected — completed workouts upload automatically", and the image is unchanged.
- [ios] Step 4: the section reads Connected with a green tick, and Unlink replaces the button.
- [android] Step 5: the Switch is still on, with the connected subtitle.
- [ios] Step 5: the Strava section still reads Connected.
- [android] Step 6: it unlinks at once, with no confirmation; the Switch is off, the subtitle reads "Link your Strava account to auto-upload completed workouts", image unchanged.
- [ios] Step 6: Unlink brings back the Connect with Strava button at once, with no confirmation.

## Notes

*(TASK-0388)*

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0098]] (step 1), [[TST-0100]] (steps 3 and 4), [[TST-0104]] (step 3), [[TST-0101-Status-Persists-After-App-Restart]] (step 5) and [[TST-0470-Disconnect]] (step 6). All six describe one OAuth round trip on one rider, and nobody would complete the Strava authorisation six times to tick them separately.

Steps 5 and 6 were added later the same day. Two agents were briefed on this row at once, one finished first, and the second correctly backed out rather than overwrite — which left `TST-0101` and `TST-0470` unmerged until this was noticed. The overlap was a briefing error in [[TASK-0891-TakeTheUnambiguousMerges]], not a disagreement about the merge.

One tick no longer separates a control in the wrong place, an OAuth flow that opens the wrong thing, a token that does not survive a restart, and an unlink that does not take. **Step 5 is the one most worth writing down separately**, because a link that works until the app closes looks perfect during the release test and fails for every rider afterwards. Step 3 is the one worth writing down if it fails, because opening the Strava app instead of a browser silently breaks per-rider credentials rather than showing an error.

## Corrected — 2026-09-12

The linked state shows no second brand mark and no Disconnect button. This row used to expect a "Compatible with Strava" mark next to a muted `Disconnect` text button once the OAuth flow returned. `UserProfileScreen.kt:1038-1089` renders one `SettingsRow` whose `leadingContent` is `btn_strava_connect` unconditionally, and whose trailing slot holds a single `Switch` for a paid rider. Unlinking is that Switch going off, which is now step 6 of this row.

`compatible_with_strava.png` does ship in the APK, and no Kotlin file references it — it is never drawn in any state. That is [[ISS-0436-StravaBrandMarkShipsButIsNeverShown]], open, and whether Strava's brand guidelines require the mark when connected is the question it carries. Do not fix it from this row.

A FREE rider is out of scope for this check: `:1055` renders an Upgrade `Button` in place of the Switch, so there is no toggle to tap and no OAuth flow to start. [[TST-0471]] tests that path.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test read them as one part and could give the whole check only one mark. They now sit under `## Steps`, with one expectation each under `## Expect`, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

## iOS wording, 2026-09-24

Edwin decided on 2026-09-17 to accept the iOS layout where it differs from Android, and to give each check an iOS variant that names the iOS screen and the same underlying result (ADR-0007; [[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]). Since PHASE-025 the iOS app keeps Strava in the current rider's Profile, reached from the rider item in the bar or rail (`RiderProfileView`, `SettingsView.stravaSection`; [[TASK-0949-ProfileLivesUnderTheRider]]). Settings has no Strava section. It has no Switch: an unlinked rider sees the official Connect with Strava button, and a linked rider sees Connected with an Unlink button. The expectations above now name both, so the iOS test no longer asks for Android's Profile row ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit]]).

items.key: TST-0471 FREE-tier Strava row shows an Upgrade CTA
items.name: FREE-tier Strava row shows an Upgrade CTA
items.text:
On a FREE-tier rider with no Strava link, open Profile → Connected on Android, or the rider's Profile on iOS. (TASK-0388)

## Steps

1. **The Upgrade button replaces the toggle.** Read the Strava row's trailing slot.
2. **It routes to the paywall.** Tap it.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: a filled Upgrade button with a lock icon; no Switch and no Connect control.
- [ios] Step 1: "Auto-upload completed rides to Strava — available with Pro." above an "Upgrade to connect" button; no Connect control.
- Step 2: the paywall opens.

## Notes

*(partially automated: `LicensingManagerTest` covers FREE-tier resolution; the button rendering and the paywall navigation stay manual.)*

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0099]], which asked for the same lock icon and the same paywall route on the same row. TST-0099 named the control a "Link Account" button, which the screen has not had since the row became a Switch; the Lock icon it asked for is real and sits on the Upgrade button, so step 1 carries it.

One tick no longer separates a missing lock icon from a broken paywall route. Both are on one control, so name which half failed.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test read them as one part and could give the whole check only one mark. They now sit under `## Steps`, with one expectation each under `## Expect`, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

## iOS wording, 2026-09-24

Edwin decided on 2026-09-17 to accept the iOS layout where it differs from Android, and to give each check an iOS variant that names the iOS screen and the same underlying result (ADR-0007; [[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]). Since PHASE-025 the iOS app keeps Strava in the current rider's Profile, reached from the rider item in the bar or rail (`RiderProfileView`, `SettingsView.stravaSection`; [[TASK-0949-ProfileLivesUnderTheRider]]). Settings has no Strava section. It has no Switch: an unlinked rider sees the official Connect with Strava button, and a linked rider sees Connected with an Unlink button. The iOS FREE rider sees "Upgrade to connect" only while unlinked, so the release test reads this row as a rider with no Strava link. The expectation above now names both platforms ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit]]).

items.key: TST-0474 Open in Strava pill (unknown activity id)
items.name: Open in Strava pill (unknown activity id)
items.text:
On an uploaded session with no `stravaActivityId` yet, the pill reads `Open in Strava` (same solid orange). Tap opens the athlete training feed instead of a specific ride. *(TASK-0388)*

## Expect

- The pill reads `Open in Strava`, solid orange, and opens the athlete's training feed, not a specific ride.

items.key: TST-0475 A failed upload — how it gives up, and the Retry pill that follows
items.name: A failed upload — how it gives up, and the Retry pill that follows
items.text:
The failure has to be manufactured before the pill can be read, so the steps run in this order.

## Procedure

1. **Make it fail, and watch it stop trying.** With an upload in flight and the `Uploading…` pill visible, kill WiFi. Within about 10 minutes — three WorkManager retries with exponential backoff — the pill flips to `Retry`. It must not hang in `Uploading…` forever, which is what ISS-0112 was.
2. **The Retry pill.** With Strava linked and the upload failed, the pill reads `[⚠ Warning] Retry`, white with an orange border.
3. **Retry works.** Reconnect and tap the pill. The upload is re-queued, the pill flips to `Uploading…`, and the upload completes.

## Expect

- Step 1: within about ten minutes the pill flips to `Retry`. It never hangs on `Uploading…`.
- Step 2: the `Retry` pill is white with an orange border and a warning icon.
- Step 3: the pill flips to `Uploading…`, and the upload completes.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0482-Upload-Timeout-ISS-0112]] | the WiFi-kill timeout path and the reconnect-and-retry completion | steps 1 and 3 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0482** — the timeout is the ISS-0112 regression guard and the pill is a rendering check; they now share a verdict, so a spinner that hangs forever and a pill with the wrong icon are recorded identically.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- How long the pill took to flip after WiFi went down, and whether the retry completed.

items.key: TST-0477 Backlog row — upload-all flow
items.name: Backlog row — upload-all flow
items.text:
With N unuploaded sessions for the linked rider, the Backlog row shows `N rides captured locally that haven't been uploaded yet…` + an `Upload all` OutlinedButton (Strava-orange border). Tap → Toast confirms `Queued N rides for Strava upload.`, each session's pill flips to `Uploading…`, and they complete (or WorkManager holds them for network). *(TASK-0388)*

On iOS the Strava section of the rider's Profile shows an **Upload N pending rides** button instead of the Backlog row, with no confirmation toast (`SettingsView.swift`). Edwin accepted it as the iOS equivalent on 2026-09-25 ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]], decision 19).

## Expect

- [android] The row reads `N rides captured locally that haven't been uploaded yet…`, with an `Upload all` button in a Strava-orange border.
- [android] The tap shows `Queued N rides for Strava upload.`, each ride's pill reads `Uploading…`, and the uploads complete.
- [ios] The section shows `Upload N pending rides`. The tap shows `Uploading…` on the button and on each ride's History pill.
- [ios] Each upload completes, and the button disappears once nothing is pending.

items.key: TST-0478 The Strava refresh row in both of its states
items.name: The Strava refresh row in both of its states
items.text:
One row, two titles, depending on how many ride links are unresolved. Test it with unresolved links first, then again once they have resolved.

## Procedure

1. **Unresolved links — the row counts them and offers Refresh.** On a rider with M unresolved ride links — legacy uploads, or activities the async processing missed — the row title reads `Ride links`, shows the count, and carries a `Refresh` OutlinedButton. Tap it: a toast confirms `Refreshing Strava ride links…`, a `matched sessionId=… → activityId=…` log line appears for each session resolved, and once the count reaches zero the title reverts to `Refresh Strava status`.
2. **Nothing unresolved — the row is still there.** With every uploaded session carrying its `stravaActivityId`, the title is `Refresh Strava status`, not `Ride links`, and the body reads *"Re-check uploaded rides against Strava…"*. Tap Refresh: the reconcile sweep runs, and any deletion it detects flips the corresponding history row back to `[☁] Strava`. The row being visible here is the whole point — before TASK-0400 it was hidden when there was nothing to update, which left no entry point for deletion detection at all.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: `Ride links` with the count and Refresh. Refresh logs `matched sessionId=… → activityId=…` per ride, then the title reads `Refresh Strava status`.
- [android] Step 2: the row is still there as `Refresh Strava status`, its body reads *"Re-check uploaded rides against Strava…"*, and Refresh turns a ride deleted on Strava back to `[☁] Strava`.
- [ios] Step 1: one `Refresh Strava status` button, no `Ride links` count; the tap turns waiting rides' History pills to `View on Strava`.
- [ios] Step 2: the button is still there, and the tap detects a ride deleted on Strava.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0479-Ride-Links-Row-Refresh-Flow]] | the `Ride links` title, the count, and the refresh flow that clears it | step 1 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0479** — the two states are the same row rendering differently, so a title that has stopped switching now fails the same verdict as a refresh that does nothing; the evidence has to say which state was wrong.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- The row's title and body in each state, and the log lines from each Refresh.

## iOS equivalent, 2026-09-25

iOS has one **Refresh Strava status** button in the Strava section of the rider's Profile, always shown while Strava is linked. It re-links uploaded rides that lack their activity and detects rides deleted on Strava (`SettingsView.swift`, `StravaService.reconcileMissingActivityIds` and `reconcileDeletions`). Edwin accepted it as the iOS equivalent of the two-state row on 2026-09-25 ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]], decision 19). The iOS lines under Expected results say what to look for.

items.key: TST-0480 Coming back to the app checks a connected rider's Strava ride links
items.name: Coming back to the app checks a connected rider's Strava ride links
items.text:
With a rider who connected Strava, background Your Trainer (Recents → swipe to another app, or Home), wait at least 30 s, then bring it back to the front and watch logcat for about 30 s. Do not tap anything. *([[TASK-0973-StravaRideLinksAreCheckedAgainForAConnectedRider|TASK-0973]])*

## Expect

- Within about 5 s, with no tap, the log shows `StravaUpload: reconcile`: `N session(s) need activityId resolution` or `done, matched=0 / 0`.

## Rewritten 2026-09-26

This check expects the automatic ride-link check again. Connecting Strava is the rider's standing consent for automatic reads of their own data (`tools/instructions/AGENT_RULES.md`, "No silent network calls", as Edwin corrected it on 2026-09-26), so the check that TASK-0400 added is allowed, and Edwin asked for it back. For one day, 2026-09-25 to 2026-09-26, this check expected the opposite: [[TASK-0964-StravaIsCalledOnlyWhenTheRiderAsks|TASK-0964]] had removed the check under the earlier wording, which said every request needed a tap.

A rider who has not connected Strava gets no check. That is pinned by `StravaRideLinksAreCheckedForAConnectedRiderTest`, not tested here, because the PRO test that carries this check has one rider.

On iOS the check is not built yet. iOS checks ride links only from the Settings tap, and the gap is a MISSING row in `PARITY_MATRIX.md` B.1.

items.key: TST-0483 Post-restore reconciliation (ISS-0142)
items.name: Post-restore reconciliation (ISS-0142)
items.text:
Restore a rider backup that contains uploaded sessions, with Strava connected. Pick the rider and watch logcat. Do not tap Refresh. *(ISS-0142, [[TASK-0973-StravaRideLinksAreCheckedAgainForAConnectedRider|TASK-0973]])*

## Expect

- With no tap, the log shows `StravaUpload: reconcile — N session(s) need activityId resolution`, then `matched sessionId=… → activityId=…` lines.
- Those rides' History rows change from `Open in Strava` to `View on Strava`.

## Rewritten 2026-09-26

Picking a rider who connected Strava checks their ride links again. Edwin corrected the network rule on 2026-09-26: a connected account is standing consent for automatic reads of the rider's own data. For one day this check reconciled from the Refresh tap instead, because [[TASK-0964-StravaIsCalledOnlyWhenTheRiderAsks|TASK-0964]] had removed the rider-select check; TASK-0973 restored it. On iOS the check is not built yet: iOS reconciles only from the Settings tap, and the gap is a MISSING row in `PARITY_MATRIX.md` B.1.

items.key: TST-0484 Deletion detection (ISS-0125)
items.name: Deletion detection (ISS-0125)
items.text:
Delete an activity on Strava's web UI for a session your device has uploaded. Tap Refresh in the Strava section of the rider's Profile. Picking the rider no longer reconciles ([[TASK-0964-StravaIsCalledOnlyWhenTheRiderAsks|TASK-0964]]). Verify logcat emits `reconcile — detected deletion of sessionId=…` and the corresponding history row flips from `View on Strava` back to the white `[☁] Strava` upload pill. *(ISS-0125)*

On iOS, tap **Refresh Strava status** in the Strava section of the rider's Profile. iOS writes no such log line; the deleted ride's History row shows the **Upload to Strava** pill instead (`StravaService.reconcileDeletions`). Edwin accepted this as the iOS equivalent on 2026-09-25 ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]], decision 19).

## Expect

- [android] The log shows `reconcile — detected deletion of sessionId=…`, and that ride's pill turns from `View on Strava` back to the white `[☁] Strava`.
- [ios] That ride's History row shows the `Upload to Strava` pill instead of `View on Strava`.

items.key: TST-0642 Garmin Connect accepts an exported FIT (ISS-0387)
items.name: Garmin Connect accepts an exported FIT (ISS-0387)
items.text:
Complete a ride, export the session as FIT, and upload the file to Garmin Connect at <https://connect.garmin.com/modern/import-data>. The import must succeed and the activity must open as an indoor cycling ride with power, heart rate and cadence present.

The defect this guards is a file missing its `lap` and `activity` messages, which Garmin rejected outright with *"This file is not supported for the .fit format"* while Strava and intervals.icu accepted the same file. Run the same upload from an iOS export as well — the two encoders are separate implementations and only a real upload distinguishes them.

[[TST-0643]] asserts the messages are in the file on every build. It cannot assert Garmin's importer is happy with them, which is why this check exists and has to be discharged by hand once. Neither can the Garmin SDK: it decodes the *pre-fix* file cleanly and reports `checkFileIntegrity: OK`, so a green decode says the file is well-formed and says nothing about whether the service will take it.

## Expect

- Garmin Connect accepts the file, and it opens as an indoor cycling ride with power, heart rate and cadence present.

## Partial evidence already in hand, 2026-09-02

The rider's own ride, re-encoded through the fixed encoder, **was accepted by Garmin Connect**. The same bytes before the fix were refused twice — once on type without an extension, once on validation with one. So the encoder half of the fix is proven on real rider data, and the `DEVELOPMENT` manufacturer is proven acceptable to Garmin.

**This check is still open**, because that file was built by a test harness and uploaded from a desktop. What remains is the rider's actual path: finish a ride on a device with the new build, tap **Export FIT**, share it, **check the filename that lands** (it must end `.fit`), then upload. The share half — `EXTRA_TITLE` on `ACTION_SEND` — is not a documented contract and has only unit coverage, so it is exactly the half a real device pass is needed for.

**A ready-made pair sits in `docs/issues/evidence/`** — the same synthetic ten-minute ride through the old and the new Android encoder:

- `ISS-0387-android-export-after-fix-2026-09-02.fit` — **upload this one first.** It is the post-fix encoder's output with a correct extension and the full message set. Accepted means the rider is unblocked by the next release; refused means something beyond the two known defects is at work.
- `ISS-0387-android-export-before-fix-2026-09-02.fit` — the same ride through the old encoder, for contrast.

**Do not read the error text as a diagnosis.** Garmin returns *"We don't support the file type you tried to import"* for validation failures as well as for genuinely unsupported types — its own forums show it on files that plainly carry a `.fit` extension. The message tells you it failed, not why.

If the after-fix file is refused, the next suspect is the `manufacturer` field: the encoder writes `DEVELOPMENT` (255) with serial `12345`, and Garmin's developer forum carries recurring (unconfirmed) reports that Connect rejects FIT without a registered manufacturer.

Uploading both is the whole check, and it is also the experiment: a refusal of the first is what proves the diagnosis rather than merely being consistent with it. **If the before-file imports fine, the diagnosis is wrong and ISS-0387 should be reopened** — the fix would still be correct, but it would not be the fix for this rider's problem.

## The share half was run on 2026-09-05, and it failed

Edwin exported a ride on the tablet (build 2.1.8 / versionCode 182, which contains the TASK-0802 fix) and saved it to Google Drive. The file landed as `Your Trainer Ride <date>_<time>` — **no `.fit`**. Exactly the half this check warned was untested.

Cause and fix are [[ISS-0393-DriveNamesTheSharedFitFromTheSubject]] and [[TASK-0805-ShareSubjectIsTheFilename]]: Drive names the saved file from `EXTRA_SUBJECT` and ignores the `EXTRA_TITLE` TASK-0802 relied on. The subject is now the filename.

**This check stays open, and its device leg has to be re-run on a build containing TASK-0805.** The sequence is unchanged: finish or open a ride, tap **Export FIT**, **Save to Drive**, confirm the saved name ends `.fit`, then upload it at <https://connect.garmin.com/app/import-data>.

Worth capturing on the same run: which apps the share sheet offers. The declared type narrowed to `application/vnd.ant.fit` in TASK-0802 and nobody has looked at a real share sheet since.

## The rider ran the whole path on 2026-09-08 and Garmin took the file

> "I tested the FIT file export and it imported into Garmin without any issues." — Paul Evans, 2026-09-08

This is the leg the check has been open for: a real ride, exported from a device on a released build, uploaded by the rider to the real service, accepted. Every pass before it was a synthetic file, a desktop upload, or both.

**The file itself is in the repo** at `docs/issues/evidence/ISS-0387-rider-export-accepted-by-garmin-2026-09-08.fit`, and decoding it confirms it is this app's output rather than something Garmin re-exported: `manufacturer` 255 (`DEVELOPMENT`), `serial_number` 12345, 1800 record messages over a 30-minute ride, `sport` 2 / `sub_sport` 6, and **one `lap` and one `activity` message present** — the two the defect was the absence of. The filename Paul's export produced was `Ride_20260907_1755.fit`, which answers the share-half question this note asked separately: the extension survived.

**One question stands before the mark moves.** Nobody has established which app version he exported from. v2.1.8 (versionCode 185) is the build carrying both the missing-messages fix and TASK-0805's filename fix, and it reached Play on 2026-09-06 — two days before the mail, which is tight enough to be worth asking rather than assuming. His 2026-09-02 report of the same export failing makes the inference a strong one, and it is still an inference. **Ask him the version; on 2.1.8 or later this check is discharged.**

Decoding the file also turned up a defect nobody had reported — the session's work field carries kilojoules where FIT defines joules, and iOS omits the field entirely ([[ISS-0420-TotalWorkIsWrittenInKilojoulesIntoAJoulesField]]). It does not affect this check: Garmin accepted the file, and Garmin derives work from the power stream rather than that field.

items.key: TST-0647 The HR-Zone terrain draws the same bands the controller drives
items.name: The HR-Zone terrain draws the same bands the controller drives
items.text:
## What automation already covers

`HrZonesTest` (Android) pins the drivable band values at a known LTHR and asserts they equal `HrZoneLockController.getZoneBounds`. `HrZoneTerrainBandsTests` (iOS) pins the same values and asserts a heart rate at a zone's midpoint maps into that zone's strip. Both were seen red against the old table and mapping.

**What they cannot cover** is that the *renderers* use them. Both are Compose/SwiftUI Canvas drawing; there is no seam a unit test can read a drawn rectangle through. That is what this check is for, and it is why the check exists rather than being folded into the suites.

## The release test

Use a rider whose LTHR is not a round fraction of Max HR — set **Max HR 185** and an explicit **LTHR 162** — because a mismatch is invisible when the two happen to agree.

1. Start an HR-Zone workout containing a **Z2** interval.
2. Read the bpm range printed against the zone target. For this rider it must be **129–144**.
3. Look at the Z2 stripe in the terrain. Its edges must be the same two numbers — the stripe must not sit lower than the label, which is the ISS-0394 symptom.
4. Ride until HR settles inside Z2 around **136 bpm**. **The trace must sit inside the Z2 stripe**, and be drawn in the Z2 colour rather than the below-floor blue or above-ceiling red.
5. Let HR drift above 144 and confirm the line turns red at the same bpm the stripe's top edge sits at.
6. Repeat on the **free ride** HR-zone screen, which is the other renderer (`GrowingProfileGraph` on Android).
7. Repeat both on iOS.

## Start cold — the warm-up leg

**Test this before step 1, from a resting heart rate, not from a rider already in zone.** Its absence from the first version of this check is why [[ISS-0396-HeartRateInvisibleBelowZone1]] shipped: every step above starts with HR inside a band, so nothing ever looked below Z1, and the whole warm-up climb was being drawn off the bottom of the canvas.

1. Begin the ride with HR at rest — for this rider, somewhere in the 60s or 70s.
2. **The trace is visible immediately.** Below Z1's floor (113 bpm here) it is drawn in the compressed band that occupies the bottom 15% of the terrain, spanning `0.45 × LTHR` up to Z1's floor — **73 to 113 bpm** for LTHR 162.
3. **The climb moves.** As HR rises from about 90 to 113 the trace should travel roughly 9% of the canvas height. A trace that sits still, or is absent, is the ISS-0396 symptom returning.
4. **Below 73 bpm it clamps to the bottom edge** rather than disappearing. Above Z5's ceiling it clamps to the top, and the red above-ceiling colour is what signals the overshoot — there is deliberately no mirrored band up there.
5. **The band is labelled `<Z1`, not `Z0`.** The FEAT-0090 seven-zone display scheme has no Z0; its Z1 already starts at 0% LTHR, so a `Z0` label would contradict the Profile zone panel.
6. **Six bpm boundary labels run down the left edge**, zone names down the right, on both platforms. Android skips a label when two boundaries are closer than 30px (Z2/Z3 at 144 and Z3/Z4 at 150 collide at LTHR 162); iOS has equal-height strips and skips nothing. Each label must read the same number as the zone target printed for that band.
7. Test it on both renderers and both platforms, as above.

*Added 2026-09-06 after `CHG-20260905-SubZone-Band-And-Boundary-Labels`. The Android test recorded as a pass in the working ledger that day did include this leg — Edwin confirmed it the same day — so the pass covers the amended text and not only the original seven steps.*

## Expect

- From rest, the trace shows at once, in the bottom band from 73 to 113 bpm. The band is labelled `<Z1`, not `Z0`.
- As HR climbs from about 90 to 113, the trace rises about 9% of the height.
- Below 73 bpm the trace sits on the bottom edge. Above Z5 it sits on the top edge, in red.
- The Z2 target reads 129–144, and the Z2 stripe has the same two edges.
- At about 136 bpm the trace sits inside the Z2 stripe, in the Z2 colour.
- Above 144 the line turns red at the stripe's top edge.
- [android] Six bpm labels run down the left edge, zone names down the right, each matching its band's target. One may be skipped where two collide.
- [ios] Six bpm labels run down the left edge, zone names down the right, each matching its band's target. None is skipped.
- The same holds on the Zone Ride screen.

## What a failure looks like

Stripe edges that do not match the printed range mean a renderer is still reading its own table. A trace in the wrong stripe while the edges are right means the axis mapping is wrong, not the bands — on iOS that is `bandFraction`, on Android `bpmToY`.

## Settled — 2026-09-06

> [!note] Edwin, 2026-09-06
> It is acceptable.

The unequal Android band heights read acceptably; no design follow-up is owed. The question below stays in the release test as a prompt for the next reader, but it has an answer now and a re-test does not need to re-open it.

## Also confirm, because it changed

Android bands are drawn bpm-proportionally, so on the LTHR axis they are **no longer equal heights**: Z1 is the tallest and Z3 the shortest. That is intended (Z3 really is ~6 bpm wide here) but it is a visible change, and this is the moment to say whether it reads acceptably or wants a design follow-up. iOS keeps five equal strips, so the two platforms will look different side by side — a known, recorded divergence, not a defect.

## Not covered here

The seven **display** zones on the Profile panel and in post-ride time-in-zone. Those are a different table on purpose, and they legitimately differ from the drivable bands at Z1 and Z5.

## A feature check since 2026-09-29

This check came from a fixed defect, and its Expect lines also say how the cockpit looks now. FEAT-0131 redrew that part on phones, so it carries `kind: feature` and was reopened (`TESTING.md`, "When to invalidate"; [[CHG-20260929-The-Cockpit-Fits-Every-Screen-And-The-Terrain-Keeps-Its-Share]]).
