*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Expect

- Step 1: the CSV export is locked and opens the paywall. No file is written.
- Step 2: the export writes a file that opens with the expected header row and one row per session.

items.name: The History stats card — the 28-day chart and the training overview above it
items.text:
Both halves live in the same expanded stats card, so one expansion reads both. Steps 1–3 need a rider with sessions spread across the last four weeks; steps 4 and 5 need riders with sparser histories, so plan which accounts to use before starting.

## Procedure

1. **The 28-day chart.** Open History and **expand** the stats card. The chart is in the expanded half, under the heading *Last 4 Weeks*. It has 28 day slots, each carrying **two bars side by side**: duration in minutes in the theme's primary colour, and energy in orange. The colour says which measure the bar is, not what type of workout it was. The left axis is ticked in minutes and the right in the rider's energy unit; the top-left axis label reads `min` and the top-right reads `kJ` or `kcal` to match Settings. A Monday marker line falls every seven slots, and the most recent day is drawn in the tertiary colour. Tap a slot — a detail line appears under the chart with that day's date, ride count, minutes and energy (`:1068-1080`). There is no metric selector; duration and energy are always both drawn and distance is not in the chart at all.
2. **A rider with no sessions sees no chart.** Not an empty one — `:627` wraps the heading and the chart together in `if (stats.dailyActivity.isNotEmpty())`, and the canvas returns early on an empty list at `:916`. Absent is the shipped behaviour.
3. **The This Week block.** Also in the expanded card, on a rider who rode in at least two of the last four completed weeks: a **This Week** block with one stat card each for rides, hours, distance, energy (kJ or kcal, following Settings), average power and best power. The first four show this week's figure large with the all-time figure beneath. Collapsed, the card carries the activity heatmap instead.
4. **The comparison line and the sign of the deltas.** The line under the heading reads *"compared to your 4-week average"*, and the deltas are signed the right way round — more training this week reads as positive.
5. **Suppression below the threshold.** On a rider who rode in **fewer than two** of the last four completed weeks, the *"compared to your 4-week average"* line is absent and every card renders its figure with no delta at all. `WorkoutHistoryScreen.kt:650-653` and `:670-715` both key off `stats.hasFourWeeks`, and `WorkoutHistoryViewModel.kt:690-698` defines it: the four complete weeks before this one, summed and **always divided by four**, with `hasFourWeeks` true when at least two of those weeks contain any ride.

## Expect

- Step 1: every slot draws a minutes bar and an energy bar against two axes. Tapping a slot shows that day.
- Step 2: with no sessions there is no Last 4 Weeks chart at all, not an empty one.
- Step 3: This Week shows cards for rides, hours, distance, energy, average power and best power.
- Step 4: the line reads "compared to your 4-week average", and more training this week reads as positive.
- Step 5: with fewer than two weeks of riding there is no comparison line and no deltas.

## Two things raised rather than asserted

**The average-power card's halves disagree.** Its hero value is `stats.avgPower`, the all-time average (`:710`), while its delta is `thisWeek.avgPower - fourWeekAvg.avgPower` — a this-week number under an all-time headline. The best-power card is all-time in both halves. Whether that is intended is Edwin's call, so this row does not claim either reading is correct.

**TSS is not on this card.** It appears in History per session, in the session detail's training-metric row (`:1825`), alongside IF and VI.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0620-History-Training-Overview-Card]] | the This Week block, the four-week comparison line, and the suppression case | steps 3–5 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0620** — the chart and the overview are different computations in one card, and the suppression threshold in step 5 is the subtle one; a delta shown to a rider with one week of data now fails the same row as a chart with the wrong axis label.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- Screenshots of the expanded card for each rider used, and the delta values read off step 4.

items.name: Session detail — the HR-zone bars, the lap splits, and what is absent when the data is
items.text:
Steps 1–2 read one session: a completed multi-lap route ride taken with an HRM. Steps 3 and 4 each need a different session, so pick them before starting.

## Procedure

1. **The HR-zone bars.** Find the **HR Zones** column in the session detail. Five horizontal bars, labelled Z1 to Z5, one per zone, each in that zone's muted colour from `ZoneColorUtils.getHrZoneColor`. Each bar carries **whole minutes**, suffixed `m`. The bars are **not stacked and carry no percentages**: each bar's length is its own time as a fraction of the largest zone's time, so the longest zone always fills its row. The minutes across the five bars account for the session's HR-covered time. Five zones is correct and not an oversight — FEAT-0090 makes Z6 and Z7 display-only, and the drivable Z5 already merges icu's Z5 and Z6 into 100–105 % LTHR.
2. **The lap splits.** A lap-splits table lists one row per completed lap, with its time.
3. **A single-lap session shows no lap-splits table.** Not an empty table — no table. Open a single-lap session and confirm the table is absent.
4. **A session with no HR data shows no HR Zones column.** Not five empty bars, and not an empty axis — the column is not rendered. `:1846` computes `hasHrZones` as "any zone has non-zero time" and `:1887` renders the column only when that holds, so a power-only session shows Peak Power with nothing beside it.

Steps 3 and 4 are the two absent-data cases and are numbered separately: they are different conditions on different widgets, and each is the kind of check that passes by accident when the widget above it is broken.

The NP/TSS/IF/VI grid is covered by TST-0414 and the peak-power row by TST-0416. TST-0557 covers the zone calculation as a unit test; nothing automated looks at the rendering.

## Expect

- Step 1: HR Zones shows five bars, Z1 to Z5, in whole minutes, unstacked and with no percentages.
- Step 2: a lap table with one row per completed lap, with its time.
- Step 3: a single-lap session shows no lap table at all.
- Step 4: a session with no HR data shows no HR Zones column at all.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0622-HR-Time-In-Zone-Bars-Render]] | the five zone-coloured bars, their minutes, and the absent column without HR | steps 1 and 4 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0622** — the zone chart and the lap table are independent widgets that happen to share a screen, so a zone chart drawn with the wrong unit now records as the same failure as a missing lap table; the two absent-data cases are kept as steps 3 and 4 for the same reason.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- The five bar labels and values, and a note for each of steps 3 and 4 saying what was present or absent.

items.name: A ride says where its power was measured, and a best set on the pedals still ranks beside one set on the trainer
items.text:
A ride now records whether its watts were measured at the pedals or at the trainer. The field exists to serve one decision: **a change of power source does not break personal-best lineage**, the way a change of physics version does. A rider who buys pedals keeps one list of bests rather than gaining a second one, and the marker on the ride lets them judge the comparison for themselves.

That is a first value, and it is Edwin's to change. So it needs a check that shows what the current answer looks like on screen.

Test on **both platforms**.

## Setup

Developer Options: "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)" on, as the trainer. "Show debug workouts" on, for the two-minute **[Debug] ERG Verify** workout used in steps 4 to 6.

On Android, use an awake KICKR in Power Source with the fake trainer in Smart Trainer. The KICKR only reports the watts you pedal; nothing controls it. On iOS, turn on **Use mock trainer** in Settings → Developer · Trainer, fully restart, then choose **Mock Power Meter** in Power Source beside **Mock Wahoo KICKR** in Smart Trainer. The iOS mock replaces the app's entire Bluetooth provider, so a physical KICKR cannot join that mock trainer. Neither fixture is a pair of physical pedals.

A ride saved **before this release**, for step 3.

A rider with FTP set to 200 W and no personal best yet on [Debug] ERG Verify. No heart-rate strap connected during steps 4 to 6, so the workout's best is target adherence: the share of the ride spent within 5 % of the target watts (REQ-0130).

The iOS build on a second device.

## Steps

### The marker in History

1. Ride ten minutes with the platform's separate power source in Power Source and save the ride. In History, expand it.
2. Open the Equipment Hub from the equipment icons at the end of the top bar, tap the Power row, then Forget this power source, and confirm. Ride ten minutes on the fake trainer alone and save. Expand that ride.
3. Expand a ride saved before this release.

### One best across power sources

4. With the separate power source in Power Source, ride [Debug] ERG Verify to its end and save it. On Android, pedal the KICKR at least 20 % above every target, so almost none of the ride is within 5 %.
5. Forget the power source from the Power row in the Equipment Hub. Ride the same workout to its end on the fake trainer alone and save it. Read the personal-best result on the completion screen.
6. Put the separate power source back in the Power row in the Equipment Hub. Ride the same workout to its end and save it. On Android, hold each target within 5 % on the KICKR. Read the personal-best result.
7. Open Personal Bests. Open the workout's best, then tap **View session**.

### Both platforms

8. Repeat on the other platform, and read the two History screens together.

The iOS mock proves that a separately bound Cycling Power source stamps the History marker and shares personal-best lineage with trainer power. It does not prove a physical KICKR's Bluetooth connection or real pedal behavior; those remain with TST-0652's hardware checks and exception. On iOS the mock's watts cannot be steered, so steps 5 and 6 may rank either way; the expectations below hold regardless.

## Expect

- Step 1: the ride reads **"Power measured at the pedals"**, in the rider's language.
- Step 2: **no source line at all**. That is the design, not a miss.
- Step 3: no source line. The app does not guess what measured it.
- Step 4: the ride runs to its end and saves.
- Step 5: the completion screen reports better, equal or worse against the separate-source best, **never a first best**.
- Step 6: compared with the existing best the same way, never as a first best. The rule has no direction.
- Step 7: **one best for this workout**, not split by source, none retired. Its session shows the pedals line, or none for trainer power.
- Step 8: the same sentence, translated, and the marker in the same place.

## Not this check

- That the source is recorded, and that the FIT export's second device record still imports: [[TST-0652-PedalsInThePowerSlot]].
- The physics-version lineage rule: TST-0636.
- The History trophy, PBs filter and delete promotion over three improving rides: [[TST-0321]]. On Android, steps 4 to 6 produce those three rides.

## What a failure means

A step 5 or step 6 ride reported as a first best means somebody made the power source part of the lineage key. That is the opposite of the decision. It is also the shape TST-0636 asserts for the physics version: the two cases look alike in the code and were deliberately answered differently.

A missing "View session" path in step 7 leaves the rider a shared list and no way to see why one entry is not comparable. That is worse than either clean answer.

## Notes

- Step 2: a source line on every ride would be noise.
- Step 7: the path from best, to ride, to marker is the whole of what makes the shared ranking judgeable. If any link in it is missing, the decision becomes a silent lineage break rather than a visible one.
- Steps 4 to 6 on Android: the fake trainer reports random power between 100 and 250 W whatever the target (`BluetoothManager.observeMockIndoorBikeData`), so its adherence lands a few percent above zero. Pedalling far off target sets a lower first best, and holding target sets a higher last one, so each ride beats the one before.

## Provenance

Steps 2, 5 and 6 were reworded on 2026-09-28 for FEAT-0130, which made the power slot the Hub row titled *Power* and moved Forget into the details sheet the row opens. What the check asserts is unchanged, so it was not reopened.

Corrected 2026-09-17 after Edwin's decision in [[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]. The earlier steps asked for a "five-minute power best", which the app does not have: a Power workout's best is average heart rate, or target adherence without a strap (REQ-0130). The rewrite uses one workout's real best and checks that rides on either source are compared with it. Step 9 became step 8.

items.name: History's Share opens a past ride's celebration with the headline it had, and shares it from there
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies the Share entry in each ride's menu in History (DES-0005 section 4): it reopens that ride's celebration with the same headline and colours, and its Share opens the share picker.

## Setup

Any tier. A ride saved on this build whose headline you noted when it was saved, and a ride saved before this release. Importing Demo Data's `demo-dave` rider gives rides from before.

## Steps

1. In History, open the menu of the ride saved on this build.
2. Tap Share.
3. Tap Share on the celebration.
4. Close the picker, and tap Done.
5. Open the menu of a ride saved before this release, and tap Share.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: the menu offers Share.
- [ios] Step 1: Share is the first entry in the menu.
- Step 2: that ride's celebration opens, with the same headline and colours as when it was saved.
- Step 3: the share picker opens for that ride.
- Step 4: History shows again, where it was.
- Step 5: the celebration opens with a headline worked out from the ride, such as `Second ride this week`, or the ride's name.

## Not this check

- The share picker itself: [[TST-0689-TheCelebrationSharesTheRideAsAPictureInFourShapes]].
- Export FIT in the same menu, which keeps its PRO check: [[TST-0092-FIT-Export]].

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the iOS build: `history.share`, offered first by `HistorySessionAction.offered`, also on rides inside a thread, presenting `CelebrationView`. A ride saved before the celebration existed works out the facts that can still be worked out when it opens (TASK-1032). On Android the entry is [[TASK-1039-OnAndroidHistoryCanShareAPastRide]]: Share (`HISTORY_SHARE_TAG`, `ws_dropdown_share`) is first in `SessionItem`'s menu. It landed on 2026-10-10, and the `readiness_for` mark was removed.

items.name: AI Coach — Paid, Key Configured
items.text:
On Pro/Family tier with API key, verify question/answer flow works and "Copy AI Context" is shown. *(partially automated: AiCoachCardTest.paidWithKeyShowsCopyContext — actual AI response requires real API)*

## Expect

- A question gets an answer, and "Copy AI Context" is shown.

items.name: Coach answers cite the MCP training-load figures, not invented numbers
items.text:
**The app does not compute CTL, ATL or TSB, so there is no local figure to compare the coach's answer with.** The app sends the rider's per-day TSS totals for the last 90 days to the `training_load` tool on the MCP server and renders the `ctl`, `atl` and `tsb` it gets back into one line of the coach's context (`WorkoutAiService.fetchTrainingLoadSummary:902`, `buildDatedTssArray:492`, `formatTrainingLoadSummary:555`). The Training Overview card on History shows rides, duration, distance and energy — no training load at all (`WorkoutHistoryScreen.kt:545-615`), so it is not a cross-check. Whether the server's arithmetic is right belongs to the sibling `yourtrainer-mcp` repo, not to this row.

What this row still catches is the failure that matters: the coach making figures up. Test it as four checks.

**Preconditions.** A BYOK key configured, a PRO or Family seat, at least six weeks of history whose sessions carry a TSS, and the MCP toggle left on in Settings (`SettingsScreen.kt:560`). Open a session's detail and confirm the Training metrics row shows a TSS value (`WorkoutHistoryScreen.kt:1824`); a session with no TSS contributes nothing to the input.

## Steps

1. **The coach cites the three figures.** Ask the History coach about current form.
2. **The figures are self-consistent.** Read the CTL, ATL and TSB in that answer, and the form-state word the app appends.
3. **The figures disappear when the grounding does.** Turn the MCP toggle off in Settings and ask the same question again.
4. **The figures move with the work.** Ride a hard session, confirm its TSS in the session detail, then ask again.

## Expect

- Step 1: the answer gives CTL, ATL and TSB as numbers, not form in the abstract.
- Step 2: TSB is CTL minus ATL, within rounding. Form word: very fresh at 25+, fresh 10+, neutral above −10, fatigued above −25, else very fatigued.
- Step 3: the answer stops giving CTL, ATL and TSB as figures. **A confident number here is invented, and the check fails.**
- Step 4: ATL rises and TSB falls.

## Provenance

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.text:
With Your Trainer installed, hand it a route file from outside the app three times, once per format. Open the file from a Gmail attachment, from Drive, or from a file manager.

This is the Android incoming-share path registered with `ACTION_SEND`. The iOS app has an in-app Files importer but no incoming document or URL handler in the current project. Its ledger still owes this check; decide iOS applicability or add the receiving path before recording an iOS result.

## Steps

2. **FIT.** Same with a `.fit` attachment.
3. **TCX.** Same with a `.tcx` attachment.

- Step 1: Your Trainer is in the share sheet, and picking it opens the import summary.
- Step 2: the same for the `.fit`.
- Step 3: the same for the `.tcx`.

| `TST-0247` | 2 | A manifest that stopped claiming FIT now records the same result as one that stopped claiming GPX, so the tick cannot say which MIME type was dropped. |
| `TST-0248` | 3 | The same for TCX. Write the failing format next to the tick. |

items.text:
Open a system file manager (Files by Google + one third-party such as Solid Explorer or X-plore).

## Steps

1. For each of `.gpx`, `.fit`, `.tcx`, `.zwo`, `.ytw`, **tap the file** (or long-press → Open with…).
2. Pick Your Trainer for a Route format (`.gpx`, `.fit`, `.tcx`).
3. Pick Your Trainer for a workout format (`.zwo`, `.ytw`).
4. Repeat for a downloaded copy (`file://`) and a SAF / Drive copy (`content://`).

## Expect

- Step 1: "Your Trainer" is in the chooser.
- Step 2: picking it opens the route summary dialog.
- Step 3: picking it imports the workout directly.
- Step 4: downloaded (`file://`) and Drive (`content://`) copies both open.

## Notes

This is an Android Open-With and URI-handling check. The current iOS app imports files from its own Files picker and has no registered incoming document or URL handler. Its ledger still owes this check; settle iOS scope or supply that handler before attempting an iOS verdict.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.text:

This is the Android external Open-With and task-reuse path. The current iOS app has no incoming document or URL handler, and its app switcher does not test Android's `singleTask` behavior. Keep the iOS result unresolved until its scope or an iOS equivalent is decided.

items.name: A promo code validates and applies
items.text:
## Steps

1. Open the paywall and enter a valid promo code in the redeem field.
2. Force-stop and relaunch the app.
3. Enter an invalid code.
4. Enter an already-redeemed code.

## Expect

- Step 1: the code is accepted through the store, and the tier changes to the granted tier.
- Step 2: the granted tier survives the relaunch.
- Step 3: a message says what went wrong. It does not fail silently or seem to succeed.
- Step 4: a message says what went wrong. Nothing fails silently or seems to succeed.

## Provenance

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: Restore recovers an entitlement after a reinstall
items.text:
A purchase lives on the store account, not on the device. After a reinstall, or on a second device signed into the same account, the app asks the store for purchases as soon as it starts. The paid tier returns with no tap. Restore Purchase is the manual fallback, and it must still give a clear answer.

## Setup

- A store account holding a **real PRO or FAMILY purchase**: a Play test account on Android, a sandbox account on iOS. The debug tier override bypasses billing and would prove nothing here.
- Either uninstall and reinstall Your Trainer, or install it on a second device signed into that same account.
- A second store account with **no** purchase, for the last step.

## Steps

1. Launch the reinstalled app. Wait up to ten seconds, then read the tier in **Settings → About**.
2. Open the paywall from the **Upgrade to Family** button in Settings → About.
3. Tap **Restore Purchase**.
4. Force-stop the app and cold start it.
5. Sign in with the account that has no purchase, reinstall, open the paywall and tap **Restore Purchase** there.

## Expect

- Step 1: the paid tier, **PRO** or **FAMILY**, shows with no tap. A tier that stays FREE is a fail.
- Step 2: the paywall opens.
- Step 3: **"Purchase restored!"** appears, and the tier stays PRO or FAMILY.
- Step 4: the tier **survives the restart**. Reverting to FREE is a fail.
- Step 5: the app says plainly there is nothing to restore. It does not look failed or hang.

## Not this check

- Whether PRO survives the store being *unreachable*, and whether the app waits for the store before guessing: [[TST-0018-EntitlementResolution]].
- Whether the purchase completes: [[TST-0074-Purchase-Flow]].
- Which rider holds the seat after a reinstall: [[TST-0016-SeatResolutionAndArrivalStates]].

## Provenance

Covers [[FEAT-0011]].

Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20, one of the 44 rows that audit found uncovered. Written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms.

Rewritten 2026-09-06 into the Setup / Steps / Expect shape. The previous text sent the tester to "Settings → Subscription → Restore", which does not exist on Android — the control is **Restore Purchase** on the paywall screen (`PaywallScreen.kt:527`), and that error alone could have failed the check.

Corrected 2026-09-17 after Edwin's decision in [[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]. Step 1 used to expect FREE until Restore was tapped, which contradicted TST-0018. Android queries Play as soon as billing connects (`BillingManager.startConnection`), and iOS reads `Transaction.currentEntitlements` at launch, so a reinstall returns the paid tier with no tap. On iOS, Restore Purchase currently calls `AppStore.sync()` and shows no confirmation or "nothing to restore" message (`PaywallSheet.swift`); steps 3 and 5 record that as a fail if it persists.

items.name: PRO seat selection and hidden riders — the warned, irreversible choice, and what stays reachable afterwards
items.text:
## Purpose

The seat choice cannot be undone, so the warning surface is the only thing standing between a rider and a decision they will live with. This test exists to catch the failure where the logic is correct and the communication is not — which is the likely failure, since this half is copy and confirmation rather than code.

Manual because it is a judgement about whether a person understands what is about to happen. An instrumentation test can prove the dialog rendered; it cannot prove it was clear.

## Setup

Debug build. Use the tier override chips in Developer Settings (`dev_tier_override`) to move between FREE, PRO and FAMILY without Play. Real Play Billing rows are called out separately below and need the Play Console test track.

## Steps

1. **FREE, five riders.** On FREE, add riders until the cap. Verify each has its own history, PBs and FTP/HR settings, and that competitive sort chips, household ghosts and the leaderboard all still show locks. Verify the add-rider card at five shows a plain maximum-reached state and **not** an upgrade prompt — FAMILY grants no extra seats and offering one would be false. On iOS the Add Rider button disappears at five riders, and the Activate Family Leaderboard card that stays is not an upgrade prompt, because it offers no seats (accepted by Edwin, 2026-09-25).
2. **The warning.** With three riders, begin a PRO purchase. Before the purchase completes, verify the rider count, that PRO keeps one, that the others become inaccessible, and that nothing is deleted are all stated. Verify FAMILY is the presented default and PRO is still selectable.
3. **The chooser.** Verify each rider shows ride count, hours and last-ride date. Verify **nothing is pre-selected**. Verify the confirm step **names** the riders that will become inaccessible.
4. **After.** Verify the other riders are gone from the picker, sorts, ghosts, leaderboard and PB comparison — absent, not greyed. Verify the seat cannot be re-chosen anywhere in the app.
5. **Reachable data.** Settings → verify hidden riders can be exported and deleted, and that this is the only place they appear.
6. **Restore.** Upgrade via `pro_to_family` (real SKU, Play test track) and verify every hidden rider returns with history intact.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: each rider keeps their own history, PBs and FTP/HR. Sort chips, ghosts and leaderboard show locks. At five, a plain maximum-reached card, not an upgrade prompt.
- [ios] Step 1: each rider keeps their own history, PBs and FTP/HR. Sort chips, ghosts and leaderboard show locks. At five, Add Rider disappears; no card offers seats.
- Step 2: before paying, it plainly states the rider count, that PRO keeps one, the rest become inaccessible, nothing is deleted. FAMILY default; PRO selectable.
- Step 3: each rider shows ride count, hours and last-ride date. **Nothing is pre-selected.** The confirm step **names** the riders who become inaccessible.
- Step 4: the other riders are absent, not greyed, from picker, sorts, ghosts, leaderboard and PB comparison. The seat cannot be chosen again anywhere.
- Step 5: hidden riders can be exported and deleted here, and appear nowhere else.
- Step 6: every hidden rider returns with history intact.

## Pass criteria

A rider who has not read this document can state, before paying, how many riders they are about to lose and that they are recoverable. If that is not true the test fails regardless of whether the software behaved correctly.

## Levelled 2026-08-19 — `system` → `acceptance` (ISS-0213 / TASK-0507)

`level:` decides where a test appears, and this one said `system` while the note describes a person verifying rider-facing behaviour. The seat choice cannot be undone, so this verifies a warning surface — copy and confirmation, checked by a person looking at a screen.

`status:` goes to `active` and the verdict moves to `mark:` in the same edit — ADR-0031: an acceptance test rests at `active` and a runner-written `passing`/`ready` is not its verdict. The validator caught the half-migration immediately, which is the rule doing its job.

Safe to relevel because this note is **one procedure**, which is the shape ADR-0030 requires: one note, one check. `TST-0011`, `TST-0012` and `TST-0013` are the same kind of test in the *old* shape — 18, 15 and 107 checklist rows in one note each — and are left alone pending migration.

items.name: Cockpit slope-mode chip — Route and Free Ride
items.text:
Read the slope-mode chip on both ride types under each Slope behaviour setting. Steps 4 and 8 need a trainer that does not support FTMS SIM; the rest run on a SIM-capable one. On Android, set Developer Options → Trainer Capability Override (Debug) to "No simulation support" and reconnect the SIM-capable trainer for steps 4 and 8. On iOS, bring a real trainer without SIM support, because no debug setting removes it. Slope behaviour is in Settings → Hardware on Android and Settings → Equipment on iOS.

## Steps

1. **Route, `ERG`.** Settings → Slope behaviour → `ERG`. Start any Route ride. The grade line reads `GRADE 3.2 % · ERG` in subordinate gray, the chip appended directly to the grade text with a `·` separator.
2. **Route, `Resistance`.** The grade line reads `… · RES`.
3. **Route, `Auto` on a SIM-capable trainer — no chip.** Nothing is appended to the grade line. True SIM is the implicit default and stays unannotated.
4. **Route, `Auto` on a trainer with no SIM support.** The grade line reads `… · ERG (auto)` — the Route fallback.
5. **Free Ride, `ERG`.** Start a Free Ride from the Route tab. The slope `%` is the primary display with `ERG` rendered directly underneath in subordinate gray. A Column wraps the slope Row and the chip; the GEARS row stays a sibling beneath, so the primary / secondary stacking is preserved.
6. **Free Ride, `Resistance`.** The chip reads `RES`.
7. **Free Ride, `Auto` on a SIM-capable trainer — no chip.**
8. **Free Ride, `Auto` on a trainer with no SIM support.** The chip reads `RES (emulated)`, which is different from Route's `ERG (auto)`. That asymmetry is the thing to look at.

## Expect

- Step 1: the grade line reads `GRADE 3.2 % · ERG` in grey, the chip joined to the grade by a `·`.
- Step 2: the grade line reads `… · RES`.
- Step 3: no chip. Nothing is appended to the grade line.
- Step 4: the grade line reads `… · ERG (auto)`.
- Step 5: the slope `%` is the main display, with `ERG` in grey directly under it. The GEARS row stays beneath.
- Step 6: the chip reads `RES`.
- Step 7: no chip.
- Step 8: the chip reads `RES (emulated)`, not Route's `ERG (auto)`.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0141` | 5, 6, 7, 8 | The Route chip and the Free Ride chip share one result, so the two `Auto` fallbacks reading the same text — the exact regression the asymmetry guards against — records as one failure rather than showing up as a contradiction between two rows. |

Steps 3 and 7 are the negatives and keep their own named steps. A chip that renders under `Auto` on a SIM-capable trainer is a change nobody asked for, and it passes every positive step above.

items.name: HRM Disconnect Auto-Pauses HR Zone Ride
items.text:
Mid-ride on Zone Ride or HR-Zone structured workout, take HRM out of range / power it off. Verify the ride **auto-pauses** (timer freezes) within ~2 s. The HR display shows `--` with the passive label *"Heart-rate signal lost"* (red, no longer "tap to reconnect"). The middle item of the cockpit's bottom bar becomes **LINK HRM**, and **FINISH** stays beside it so you can save a partial session if needed. (TASK-0399 / ISS-0183.)

## Expect

- Within about 2 s the ride pauses and the timer freezes.
- HR shows `--` with *Heart-rate signal lost* in red, not "tap to reconnect".
- The bottom bar's middle item becomes LINK HRM, with FINISH beside it.

## Reworded 2026-09-30

Since FEAT-0132 LINK HRM and FINISH are items in the cockpit's bottom bar, not round buttons, and the old STOP label is gone ([[REQ-0236-TheCockpitsActionsAndTheRiderSitInABottomBarShapedLikeTheNavigationBar]]). [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]] reworded the button names; what the check asks is unchanged.

items.name: HRM Reconnect Resumes Through Button
items.text:
## Setup

Continue from [[TST-0180-HRM-Disconnect-Auto-Pauses-HR-Zone]]: an HR-Zone ride auto-paused because its heart-rate strap was switched off. Keep the strap to hand.

With ride paused via the previous row, power HRM back on. Wait ~10 s. Verify (a) the heart-rate icon, one of the four equipment icons at the end of the cockpit's top bar, is drawn in the bar's text colour again with no dot and no slash, (b) cockpit HR display picks up live samples, (c) the middle item of the cockpit's bottom bar turns from LINK HRM to RESUME. Tap RESUME and the ride continues. (TASK-0399 / ISS-0183.)

## Expect

- The heart-rate icon in the top bar is in the bar's text colour again, with no dot and no slash, and HR shows live samples.
- The bottom bar's middle item becomes RESUME. Tapping it continues the ride.

## Rewritten 2026-09-28

The icon used to turn green on reconnect. Since FEAT-0130 a connected device is drawn in the bar's text colour, and only a failed connect is in colour ([[REQ-0224-TheTopBarDrawsAllFourEquipmentIconsAndOnlyAFailureIsInColour]]).

## Reworded 2026-09-30

Since FEAT-0132 a heart-rate strap that is not connected is drawn faint grey with a slash, and RESUME is an item in the cockpit's bottom bar ([[REQ-0235-ADeviceThatIsNotConnectedIsDrawnWithASlashInTheTopBarAndEveryHubRow]], [[REQ-0236-TheCockpitsActionsAndTheRiderSitInABottomBarShapedLikeTheNavigationBar]]). items.name: HRM disconnect and reconnect, in both cockpit layouts
items.text:
**The disconnect is the expensive part, and the two cockpit layouts show it differently, so this needs one ride of each type.** Start with the HRM connected, then disconnect it mid-ride by moving out of range or turning it off.

## Steps

1. **HR-hero layout — "Heart-rate signal lost".** In an HR-Zone workout, heart rate is the centre hero. Disconnect the HRM mid-ride.
2. **Default layout — "tap to reconnect".** In a Power workout, heart rate is the left-hand metric. Disconnect the HRM mid-ride.
3. **Reconnect.** Tap that cell, then bring the HRM back.
4. **The ride does not notice.** Watch the workout timer, power and cadence through the whole disconnect and reconnect.

## Expect

- Step 1: HR reads "--", not frozen, over *Heart-rate signal lost* in red. The hero is not tappable; LINK HRM in the bottom bar reconnects.
- Step 2: the left metric reads *tap to reconnect*, underlined in the accent colour, and is tappable. Neither string shows in the other's layout.
- Step 3: it reads *reconnecting…* in amber, no longer underlined. Then HR updates again.
- Step 4: the workout timer, power and cadence keep running throughout.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0381]] (step 3) and [[TST-0382]] (step 4). Setting up an HRM and forcing it to drop is the costly part, and both absorbed rows hang off that one disconnect.

Both disconnect strings are kept. `ActiveWorkoutScreen.kt:1376` renders `workout_hrm_signal_lost` in the HR-hero layout and `:1448` renders `workout_hrm_tap_reconnect` in the default layout. Merging them into one expected string would let either layout render the other's copy and still pass.

One tick now covers two rides, one per layout. It no longer says which layout was at fault, nor whether the failure was the string, the tap target, or a ride that stalled while the HRM was away. Write down the step number and the workout type.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

## A feature check since 2026-09-29

This check came from a fixed defect, and its Expect lines also say how the cockpit looks now. FEAT-0131 redrew that part on phones, so it carries `kind: feature` and was reopened (`TESTING.md`, "When to invalidate"; [[CHG-20260929-The-Cockpit-Fits-Every-Screen-And-The-Terrain-Keeps-Its-Share]]).

## Reworded 2026-09-30

Since FEAT-0132 LINK HRM is an item in the cockpit's bottom bar, not a round button ([[REQ-0236-TheCockpitsActionsAndTheRiderSitInABottomBarShapedLikeTheNavigationBar]]). [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]] reworded step 1's button name; what the check asks is unchanged.

items.name: A number to reach and a direction to turn, in Power, HR-Zone and Route alike
items.text:
Test on **both platforms**.

## Setup

Developer Options on Android: under "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)", turn on "Fake a connected trainer", then fully quit and reopen the app. Set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to "Data-only — feature word reports no target bits"; it applies on the next connect.

On Android, do not use "Failure mode:" for this. That list only reaches the compatibility test's own mock (the "Run this test against a mock trainer (no hardware; ~15 s, not remembered)" checkbox), not the fake trainer the rest of the app connects to.

On iOS, turn on Use mock trainer in Settings → Developer · Trainer, set Mock trainer capability to Data-only and Mock failure mode to None, fully close and reopen the app, then connect the mock. The iOS mock capability picker changes the feature word the whole-app mock reports; it is separate from Mock failure mode.

Pedal the fake trainer through its power range, so the cue has something to react to.

A KICKR, or another trainer that accepts control, for the drivable leg (step 13). On iOS turn Use mock trainer off and restart before connecting it. Have the parity gallery captures open for comparison.

The iOS build on a second device.

## Steps

### Power workout

1. Start a structured Power workout and read the intensity row.
2. Ride under the target, then over it, and hold power on a boundary for a moment.
3. Read the centre column.
4. Start Quick Ride, the ERG free ride, and read the intensity row.

### HR-Zone workout

5. Start an HR-Zone workout and read the large number and the row beneath it.
6. Hold a power well away from the suggestion for two minutes, watching the suggestion.
7. Stop pedalling until power reads 0.
8. Time how often the suggestion changes, going up and going down.
9. Start Zone Ride, the HR-Zone free ride.

### Route and free-ride SIM

10. Start a route.
11. Start a free ride in SIM.
12. Look across every screen above for anything that suggests a speed.

### The drivable leg

13. Set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to "Off — the trainer's real answer", disconnect the fake trainer, connect the KICKR and repeat steps 1 to 12. Compare each screen against the gallery captures rather than from memory.

### The manual

14. Open the sibling site's *riding a bike the app cannot control* page, in English and in one other locale.

## Expect

- Step 1: the intensity row reads `TARGET 210 W` with an up, down or on-target cue. There is no `− 100% +` control.
- Step 2: the cue changes at ±5% and again at ±10%, without flickering on a boundary. The power number keeps its normal colour throughout.
- Step 3: the centre column is unchanged: current watts, w/kg, `AVG | MAX`, `TARGET: N W`.
- Step 4: Quick Ride is unchanged, with watts ± still there.
- Step 5: the large number is the rider's own power. The suggestion sits where the intensity row was, as a wattage with an arrow.
- Step 6: the suggestion stays near what the rider is doing. It does not walk down 309, 299, 289… as the controller's own target does.
- Step 7: the suggestion holds its last value rather than collapsing toward zero.
- Step 8: the suggestion changes no more often than every 20 s upward and every 10 s downward.
- Step 9: Zone Ride has the same design, and the zone selector is still present.
- Step 10: no gear control and no slope-mode chip, and the grade is still displayed. The rider's speed still responds to the gradient.
- Step 11: SLOPE ± is still present. The gear control and the chip are gone.
- Step 12: nothing anywhere suggests a speed.
- Step 13: on the KICKR the cockpit is as before this phase: gear control, slope chip, intensity percentage, and the pill's Applied and Predicted states.
- Step 14: the page describes what the data-only cockpits showed, and says plainly that the bike's wattage is an estimate.

## Not this check

- The pacer and the segment line: [[TST-0651-PacerGhostOnAndOff]]. A route on a data-only trainer has the pacer forced on, so the target in step 10 is the pacer's.
- How the app decides a trainer cannot be driven, and what the log says about it: [[TST-0648-DataOnlyDetectionOnAMockRefusingTrainer]].
- The same screens tested in one pass for consistency: [[TST-0653-DataOnlySixScreenWalk]].

## What a failure means

A suggestion in step 6 that drifts away from the rider's power means the transform is anchored to the controller rather than to measured power. That is the option-A design the review rejected. A cue that flickers in step 2 means the cause of the flicker that removed REQ-0072's bands was never found, only re-introduced.

## Notes

- Step 3: the target was deliberately not promoted to the large number, because the wattage is already on the profile bars.
- Step 7: the 800IC reports 0 W below about 100 W, so a rider stopping or easing off is the real case, not an edge case.
- Step 8: 20 s up and 10 s down is the controller's own cadence.
- The Expect lines were shortened on 2026-09-27 ([[TASK-0977-ShortenTheExpectLinesOfTheOwedChecks]]). Step 2's two lines became one, so the lines pair with the steps; neither assertion changed.

items.name: The rider is identifiable in every cockpit, and the bike on the terrain is theirs
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies DES-0003's token where it is hardest: on the terrain against ghosts and grade bands, in the free-ride cockpits that have no terrain marker, and while the ride runs. Since FEAT-0132 every cockpit ends in a bottom bar, and the rider sits in its left slot in every ride state: the rider's mark in their colour, with the name under it. START, PAUSE, RESUME or FINISH sit beside it. The hub-screen chip is asserted by [[TST-0666-TheNavigationContainerCarriesARiderThroughAWholeSession]].

## Setup

A phone on the release candidate; repeat steps 5 and 6 on a tablet. Two riders in the household: one in **Red**, one in **Orange**. The Red rider holds a personal best on a bundled route with a climb steeper than 12% (Alpe d'Huez will do), so a ghost in Red and a grade band in red are both on screen. Fake Trainer on. Restore a rider export made without a colour, or delete a rider's colour in a debug build, for step 1.

## Steps

1. Open the Riders list with the colourless rider present.
2. As the Red rider, pick the route with the steep climb and read the cockpit before START. Tap the rider in the bottom bar.
3. Press START and ride to the steep climb, with the Red rider's own personal-best ghost active.
4. Discard. Pick a structured HR-Zone workout and read the cockpit before START.
5. Discard. Start a Free Ride, then a Quick Ride, then a Zone Ride, reading the bottom bar before START. In one of them press START, then Pause.
6. Switch to the Orange rider and repeat step 2.

## Expect

- Step 1: the colourless rider has a colour no other rider holds. The picker greys the colours the others hold.
- [android] Step 2: bar: the Red rider's mark and name on the left, ignoring taps. Terrain: a plain bike in the mode's colour, its middle over the line.
- [ios] Step 2: title line: no rider. Bar: the Red rider's mark and name on the left, ignoring taps; START in the middle. Red terrain bike.
- [android] Step 3: the rider stays in the bar beside PAUSE and FINISH. The terrain bike is the mode's colour; the initialled ghost is its rider's.
- [ios] Step 3: the rider stays in the bar beside PAUSE and FINISH. The Red terrain bike stands out from the red band and the initialled ghost.
- Step 4: the HR-Zone terrain shows the rider before START, as the Power and Route terrains do.
- Step 5: in each, the rider on the bar's left, START beside it. The rider stays while pedalling, beside PAUSE and FINISH; after Pause, RESUME and FINISH.
- [android] Step 6: the bar's mark is Orange and names the Orange rider. The terrain bike keeps the mode's colour. The Red rider's ghost is Red.
- [ios] Step 6: the bar's mark and the terrain bike are Orange, and the bar names the Orange rider. The Red rider's ghost, if shown, is Red.

## Not this check

- The chip on the navigation item and the Riders list: [[TST-0666-TheNavigationContainerCarriesARiderThroughAWholeSession]].
- The bottom bar's items, the slashed equipment icons, and the bar in dark theme on a phone: [[TST-0680-NotConnectedIsSlashedAndTheCockpitBottomBarCarriesTheRiderAndTheActions]].
- The pacer's colour and behaviour: [[TST-0651-PacerGhostOnAndOff]].
- The rider card's own layout and attributes.

## Provenance

- 2026-09-30, [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]]: rewritten for FEAT-0132. The *Riding as* chip beside START is gone. The rider now sits in the left slot of the cockpit's bottom bar in every ride state, so steps 3 and 5 expect the rider while pedalling, where they used to expect none. Step 2 gains the tap on the rider, and step 5 expects FINISH while paused on both platforms, where it used to be iOS only ([[REQ-0236-TheCockpitsActionsAndTheRiderSitInABottomBarShapedLikeTheNavigationBar]]).
- 2026-09-29: [[TASK-1010-TheCockpitBarLosesTheCadenceButtonAndTheRiderMovesBesideStart]] moved the rider from the title line to a *Riding as* chip in the action row, and [[TASK-1011-EdwinsAnswersTheLapLineWrapsAndTheRidingAsLabelMovesLeft]] moved the chip to the row's left edge. Free rides showed no rider while pedalling, which Edwin accepted that day.
- 2026-09-22: step 4 used to leave the tester to look up which way [[ISS-0498-TheHrZoneTerrainHidesTheRiderBeforeStartWhilePowerAndRouteShowIt]] went. It was fixed that day by [[TASK-0956-TheTerrainMarkerWearsTheRidersColour]]: all three programmed cockpits show the rider at the start of the terrain before START. The expectation says so (TASK-0960, 2026-09-24).

items.name: On the smallest phone every cockpit shows its terrain above the bottom bar, every number is whole, and a tablet keeps its full size
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies that on the smallest supported phone each of the six cockpit modes keeps its terrain and shows every number whole, at the default and the largest text size, and that a tablet's cockpit keeps its full size. Since FEAT-0132 every cockpit ends in a bottom bar with the rider and the actions. The bar keeps one size on every screen, so the terrain's share is taken of the space above it.

## Setup

The release candidate on the smallest supported phone, and on Android a tablet for step 11. Both platforms have all six modes.

- On Android, use any phone or emulator and run `adb shell wm size 720x1280` and `adb shell wm density 320`, which gives a 360 × 640 dp screen. Undo it after step 10 with `adb shell wm size reset` and `adb shell wm density reset`.
- On iOS, use the iPhone SE (3rd generation) simulator, which is 375 × 667 pt.
- A trainer that accepts control, so every mode starts and Free Ride and Route show their gear row. On Android turn on **Fake a connected trainer** in Developer Options; on iOS turn on **Use mock trainer** in Settings → Developer · Trainer. Restart after either.
- A heart-rate strap for steps 3, 7 and 8: a real one on Android, **Mock HRM Strap** on iOS.
- Default text size for steps 1 to 8. For steps 9 and 10, the largest text: on Android, Settings → Display → Font size at its largest; on iOS, Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → Larger Text at the largest size. Set it back afterwards.
- For step 11 on Android, before the tablet gets the release candidate, start a structured Power workout on the build it already has and take a screenshot of the cockpit. That build is v2.1.8 from the Play Store; use the SM-X910 if it is on the bench.
- For step 11 on iOS, nothing to prepare. iOS has never shipped, so there is no earlier build to compare with.

## Steps

1. Start a structured Power workout and look at the whole cockpit.
2. Read the power, heart-rate and cadence numbers.
3. Start a structured HR-Zone workout and look at the terrain.
4. Start a Route ride and look at the terrain.
5. Start a Free Ride. Tap − and + on the slope, then on the gear row under it, several times each.
6. Start a Quick Ride and tap − and + on the target watts several times.
7. Start a Zone Ride and look at the terrain.
8. Start a Route ride with the repeat button set to 1, which rides the route twice. Read the small line under heart rate, power and cadence.
9. With the largest text, start the Power workout again and look at the whole cockpit.
10. With the largest text, start a Route ride and read the gear row.
11. On Android, start the same Power workout on the tablet and compare the cockpit with the screenshot from the earlier build. On iOS, open the latest CI run of the candidate's commit and find the result of TST-0679's grid.

## Expect

- Step 1: the profile takes about a third of the space above the bottom bar or more. The bar shows the rider and START whole.
- Step 2: each number sits whole on one line. Heart rate and cadence are the same size, and power is the largest.
- Step 3: the HR-Zone profile is visible, about as tall as the Power workout's.
- Step 4: the route's terrain is at least as tall as the Power workout's profile.
- Step 5: each tap lands on the button aimed at. The slope stays on one line, and the gear row reads a small GEAR beside larger numbers.
- Step 6: each tap lands on the button aimed at, and the target watts, such as `124W`, stay whole on one line.
- Step 7: the Zone Ride terrain is visible.
- Step 8: each shows LAP, AVG and MAX. Where one line is too narrow, LAP n sits above AVG n | MAX n. Nothing split or cut.
- Step 9: the terrain is still visible, and no number is cut off or broken across lines.
- Step 10: GEAR and its numbers stay on one line, and nothing is cut off.
- [android] Step 11: the numbers are the same size as in the screenshot, the terrain about as tall. The bottom bar replaces the old buttons.
- [ios] Step 11: TST-0679's `CockpitLayoutRulesTests` passed. Its scale rule fails if an iPad that fitted before FEAT-0131 draws the cockpit below scale 1.0 (`tabletsThatFit`).

## Not this check

- The ride-end summary and the other screens on the smallest phone: [[TST-0677-OnTheSmallestPhoneTheRideEndAndThreeOtherScreensShowEverything]].
- Every size, font scale and language in turn: the automated grids [[TST-0678-AndroidCockpitLayoutRulesAtEverySupportedSize]] and [[TST-0679-IosCockpitLayoutRulesAtEverySupportedSize]].
- Phone landscape: out of scope ([[ISS-0334-IphoneLandscapeCockpitOverlap]]).
- What each cockpit mode's numbers mean: the mode's own checks, such as [[TST-0649-RidingByHandInEveryMode]].

## Provenance

Rewritten on 2026-09-30 by [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]] for FEAT-0132. The cockpit's action row became a bottom bar of fixed size, outside the cockpit scale, on phones and tablets alike ([[REQ-0236-TheCockpitsActionsAndTheRiderSitInABottomBarShapedLikeTheNavigationBar]]). So step 1 measures the terrain against the space above the bar and asks for the bar whole, and the tablet's step 11 no longer expects the bottom of the cockpit to look as before ([[REQ-0231-ATabletCockpitThatFitsTodayDrawsExactlyAsToday]], amendment of 2026-09-30). Steps 2 to 10 are read again against the bar; their words still hold.

Written on 2026-09-29 with FEAT-0131's planning, from Edwin's decision that 360 × 640 dp and 375 × 667 pt must look right. It sat at `level: system` until the feature was built, so the v2.2.0 release test did not owe it early. [[TASK-1009-TheChecksTheFittedCockpitReopens]] moved it into the release test on 2026-09-29 and corrected two steps to what was built. Quick Ride has a target-watts row, not a gear row, so the gear readout is read on Free Ride's second row instead. Heart rate is a side tile in a Power workout, so it is compared with cadence, not with power. The v2.1.8 gallery holds no cockpit picture, so the tablet step, now step 11, compares against a screenshot taken before the tablet is updated. iOS has no earlier build at all, so on iOS that step reads the result of TST-0679's automated iPad check instead of comparing by eye. On 2026-09-30 step 8 was added, and the three steps after it were renumbered 9 to 11. It reads the Route lap line, which breaks into two lines where it does not fit, as Edwin chose on 2026-09-29 ([[TASK-1011-EdwinsAnswersTheLapLineWrapsAndTheRidingAsLabelMovesLeft]], answer 2B). Before that, a Route ride with laps was left out of this check while the question was open.

items.name: Not-connected devices are slashed, and the cockpit's bottom bar shows the rider and the actions
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies FEAT-0132 on a phone in dark theme, where connected and not-connected icons were hardest to tell apart. The top bar and the Hub rows must use one drawing, and the cockpit must end in a bar with the rider in every ride state.

## Setup

A phone under 600 dp wide on the release candidate, in dark theme, with one rider. No heart-rate strap set up. A bundled Power workout and Free Ride.

- On Android, turn on **Fake a connected trainer** in Developer Options and restart, with Mock Wahoo KICKR as the Smart Trainer. Discarding a ride disconnects every device, which step 6 uses.
- On iOS, use the real KICKR as the Smart Trainer, with **Use mock trainer** off in Settings → Developer · Trainer. A mock device cannot be switched off, and iOS keeps its devices connected after a ride, so step 6 switches the KICKR off instead.

## Steps

1. With the trainer connected, read the four icons in the top bar on Workouts.
2. Open the Equipment Hub from the icons and read each row's icon. Close it.
3. Open the Power workout and read the bottom of the cockpit before START.
4. Tap START and read the bottom bar while riding.
5. Tap PAUSE and read the bottom bar.
6. Tap FINISH, then Discard. On iOS, also switch the trainer off. Read the top bar, then open the Hub and read it.
7. Switch the trainer back on if it is off. Tap Reconnect on its row and watch its icon and row until it is connected.
8. Open Free Ride, tap START and read the bottom bar.
9. Tap the rider in the bottom bar.

## Expect

- Step 1: trainer, power and cadence are plain, in the bar's text colour. Heart rate is faint grey with a diagonal slash.
- Step 2: row icons match the top bar; no tile is in the accent colour. Heart rate: slashed, on a dashed tile, *Not set up*.
- Step 3: a full-width bar like the Workouts navigation bar. Left: the rider's mark in their colour, name under it. Middle: START. Right: empty.
- Step 4: the rider, then PAUSE and FINISH, each an icon in a tinted pill with its label under it.
- Step 5: the rider, RESUME and FINISH.
- Step 6: trainer, power and cadence are faint grey and slashed, in the top bar and in their rows. The trainer row reads *Disconnected*.
- Step 7: while connecting, the icon is in the accent colour with no slash, and the row shows a spinner. Then it is plain.
- Step 8: the rider stays on the left while Free Ride runs, beside PAUSE and FINISH.
- Step 9: nothing happens. The rider is not a button.

## Not this check

- Every state of the top bar from first run to a failed connect: [[TST-0675-TheTopBarIconsFromFirstRunToAFailedConnect]].
- Setting up, inspecting and forgetting a device in the Hub: [[TST-0674-TheEquipmentHubListSetsUpInspectsAndForgetsADevice]].
- The rider's colour on the terrain: [[TST-0668-TheRiderIsIdentifiableInEveryCockpit]].
- The cockpit fitting the smallest phone: [[TST-0676-OnTheSmallestPhoneEveryCockpitShowsItsTerrainAndWholeNumbers]] and the layout grids.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-09-30 with FEAT-0132's planning, and held at `level: system` until the feature was built, the way TST-0676 was held for FEAT-0131.

- 2026-09-30, [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]]: checked against the build, given `level: acceptance` and moved to `active`, so the v2.2.0 release test owes it. Three things were corrected. A paused ride shows FINISH beside RESUME on both platforms, not an empty right slot. The details sheet has no Disconnect action, so step 6 reaches *Disconnected* by discarding a ride on Android and by switching the real trainer off on iOS. "Tapping the rider does nothing" became step 9, so each step has one expected line.

items.text:
## Steps

1. On the Workouts screen, choose **Route** in the ride-mode strip and tap the Free Ride card. Verify the session starts in SIMULATION.
2. Adjust slope with +/- buttons through 0.5% steps from -15% to 20%. Verify trainer resistance changes with slope.

## Expect

- Step 1: the session starts in SIMULATION.
- Step 2: the slope moves in 0.5 % steps from −15 % to 20 %, and the trainer resistance changes with it.

## Coverage

`WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.startFreeRide_default_is_SIMULATION_for_Route_tab` covers the mode dispatch. The slope +/- UI and trainer resistance stay hardware dependent.

## Path corrected 2026-09-24

Step 1 named the Route tab that PHASE-025 replaced with the ride-mode strip. The expectation is unchanged.

items.name: Simulation Gear Shifting
items.text:
In simulation free ride, check the gear controls, shift gears, and read the gear label.

## Steps

1. In simulation free ride, look at the gear controls.
2. Shift gears.
3. Read the `GEAR N of M` label, on the rider's preset and again after changing the preset.

## Expect

- Step 1: gear up and down buttons sit below the slope controls.
- Step 2: resistance changes on the trainer.
- Step 3: the `GEAR N of M` label renders, and its `M` follows the rider's preset.

## Narrowed 2026-09-12 — the counts moved to a note CI runs

This row is now the rendering half only: the buttons are where they should be, the label draws, and a shift is felt. The numbers behind the label — 26 for Linear, 22 for Road, 12 for MTB — are asserted on every build by [[TST-0660]], which runs `VirtualGearTablesTest`.

The row keeps `automation: manual` and no `command:` on purpose. A `command:` would take it out of the release test entirely (`tools/instructions/TESTING.md` § "Release gating"), and the layout half would stop being asked for — which matters here, because this row also carries an `invalidated_by` from TASK-0460 about the cockpit's slope Row moving inside a Column.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: Slope control — range, limits, and where the number is shown
items.text:
In simulation mode, work the slope control through its range and then read the cockpit.

## Steps

1. **Range and step size.** Slope adjusts from −15 % to 20 % in 0.5 % steps.
2. **It stops at both limits.** Pushing past −15 % or past 20 % does nothing.
3. **The slope percentage is shown in the intensity control area.**
4. **The slope number is not duplicated anywhere else in the cockpit.** With Slope behaviour set to something other than `Auto` on a SIM-capable trainer, a chip renders directly under the slope `%` (TASK-0460). Confirm there is still no second slope number elsewhere on the screen.
5. **Elevation gain sits next to distance in the header.**

## Expect

- Step 1: the slope adjusts from −15 % to 20 % in 0.5 % steps.
- Step 2: pushing past −15 % or past 20 % does nothing.
- Step 3: the slope percentage shows in the intensity control area.
- Step 4: a chip renders directly under the slope `%`, and no second slope number shows elsewhere.
- Step 5: elevation gain sits next to distance in the header.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0117` | 3, 4, 5 | Where the slope number is shown now shares a result with what values it can take, so a control that reaches 20 % but prints the figure twice records as the same failure as one that stops at 15 %. Step 4 stays a named step because it is the negative — a duplicate slope number passes every other step here. |

items.name: Slope + Gears
items.text:
## Steps

In the Free Ride cockpit, set the slope to 5 % and shift gears.

## Expect

- The slope row and its chip sit inside one column, with the gear row beneath it.
- Every tap target still works at the size it had before TASK-0460.
- A gear shift gives the same resistance step whether or not the chip is showing.

## Original wording

In the Free Ride cockpit, set slope to 5 % and shift gears. Confirm the slope Row and its chip sit inside their Column with the gear Row as a sibling beneath, that every tap target still works at the size it did before TASK-0460, and that a gear shift produces the same resistance step whether or not the chip is showing.

## Narrowed 2026-09-12 — the arithmetic moved to a note CI runs, the layout stayed here

[[TST-0663]] asserts what the slope and the gear each do to resistance, on every build, via `PhysicsUtilsLinearSnapshotTest`. The sibling row [[TST-0430-Slope-Gears-Together]] makes the same arithmetic claim under ISS-0130 and took that command directly, because it carries no layout remainder.

This row does carry one. Its `invalidated_by` from TASK-0460 asks for the cockpit's tap targets after the slope Row moved inside a Column, and no unit test looks at a layout. That is why the row keeps `automation: manual` and no `command:` — a `command:` would take it out of the release test and the layout check would never be asked for again (`tools/instructions/TESTING.md` § "Release gating").

## Steps

2. Resume, and shift gears.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

items.name: The four 5 % corners — SIM and Resistance, gear 9 and gear 15
items.text:
Free Ride at a 5 % slope and read the watts at four operating points. Pedal at your usual cadence at each one. **Write each reading into the table below before moving to the next point**, because these are hard efforts and stopping part-way through is the likely outcome.

## Steps

Set the slope to 5 % in every case.

1. **SIM / gear 9.** Slope-mode `Auto` on a SIM-capable trainer, gear 9.
2. **SIM / gear 15.** Same trainer and mode, gear 15.
3. **Resistance / gear 9.** Slope-mode `Resistance`, gear 9.
4. **Resistance / gear 15.** Slope-mode `Resistance`, gear 15.

Points 1 and 3 should read the same watts as each other, and so should points 2 and 4. That agreement between the two modes is what the four corners exist to show.

## Expect

- Step 1: about 255 W for the reference rider.
- Step 2: about 358 W for the reference rider.
- Step 3: the trainer holds a fixed level, about 52 %, and reads about 255 W, matching SIM (reference rider).
- Step 4: the trainer holds a fixed level, about 64 %, and reads about 358 W, matching SIM (reference rider).

## Write the four readings down

| Point | Mode | Gear | Reference | Watts read | Ridden |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | SIM | 9 | about 255 W | | |
| 2 | SIM | 15 | about 358 W | | |
| 3 | Resistance | 9 | about 255 W | | |
| 4 | Resistance | 15 | about 358 W | | |

A partial run is expected. Fill in the rows that were ridden, leave the rest blank, and say in the verdict reason which points went unridden rather than treating the whole row as unrun.

## The gear sweep does not ride this point, and that is deliberate

[[TST-0658-TheGearSweepRidesTheGearTable]] derives every gear it visits from the rider's FTP, climbing only while the predicted effort stays at or below 0.9 × FTP. At a 5 % slope that lands near **gear 4** for the reference rider. This row's gear predicts 255 W for that rider, which is 1.3 × FTP.

Edwin opened [[FEAT-0117-GearSweep]] saying he could not hold cadence in the higher gears, and these 5 % points are harder than anything in the sweep's climb. So the sweep avoids them on purpose. **Do not add `covered_by:` here.** A later reader who notices the omission and "fixes" it would put the effort back that the whole feature exists to take away.

The row therefore stays a ride of its own, for a rider willing to hold it. The watt figure above is a reference, not a threshold. It comes from one constant fitted to one rider on one trainer (`V_REF_FTP_FRACTION` in `PhysicsUtils.kt`), and the rider is the actuator — watts at a given resistance depend on the cadence being held that second. Edwin, 2026-09-12: *"it needs to have some correlation with the original measurements but I don't think we can be very precise?"*

Gear 15 is harder again: it predicts 358 W for the reference rider, which is 1.8 × FTP. Everything the section above says about gear 9 applies to it with more force.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Point | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0146` | 2 | SIM at gear 15 no longer records apart from SIM at gear 9, so a gear table that is wrong only at the top of its range reads as one failure among four. |
| `TST-0153` | 3 | Resistance mode no longer records apart from SIM mode, which matters because the two agreeing is the point being checked. |
| `TST-0154` | 4 | Resistance at gear 15 no longer records apart from the other three. |

The table above is the mitigation: it records the four readings side by side. Since 2026-09-17 each point is also its own step with its own mark.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test read them as one part and could give the whole check only one mark. They now sit under `## Steps`, with one expectation each under `## Expect`, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: Power Nudge
items.text:
Start a structured HR-Zone workout and work the watts +/- row. All four steps happen on that one screen.

## Steps

1. **Auto-adjusted display.** Read the watts row.
2. **Nudge step size.** Tap + and then -.
3. **Manual pill.** Read the delta pill after the nudge.
4. **The controller resumes.** Keep riding until `MANUAL` expires.

## Expect

- Step 1: the current auto-adjusted watts, with the delta pill beside it and the heartbeat bar below.
- Step 2: each tap moves the watts by 5 W.
- Step 3: the pill reads `MANUAL`, and holds for the first half of the controller's decision window.
- Step 4: after `MANUAL` expires, the controller adjusts the watts on its own again.

## What is automated

*(partially automated: `HrZoneLockControllerTest` covers the converge/locked/adjusting status machine and the manual-nudge watt step and status bump; the +/- button rendering and the pill label stay visual.)*

## Notes

The `auto · converging / locked / adjusting` banner this row used to name was removed by ISS-0166 and ISS-0167. What replaced it, at `ActiveWorkoutScreen.kt:1842-1852` and `:2641`, is a persistent delta pill reading `MANUAL`, `▲ Nw`, `▼ Nw` or `HOLD`, plus a 3 dp progress bar that refills over the controller's decision window.

There is no zone selector on this screen to nudge next to. ISS-0166 R-2 made the Z1–Z5 selector free-ride-only, because a structured workout takes its target zone from the interval plan (`ActiveWorkoutScreen.kt:1649-1653`). The watts row is the only control there, and it is upsized to `displayMedium` with 72 dp buttons to say so (`:1685-1687`). The 5 W step is at `WorkoutViewModel.kt:818-819`; `MANUAL` expires on its own at `WorkoutViewModel.kt:1761-1771`.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0197` (Wattage Nudge) — the same +/- row in the same structured HR workout, asking for the 5 W step and the `MANUAL` pill. Its step size is now the **Nudge step size** step; its pill assertion merged into **Manual pill**.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates a wrong nudge step size from a pill that never says `MANUAL`. Both are sub-steps of one nudge, so a rider must record which of the four named steps failed.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were bold-headed paragraphs, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.name: Zone Look-Ahead
items.text:
Start `hr_z4_threshold_3x8` (HR Z4 Threshold 3×8min). Each of its three Z4 blocks is preceded by a 120-second Z3 interval — `z3_climb`, `z3_up_1`, `z3_up_2`. During the last 60 seconds of one of those Z3 intervals, verify the controller starts raising power before the Z4 boundary fires. The watts number blinks and the delta pill reads `▲ Nw` on each pre-ramp adjustment. *(partially automated: `HrZoneLookaheadTest` covers the pre-ramp window arithmetic, including the 50 % clamp on short intervals; live HRM + interval clock stays hardware-dependent.)*

The pre-ramp only runs on upward transitions: `hrZoneLookaheadDownSeconds = 0` (`WorkoutViewModel.kt:1705`), so a Z4→Z3 boundary never pre-ramps and there is no point watching one for this check. The 60-second lead is capped at half the interval (`HrZoneLookahead.kt`), which for these 120-second Z3 intervals leaves the full 60 seconds — `hrZoneLookaheadUpSeconds = 60` at `WorkoutViewModel.kt:1704`.

## Expect

- In the last 60 seconds of the Z3 interval, power starts rising before the Z4 boundary.
- The watts blink and the pill reads `▲ Nw` at each early step up.

items.name: Down-Step Speed
items.text:
During `hr_z4_threshold_3x8` (HR Z4 Threshold 3×8min), at the boundary out of a Z4 block, verify power drops noticeably within the first 20 seconds of the interval that follows (faster than the 10W/20s up-ramp). *(partially automated: `HrZoneLockControllerTest` covers the asymmetric up-ramp vs down-step rates; runtime playback stays manual.)*

The boundary to watch is Z4→Z3, not Z4→Z2. This workout steps down one zone at a time — each `z4_work_N` is followed by a 120-second `z3_down_N` and only then by a 180-second `z2_recovery_N` — because HR cannot drop a full zone on command (`AGENT_RULES.md` § "Authoring HR Z5 workouts"). No bundled HR-Zone workout puts a Z4 interval directly next to a Z2 one.

## Expect

- Within 20 seconds of leaving the Z4 block, power drops noticeably: faster than the 10 W per 20 s ramp up.

items.name: The HR-Zone terrain draws the same bands the controller drives
items.text:
## What automation already covers

`HrZonesTest` (Android) pins the drivable band values at a known LTHR and asserts they equal `HrZoneLockController.getZoneBounds`. `HrZoneTerrainBandsTests` (iOS) pins the same values and asserts a heart rate at a zone's midpoint maps into that zone's strip. Both were seen red against the old table and mapping.

**What they cannot cover** is that the *renderers* use them. Both are Compose/SwiftUI Canvas drawing; there is no seam a unit test can read a drawn rectangle through. That is what this check is for, and it is why the check exists rather than being folded into the suites.

## The release test

Use a rider whose LTHR is not a round fraction of Max HR — set **Max HR 185** and an explicit **LTHR 162** — because a mismatch is invisible when the two happen to agree.

1. Start an HR-Zone workout containing a **Z2** interval.
2. Read the bpm range printed against the zone target. For this rider it must be **129–144**.
3. Look at the Z2 stripe in the terrain. Its edges must be the same two numbers — the stripe must not sit lower than the label, which is the ISS-0394 symptom.
4. Ride until HR settles inside Z2 around **136 bpm**. **The trace must sit inside the Z2 stripe**, and be drawn in the Z2 colour rather than the below-floor blue or above-ceiling red.
5. Let HR drift above 144 and confirm the line turns red at the same bpm the stripe's top edge sits at.
6. Repeat on the **free ride** HR-zone screen, which is the other renderer (`GrowingProfileGraph` on Android).
7. Repeat both on iOS.

## Start cold — the warm-up leg

**Test this before step 1, from a resting heart rate, not from a rider already in zone.** Its absence from the first version of this check is why [[ISS-0396-HeartRateInvisibleBelowZone1]] shipped: every step above starts with HR inside a band, so nothing ever looked below Z1, and the whole warm-up climb was being drawn off the bottom of the canvas.

1. Begin the ride with HR at rest — for this rider, somewhere in the 60s or 70s.
2. **The trace is visible immediately.** Below Z1's floor (113 bpm here) it is drawn in the compressed band that occupies the bottom 15% of the terrain, spanning `0.45 × LTHR` up to Z1's floor — **73 to 113 bpm** for LTHR 162.
3. **The climb moves.** As HR rises from about 90 to 113 the trace should travel roughly 9% of the canvas height. A trace that sits still, or is absent, is the ISS-0396 symptom returning.
4. **Below 73 bpm it clamps to the bottom edge** rather than disappearing. Above Z5's ceiling it clamps to the top, and the red above-ceiling colour is what signals the overshoot — there is deliberately no mirrored band up there.
5. **The band is labelled `<Z1`, not `Z0`.** The FEAT-0090 seven-zone display scheme has no Z0; its Z1 already starts at 0% LTHR, so a `Z0` label would contradict the Profile zone panel.
6. **Six bpm boundary labels run down the left edge**, zone names down the right, on both platforms. Android skips a label when two boundaries are closer than 30px (Z2/Z3 at 144 and Z3/Z4 at 150 collide at LTHR 162); iOS has equal-height strips and skips nothing. Each label must read the same number as the zone target printed for that band.
7. Test it on both renderers and both platforms, as above.

*Added 2026-09-06 after `CHG-20260905-SubZone-Band-And-Boundary-Labels`. The Android test recorded as a pass in the working ledger that day did include this leg — Edwin confirmed it the same day — so the pass covers the amended text and not only the original seven steps.*

## Expect

- From rest, the trace shows at once, in the bottom band from 73 to 113 bpm. The band is labelled `<Z1`, not `Z0`.
- As HR climbs from about 90 to 113, the trace rises about 9% of the height.
- Below 73 bpm the trace sits on the bottom edge. Above Z5 it sits on the top edge, in red.
- The Z2 target reads 129–144, and the Z2 stripe has the same two edges.
- At about 136 bpm the trace sits inside the Z2 stripe, in the Z2 colour.
- Above 144 the line turns red at the stripe's top edge.
- [android] Six bpm labels run down the left edge, zone names down the right, each matching its band's target. One may be skipped where two collide.
- [ios] Six bpm labels run down the left edge, zone names down the right, each matching its band's target. None is skipped.
- The same holds on the Zone Ride screen.

## What a failure looks like

Stripe edges that do not match the printed range mean a renderer is still reading its own table. A trace in the wrong stripe while the edges are right means the axis mapping is wrong, not the bands — on iOS that is `bandFraction`, on Android `bpmToY`.

## Settled — 2026-09-06

> [!note] Edwin, 2026-09-06
> It is acceptable.

The unequal Android band heights read acceptably; no design follow-up is owed. The question below stays in the release test as a prompt for the next reader, but it has an answer now and a re-test does not need to re-open it.

## Also confirm, because it changed

Android bands are drawn bpm-proportionally, so on the LTHR axis they are **no longer equal heights**: Z1 is the tallest and Z3 the shortest. That is intended (Z3 really is ~6 bpm wide here) but it is a visible change, and this is the moment to say whether it reads acceptably or wants a design follow-up. iOS keeps five equal strips, so the two platforms will look different side by side — a known, recorded divergence, not a defect.

## Not covered here

The seven **display** zones on the Profile panel and in post-ride time-in-zone. Those are a different table on purpose, and they legitimately differ from the drivable bands at Z1 and Z5.

## A feature check since 2026-09-29

This check came from a fixed defect, and its Expect lines also say how the cockpit looks now. FEAT-0131 redrew that part on phones, so it carries `kind: feature` and was reopened (`TESTING.md`, "When to invalidate"; [[CHG-20260929-The-Cockpit-Fits-Every-Screen-And-The-Terrain-Keeps-Its-Share]]).
