items.name: The repeat button — its cycle, its place in the header, and the one route that refuses it
items.text:
Start a structured workout and drive the repeat button through its whole life. The last step needs a second ride, on a route.

**Cycle.** Tap the button repeatedly. It goes Off (grey icon) → 1 (accent icon and badge "1") → 2 (badge "2") → 3 (badge "3") → ∞ (badge "∞" on an opaque pill) → Off. The ∞ step is five taps to get back to Off, not four.

**Header placement.** The button sits between duration and distance in the header.

**Re-arm after exhaustion.** Let the repeats run out, so the badge disappears and the icon goes grey. Tap the button once: it goes Off → 1 and looping resumes for one more extra pass.

**Still tappable with repeats active.** With repeats already set, the button can always be tapped to increase or to turn off. Check it on a Power workout, on an HR-Zone workout, and on a Route that is a circuit.

**Refused on a point-to-point route.** Ride a route that is not a closed loop, such as `route_alpe_d_huez` — 720 m to 1861 m, start and finish nowhere near each other. The button is greyed out and carries the `route_repeat_unavailable_cd` description.

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.toggleLoop_cycles_off_1_2_3_unlimited_off` covers the state cycle and the 0 → 1 re-arm; the icon, the badge, the header placement and the route-disabled state stay visual.)*

The ∞ step was added by TASK-0374 and this row never named it. `ActiveWorkoutScreen.kt:690` renders its badge as `"∞"` and `WorkoutViewModel.kt:1497-1500` short-circuits it back to Off. The cycle step above was corrected on 2026-09-12 as part of this merge, because writing the old four-tap cycle into a freshly authored body would have shipped a claim already known to be wrong.

That last case is disabled by design. TASK-0661 greys the button out on a route that is not a closed loop, because the lap reversal it would cause half-breaks ghost racing, and TASK-0178 already hides ghosts on a reversed lap. The gate is `isRouteWorkout && !routeIsCircuit` at `ActiveWorkoutScreen.kt:666`. Power and HR-Zone repeats are untouched.

## Expect

- Taps go Off (grey icon) → 1 → 2 → 3 → ∞ → Off. From 1 the icon is accent with a count badge; ∞ has an opaque pill.
- The button sits between duration and distance in the header.
- After the repeats run out, one tap sets it to 1 and one more pass plays.
- With repeats set, it can always be tapped up or off: on Power, on HR-Zone and on a circuit Route.
- On a route that is not a loop it is greyed out, described by `route_repeat_unavailable_cd`.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0167` (Re-loop After Exhaustion) — tapping the button back to 1 after all repeats are done. It is the **Re-arm after exhaustion** step.
- `TST-0160` (The repeat button stays tappable, except on a route that is not a loop) — the button staying tappable across workout types, and the one route case where it is greyed out. They are the **Still tappable with repeats active** and **Refused on a point-to-point route** steps.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates a broken cycle from a button in the wrong place in the header, nor a failed re-arm from a button that will not accept a second tap mid-ride. A rider must write down which named step failed.

The **Refused on a point-to-point route** step is the one that costs a separate ride, because it needs a non-circuit route loaded. Test it last, and record it separately if the rest of the row passes.

items.name: Loop countdown — the badge counts down and the header duration grows

**Header duration.** The moment repeat is set to 2, the total duration in the header grows to include the extra body passes.

**Badge countdown.** The badge shows "2". After the first loop restart it shows "1". After the second loop restart it disappears and the icon turns grey.

*(partially automated: `WorkoutLoopTest` covers both the decrement math and the extended duration calculation; the badge and the header rendering stay visual.)*

- The badge shows "2", then "1" after the first restart. After the second it goes and the icon turns grey.

## What this row absorbed

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates a badge that fails to count down from a header duration that never grows. They come from the same `WorkoutLoopTest` math but render in two different places, so a rider must write down which of the two was wrong.

items.name: Split-screen — a structured workout renders, and resizing while it runs does not break it
items.text:
One structured workout, started beside another app and resized while it is running. Use Android split-screen on an Android tablet or Split View on an iPad.

## Procedure

1. **The structured workout renders.** Put Your Trainer beside another app such as a browser using the tablet's split view. Start a structured workout. The terrain graph renders correctly, the watts labels are readable, coaching cues display within the terrain bounds, the cockpit metrics are not clipped, and the timeline ruler ticks are visible.
2. **Resize while it runs.** With the workout still active, drag the split-screen divider. The UI adapts without crashing and without layout corruption. Then re-check the five items from step 1 at the new size.

## Expect

- Step 1: terrain, watts labels, cues inside the terrain, cockpit metrics and ruler ticks all show, none clipped.
- Step 2: no crash or broken layout, and the same five things still show.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0327-Resize-During-Workout]] | resizing the divider mid-workout without crash or corruption | step 2 |

**[[TST-0326-Split-Screen-Free-Ride]] was deliberately left standing.** Its three free-ride modes — Simulation, ERG and HR Zone — are already three sub-checks inside one row, and folding them under a structured-workout row would make four modes one tick. It stays a separate row.

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0327** — a crash on resize is a much harder failure than a clipped label, and the two now share a verdict; step 2 asks for the step-1 items to be re-read after the resize so the evidence can say which it was.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- Screenshots at the initial split and after the resize.

items.name: Coaching cues — display, auto-dismiss, and long-cue wrapping
items.text:
One run of the "[Debug] Coaching Cues & Ramps" workout answers all three questions. Start it and watch the terrain graph.

## Procedure

1. **Display.** Coaching cues appear as a floating banner overlaid on the terrain graph, at the times the workout specifies.
2. **Auto-dismiss.** Each cue disappears after its duration — 5 s by default — without a tap.
3. **Long-cue wrapping.** At 20 s into the warmup, the long cue wraps to two lines and does not overflow the banner.

## Expect

- Step 1: cues appear as a banner over the terrain, at the times the workout sets.
- Step 2: each cue clears by itself after its duration, 5 s by default.
- Step 3: the long cue 20 s into the warm-up wraps to two lines inside its banner.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0397-Cue-Auto-Dismiss]] | cues disappear after their duration | step 2 |
| [[TST-0398-Long-Cue-Wrapping]] | the long warmup cue wraps to two lines | step 3 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0397** — a cue that shows but never clears now records the same as a cue that never shows, which is a difference a rider mid-ride cares about a great deal.
- **TST-0398** — a layout overflow on one long cue disappears into the same verdict as the cue system being broken.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- Which of the three observations held, named one by one.

items.name: Cadence targets in the cockpit — display, nudges, arrows, and their absence
items.text:
One ride through a workout with cadence targets, "Easy Spin" (target 90) and a "Recovery" interval that has none.

## Steps

1. **The target shows.** During "Easy Spin", read the cadence metric's subtext.
2. **Colour nudges.** Pedal above 100 RPM.
3. **Arrows point the way.** Pedal below the target, then above it.
4. **Negative — an interval with no target wears no decoration.** Ride into the "Recovery" interval and read the cadence. This step keeps its own line because an absence folded under a positive is how a gate quietly stops checking it.

## Expect

- Step 1: the subtext reads "TARGET: 90".
- Step 2: the value turns orange 5–10 RPM off target, red more than 10 off.
- Step 3: ▲ shows below target, ▼ above it.
- Step 4: plain cadence: no TARGET subtext, no colour, no arrow.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0405]] (step 2), [[TST-0406]] (step 3) and [[TST-0407]] (step 4). All four read the same cadence metric during one ride on one trainer, and the expensive part is the ride.

Step 4 is the negative case and is named separately on purpose, per the rule TASK-0891 states: a workout that decorates an untargeted interval is a defect no positive step can see.

One tick no longer separates a missing target subtext from wrong nudge colours, wrong arrows, or decoration leaking into an interval that has no target. Write down the step number.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: Cadence coaching banner announces the next target
items.text:
Ride a workout whose intervals carry different cadence targets.

## Steps

1. **The banner appears ahead of the change.** Watch the last 10 seconds before "Low Cadence Grind" starts.
2. **It appears for every change, not just the first.** Ride on.

## Expect

- Step 1: 10 s before, a banner reads "Next: Low Cadence Grind — 65 RPM".
- Step 2: a banner comes before every interval whose cadence target differs.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0409]] (step 2). Both rows watch the same banner during the same ride; TST-0409 asked for the general rule where this row named one instance of it.

One tick no longer separates a banner that never appears from one that appears once and then stops. The second is the more likely regression, so stay on the ride past the first interval change.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: Spiral of death — relief and recovery
items.text:
Ride the "Spiral Test" interval (120 % power, target 50 RPM) on a real trainer.

## Steps

1. **Relief.** Stop pedalling, or drop below 50 RPM, for 3 or more seconds.
2. **Recovery.** Resume pedalling above 70 RPM.

## Expect

- Step 1: the target power halves and a "Low cadence detected" cue appears.
- Step 2: the target power returns to normal within 10 seconds.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0411]] (step 2). Recovery cannot be tested without triggering relief first, so the two were always tested in one go on one trainer.

One tick no longer separates relief that never fires from relief that fires and never lets go. The second is the worse failure — the rider is left at half power for the rest of the interval — so note which step failed.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: Interval transitions — the tablet buzzes and the app survives
items.text:
Start a structured workout with at least four intervals and ride it to the end, so at least three interval transitions happen. Both steps are watched across those transitions.

**Vibration.** At each interval transition the tablet vibrates briefly.

**No freeze or crash.** The app does not freeze or crash at any transition, and the ride continues to the end.

These two were one bug. The missing `VIBRATE` permission was what crashed the app at a transition, so the buzz and the survival come from the same fix and fail together.

## Expect

- The tablet buzzes briefly at each interval transition.
- No freeze or crash at any transition. The ride reaches the end.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0433` (No Crash on Transition) — riding three or more transitions and confirming no freeze or crash. It is the **No freeze or crash** step, on the same ride.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates a transition that does not buzz from a transition that takes the app down. They shared a root cause once, but a regression could bring back either alone — a silent transition is a missing haptic call, a crash is a permission or effect problem. A rider must write down which named step failed.

items.name: Power cockpit grid: hero, flanks and footers
items.text:
Start a Power workout with an HRM connected. (Hero placement is covered by TST-0233, the LAP/RIDE sub-value variants by TST-0269 and W/kg correctness by TST-0020; this check is the full grid and the footer row those do not assert.)

## Steps

1. Read the centre of the cockpit grid.
2. Read the two flanks of the grid.
3. Read the footer row.
4. Rotate between portrait and landscape.

## Expect

- Step 1: POWER is the centred hero, with AVG and MAX beneath it.
- Step 2: HR is large on one flank, cadence on the other.
- Step 3: the footer row carries W/kg, energy in the rider's unit, and speed.
- Step 4: the grid reflows without clipping or sideways scrolling.

## Notes

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

items.name: Countdown beeps and the timer flash fire on the same instant
items.text:

## Steps

1. In the last 10 seconds before a transition — on any interval that is not the last — watch the timer.
2. In the same countdown, listen for the beeps and watch for the timer blinks.
3. Ride the final interval to its end.

## Expect

- Step 1: the timer takes the *upcoming* interval's zone colour and bumps in scale.
- Step 2: a beep and a timer blink land together at 10 s, 3, 2 and 1 s, and 0 s.
- Step 3: no countdown fires on the final interval.

It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

items.name: Structured Workout Simulation
items.text:
## Steps

1. On a trainer that supports FTMS simulation parameters, start a Route ride — `route_flat_10k` or `route_rolling_medium`. Read the top of the control block.
2. Read the grade below the gear control.
3. Pedal and read the terrain view.

## Expect

- Step 1: the gear row sits on top of the control block: a small GEAR beside large numbers, such as `GEAR 9 / 26`, between − and + buttons.
- Step 2: the grade sits below it, smaller and grey, read-only (`GRADE  N.N%`), with no +/− of its own.
- Step 3: the terrain view shows the route's gradient profile, with the rider's marker moving along it.

## A Route ride is the only way to reach this layout

The row used to open "Start a structured workout. Toggle to SIMULATION." There is no such toggle, because FEAT-0051 removed it, and no code path would honour one. `WorkoutViewModel.selectWorkout` sends every structured workout that is not a Route to `FreeRideMode.ERG` unconditionally. It sets `SIMULATION` for a selected workout only in its Route branches.

The layout claim itself is live. In `ActiveWorkoutScreen`, the control block's `isStructuredSimulation` reads `selectedWorkout != null && (isSimulationMode || isRouteWorkout)`. The `isRouteWorkout` half is the one a rider can reach, so a Route ride draws the block the row describes: the `isStructuredSimulation` branch puts the gears first in a `CockpitStepperRow` with `GearReadout`, and the grade under it as read-only `workout_grade_label` text.

Two sentences the old row carried do not survive the move. The grade is not a `+/-` control on a Route: it is read-only text, because the profile drives it. And "terrain still shows planned intervals" is wrong for a Route. The interval-timer card, the cockpit's "PROGRESS ZONE", is drawn only when `selectedWorkout != null && !isRouteWorkout`, and the visualisation is `RouteTerrainView`, the gradient profile, not a planned-interval strip.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

## Step 1 rewritten for FEAT-0131, 2026-09-29

Step 1 used to ask for `GEAR N / <total>` in large type with 72 dp buttons. FEAT-0131 split the readout into a small GEAR label beside large numbers (`GearReadout` on Android, `GearReadoutView` on iOS), and the buttons now shrink to 56 dp on a phone, so the line names what the rider sees instead of a size ([[CHG-20260929-The-Cockpit-Fits-Every-Screen-And-The-Terrain-Keeps-Its-Share]]).

items.name: Route ride — the cockpit through one bundled route
items.text:
Tap a bundled Route on a SIM-capable trainer and ride it. Do not set repeats; step 5 depends on the ride being single-lap. One ride answers all five steps.

## Steps

1. **The ride starts in SIM.** Trainer resistance is driven by terrain grade. Watts are measured, not a target — the rider controls power through effort and gearing.
2. **The rider marker advances.** The 2D elevation profile shows a marker moving left to right as the rider pedals, and distance covered increases smoothly.
3. **Power is the hero metric.** The cockpit renders power large and speed as the secondary figure.
4. **No ERG watt controls.** The `+` / `−` watt buttons must not appear anywhere in the Route cockpit. On a Route, watts are measured from the rider's effort rather than set.
5. **No LAP | RIDE sub-values.** With no repeats set, the cockpit shows today's `AVG | MAX` everywhere. The `LAP | RIDE` variant must not appear.

## Expect

- Step 1: the ride is in SIM: grade drives resistance, and watts are measured, not a target.
- Step 2: the marker moves left to right, and distance covered rises smoothly.
- Step 3: power is the large figure; speed is the smaller one.
- Step 4: no `+` / `−` watt buttons anywhere in the Route cockpit.
- Step 5: `AVG | MAX` everywhere; `LAP | RIDE` never appears.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0231` | 2 | A marker that never moves no longer records apart from a ride that never entered SIM. |
| `TST-0233` | 3, 4 | The hero-metric layout and the absent ERG controls share one result, so a cockpit that shows speed large and a cockpit that offers watt buttons read the same. |
| `TST-0270` | 5 | Lap sub-values leaking onto a single-lap ride now fails the same tick as the wrong hero metric. |

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.selectWorkout_ROUTE_with_sim_capable_trainer_uses_SIMULATION` and `.selectWorkout_ROUTE_populates_initial_grade_from_profile` cover mode dispatch, the initial grade and distance-driven profile indexing; BLE resistance and every on-screen figure stay manual.)*

items.name: Grade drives resistance, and it changes continuously
items.text:
Ride a route with varied but smoothly varying terrain — no stepped intervals. One ride answers both steps.

## Steps

1. **Resistance follows the terrain.** Trainer resistance increases on climbs and decreases on descents, and speed changes follow from physics given the rider's weight and power.
2. **No abrupt jumps between grade samples.** Resistance changes smoothly across sample boundaries. The engine interpolates grade rather than stepping it.

## Expect

- Step 1: resistance rises on climbs and falls on descents, and speed follows from weight and power.
- Step 2: resistance changes smoothly, with no jumps between grade samples.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0234` | 2 | A stepped, jumpy resistance curve now records the same result as resistance that does not respond to grade at all. |

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.selectWorkout_ROUTE_populates_initial_grade_from_profile` covers grade computation from the profile and the interpolation path between samples; the trainer's physical response stays hardware-dependent.)*

items.name: ERG fallback on a trainer with no SIM support
items.text:
Start a bundled Route ride on a trainer that does not support FTMS SIM — an older direct-drive unit or a basic smart trainer. On any trainer, pinning Slope behaviour to `ERG` in Settings → Hardware exercises the same dispatch path. One ride answers both steps; step 2 is about the first five seconds, so watch the target from the moment the ride starts.

## Steps

1. **Targets are computed from grade and weight.** Target watts follow grade plus rider weight and are sent as ERG targets, and the trainer's resistance changes with them.
2. **The first five seconds ramp rather than jump.** Target watts are not artificially inflated at the start. They ramp with actual speed instead of being clamped to a value that assumed 10 km/h, so the target feels proportional to the rider's effort from the first pedal stroke.

## Expect

- Step 1: target watts follow grade and rider weight, are sent as ERG targets, and the resistance changes with them.
- Step 2: the target ramps with actual speed from the first stroke; it is not inflated at the start.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0455` | 2 | The ride-start ramp and the steady-state computation now share one result, so a fallback that is right after ten seconds and wrong at t=0 reads as a pass unless the rider watches the opening. |

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.selectWorkout_ROUTE_without_sim_support_falls_back_to_ERG` covers the fallback dispatch; the trainer's response and the opening ramp stay hardware-dependent.)*

items.text:

2. Ride to the end of lap 2.

## Notes

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.toggleLoop_cycles_off_1_2_3_off` + `WorkoutLoopTest` cover the loop-count state machine and boundary logic that drive the rider-marker reset; distance accumulation stays visual.)*

## Corrected 2026-09-17

This check used to set the repeat button to 2 and expect a route ridden twice. The button counts extra laps after the first, so 2 rides the route three times ([[TST-0188-Loop-Label-Uniform-Across-Paradigms]]). Edwin chose repeat 1 on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]), the shortest ride that still crosses a lap boundary.

items.name: Lap-times strip on a velodrome ride — overflow, personal-best deltas, and the rollover banner
items.text:
Run a velodrome (∞) ride past 6 laps on a course where you already hold a personal best. One ride answers all four steps.

## Steps

1. **Every closed lap is shown.** The strip lists each closed lap with no truncation and no leading ellipsis.
2. **The newest lap is pinned right.** Older laps push left and overflow off-screen as new ones land; swipe left and the older laps pan back into view. The strip auto-scrolls to the new lap on each rollover, via `LaunchedEffect(laps.size)`.
3. **Personal-best delta suffix.** Each strip entry shows `(−m:ss)` in green or `(+m:ss)` in muted grey. Lower is better, so a minus sign is the faster lap.
4. **The lap-rollover banner does not swallow touches.** While the banner is on screen after a rollover, tap STOP. The tap is processed and the session ends.

## Expect

- Step 1: every closed lap is shown, with no truncation and no leading ellipsis.
- Step 2: the newest lap is on the right; older laps scroll off left and swipe back; each rollover scrolls to the new lap.
- Step 3: each lap shows `(−m:ss)` in green or `(+m:ss)` in muted grey against the personal best.
- Step 4: the tap is processed and the session ends.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0264` | 3 | A delta with the wrong sign now records the same result as a strip that truncates its laps, though one is a formatting bug and the other a layout one. |
| `TST-0266` | 4 | A banner that eats the STOP tap now fails the same tick as a mis-anchored strip, so note which half failed — a swallowed STOP is the one that traps a rider mid-ride. |

items.name: Ghosts on a second ride — personal best, today, and both at once
items.text:
Complete a Route workout including at least one full lap, then start the same workout again and produce a lap faster than the stored personal best. One repeat ride answers all three steps.

## Steps

1. **Personal-best ghost.** A small bike icon (20 dp, 40 % alpha) renders in the **rider's accent colour** with a **trophy glyph above it** (10 dp, 75 % alpha — the personal-best shape-coded marker). The ghost line and icon advance during the ride.
2. **Today ghost.** The session-best ghost renders in **grey**, not the rider's colour, with a **dashed line** (5 dp on / 3 dp off, 0.75 dp wide) and a **⟳ refresh glyph above the bike icon** (10 dp, 75 % alpha). The refresh glyph replaced the earlier "TODAY" text label.
3. **Both together.** After the faster lap, both ghosts render on the same y-row and stay legible: personal best in the accent colour with a solid line and trophy glyph, today in grey with the dashed line and refresh glyph. The earlier "adjacent y-rows" design was replaced by these shape-coded markers (`RouteTerrainView.kt:326-335`).

## Expect

- Step 1: a small bike in the rider's accent colour with a trophy above it; the line and bike advance.
- Step 2: the today ghost is grey, with a dashed line and a ⟳ refresh glyph above the bike.
- Step 3: both ghosts share one row and stay legible: accent, solid line and trophy; grey, dashed line and ⟳.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0310` | 2 | The today ghost's colour, line style and glyph now share a result with the personal-best ghost's, so a marker regression that hits only one of them reads the same as one that hits both. |
| `TST-0311` | 3 | Coexistence is no longer ticked apart from the two ghosts existing at all. Write down which of the three steps failed, since "neither drew" and "they drew on top of each other" have different causes. |

*(partially automated: `GhostRepositoryTest` covers the reconstruction path from session, lap and metric points into a distance series; on-device marker visibility stays manual.)*

items.text:
## Steps

2. Resume.

## Expect

- Step 2: it continues from the same position, with no jump ahead.

## Notes

*(partially automated: the pause-freeze mechanism relies on `lapElapsedSeconds` being derived from the paused timer; live visual freeze stays manual.)*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.name: Ghost Rewinds On Lap Rollover
items.text:
On a multi-lap ride, observe the ghost's position at the instant lap 1 rolls over to lap 2. Verify the ghost marker snaps back to the start of the terrain and begins racing lap 2. *(partially automated: `lapElapsedSeconds` reset happens via the existing `_currentLapStartSec` flow used for PB lap bookkeeping; visual snap-back stays manual.)*

## Expect

- At the rollover the ghost marker snaps back to the start of the terrain and races lap 2.

items.name: Family Ghost Colors + Labels (Family tier)
items.text:
With ≥2 riders who have each completed the same course, ride it on a third rider. Verify each family ghost has a distinct colour and is labelled with the rider's **first initial inside a coloured circle** above the bike icon (10dp, white text, 75 % alpha). Replaces the prior "rider name" text label per `RouteTerrainView.kt:326-335`. *(partially automated: `GhostRepositoryTest.getFamilyBestLaps picks one fastest lap per other rider`; colour stability + initial markers stay manual.)*

## Expect

- Each family ghost has its own colour, and the rider's first initial in a coloured circle above the bike.

items.name: Own ghosts always render and family ghosts stay behind the chip, on FREE and on PRO
items.text:
Ride a course that carries both your own ghost data and another rider's. That needs an account that was once FAMILY and has been downgraded, since neither FREE nor PRO writes another rider's ghosts. Ride it once on FREE, then flip the tier in Developer Settings and ride it again on PRO.

## Steps

1. **FREE — own personal best renders.** The trophy glyph in your accent colour draws on the terrain.
2. **FREE — the today ghost renders too.** After lap 1 the grey dashed line with the ⟳ refresh glyph appears alongside the personal best. Own data is never gated (ISS-0171).
3. **FREE — family ghosts do not render.** No other rider's ghost line or marker may appear anywhere on the terrain.
4. **FREE — the lock chip appears and leads to the paywall.** A "🔒 Family ghosts" chip sits top-left; tapping it opens the paywall.
5. **PRO — own personal best and today ghost both render.** Flip the tier to PRO in Developer Settings and ride the course again. Steps 1 and 2 must hold unchanged.
6. **PRO — family ghosts do not render.** Same negative as step 3, at the higher tier.
7. **PRO — the lock chip appears and leads to the paywall.** Same as step 4.

## Expect

- Step 1: FREE: your personal best, a trophy in your accent colour, draws on the terrain.
- Step 2: FREE: after lap 1 the grey dashed today ghost with ⟳ appears beside the personal best.
- Step 3: FREE: no other rider's ghost line or marker anywhere on the terrain.
- Step 4: FREE: a "🔒 Family ghosts" chip sits top-left, and tapping it opens the paywall.
- Step 5: PRO: your personal best and the today ghost both draw, as on FREE.
- Step 6: PRO: no other rider's ghost line or marker anywhere on the terrain.
- Step 7: PRO: the chip sits top-left, and tapping it opens the paywall.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0307` | 5, 6, 7 | FREE and PRO now share one result, so a gate that leaks family ghosts at exactly one tier reads as a plain failure without saying which tier leaked. Write the tier next to the tick. |
| `TST-0312` | 5 | The today ghost at PRO no longer records apart from the personal-best ghost at PRO. |
| `TST-0313` | 2 | The today ghost at FREE no longer records apart from the personal-best ghost at FREE. |

The negatives — steps 3 and 6 — stay named steps of their own at both tiers, because a leak of another rider's data is the failure this row exists to catch and it would otherwise pass silently under "my own ghost drew".

**This merge still costs two rides.** The tier flip cannot be done mid-ride, so steps 5 to 7 mean restarting. What the merge saves is the expensive part: building the downgraded-FAMILY ghost data once instead of four times.

*(partially automated: the tier filter and the `ghostLock` decision live in `ActiveWorkoutScreen`; chip rendering and paywall navigation stay manual.)*

items.name: No lock chip when the course carries no family ghosts, on FREE and on PRO
items.text:
Ride a course that carries only your own ghost data — the ordinary case on both tiers. Ride it on FREE, then flip the tier in Developer Settings and ride it again on PRO.

## Steps

1. **FREE — own personal best renders.**
2. **FREE — no lock chip appears.** With nothing of another rider's to gate, there is nothing to upsell and the "🔒 Family ghosts" chip must not draw.
3. **PRO — own personal best renders.**
4. **PRO — no lock chip appears.** Same negative at the higher tier.

## Expect

- Step 1: FREE: your own personal best draws.
- Step 2: FREE: no "🔒 Family ghosts" chip.
- Step 3: PRO: your own personal best draws.
- Step 4: PRO: no "🔒 Family ghosts" chip.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0308` | 3, 4 | A stray chip at exactly one tier now records the same result as a stray chip at both. Write the tier next to the tick. |

Steps 2 and 4 are the negatives and each keeps its own named step, because a chip that appears with nothing behind it is a paywall pitch shown to a rider who has nothing locked.

*(partially automated: `ghostLock` is null when no other-rider ghosts exist; the on-device absence of the chip stays manual.)*

items.name: FAMILY Tier Shows All Ghosts
items.text:
On FAMILY tier, ride a course with multiple riders' ghost data. Verify all ghosts appear and no lock chip is shown. *(partially automated: tier filter returns the full ghost list.)*

## Expect

- Every rider's ghost appears, and no lock chip is shown.

items.name: Route view modes, the inset, and the docked elevation strip
items.text:
Start a Route ride and work through the view modes. Step 7 wants ghost data on the course and decorations enabled, so ride a route you have completed before.

## Steps

1. **The layers button cycles four states.** Terrain with map inset, map with terrain inset, terrain only, map only.
2. **The inset moves and resizes.** Put it in each of the four corners and set each size — S, M, L. On Android, also drag the grip in the inset's corner, then tap it.
3. **The inset stays in overview.** While the primary view follows the rider, the corner inset keeps showing the whole route.
4. **The mode persists per rider.** End the ride, force-stop the app, reopen and start the same route on the same rider. The mode and inset size come back as they were left.
5. **A second rider has their own mode.** Switch riders and confirm that rider's mode is their own, not the first rider's.
6. **Defaults by width.** A compact width defaults to terrain only; a regular width defaults to terrain with map inset.
7. **The docked overview elevation strip is always there.** Cycle every view mode again, terrain-primary included. The docked strip under the route visual shows in all of them, carries the rider glyph at the current position, and — with decorations enabled and ghost data present — carries the personal-best, today and family-initial ghosts at their own positions, each coloured by the grade beneath it. This is the strip under the route visual, not the lap-times strip covered by `TST-0262` and `TST-0263`.

## Expect

- Step 1: the layers button cycles terrain with map inset, map with terrain inset, terrain only, map only.
- [android] Step 2: the inset moves to each corner and takes each size. The grip faces the screen's middle; dragging it resizes, tapping it steps the size.
- [ios] Step 2: the inset moves to each corner and takes each size.
- Step 3: while the main view follows the rider, the inset still shows the whole route.
- Step 4: the rider's view mode and inset size come back as they were left.
- Step 5: the second rider has their own view mode, not the first rider's.
- Step 6: a compact width opens in terrain only; a regular width in terrain with map inset.
- Step 7: the docked strip shows in every mode, with the rider and the personal-best, today and family ghosts, each grade-coloured.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0601` | 7 | The docked strip disappearing in one view mode now records the same result as the layers button failing to cycle, so note which of the seven steps failed. |

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This row and the row it absorbed were both among the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

items.name: The pacer rides the route the way a rider would, draws for every tier, and leaves the cockpit untouched when it is off
items.text:
Test on **both platforms**. The engine's arithmetic is covered by unit tests: the Alpe d'Huez times against the ZwiftPower table are asserted in code, not here. This check is for what a rider sees.

## Setup

A KICKR, or another trainer that accepts control, for steps 1 to 13. Have the parity gallery captures open for step 1.

A route with climbs and bends, and an out-and-back route with a turn, for step 10.

Developer Options: "Tier Override (Debug)", to switch between Free, Pro and Family in step 9. Restart the app after each change.

A phone in portrait, for step 13.

Developer Options on Android: under "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)", turn on "Fake a connected trainer", then fully quit and reopen the app. For steps 14 and 16, set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to "Data-only — feature word reports no target bits" and reconnect; set it back to "Off — the trainer's real answer" afterwards.

The iOS build on a second device.

## Steps

### Off, which is the default on a trainer that works

1. On the KICKR, start a route without touching the pacer row. Compare the cockpit with the gallery captures.
2. Start a free ride in SIM without touching the pacer row.

### On, on a drivable trainer

3. Start the same route with the pacer set to **Steady**.
4. Read the control row.
5. Look at the terrain view ahead of the rider.
6. Ride a steep pitch, then shallow ground, then a climb with hairpins. Watch the CADENCE tile and the power target.
7. Tap the preset chip up to **Hard**, watching the pacer on the terrain.
8. Ride under the pacer's number, then over it, watching the power tile.

### Every tier sees it

9. Repeat step 3 as a **FREE** rider, then a **PRO** rider, then a **FAMILY** rider.
10. On the out-and-back route, ride past the turn onto a **reversed lap**.

### Free-ride SIM

11. Start a free ride in SIM with the pacer on, and change the slope.
12. Read the growing profile while changing power.

### The phone

13. On a phone in portrait, with the pacer on, read the control row.

### Data-only

14. Connect the data-only fake trainer and start a route. Try to switch the pacer off.

### A cockpit entered part-way through

15. With the pacer on, on the KICKR, ride ten minutes of a route. Leave the cockpit and come back to it.
16. Repeat step 15 on the data-only fake trainer, where the verdict can arrive after the ride has begun.

## Expect

- Step 1: as before this phase: gear control and slope-mode chip; no segment line, preset chip, `PACER` ghost or power-tile cue.
- Step 2: the free ride is as before this phase too: gear control; no segment line, preset chip, `PACER` ghost or power-tile cue.
- Step 3: a `PACER` ghost draws on the terrain, on the elevation strip and on the map.
- Step 4: the row shows the segment and distance left on one side, **`PACER 230 W ▲`** on the other; `PACER`, not `TARGET`.
- Step 5: the next segment is marked with its target as a chip, and the profile is tinted by segment target zone.
- Step 6: CADENCE reads `AIM 75` on a steep pitch and higher on shallow ground. **The power target holds through the hairpins**, with a slight negative split.
- Step 7: the target rises, and **the pacer's drawn position does not jump**.
- Step 8: the cue on the power tile responds at ±5% and ±10%.
- Step 9: the pacer draws for all three tiers, and **the "Family ghosts" lock chip never appears because of it**.
- Step 10: every other ghost is hidden on the reversed lap, and **the pacer still draws**.
- Step 11: **the target moves within a tick**, and the cadence hint follows.
- Step 12: the profile carries `PACER +120 m` or `−120 m`, and it changes as the rider's power does.
- Step 13: nothing is clipped or wrapped, and there is no per-device layout.
- Step 14: **the pacer is on and cannot be switched off**, and the row reads `TARGET`, not `PACER`.
- Step 15: **the pacer is beside the rider**, where its plan puts it for the elapsed time; not on the start line or kilometres behind.
- Step 16: the pacer is beside the rider, at its planned position for the elapsed time; not on the start line or far behind.

## Not this check

- Whether the pacer choice belongs to the rider and survives a restart, a rider switch and a backup: [[TST-0654-PacerAndPowerSourceBelongToTheRider]].
- The rest of the data-only cockpit: [[TST-0649-RidingByHandInEveryMode]].
- The pacer engine's arithmetic, which unit tests assert.

## What a failure means

A lock chip in step 9 means the pacer's sentinel id is in the visibility filter but not in the lock predicate, which is half the fix. A pacer that vanishes in step 10 means it is being filtered with the ghosts that ignore direction, which it does not resemble. A pacer sitting at the start line in step 15 means its position is still a side effect of the per-second tick rather than a property of the plan.

## Notes

- Step 6: a target that jumps on every bend is the pacing the climb-pacing evidence rejects.
- Step 9 is the second critical finding of the design review, and it is invisible unless the check is tested at each tier.
- Step 10: the pacer was generated for the direction being ridden, which is why it survives the reversed lap.

## History of this check

Steps 15 and 16 were added by TASK-0851. The defect they describe was real, and it was fixed on both platforms while the gallery was being built: only the per-second tick moved the pacer, so a cockpit entered part-way through drew it where the ride started. Nothing asserted it, and leaving and re-entering the cockpit is an ordinary thing a rider does.

items.name: Completion — Save
items.text:
## Setup

Any rider and a trainer that accepts control, or the fake trainer.

## Steps

Ride a workout to its end, tap Save ride, then tap Done on the celebration.

## Expect

- The ride is in History with its time, distance and power.

## Not this check

- The dialog's buttons: [[TST-0684-WhenARideEndsADialogAsksOnlyWhetherToSaveItKeepRidingOrDiscardIt]].
- The celebration between Save ride and Done: [[TST-0685-AfterSaveTheCelebrationLeadsWithTheHeadlineThenTheNumbersAndDoneGoesToHistory]].

Rewritten on 2026-10-10 for [[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]]: Save ride now opens the celebration, and its Done goes to History, on both platforms.
