items.name: Setting a power PB — the celebration's headline, and the chip it leaves on the library
items.text:
## Setup

A heart-rate strap connected for at least 80 % of each ride. A Power workout this rider has never ridden, such as [Debug] ERG Verify (Show debug workouts on). A second rider in the household.

## Steps

1. Ride the workout to its programmed end, tap Save ride, and read the celebration's headline.
2. Ride it to its end again with a lower average heart rate, save, and read the headline.
3. Open Workouts and find that workout's card.
4. Switch to the second rider, then back.

## Expect

- Step 1: `First time on <workout>` is the headline, or one of the Also this ride chips under a higher-ranked fact.
- Step 2: the headline reads `New best on <workout>`, with the heart-rate cost in bpm and `<n> bpm lower than the best from <date>`.
- Step 3: the card carries a `🏆 PB: <n> bpm` chip.
- Step 4: the chip hides for the second rider, and shows again on the way back.

## Not this check

- The trophy in History and the PBs filter: [[TST-0321-History-Trophy-Filter]], which builds a three-ride history of its own.
- The rest of the celebration: [[TST-0685-AfterSaveTheCelebrationLeadsWithTheHeadlineThenTheNumbersAndDoneGoesToHistory]].

## What is automated

*(mostly automated: `PbCalculatorTest` covers the average-HR formula and the validity gate; `PersonalBestServiceTest` covers the FIRST and BETTER transitions; `CelebrationRankerTest` (Android) and `CelebrationRankerTests` (iOS) pick `first` and `best` from the same case table; `CelebrationTextTest` and `CelebrationTextTests` word them; `PbChipTest` covers chip-label rendering for all four domain formats. The end-to-end rides, the rider-switch atomicity and the chip's position on `WorkoutItem` stay manual.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the personal-best card from the end of a ride. The best is now the celebration's headline after Save, as [[REQ-0131-SessionEndComparison]] was amended to say. Step 1 allows a higher-ranked fact, such as a peak power, to take the headline, because a rider who has ridden other workouts that day can earn one; the first time then shows as a chip. The four steps are numbered so each gets its own result.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0320` (Library PB Chip) — the `🏆 PB:` chip on the library card, and its disappearance and return across a rider switch. It is steps 3 and 4.

items.name: Power PB Adherence Fallback (no HRM)
items.text:
## Setup

No heart-rate strap. Show debug workouts on. The rider has ridden [Debug] Mini Ramp to its end once without a strap, stopping pedalling for 30 seconds in the middle, and saved it.

## Steps

1. Ride [Debug] Mini Ramp to its end again without a strap, pedalling throughout. Save, and read the headline.

## Expect

- Step 1: the headline reads `New best on [Debug] Mini Ramp`, with an adherence percentage such as `94 %` and `<n> points better than the best from <date>`.

## Not this check

- The heart-rate cost a strap gives: [[TST-0314-Power-PB-Happy-Path-With-HRM]].

## What is automated

*(mostly automated: `PbCalculatorTest.power falls back to adherence when hrm uptime below 80 percent`; the celebration words a `percent` best with `celebration_comparison_best_points` on Android and the same sentence on iOS, covered by `CelebrationTextTest` and `CelebrationTextTests`. An HRM drop mid-ride stays hardware.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the personal-best card and its footer. The adherence figure now shows as the large number under a `New best on` headline, so the check rides the workout twice: the first ride is setup, and only a better second ride has a best to state ([[REQ-0131-SessionEndComparison]]).

items.name: Route PB Happy Path
items.text:
## Setup

A trainer that accepts control. A circuit route that rolls over at the end of each lap, such as Velodrome, with no personal best for this rider in the current physics version.

## Steps

1. Ride the route through at least one full lap, then tap FINISH, Save ride, and read the headline.
2. Ride it again with a faster lap, to the end, save, and read the headline.

## Expect

- Step 1: `First time on <route>` is the headline, or one of the Also this ride chips under a higher-ranked fact.
- Step 2: the headline reads `New best on <route>`, with the lap time, such as `24:06`, and `<delta> faster than the best from <date>`.

## Not this check

- That a route best from before 2026-06-18 does not compete: [[TST-0636-Physics-Constants-And-PB-Lineage-ISS-0335]].
- The household best on a route, which needs FAMILY and a second rider: the ranking unit tests, `CelebrationRankerTest` and `CelebrationRankerTests`.

## What is automated

*(mostly automated: `PbCalculatorTest` covers per-lap attempt generation and tolerance; `PersonalBestServiceTest.route multi-lap picks the best news for the outcome`; `route lap exactly 1 second faster than pb reports BETTER not EQUAL`; `CelebrationTextTest` and `CelebrationTextTests` word a route best with its delta. The ride stays manual.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the personal-best card. A route best is now the celebration's headline after Save, with the lap time as its large number and the comparison under it ([[REQ-0131-SessionEndComparison]]). Step 1 used to read `Time: 24:18` on the card; a first time has no previous best to compare with.

items.name: HR-Zone PB Happy Path
items.text:
## Setup

A heart-rate strap connected for at least 80 % of each ride. An HR-Zone workout this rider has never ridden, such as [Debug] Single Z3.

## Steps

1. Ride the workout to its programmed end, tap Save ride, and read the headline.
2. Ride it again to its end with a better result, save, and read the headline.

## Expect

- Step 1: `First time on <workout>` is the headline, or one of the Also this ride chips under a higher-ranked fact.
- Step 2: the headline reads `New best on <workout>`, with the efficiency in W/bpm, such as `1.82 W/bpm`, and how much better than the previous best.

## Not this check

- The headline for a ride held in its zone: [[TST-0686-TheCelebrationsHeadlineNamesTheRidesMostNotableFact]].

## What is automated

*(partially automated: `PbCalculatorTest.hr zone primary is efficiency factor np over avg hr`, `PersonalBestServiceTest.first power attempt writes FIRST and upserts pb` (same evaluation path), and the `W/bpm` best in `CelebrationRankerTest` and `CelebrationRankerTests`.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the personal-best card. The best is now the celebration's headline after Save ([[REQ-0131-SessionEndComparison]]). A first ride held mostly in its zone can take the zone headline instead, which is why step 1 also accepts First time on as a chip.

items.name: Manual Stop Disqualifies PB
items.text:
## Setup

A heart-rate strap. A Power or HR-Zone workout this rider has ridden to its end before.

## Steps

Start the workout with repeat off. At about 80 % of its duration, tap FINISH, then Save ride, and read the headline and the chips under it.

## Expect

- Neither the headline nor a chip reads `New best on` or `First time on`: a ride stopped early never counts as a personal best.

## Not this check

- What the headline does say, which depends on the rider's other rides: [[TST-0686-TheCelebrationsHeadlineNamesTheRidesMostNotableFact]].

## What is automated

*(mostly automated: `PbCalculatorTest.power rejects session manually ended at 98 percent of target duration` and `PersonalBestServiceTest.session manually stopped below 99 percent natural completion gate is not qualifying`; the rankers leave `best` and `first` out for an incomplete ride, in `CelebrationRankerTest` and `CelebrationRankerTests`.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the personal-best card and its "Session too short to compare" line. An incomplete ride can still take other headlines, such as a peak power or the week's ride count (DES-0005 section 3), so the check asserts what must be absent.

items.name: A free ride never takes a personal-best headline
items.text:
## Setup

Any rider and a trainer that accepts control.

## Steps

Start a free ride in any mode, end it by hand, tap Save ride, and read the headline and the chips under it.

## Expect

- Neither the headline nor a chip reads `New best on` or `First time on`; a free ride has no target to compare.

## Not this check

- The headlines a free ride can take, such as a distance milestone: [[TST-0686-TheCelebrationsHeadlineNamesTheRidesMostNotableFact]].

## What is automated

*(mostly automated: `PersonalBestServiceTest` free-ride fallback returns NOT_QUALIFYING, and the rankers' free-ride cases in `CelebrationRankerTest` and `CelebrationRankerTests`.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the personal-best card from the end of a ride, so "no card" became "no personal-best headline" on the celebration after Save.

items.name: Ramp Test FTP Calculation
items.text:
## Setup

Show debug workouts on (Android Developer Options; iOS Settings → Developer · Workouts). A trainer that accepts control. Note the rider's FTP before starting.

## Steps

1. Run `[Debug] FTP Ramp` to completion.
2. Tap Save and update FTP, then read the profile FTP.

## Expect

- Step 1: the dialog reads `New FTP detected: <n> W`, about 90 % of the profile FTP, and offers Save and update FTP.
- Step 2: the profile FTP updates.

## Not this check

- The dialog's other cases: [[TST-0684-WhenARideEndsADialogAsksOnlyWhetherToSaveItKeepRidingOrDiscardIt]].

## What is automated

*(partially automated: `RideEndDecisionDialogTest` checks the new-FTP line and Save and update FTP on Android, and `RideEndDecisionTests` on iOS.)*

## Rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] replaced the ride-end summary with a decision dialog. The detected FTP is now a line in that dialog, and UPDATE PROFILE & FINISH is Save and update FTP, which updates the FTP and saves the ride.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: On the smallest phone the ride-end dialog, the celebration, Workouts, History and the rider screen show everything and every action is reachable
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies that the ride-end dialog and the celebration after Save, Workouts, History and the rider selection screen show all their content and keep every action reachable on the smallest supported phone at the largest text size.

## Setup

The release candidate on the smallest supported phone, with the largest text.

- On Android, run `adb shell wm size 720x1280` and `adb shell wm density 320` for a 360 × 640 dp screen, and set Settings → Display → Font size to its largest. Undo both afterwards with `adb shell wm size reset`, `adb shell wm density reset` and the font size.
- On iOS, use the iPhone SE (3rd generation) simulator, 375 × 667 pt, with Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → Larger Text at the largest size.
- A trainer so a ride starts: **Fake a connected trainer** in Android Developer Options, or **Use mock trainer** in iOS Settings → Developer · Trainer, then restart.
- Three riders in the household, one with at least five saved rides. Importing `demo-dave` from Demo Data as a new rider gives one with 18 saved rides.

## Steps

1. Ride any workout for a minute, then tap FINISH, and look at the dialog.
2. Scroll the dialog to its end.
3. Tap Keep riding, finish again, tap Save ride, and scroll the celebration to its end.
4. Open Workouts, pick Heart Rate in the ride-mode strip, and look at the header above the list.
5. As the rider with saved rides, open History, expand the stats card, then expand a ride and scroll through its charts.
6. Open the rider screen and scroll to the last rider.

## Expect

- Step 1: the dialog is a sheet at the bottom; its eyebrow, title and totals are readable, and nothing is cut off at the sides.
- Step 2: Save ride, Keep riding and Discard ride are all visible.
- Step 3: Keep riding returns to the ride; after Save ride, the celebration's numbers, zones and Done can all be reached.
- Step 4: the title and every header button are whole, and at least one workout row is visible.
- Step 5: the This Week cards and every chart are whole, and no chart hides another or the text under it.
- Step 6: every rider and every rider's actions can be reached.

## Not this check

- The cockpit itself: [[TST-0676-OnTheSmallestPhoneEveryCockpitShowsItsTerrainAndWholeNumbers]].
- What the dialog and the celebration say: [[TST-0684-WhenARideEndsADialogAsksOnlyWhetherToSaveItKeepRidingOrDiscardIt]] and [[TST-0685-AfterSaveTheCelebrationLeadsWithTheHeadlineThenTheNumbersAndDoneGoesToHistory]].
- Every size and font scale in turn: the automated grid, `ScreenLayoutRulesTest` and `CelebrationLayoutRulesTest` on Android, `CockpitLayoutRulesTests` (`testRideEndDialog`, `testCelebration`) on iOS.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-09-29 with FEAT-0131's planning. It sat at `level: system` until the feature was built, so the v2.2.0 release test did not owe it early. [[TASK-1009-TheChecksTheFittedCockpitReopens]] moved it into the release test on 2026-09-29. Step 4 now names the Heart Rate library, whose title is the longest, and step 5 names the stats card, whose This Week cards changed.

Steps 1 to 3 rewritten on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]]: [[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] replaced the ride-end summary with a decision dialog, a bottom sheet on a phone, and put the numbers on the celebration after Save. On a phone at the largest text the upload chips move into the celebration's scrolling page and its bottom bar keeps Done.

items.name: When a ride ends, a dialog asks only whether to save it, keep riding or discard it
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies the decision dialog that replaced the ride-end summary on both platforms (DES-0005 section 1): its eyebrow and title for each way a ride ends, its one line of totals, and its three buttons. Steps 8 and 9 verify that a ride that has started cannot be left any other way (ISS-0545).

## Setup

A tablet with a trainer that accepts control. The fake trainer is the cheapest: **Fake a connected trainer** in Android Developer Options, or **Use mock trainer** in iOS Settings → Developer · Trainer, then restart. Any rider. A Power workout with time to spare, such as Sweet Spot Base, and any bundled route.

## Steps

1. Start a Power workout, ride a minute, and tap FINISH.
2. Read the line under the title, and the buttons.
3. Tap Keep riding.
4. Ride the workout to its end.
5. Tap Discard ride.
6. Start a bundled Route ride, ride a minute, and tap FINISH.
7. Discard it. Pick Route, start a Free Ride, ride a minute, and tap FINISH.
8. Tap Keep riding, then PAUSE. Try to go back: the back gesture or key on Android, a back button at the top left on iOS.
9. With the dialog open (on iOS, tap FINISH to open it), try to go back again.

## Expect

- Step 1: eyebrow `<WORKOUT> · <elapsed> OF <planned>`, title Finish the ride?
- Step 2: `<time> · <distance> · <watts> W average`, then Save ride, Keep riding and Discard ride in muted red.
- Step 3: the dialog closes and the workout carries on from where it stopped.
- Step 4: eyebrow `<WORKOUT> · EVERY INTERVAL DONE`, title Ride complete, and only Save ride and Discard ride.
- Step 5: the dialog closes at once, with no second question.
- Step 6: the eyebrow gives the distance ridden of the route's length, such as `STELVIO · 0.6 km OF 24.3 km`.
- Step 7: the eyebrow reads `FREE RIDE · <elapsed>`, and Keep riding is offered.
- Step 8: on Android the dialog opens over the ride. On iOS there is no back button, and FINISH is in the bottom bar.
- Step 9: nothing changes. The dialog stays open and the ride does not start again.

## Not this check

- What Save ride does next, the celebration: [[TST-0685-AfterSaveTheCelebrationLeadsWithTheHeadlineThenTheNumbersAndDoneGoesToHistory]]. That a saved ride reaches History: [[TST-0040-Completion-Save]].
- That Discard ride saves nothing: [[TST-0041-Completion-Discard]].
- That Keep riding returns to a free ride: [[TST-0042-Completion-Resume-Free-Ride]].
- The ramp test's new FTP and Save and update FTP: [[TST-0328-Ramp-Test-FTP-Calculation]].
- The dialog as a bottom sheet on the smallest phone: [[TST-0677-OnTheSmallestPhoneTheRideEndAndThreeOtherScreensShowEverything]].
- The eyebrow of a Quick Ride or a Zone Ride. Android names the mode (`QUICK RIDE · 1:05`), iOS reads `FREE RIDE`; that difference is recorded in TASK-1041 for a decision.
- Every size and text scale: `ScreenLayoutRulesTest` (Android) and `CockpitLayoutRulesTests.testRideEndDialog` (iOS).

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the built dialog: Android `RideEndDecisionDialog` (`RIDE_END_SAVE_TAG`, `RIDE_END_KEEP_RIDING_TAG`, `RIDE_END_DISCARD_TAG`) and iOS `RideEndDecisionDialog` (`rideEnd.save`, `rideEnd.keepRiding`, `rideEnd.discard`). Both platforms upper-case the eyebrow.

items.name: After Save, the celebration leads with the ride's headline, then shows its numbers and zones, and Done goes to History
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies layout B of DES-0005 section 2 on both platforms: the band with the headline, the six numbers for each kind of ride, the time in each heart-rate zone, and Done.

## Setup

A tablet with a trainer that accepts control, or the fake trainer (Android Developer Options → **Fake a connected trainer**; iOS Settings → Developer · Trainer → **Use mock trainer**; restart). A heart-rate strap for steps 4 to 7. Any rider, a Power workout, an HR-Zone workout and a bundled route.

## Steps

1. Without a strap, ride a Power workout to its end and tap Save ride.
2. Read the numbers under the band.
3. Tap Done.
4. With the strap connected, ride a Power workout to its end, save, and read the numbers.
5. Read the heart-rate zone bar under the numbers.
6. Ride an HR-Zone workout to its end, save, and read the numbers.
7. Ride a bundled route for at least one lap, save, and read the numbers.

## Expect

- Step 1: the celebration opens: eyebrow, headline, large number, comparison line, the ride's picture and a Saved to History chip.
- Step 2: time, average power, normalised power, TSS, average heart rate and energy; average heart rate reads `--`.
- Step 3: History opens, with this ride at the top.
- Step 4: the same six numbers, now with the average heart rate filled in.
- Step 5: a stacked bar under Time in heart-rate zone, and a legend for each zone with minutes, such as `Z2 Aerobic 14 min`.
- Step 6: time, average heart rate, average power, distance, TSS and energy.
- Step 7: time, distance, climbed, average power, normalised power and average heart rate.

## Not this check

- Which fact the headline states: [[TST-0686-TheCelebrationsHeadlineNamesTheRidesMostNotableFact]], and the personal-best checks [[TST-0314-Power-PB-Happy-Path-With-HRM]], [[TST-0316-Route-PB-Happy-Path]] and [[TST-0317-HR-Zone-PB-Happy-Path]].
- The upload chips in the bottom bar: [[TST-0687-TheCelebrationShowsEachConnectedAccountsUploadAndOnlyThose]].
- Share: [[TST-0689-TheCelebrationSharesTheRideAsAPictureInFourShapes]].
- The celebration on the smallest phone: [[TST-0677-OnTheSmallestPhoneTheRideEndAndThreeOtherScreensShowEverything]].
- A free ride's six numbers (time, distance, average power, normalised power, average heart rate, energy) are read in [[TST-0686-TheCelebrationsHeadlineNamesTheRidesMostNotableFact]]'s milestone ride, without a separate expectation.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the built screens: Android `CelebrationScreen` (`Routes.RIDE_CELEBRATION`, Done `CELEBRATION_DONE_TAG`) and iOS `CelebrationView` (Done `celebration.done`). Android labels the heart-rate number "Avg heart rate", iOS "Avg HR"; both are the average heart rate.

items.name: The celebration's headline names the ride's most notable fact: a peak power, the time held in a zone, or a distance milestone
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies three of the headline kinds in DES-0005 section 3 from real rides, each set up so that no higher-ranked fact applies: a peak power (rank 3), the time held in a heart-rate zone (rank 6) and a lifetime distance milestone (rank 4). It also checks one "Also this ride" chip. The personal-best headlines are checked by the personal-best checks.

## Setup

A tablet with a trainer that accepts control and a heart-rate strap. Debug builds can use the fake trainer for steps 1 and 2 (Android **Fake a connected trainer**, iOS **Use mock trainer**); steps 3 and 4 need heart rate and distance from a real ride or the mock strap.

- A new rider with no rides, added for this check. As that rider, ride a Quick Ride for six minutes at about 150 W and save it, the same week as step 1.
- Demo Data's `demo-jack` rider file (`demo/riders/demo-jack.ytrider.json.gz`), offline in Drive. Its 12 rides add up to 95.0 km, the last on 19 April 2026, so one ride of 5 km or more crosses 100 km and no earlier ride in the last 90 days competes. Import it again to test this a second time.

## Steps

1. As the new rider, ride a Quick Ride for six minutes at about 200 W, and save.
2. Read Also this ride, below the numbers.
3. Connect the strap. Ride a Zone Ride in zone 2 for ten minutes, holding zone 2, and save.
4. Import `demo-jack` as a new rider. As demo-jack, ride a Free Ride of at least 6 km, and save.

## Expect

- Step 1: `Best 5 minutes since <month>`, the watts as the large number, and `<n> W above the best from <date>`.
- Step 2: a chip reads Second ride this week.
- Step 3: `<minutes> minutes held in zone 2`, a percentage, and `of the ride inside the target zone`.
- Step 4: `100 km indoors since <first ride's date>`, `100 km`, and `13 rides on this trainer. Today is the gold dot.`

## Not this check

- New best on and First time on: [[TST-0314-Power-PB-Happy-Path-With-HRM]], [[TST-0315-Power-PB-Adherence-Fallback-No-HRM]], [[TST-0316-Route-PB-Happy-Path]] and [[TST-0317-HR-Zone-PB-Happy-Path]].
- The household, pacer, laps, week and longest headlines, and the full rank order: the unit tests `CelebrationRankerTest` (Android) and `CelebrationRankerTests` (iOS), which share one case table.
- The same headline after reopening the ride from History: [[TST-0690-HistorysShareOpensAPastRidesCelebration]].
- Each kind's colours. The pictures in DES-0005 show them; the release test does not judge colour.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]]. The setups follow the ranking rules both platforms built (TASK-1031, TASK-1032): a peak power needs an earlier ride in the last 90 days with a lower peak; a free ride never takes a personal-best headline; the longest peak duration wins. `demo-jack`'s distance was summed from the file on 2026-10-10.

items.name: The celebration shares the ride as a picture: four shapes, a card for each fact, two switches, a photo behind the sticker, Share… and Save to Photos
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies the share picker of DES-0005 section 4: the four shapes, the cards a ride earns, the two switches, a photo behind the sticker, Share… and Save to Photos, and the note about Strava. Sharing is free on every tier, so this is tested on a FREE rider.

## Setup

A tablet, a FREE rider and a heart-rate strap. The celebration of a ride saved with heart rate is open, such as the Zone Ride of [[TST-0686-TheCelebrationsHeadlineNamesTheRidesMostNotableFact]]. A photo in the device's library. On iOS, allow Your Trainer to add to Photos when asked.

## Steps

1. Tap Share.
2. Pick Story, Square post, Sticker over a photo and Wide post in turn.
3. Pick Story, and swipe through the pictures.
4. Turn Heart-rate zones off.
5. Turn My name on. Close the picker and open it again.
6. Pick Sticker over a photo, and pick a photo.
7. Tap Share…, and read the share sheet.
8. Close the share sheet. Tap Save to Photos, then open the photo library.
9. Read the note under the buttons.

## Expect

- Step 1: the share picker opens full screen: Shape, the picture, On the picture, Share… and Save to Photos.
- Step 2: the picture is redrawn in each shape, and each carries Your Trainer and `Indoor · <date>` at its foot.
- Step 3: the headline card comes first, then The numbers, then Heart-rate zones and each other card this ride earned.
- Step 4: the thin heart-rate zone strip leaves the picture.
- Step 5: My name is still on, and the rider's name sits above the date on the picture.
- Step 6: the photo fills the picture behind white text with a soft shadow.
- Step 7: the system share sheet offers the picture as an image to other apps.
- Step 8: the picture is in the photo library.
- Step 9: `Strava does not take pictures from other apps. To add this one to the activity, save it and add it in the Strava app.`

## Not this check

- Sharing a ride from History: [[TST-0690-HistorysShareOpensAPastRidesCelebration]].
- Sharing the rider card: [[TST-0691-TheRiderCardIsSharedAsAPictureWithTheWeightHiddenUnlessTurnedOn]].
- The picker as a sheet on a phone, and each card's exact drawing: the snapshot references `ShareCardTests` (iOS) and the Android references TASK-1037 adds.
- A household rival's name on the Household board card, which needs two riders who both allow names: not tested here.
- Whether the sticker stays transparent inside Instagram or Snapchat: the app hands over a PNG; what another app does with it is outside the release test.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the iOS build: Share `celebration.share`, `SharePickerView` with shape rows `share.shape.*`, the paged preview `share.preview`, switches `share.toggle.zones` and `share.toggle.name` (stored as `UserProfile.showNameOnPictures`), `share.photo`, Share… `share.share`, Save to Photos `share.saveToPhotos` and the note `share.stravaNote`. On Android the picker is [[TASK-1037-OnAndroidTheRideIsSharedAsAPicture]]: Share `CELEBRATION_SHARE_TAG` opens `SharePickerScreen`. It landed on 2026-10-10, and the `readiness_for` mark was removed.

items.name: The HR-Zone cockpit on a Zone Ride — entry, zone selector, layout and terrain bands
items.text:
Open Workouts, pick **Heart Rate** in the ride-mode strip, then tap the **Zone Ride** card. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS. A heart-rate monitor must be connected, or the start gate holds the Zone Ride at Connect or Cancel. Every step below reads off that one free ride.

## Setup

A PRO rider with a trainer and a heart-rate strap connected.

## Steps

1. **Entry.** Read the mode the session starts in.
2. **Zone selector.** Read the zone selector, then tap + and - through every zone.
3. **Cockpit layout.** Read where HR and power sit.
4. **Terrain zone bands.** Read the terrain graph.

## Expect

- Step 1: the session starts in HR Zone-Lock mode.
- Step 2: the Z1–Z5 selector, labels in zone colours. + and - cycle Z1 to Z5. Same size as Power's watts and simulation's slope controls.
- Step 3: HR is the centre number, the largest on the cockpit; power is in the left column. No TARGET POWER line.
- Step 4: all five zone bands span the graph's full height. Active zone filled at 20 %, others at 5 %. Power bars subdued.

## What is automated

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.startFreeRide_HR_ZONE_for_HR_tab` and `selectWorkout_HR_ZONE_sets_HR_ZONE_mode_and_seeds_target_from_first_interval` cover the entry-path dispatch; the selector, the layout and the terrain bands stay visual.)*

## Notes

**Test this on a Zone Ride, not on a structured HR workout.** The Z1–Z5 selector is free-ride-only. ISS-0166 R-2 made it so, because a structured workout takes its target zone from the interval plan instead (`ActiveWorkoutScreen.kt:1649-1653`). Testing the **Zone selector** step inside a structured HR workout would fail for a reason that is not a defect.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0172` (Zone Selector) — the +/- buttons cycling Z1–Z5 in zone colours at the same size as the other modes' controls. It is the **Zone selector** step.
- `TST-0175` (Cockpit Layout Swap) — HR as the 84sp centre hero, power in the left column, no TARGET POWER line. It is the **Cockpit layout** step.
- `TST-0176` (Terrain Graph — Zone Bands) — five bands at full graph height, active at 20 % and the rest at 5 %, power bars subdued. It is the **Terrain zone bands** step.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates four independent renders of the same screen. A wrong zone colour, a hero in the wrong column, a missing TARGET POWER suppression and a zone band drawn at the wrong opacity all now record as one failure, so a rider must write down which named step was wrong.

The entry path is the only step of the four that is covered by a unit test. The other three are purely visual, and a silent regression in any of them now costs the same single tick.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were bold-headed paragraphs, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

## Step 3 rewritten for FEAT-0131, 2026-09-29

Step 3 used to give the hero's size as 84sp. Since FEAT-0131 every cockpit number shrinks with one shared scale on a phone, so the hero is 84sp only where the cockpit fits at full size. The line now asks for the largest number instead ([[CHG-20260929-The-Cockpit-Fits-Every-Screen-And-The-Terrain-Keeps-Its-Share]]).
items.rerun: FEAT-0051: entry path changed from mode cycle to Heart Rate tab

invalidated_by.reason: entry path changed from mode cycle to Heart Rate tab

items.name: Auto Algorithm
items.text:
Connect HRM and start HR Zone Z2. Verify power adjusts automatically to bring HR into zone. While HR is still outside the zone the delta pill keeps showing a signed step — `▲ Nw` or `▼ Nw` — and the watts number blinks each time the controller fires. Once HR settles inside the zone the pill reads `HOLD` and the heartbeat bar keeps cycling, which is the controller watching rather than acting. *(partially automated: `HrZoneLockControllerTest` covers the converge → locked transition + ceiling-band hysteresis; live HRM stream stays hardware-dependent.)*

There is no orange "converging" or green "locked" text. ISS-0166 and ISS-0167 replaced that banner with the delta pill and the heartbeat bar; the controller's `CONVERGING` / `LOCKED` / `ADJUSTING` states are still computed but no longer named on screen.

## Expect

- Power adjusts by itself to bring HR into the zone.
- While HR is outside the zone, the delta pill shows `▲ Nw` or `▼ Nw`, and the watts blink at each adjustment.
- Once HR settles in the zone, the pill reads `HOLD` and the heartbeat bar keeps cycling.
items.rerun: ISS-0164: controller hardening — verify the converge → locked path is unaffected by the new hysteresis and sentinel changes

invalidated_by.reason: controller hardening — verify the converge → locked path is unaffected by the new hysteresis and sentinel changes

items.name: Terrain graph after a mid-ride zone switch — the HR line and the band both keep their history
items.text:
On a Zone Ride, start in Z2, ride for a minute, then switch to Z3 with the zone selector. Both steps read off the graph after that single switch.

## Steps

1. **HR line colour history.** After the switch, read the HR line.
2. **Zone band history.** Read the highlighted zone bands.

## Expect

- Step 1: the Z2 stretch stays in the Z2 colour, the Z3 stretch in Z3's. Each goes red where HR was above its zone, blue below.
- Step 2: the Z2 band is highlighted only over the minute in Z2. The Z3 band is highlighted from the switch onward.

## Notes

The zone selector is free-ride-only (ISS-0166 R-2), so this has to be a Zone Ride rather than a structured HR workout — a structured workout takes its zone from the interval plan and gives the rider nothing to switch.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0178` (Terrain Graph — Zone Band History) — the previous zone's band covering only its own time segment after a mid-ride switch. It is the **Zone band history** step.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates an HR line that loses its colour history from a zone band that bleeds across the switch point. They are two layers of the same graph and both are checked after the same single zone switch, so a rider must write down which layer was wrong.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were bold-headed paragraphs, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.name: HR Zone Start Requires HRM
items.text:
## Setup

A trainer connected and a heart-rate strap to hand, switched on. On Android, Tier Override in Developer Options sets the tier. On iOS, Settings → Developer · Tier override sets PRO or FAMILY, which is enough here.

## Steps

1. Set tier override to FREE / PRO / FAMILY (any). Open the Equipment Hub from the equipment icons at the end of the top bar and tap Forget on the Heart Rate slot, so no monitor is bound. On Workouts, pick **Heart Rate** in the ride-mode strip, tap the Zone Ride card, and read what appears. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS.
2. Tap **Connect**.
3. Connect the HRM from the scanner, then read the screen that opens.
4. Tap Start.

## Expect

- Step 1: no cockpit. A prompt reads *HR-Zone rides are steered by heart rate, so they need a heart-rate monitor.* **Connect** and **Cancel**, no Skip.
- Step 2: the heart-rate scanner opens.
- Step 3: the Zone Ride cockpit opens by itself, with `[ ▶ Start ]` as its main button.
- Step 4: the ride begins.

## Where it came from

TASK-0399 / ISS-0183.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were bold-headed paragraphs, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.name: Session Reset
items.text:
Complete an HR Zone ride. Go back and start a new free ride. Verify no stale data from previous ride visible on terrain graph. *(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.resetWorkout_clears_targetLoops_and_loopCount` + `startFreeRide_clears_previously_selected_workout` — state reset covered; terrain-graph rendering stays visual.)*

## Expect

- The new ride's terrain graph shows nothing left over from the previous ride.

items.name: HR Free Ride Unconstrained
items.text:
## Setup

A trainer and a heart-rate strap connected. On Android, set Tier Override (Debug) to Free in Developer Options. On iOS, Tier override has no FREE choice: in Settings → Developer · Tier override tap Reset to real entitlements while signed in to a sandbox account that holds no Your Trainer purchase, then fully close and reopen the app.

## Steps

1. On FREE tier, start Zone Ride (HR Free Ride), end it, and start it again.
2. **Re-verify:** ISS-0170 fix removed the leftover cockpit START-button paywall. Read the START button.

## Expect

- Step 1: it starts, and starts again, without limit.
- Step 2: the START button shows no "PRO" lock.

## What is automated

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.startFreeRide_HR_ZONE_for_HR_tab` covers the dispatch path; `LicensingManagerTest` confirms Free-Ride dispatch never touches the structured-workout counter; cockpit START-button rendering on FREE tier stays manual.)*

## Corrected 2026-09-12 — "no token is consumed" named a counter that no longer exists

The original wording asked a rider to confirm a token was *not* consumed. FEAT-0096 deleted the token counter entirely (`LicensingManager.kt:148-155`), so there was nothing to watch not happening — a negative check against an absent mechanism reads as passing whatever the app does.

What is still worth testing is the outcome: a FREE rider can start a Zone Ride as many times as they like. That is now what the row asks for.

The FREE line moved to per-workout content gating via `FreeBundledCatalog`; [[TST-0062-Free-Tier-Locks]] holds that inventory. [[TST-0217-HR-Structured-Consumes-Token-Start]] was retired by the same removal.

items.name: Profile Master/Detail Layout
items.text:
(TASK-0383)

## Setup

Any rider, on a tablet and on a phone, on each platform.

## Steps

1. On tablet, tap the rider's name in the navigation rail, then the **Profile** button under the current rider's card. Read the chips at the top.
2. Select each category in turn.
3. On phone, tap the rider's name in the bottom bar, then the **Profile** button under the current rider's card.

## On iOS

On iOS the rider's profile is its own screen since PHASE-025, reached from the rider's name in the tab bar or rail, then **Profile**, which is next to **Switch rider**. It is one scrolling list of sections rather than a category rail; Edwin accepted the list layout on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]), when it still lived in Settings. On iOS test these steps in place of the Android steps above; the step numbers match. Test each one on the tablet and on the phone.

1. Tap the rider's name in the tab bar or rail, then **Profile**, and read the **Profile** section at the top.
2. Scroll the same list through that rider's connected services (Strava, intervals.icu) and **Data** sections.
3. Change a value in one section and scroll to another.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: a strip of chips at the top: Profile, Preferences, Connected, Data, each with an icon. No second rail beside the navigation rail.
- [ios] Step 1: the **Profile** section at the top of the Profile screen belongs to the current rider.
- [android] Step 2: the section below the chips changes, and the rider-card header stays.
- [ios] Step 2: one scrolling list reaches Strava, intervals.icu and **Data**, with no category rail or chip strip. Appearance and other app settings are not here.
- [android] Step 3: on the phone, the same chip strip at the top.
- [ios] Step 3: the same rider stays selected.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one paragraph of prose on Android and one bulleted list on iOS, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

## Changed 2026-09-27

The Android lines described a category rail of the profile's own on a tablet. TASK-0959 replaced it with the chip strip at every width, which `UserProfileScreen.kt` draws, so the check now asks for the chip strip on both sizes ([[ISS-0518-TST0022StillExpectsASecondRailOnATabletProfile|ISS-0518]]). The check was already owed on Android for REL-0017, with no result since its invalidation on 2026-09-22, so no result is lost.

items.name: Rider Card on Profile
items.text:
Switch to a rider with 5+ completed sessions, then open the current rider's profile: tap the rider's name in the bottom bar on a phone or in the rail on a tablet, then **Profile**. On Android, **Profile** is the button under the current rider's card. On iOS it is next to **Switch rider**. The whole check reads off that one card, without a trainer and without a ride.

## Setup

A rider with at least five completed sessions. Only the current rider's profile opens, so switch to that rider first.

## Steps

1. **The card renders.** Look at the top of the profile.
2. **Six attributes carry numbers.** Read the six attributes on the card.
3. **The overall rating carries a band.** Read the overall rating on the card.

## Expect

- Step 1: a rider card with a six-axis radar chart, at the top of the profile.
- Step 2: PWR, SPR, CLB, END, CON and REC each show a rating from 0 to 99.
- Step 3: an overall 0–99 rating with its band label, such as "Recreational" or "Competitive".

## Notes

*(partially automated: `RiderCardTest` + `RatingEngineTest` + `RiderAttributeCalculatorTest` — text render, clamp to 0–99, anchor interpolation, null-HRE redistribution, overall weighting and band thresholds are all covered; the radar chart's Canvas rendering stays visual.)*

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0418]] (step 2) and [[TST-0419]] (step 3). All three read the same card on the same screen, so a rider was being asked to open one profile three times.

One tick no longer separates a card that failed to render at all from a card that rendered with a missing attribute or a missing band label. If the tick fails, write down which of the three steps it was.

items.name: HR zones display Z1–Z7 and derive from Max HR / LTHR
items.text:
With a Max HR set, open the current rider's profile: tap the rider's name in the bottom bar on a phone or in the rail on a tablet, then **Profile**. On Android, **Profile** is the button under the current rider's card. On iOS it is next to **Switch rider**, and these fields are in the Profile section of that screen; they are no longer in Settings. Everything below happens on that one screen. (TASK-0386 for the estimator dialog)

## Setup

Any rider with a Max HR set. Know the rider's birth year, or an age to enter, for step 3.

## Steps

1. **Seven zones render.** Read the HR zones.
2. **Typing Max HR re-derives LTHR.** Change Max HR by typing.
3. **The Max HR estimator shows both formulas.** Tap `Estimate…` next to Max HR and enter an age.
4. **The estimator writes Tanaka.** Tap `Use X bpm`.
5. **A manual LTHR survives a screen re-entry.** Edit LTHR by hand, leave the screen and come back.
6. **A manual LTHR gives way on the next Max HR change.** Change Max HR again.

## Expect

- Step 1: seven zones with bpm ranges: Recovery, Aerobic, Tempo, SubThreshold, SuperThreshold, Aerobic Capacity, Anaerobic.
- Step 2: LTHR re-derives to 88 % of Max HR, for a Max HR of 100–220 bpm.
- Step 3: both estimates show live: Simple (220 − age) and Tanaka (208 − 0.7 × age). Age pre-fills from a stored birth year.
- Step 4: the **Tanaka** value, not the Simple one, lands in Max HR, and LTHR re-derives from it as in step 2.
- Step 5: the manual LTHR is still there.
- Step 6: LTHR re-derives and replaces the manual value.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0025]] (steps 3 and 4). The estimator dialog was already the second half of step 2's derivation path, so the two rows opened the same dialog for different reasons.

Step 3's two-formula display is carried over deliberately. Showing both and writing Tanaka is the whole behaviour, and a version that shows one formula or writes the Simple value would pass a looser step.

One tick no longer separates a zone table that renders wrong from an estimator that computes or writes the wrong bpm. It also no longer separates the estimator's display from what it writes.

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps under `## Steps` with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: The rider card is shared as a picture, with the weight hidden unless the rider turns it on
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies DES-0005 section 6 and [[FEAT-0078-ShareRiderCard]]: the rider card's Share opens the share picker with two shapes, the picture carries the full card with the weight hidden by default, and the weight setting is remembered for each rider.

## Setup

Any tier, with two riders whose weight is set. Neither has turned on weight for pictures yet.

## Steps

1. Open the first rider's card Share.
2. Read the picture.
3. Turn Weight on.
4. Close the picker, and open the same rider's Share again.
5. Open the second rider's card Share.
6. Tap Share…, and read the share sheet.

## Expect

- Step 1: the share picker opens with only Story and Square post, and one picture, the rider card.
- Step 2: the full rider card on the rider's colour, with FTP but no weight, and Your Trainer and `Indoor · <today>` at the foot.
- Step 3: the rider's weight appears on the card.
- Step 4: Weight is still on.
- Step 5: Weight is off for the second rider.
- Step 6: the system share sheet offers the rider card picture as an image.

## Not this check

- The rider card on the screen, which always shows the weight: [[TST-0417-Rider-Card-Profile]].
- Sharing a ride: [[TST-0689-TheCelebrationSharesTheRideAsAPictureInFourShapes]].
- A pre-filled caption: [[TASK-0547-RiderCardSharedCaption]] was cancelled on 2026-10-10, and neither platform sends one.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the iOS build: Share is the first entry of each rider card's long-press menu on the rider screen (`riders.share`), opening `SharePickerView` with `ShareSubject.riderCard`; the Weight switch is `share.toggle.weight`, stored as `UserProfile.showWeightOnPictures` for that rider. With Weight off, iOS also hides W/kg, because FTP and W/kg together give the weight away. On Android the action is [[TASK-0546-RiderCardShareAffordance]] (`RIDER_CARD_SHARE_TAG` in `RiderCardMenu`) and the switch [[TASK-0548-RiderCardWeightToggle]] (`showWeightOnPictures`), which also hides W/kg. They landed on 2026-10-10, and the `readiness_for` mark was removed.

items.name: Strava-detail subsection — full localisation (CHG-20260502 Strava L10n gap fix)
items.text:
With Strava linked on the active rider, switch device language to German. Open Profile → the Strava section expands to show the "Connected" subsection with three rows: **Backlog** (count of pending uploads with retry button), **Reconnect for read access** (only when the rider authorised the legacy write-only scope), **Refresh now** (force-pull historical activities). Verify every label, subtitle, button text, and plural form (e.g. `1 Workout in Warteschlange` vs `7 Workouts in Warteschlange`) renders in German — no English literals slip through. Spot-check French and Japanese for the same three rows. **Pre-fix:** seven hardcoded EN literals in `StravaDetailRow.kt` (body / actionLabel / message / hint / errorText) leaked through even when device locale was non-EN; the new `HardcodedComposeTextTest` regex set (named-arg literals + body / subtitle / actionLabel / message / hint / errorText / prompt / confirmText / dismissText) catches this class of regression at unit-test time.

On iOS the Strava section of the rider's Profile has no Backlog, Reconnect for read access or Refresh now row. It shows Connected with Unlink, a **Refresh Strava status** button and, while rides wait, an **Upload N pending rides** button (`SettingsView.swift`). Edwin accepted these as the iOS equivalent on 2026-09-25 ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]], decision 19), so on iOS check that those labels render in German, French and Japanese.

## Expect

- [android] Backlog, Refresh now and, where shown, Reconnect for read access: every label, subtitle, button and plural is translated, with no English.
- [ios] Connected, Unlink, Refresh Strava status and Upload N pending rides are translated in each language, with no English.

items.name: One Strava round trip on one rider — link, survive a restart, unlink
items.text:
In Profile → Connected on Android, or the Strava section of the rider's Profile on iOS, on a **PRO or FAMILY** rider with no Strava link.

## Steps

1. **The control lives on the rider profile.** Look for a Strava connection in Settings, then on the rider profile.
2. **The unlinked render.** Read the Strava row.
3. **The Switch opens a browser, not the Strava app.** Tap the Switch. On iOS, tap the Connect with Strava button.
4. **On return.** Complete the flow.
5. **The link survives a restart.** Fully close the app and reopen it.
6. **Unlinking is the same Switch, going off.** Turn the Switch off. On iOS, tap Unlink.

## Expect

- Step 1: Strava link and unlink are on the rider's profile; nothing in Settings offers a Strava connection.
- [android] Step 2: the orange "Connect with Strava" image leads the row, with a Switch on the right, off.
- [ios] Step 2: the orange "Connect with Strava" button is the section's only control; there is no Switch.
- [android] Step 3: Strava sign-in opens in Chrome, not the Strava app.
- [ios] Step 3: Strava sign-in opens in a Safari sheet, not the Strava app.
- [android] Step 4: the Switch is on, the subtitle reads "Connected — completed workouts upload automatically", and the image is unchanged.
- [ios] Step 4: the section reads Connected with a green tick, and Unlink replaces the button.
- [android] Step 5: the Switch is still on, with the connected subtitle.
- [ios] Step 5: the Strava section still reads Connected.
- [android] Step 6: it unlinks at once, with no confirmation; the Switch is off, the subtitle reads "Link your Strava account to auto-upload completed workouts", image unchanged.
- [ios] Step 6: Unlink brings back the Connect with Strava button at once, with no confirmation.

## Notes

*(TASK-0388)*

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0098]] (step 1), [[TST-0100]] (steps 3 and 4), [[TST-0104]] (step 3), [[TST-0101-Status-Persists-After-App-Restart]] (step 5) and [[TST-0470-Disconnect]] (step 6). All six describe one OAuth round trip on one rider, and nobody would complete the Strava authorisation six times to tick them separately.

Steps 5 and 6 were added later the same day. Two agents were briefed on this row at once, one finished first, and the second correctly backed out rather than overwrite — which left `TST-0101` and `TST-0470` unmerged until this was noticed. The overlap was a briefing error in [[TASK-0891-TakeTheUnambiguousMerges]], not a disagreement about the merge.

One tick no longer separates a control in the wrong place, an OAuth flow that opens the wrong thing, a token that does not survive a restart, and an unlink that does not take. **Step 5 is the one most worth writing down separately**, because a link that works until the app closes looks perfect during the release test and fails for every rider afterwards. Step 3 is the one worth writing down if it fails, because opening the Strava app instead of a browser silently breaks per-rider credentials rather than showing an error.

## Corrected — 2026-09-12

The linked state shows no second brand mark and no Disconnect button. This row used to expect a "Compatible with Strava" mark next to a muted `Disconnect` text button once the OAuth flow returned. `UserProfileScreen.kt:1038-1089` renders one `SettingsRow` whose `leadingContent` is `btn_strava_connect` unconditionally, and whose trailing slot holds a single `Switch` for a paid rider. Unlinking is that Switch going off, which is now step 6 of this row.

`compatible_with_strava.png` does ship in the APK, and no Kotlin file references it — it is never drawn in any state. That is [[ISS-0436-StravaBrandMarkShipsButIsNeverShown]], open, and whether Strava's brand guidelines require the mark when connected is the question it carries. Do not fix it from this row.

A FREE rider is out of scope for this check: `:1055` renders an Upgrade `Button` in place of the Switch, so there is no toggle to tap and no OAuth flow to start. [[TST-0471]] tests that path.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test read them as one part and could give the whole check only one mark. They now sit under `## Steps`, with one expectation each under `## Expect`, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

## iOS wording, 2026-09-24

Edwin decided on 2026-09-17 to accept the iOS layout where it differs from Android, and to give each check an iOS variant that names the iOS screen and the same underlying result (ADR-0007; [[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]). Since PHASE-025 the iOS app keeps Strava in the current rider's Profile, reached from the rider item in the bar or rail (`RiderProfileView`, `SettingsView.stravaSection`; [[TASK-0949-ProfileLivesUnderTheRider]]). Settings has no Strava section. It has no Switch: an unlinked rider sees the official Connect with Strava button, and a linked rider sees Connected with an Unlink button. The expectations above now name both, so the iOS test no longer asks for Android's Profile row ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit]]).

items.name: Backlog row — upload-all flow
items.text:
With N unuploaded sessions for the linked rider, the Backlog row shows `N rides captured locally that haven't been uploaded yet…` + an `Upload all` OutlinedButton (Strava-orange border). Tap → Toast confirms `Queued N rides for Strava upload.`, each session's pill flips to `Uploading…`, and they complete (or WorkManager holds them for network). *(TASK-0388)*

On iOS the Strava section of the rider's Profile shows an **Upload N pending rides** button instead of the Backlog row, with no confirmation toast (`SettingsView.swift`). Edwin accepted it as the iOS equivalent on 2026-09-25 ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]], decision 19).

## Expect

- [android] The tap shows `Queued N rides for Strava upload.`, each ride's pill reads `Uploading…`, and the uploads complete.
- [ios] The section shows `Upload N pending rides`. The tap shows `Uploading…` on the button and on each ride's History pill.
- [ios] Each upload completes, and the button disappears once nothing is pending.

items.name: The Strava refresh row in both of its states
items.text:
One row, two titles, depending on how many ride links are unresolved. Test it with unresolved links first, then again once they have resolved.

## Procedure

1. **Unresolved links — the row counts them and offers Refresh.** On a rider with M unresolved ride links — legacy uploads, or activities the async processing missed — the row title reads `Ride links`, shows the count, and carries a `Refresh` OutlinedButton. Tap it: a toast confirms `Refreshing Strava ride links…`, a `matched sessionId=… → activityId=…` log line appears for each session resolved, and once the count reaches zero the title reverts to `Refresh Strava status`.
2. **Nothing unresolved — the row is still there.** With every uploaded session carrying its `stravaActivityId`, the title is `Refresh Strava status`, not `Ride links`, and the body reads *"Re-check uploaded rides against Strava…"*. Tap Refresh: the reconcile sweep runs, and any deletion it detects flips the corresponding history row back to `[☁] Strava`. The row being visible here is the whole point — before TASK-0400 it was hidden when there was nothing to update, which left no entry point for deletion detection at all.

## Expect

- [android] Step 1: `Ride links` with the count and Refresh. Refresh logs `matched sessionId=… → activityId=…` per ride, then the title reads `Refresh Strava status`.
- [android] Step 2: the row is still there as `Refresh Strava status`, its body reads *"Re-check uploaded rides against Strava…"*, and Refresh turns a ride deleted on Strava back to `[☁] Strava`.
- [ios] Step 1: one `Refresh Strava status` button, no `Ride links` count; the tap turns waiting rides' History pills to `View on Strava`.
- [ios] Step 2: the button is still there, and the tap detects a ride deleted on Strava.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0479-Ride-Links-Row-Refresh-Flow]] | the `Ride links` title, the count, and the refresh flow that clears it | step 1 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0479** — the two states are the same row rendering differently, so a title that has stopped switching now fails the same verdict as a refresh that does nothing; the evidence has to say which state was wrong.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- The row's title and body in each state, and the log lines from each Refresh.

## iOS equivalent, 2026-09-25

iOS has one **Refresh Strava status** button in the Strava section of the rider's Profile, always shown while Strava is linked. It re-links uploaded rides that lack their activity and detects rides deleted on Strava (`SettingsView.swift`, `StravaService.reconcileMissingActivityIds` and `reconcileDeletions`). Edwin accepted it as the iOS equivalent of the two-state row on 2026-09-25 ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]], decision 19). The iOS lines under Expected results say what to look for.

## Setup

A PRO rider and an intervals.icu account with at least one workout.

## Steps

Tap Link for intervals.icu and complete the OAuth flow in the system browser.
2. Force-stop and reopen.
3. Tap disconnect, then browse the intervals.icu library.

## Expect

- Step 1: back in the app, intervals.icu reads **Linked**, names the athlete, and offers disconnect.
- Step 2: the link survived.
- Step 3: it reads unlinked, and the library asks to link again instead of loading.

## Notes

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

items.name: Per-rider export — location, tier gate and default filename
items.text:
## Setup

**PRO or FAMILY tier, with at least two riders, one of them named something like "Sarah Jones".**

## Steps

1. **The row lives on the rider profile.** Open the current rider's profile → Data: tap the rider's name in the bottom bar or rail, then **Profile**. On Android, **Profile** is the button under the current rider's card. On iOS it is next to **Switch rider**, and Data is a section of the same Profile screen.
2. **It is per-rider.** Switch to a different rider, then open their Profile. To switch on Android, tap the rider's name, then the other rider's card. On iOS, tap the rider's name, then **Switch rider**, and pick the other rider.
3. **PRO and FAMILY are not gated.** With a rider selected, run the Export row.
4. **The default filename is pre-filled.** Read the filename in the SAF "Save As" dialog. On iOS, read the filename the Files save sheet offers.

## Expect

- Step 1: an "Export My Data" row, with the rider's name in the default filename.
- Step 2: the same row, carrying this rider's name.
- [android] Step 3: the row is enabled, and it saves a `.ytrider.json.gz` file through the Save As dialog (SAF).
- [ios] Step 3: the row is enabled, and it saves a `.ytrider.json.gz` file through the Files save sheet.
- [android] Step 4: the Save As dialog offers `Sarah-Jones-YYYY-MM-DD.ytrider.json.gz`.
- [ios] Step 4: the Files save sheet offers `Sarah-Jones-YYYY-MM-DD.ytrider.json.gz`.

## Notes

The export was previously surfaced in Settings; it lives on the rider profile so the rider context is unambiguous.

The full sanitisation and date contract is pinned in `RiderFilenameTest` (12 tests); step 4 exists only because Compose-test cannot drive the system SAF dialog.

*(partially automated: `UserRepositoryTest.empty_db_has_no_users` + `insert_persists_user_and_surfaces_in_allUsers_flow` cover the visibility data condition, `LicensingManagerTest` covers tier resolution, and `RiderFileSerializationTest` covers the produced file's shape; the Profile-screen rendering, the button enable-state and the SAF dialog stay manual.)*

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0278]] (step 3) and [[TST-0279]] (step 4). One screen, one rider, one SAF invocation — nobody would set this up three times.

[[TST-0277]] stays separate. It tests the FREE tier's export gate, and a leaking export gate is a revenue defect rather than another reading of this screen.

One tick no longer separates a missing row from a disabled button from a wrong filename. The three fail for different reasons in different files, so write down the step number.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps under `## Steps` with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is otherwise unchanged.
