items.name: Each tab's primary card starts its own ride mode, in that tab's accent
items.text:
Three rides, one from each ride mode's primary card. The modes are picked in the ride-mode strip. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS. Read the ride mode and the cockpit accent on each before ending it.

## Setup

A FREE rider with a trainer connected and a heart-rate strap connected, or the mock HRM from Developer Options. Step 3 needs the strap: an HR-Zone ride does not start without one.

## Procedure

1. **Power → ERG.** Pick **Power** in the ride-mode strip, then tap its primary card. The session starts in ERG mode: watt plus/minus controls, no gear, no slope.
2. **Route → Simulation.** Pick **Route** in the ride-mode strip, then tap its primary card. The session starts in SIMULATION mode, with slope and gear controls visible.
3. **Heart Rate → Zone lock.** Pick **Heart Rate** in the ride-mode strip, then tap its primary card. A heart-rate monitor must be connected: without one the start gate stops the Zone Ride with Connect and Cancel, and offers no Skip. The session starts in HR Zone-Lock, with the Z1–Z5 zone selector visible.
4. **The cockpit accent matches the mode it came from.** On each of the three rides, the cockpit header metrics — duration, distance, HR — use that mode's accent colour. In HR Zone mode additionally: the per-zone elements (zone label text, progress-bar fill, Z# selector) use **per-zone** colours, green at Z2 and red at Z5, while the hero HR number stays in the HR tab's colour.

*(Partially automated: `FreeRideCardTest` covers each tab's card copy and `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest` covers each tab's ride-mode dispatch. The ERG watt controls, the slope and gear controls, the zone selector and every colour above stay visual.)*

## Expect

- Step 1: the ride starts in ERG, with watt + and − controls, no gear and no slope.
- Step 2: the ride starts in SIMULATION, with slope and gear controls.
- Step 3: the ride starts in HR Zone-Lock, with the Z1–Z5 zone selector.
- Step 4: header metrics take the mode's accent. HR Zone: zone label, bar and Z# green at Z2, red at Z5; HR number in tab colour.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0185-Route-Tab-Free-Ride-Simulation]] | the Route tab's card starts a SIMULATION ride | step 2 |
| [[TST-0186-HR-Tab-Zone-Ride-Zone-Lock]] | the HR tab's card starts an HR Zone-Lock ride | step 3 |
| [[TST-0189-Cockpit-Accent-Matches-Tab]] | the cockpit accent follows the tab, with per-zone colours in HR mode | step 4 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0185** — one tab dispatching the wrong ride mode now records the same as all three doing so, which matters because a single wrong dispatch is the likelier regression.
- **TST-0186** — the HR path is the one with a second control surface, the zone selector, and its absence no longer fails a row of its own.
- **TST-0189** — colour is checked on all three rides at once, so a single tab whose accent has drifted is written in the evidence rather than in the verdict.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- Ride mode and accent observed on each of the three rides, named per tab.

items.name: Route Library Populated
items.text:
## Setup

Any rider on a fresh install, with Show debug workouts off in Developer Options. The ride modes are picked in the ride-mode strip. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS.

2. Pick **Heart Rate** in the ride-mode strip.

## Expect

- Step 1: 21 bundled routes are listed, from `route_flat_10k` to `route_mont_ventoux`.
- Step 2: 12 bundled HR-Zone workouts are listed.

## Notes

*(partially automated: `WorkoutRepositoryLibraryTest.getAllWorkouts_returns_bundled_assets_for_fresh_install` verifies ≥20 bundled workouts surface; per-tab filtering + card rendering stay visual.)*

`assets/workouts/` holds 25 files with `workoutType: ROUTE` and 16 with `workoutType: HR_ZONE`. Four of each are `debug_route_*` / `hr_debug_*` fixtures, hidden unless Developer Settings → **Show debug workouts** is on, which is why the visible counts are 21 and 12. The empty "coming soon" state this row was written against is long gone; the note carried a `Phase 3` invalidation condition until 2026-09-12 that the shipped assets had already satisfied.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.name: Loop Label — uniform across paradigms
items.text:
Start a multi-lap ride on each of Power, Route, HR-Zone (set repeat to 3 on each). Verify the loop indicator renders as `[Repeat icon] N / 4` at TopCenter on all three (Route's out-and-back uses `[SwapHoriz icon]`). Note: total = `targetLoops + 1` because the engine treats `targetLoops` as repeats AFTER the initial lap (so "repeat 3" = 4 total laps). On the **last lap** (lap 4 of 4), the lap label `[icon] 4 / 4` stays visible but the structured-workout LOOP BRACKET hides (no more repeats coming). Mid-ride, tap the repeat button to cycle off → label collapses to `[icon] N / N`; bracket also hides. Set repeat to ∞ → label reads `[icon] N / ∞`. (TASK-0405 / ISS-0182 — total semantics + bracket-vs-label separation, 2026-04-26.)

## Expect

- The loop label reads `[Repeat icon] N / 4` at top centre on Power, Route and HR-Zone.
- On lap 4 of 4 the label stays and the loop bracket hides.
- Cycled off, it reads `[icon] N / N` and the bracket hides. At ∞ it reads `[icon] N / ∞`.

items.name: Favourites — the star turns red and stays red

**Persistence.** Leave the screen and come back. The workout is still favourited and the star is still red.

items.name: Export HR Workout
items.text:
## Steps

1. Name an HR-Zone workout `Sweet Spot: 2x20`. Tap Share on it and save the shared file to Drive.
2. Import the saved file back into Your Trainer.

## Expect

- Step 1: the name that lands in Drive ends `.ytw`.
- Step 2: the file imports back into Your Trainer.

## Notes

*(partially automated: `BackupFileSerializationTest` covers `.ytw` JSON round-trip for HR_ZONE workoutType; Share intent + SAF save stay manual.)*

**Check the file that lands, not the one that is produced (ADR-0013, 2026-09-05).** "A `.ytw` file is produced" was true of the cache file and false of what the rider ended up with: the share subject was `Your Trainer Workout: <name>`, Google Drive names the saved file from the subject, and the `.ytw` was lost. Save the shared file to Drive and confirm the landed name ends `.ytw`, then import it back into Your Trainer — `WorkoutSelectionScreen` refuses an import whose name has no known extension, so a lost extension breaks the round trip into our own app. Name the workout `Sweet Spot: 2x20` first; the colon is the character that caused ISS-0387. Full test: [[TST-0646-SharedFileSurvivesADriveRoundTrip]].

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.name: Import on the Heart Rate tab — a .ytw lands, a .zwo is refused
items.text:
## Setup

A PRO rider. A previously exported `.ytw` and a `.zwo` file on the device or in Drive.

On Workouts, pick **Heart Rate** in the ride-mode strip. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS. Tap Import twice and feed the picker a different file each time.

**A .ytw imports.** Pick a previously exported `.ytw`. It imports and appears in the Heart Rate library with its zones intact.

**A .zwo is refused.** Tap Import again and pick a `.zwo` file. A snackbar reads "Unsupported file type — please select a .ytw file" and carries a Retry action that re-opens the picker. The workout does not import.

*(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` covers the tier gate; `IntervalDeserializerTest` covers the `targetHrZone` round trip through Gson; `ZwoParserTest` covers `.zwo` parsing. The SAF picker, the snackbar copy and the per-tab extension allowlist stay manual.)*

The allowlist is per tab: the Heart Rate tab accepts `.ytw` only, while the Power tab also takes `.zwo` (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:938-942`). That is why the refusal has to be tested on this tab specifically — the same `.zwo` would import happily one tab over.

## Expect

- The `.ytw` imports into the Heart Rate library with its zones intact.
- The `.zwo` is refused: "Unsupported file type — please select a .ytw file", with Retry, and nothing imports.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0213` (ZWO Blocked on HR Tab) — picking a `.zwo` on the Heart Rate tab and reading the refusal message. It is the **A .zwo is refused** step, and it keeps its own named step because it is the negative half of the same Import button.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates a `.ytw` that fails to import from a `.zwo` that imports when it should not. Those are opposite failures of the same allowlist, so a rider must write down which named step failed.

`TST-0213` said "toast". The message is a snackbar with a Retry action (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:944-951`); a toast is only the fallback when no scaffold snackbar host is available. The copy itself was and remains exact. Corrected here on 2026-09-12 rather than carried into a freshly authored body.

items.name: The Heart Rate tab on FREE — New, Import and Share are all gated
items.text:
## Setup

A FREE rider. Tier Override in Developer Options sets FREE without a purchase.

On FREE tier, open Workouts and pick **Heart Rate** in the ride-mode strip. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS. All three steps are on that one screen, on that one tier.

**New.** Tap the "New" button. It carries a lock icon, and the tap goes to the paywall.

**Import.** Tap "Import". It carries a lock icon, and the tap goes to the paywall.

**Share.** Open an HR-Zone workout's context menu and look for Share. It is either absent or locked with a paywall redirect.

*(partially automated: `LicensingManagerTest` covers tier resolution; `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` covers the view-model import gate that triggers the paywall; `ImportPaywallNavigationTest` covers the paywall navigation dispatch. The per-button lock-icon rendering on this specific tab stays visual.)*

The gate itself is shared with the Power tab. What this row checks is that the Heart Rate tab is wired into it too, which is a per-tab render rather than a per-tier rule.

## Expect

- New and Import each carry a lock and open the paywall. Share is absent, or locked and opens the paywall.

## What this row absorbed

- `TST-0220` (HR Import Pro Only) — the Import button's lock and paywall redirect on the HR tab. It is the **Import** step.
- `TST-0221` (HR Export Pro Only) — Share being unavailable or locked in an HR-Zone workout's context menu. It is the **Share** step.

## What a single tick no longer distinguishes

One tick no longer separates three independently rendered gates. A New button that lost its lock, an Import button that lets a FREE rider through, and a Share action that is still live in the context menu all record as one failure now, so a rider must write down which named step was open.

items.name: Route library — one glance at the Route tab
items.text:
Open Workouts, pick **Route** in the ride-mode strip, and read the whole screen once. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS. Nothing in this row needs a trainer, a ride or a connection. Two routes must already be in the library for step 4: one flat, total ascent under 100 m (*Endurance Flats*), and one mountain, total ascent over 1000 m (*Alpe d'Huez*). Turn the developer toggle on so the `[Debug]` routes draw.

## Setup

A PRO rider with the two routes step 4 names already imported, and Show debug workouts on in Developer Options. A tablet for steps 1 to 7, and a phone in portrait for step 8.

## Steps

1. **The list is populated.** At least 15 bundled routes are listed, plus the `[Debug]` routes while the developer toggle is on.
2. **No "coming soon" card.** The placeholder card that once stood in for an empty library must not appear anywhere in the list.
3. **Card silhouette.** Each Route card draws a monochrome elevation silhouette, not a power-bar waveform.
4. **The silhouette scales with the climb.** The flat route's silhouette is a visibly thin band at the bottom of its card, its ~50 m of relief drawn against a 200 m baseline. The mountain route's fills the card height and shows full relief. Before ISS-0193 both filled the card, which made difficulty impossible to compare at a glance.
5. **Card metadata.** A Route card subtitle reads its distance, ascent, steepest grade and difficulty, such as `12.4 km • 310m ↑ • 6% max • Diff: 3` (`ws_card_route_summary_with_grade_format`).
6. **A Route card carries no duration.** The minutes figure belongs to Power and HR-Zone cards only (`ws_card_power_summary_format`, "45 min • Diff: 3"), so read a Power card in the same list to see the difference.
7. **Max-grade segment.** On the tablet, read the two routes' subtitles. The steepest grade comes after the ascent, the number first, as `12% max`. It is the steepest grade over the route's 50 m windows, not the raw per-segment peak (ISS-0309). The flat route shows a single digit and the climb a double digit.
8. **The same segment on a phone.** Repeat step 7 on a phone in portrait. Since FEAT-0131 a phone and a tablet show the same subtitle; a narrow card wraps the line instead of dropping the segment (ISS-0505). Only a route whose computed max grade rounds to 0 % drops it, with no empty separator left behind.
9. **Free Ride card.** The Route mode's primary card reads "Free Ride", subtitle "Slope + virtual gears", in the green accent.
10. **Import button.** The library header's Import button reads "Import (.gpx .fit .tcx)", in the same green accent.
11. **The library lists on FREE.** Switch the tier to FREE in Developer Settings and reopen Workouts with **Route** picked. The bundled library is still listed; listing is not tier-gated.

## Expect

- Step 1: at least 15 bundled routes, plus the `[Debug]` routes while the developer toggle is on.
- Step 2: no "coming soon" card anywhere in the list.
- Step 3: each Route card draws a monochrome elevation silhouette, not a power-bar waveform.
- Step 4: the flat route's silhouette is a thin band at the bottom; the mountain route's fills the card.
- Step 5: a Route card subtitle reads like `12.4 km • 310m ↑ • 6% max • Diff: 3`.
- Step 6: a Route card shows no minutes; the Power card does.
- Step 7: the subtitle reads `<dist> km • <ascent>m ↑ • <N>% max • Diff: <n>`: one digit on the flat route, two on the climb.
- Step 8: the phone shows the same subtitles as the tablet, `<N>% max` included.
- Step 9: the primary card reads "Free Ride", subtitle "Slope + virtual gears", in the green accent.
- Step 10: the Import button reads "Import (.gpx .fit .tcx)", in the same green accent.
- Step 11: on FREE the bundled route library is still listed.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0223` | 3 | A card drawing a power waveform where a silhouette belongs now shares its result with every other card defect on the screen. |
| `TST-0224` | 5, 6 | A wrong subtitle format and a duration that should not be there land on one tick. The missing-profile fallback it also asked for is a unit test now; see below. |
| `TST-0225` | 4 | A silhouette that ignores absolute relief no longer records apart from a silhouette that is the wrong shape entirely. |
| `TST-0226` | 7, 8 | The segment on a phone and on a tablet share one result, so a failure names the device only if the tester writes it down. |
| `TST-0227` | 9 | A missing Free Ride card no longer records apart from a missing Import button. |
| `TST-0240` | 10 | A wrong Import button label no longer records apart from a wrong Free Ride subtitle. |
| `TST-0275` | 11 | A FREE rider losing the library reads as the same failure as a PRO rider losing it. |

*(partially automated: `WorkoutRepositoryLibraryTest` covers the bundled-asset catalogue surface and that listing is not tier-gated; `RouteGpxImporterTest` covers distance and ascent computation from the route profile; `FreeRideCardTest.route_tab_renders_free_ride_with_slope_subtitle` covers the Free Ride title and subtitle; `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` exercises the per-tab extension allowlist behind the Import button's copy. Every rendering claim above stays visual.)*

## Step 7 retired, 2026-09-25

Step 7 used to read: *"A route with a missing profile falls back to the difficulty alone. Fewer than two stored profile points renders `Diff: n` and nothing else."* No rider can reach that card through the app. The GPX, FIT and TCX importers refuse a track with fewer than two points (`RouteImportOutcome.Failure.TooFewPoints`), and every point they keep becomes one profile point. `WorkoutValidator` refuses a `.ytw` route with a shorter profile, and every bundled route has at least five profile points. Only an Android `.ytwpack` install skips the validator. Edwin decided on 2026-09-25 to retire the step and cover the fallback with a unit test instead ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]], decision 7). On Android that test is [[TASK-0965-RetireTheUnreachableRouteCardStepAndUnitTestTheFallback|TASK-0965]]; the fallback is at `WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:2426-2428`, inside `WorkoutItem`, reached when `profile.size >= 2` fails at `:2392`. The step used to cite `:2839`, which is a `LibraryUiState` declaration. On iOS it is [[TASK-0963-TheIosRouteCardWithNoProfileIsUnitTested|TASK-0963]]. Steps 8 to 12 became steps 7 to 11.

## Steps 5, 7 and 8 rewritten for FEAT-0131, 2026-09-29

Step 8 used to say the steepest grade was absent below 600 dp, and that this was correct. ADR-0018 forbids a screen that changes its content by width, so [[TASK-1006-TheTwoIss0505SitesTheAmendmentDoesNotAllow]] made the route card show the grade at every width and removed `isWideRow`. Step 5's example changed with it ([[CHG-20260929-The-Cockpit-Fits-Every-Screen-And-The-Terrain-Keeps-Its-Share]]).

items.name: Import a route through the picker — GPX, FIT and TCX
items.text:
On Workouts, pick **Route** in the ride-mode strip, tap Import and run the same flow three times, once per file format. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS. The SAF picker is the part no test reaches.

items.name: Import failures — three bad files, three snackbar messages
items.text:
Import three deliberately broken `.gpx` files in one go and read the message each produces. Every message is the scaffold's snackbar, not a toast (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:961-968`); a toast appears only on a screen with no scaffold snackbar host.

## Steps

1. **Malformed file.** Import a truncated or broken `.gpx`. The snackbar reads "Import failed — File is malformed or not a valid route file."
2. **No elevation.** Import a `.gpx` whose trackpoints carry no `<ele>` tags. The snackbar reads "Import failed — Track points have no elevation data — route needs elevation to ride."
3. **Empty track.** Import a `.gpx` containing `<trk><trkseg></trkseg></trk>`. The snackbar reads "Import failed — No track points found in the file."

## Expect

- Step 1: the snackbar reads "Import failed — File is malformed or not a valid route file."
- Step 2: the snackbar reads "Import failed — Track points have no elevation data — route needs elevation to ride."
- Step 3: the snackbar reads "Import failed — No track points found in the file."

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0255` | 2 | The three rejection reasons collapse to one result, so a no-elevation file that is reported as malformed reads as a pass unless the rider notes the wrong message. |
| `TST-0256` | 3 | The same for the empty-track message. Note which of the three messages was wrong next to the tick. |

*(partially automated: `RouteGpxImporterTest` covers all three reject paths and the typed failure each produces; the snackbar copy stays manual.)*

items.name: Auto-translate on import — the blocking wait dialog, and the failure dialog behind it
items.text:
Same file, same setup, imported twice: once with a working key and once with a corrupted one.

**Setup.** Auto-translate toggle ON, AI configured, device language Dutch. The file is `test-fixtures/workouts/ytw/good.ytw` — four custom-labelled intervals, no IDs in the source.

## Procedure

1. **The happy path, behind a wait dialog.** Share the file to the app. A modal AlertDialog appears **immediately**, reading *"Workout vertalen…"* with the body *"\"Ramp Warmup Demo\" wordt naar het Nederlands vertaald. Dit duurt meestal ongeveer 10 seconden."* It is non-dismissable. After roughly 5–10 s it dismisses and the workout appears in the list **already translated**, with a Dutch name on the card. Open it: name, description and all four interval labels are Dutch. The list never shows an intermediate source-language version.
2. **The failure path.** Corrupt the AI key and import the same file again. The wait dialog appears, then dismisses, and an error dialog reads *"Vertaling mislukt"*, the locale-aware service error message, and *"De workout is in de oorspronkelijke taal geïmporteerd. Open hem om het opnieuw te proberen."*, with an OK button. Tap OK: the workout is in the list in English. Open it — the editor banner is showing. Restore the key, tap `Vertalen`, and it succeeds.

## Expect

- Step 1: the list and the editor never show the source language, even briefly.
- Step 2: the workout is still imported, the failure is explained in Dutch, and `Vertalen` works once the key is back.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0340-Auto-Translate-Failure-Dialog-TASK-0488]] | the failure dialog, its copy, and recovery through the banner | step 2 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0340** — the failure path is where a rider can lose a workout entirely if the import is abandoned along with the translation, and it now records under the same verdict as the happy path's dialog timing.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- Both dialogs' exact copy, and the state of the imported workout after each run.

items.name: A route import never calls the translator
items.text:
Routes carry no rider-facing prose to translate — a GPX is coordinates and elevations — so the auto-translate path that runs on workout imports must not run on route imports (ADR-0003).

## Setup

- **Settings → Language → "Auto-translate imported workouts" switched ON.** The toggle is the thing being tested, so it must be on.
- **An AI key configured** (Settings → AI Coach). Without a key nothing could translate anyway, so the check would pass for the wrong reason and prove nothing. This precondition is the whole reason it is stated here.
- A `.gpx` route file on the device, or shared to it from another app.
- The device **offline**, which is the cheap way to observe the negative: a translation attempt needs the network, so if one fires it fails visibly. Watching logcat for the translate service is the alternative if you would rather stay online.

## Steps

1. Share or open the `.gpx` file into Your Trainer.
2. The route import summary dialog appears. Save it.

## Expect

- Step 1: no translation banner, no "Translating…" state and no translation error.
- Step 2: the route saves offline with no error and no translation, under its own name.

## Not this check

- That a *workout* arriving in another language **is** translated when the toggle is on — that is the positive case and it is a different check.
- Whether the translation is any good. This check only asserts that no call is made.

## Provenance

Covers [[FEAT-0066]] and [[TASK-0453]], which introduced the toggle. Rewritten 2026-09-06 into the Setup / Steps / Expect shape; the AI-key precondition was added because without it the check could not fail.

items.name: Workout import — one good file and three refusals
items.text:
Four trips through the same "Import (.ytw .zwo)" button and the same file picker. Have the four files ready before starting.

## Setup

A PRO rider on Workouts. Four files ready on the device or in Drive: a valid `.zwo`, a non-workout file such as a `.pdf`, a malformed `.zwo` and a malformed `.ytw`. The ride modes are picked in the ride-mode strip. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS.

## Procedure

1. **A good `.zwo` imports.** Tap "Import (.ytw .zwo)" and pick a valid `.zwo`. The snackbar reads "Imported: \<workout name\>", and the workout appears in the library with the right intervals and terrain graph.
2. **An unsupported file type is refused, per tab.** Pick a non-workout file such as a `.pdf` or `.png`. With **Power** picked in the ride-mode strip the snackbar reads "Unsupported file type — please select a .ytw or .zwo file" and carries a **Retry** action. Pick **Route**, then **Heart Rate**, in the ride-mode strip, repeat the same import in each, and confirm each shows **its own mode-specific variant** of that message rather than the Power wording. The per-tab variants are the part most likely to rot, so check them rather than sampling one. On iOS, Files greys out a file the importer does not accept, so the `.pdf` cannot be picked in any ride mode; that is the refusal on iOS (Edwin, 2026-09-25, [[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]] decision 17).
3. **A malformed `.zwo` is refused by name.** Pick a `.zwo` whose XML is broken. The snackbar reads "Import failed — File is malformed or not a valid .zwo file."
4. **A malformed `.ytw` is refused by name.** Pick a `.ytw` whose JSON is broken. The snackbar reads "Import failed — File is malformed or not a valid .ytw workout."

*(Partially automated: `ZwoParserTest` and `IntervalDeserializerTest` cover the ZWO and `.ytw` parses including their typed failures, and `WorkoutViewModelImportGateTest` covers the tier gate. The SAF picker, the library refresh, the per-tab snackbar copy and the extension filter all stay manual.)*

## Expect

- Step 1: a snackbar reads "Imported: \<workout name\>", and the workout is listed with the right intervals and graph.
- [android] Step 2: Power reads "Unsupported file type — please select a .ytw or .zwo file", with Retry. Route and Heart Rate each have their own wording.
- [ios] Step 2: Files greys out the `.pdf` in every ride mode, so it cannot be picked.
- Step 3: the snackbar reads "Import failed — File is malformed or not a valid .zwo file."
- Step 4: the snackbar reads "Import failed — File is malformed or not a valid .ytw workout."

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0401-Unsupported-File-Type]] | the unsupported-type message, and its per-tab variants | step 2 |
| [[TST-0402-Malformed-ZWO-Toast]] | the typed malformed-`.zwo` message | step 3 |
| [[TST-0403-Malformed-YTW-Toast]] | the typed malformed-`.ytw` message | step 4 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0401** — three or four tab variants collapse into one step, so a single tab that has reverted to the Power wording records as "step 2 failed" and must be named in the evidence.
- **TST-0402** — a typed parse failure regressing to the old generic "file format not recognised" message is exactly the thing TASK-0317 fixed, and it now shares a verdict with a working import.
- **TST-0403** — the `.ytw` and `.zwo` paths are different parsers reporting through one surface, and one of them regressing no longer fails a row of its own.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- The exact snackbar text for each of the four files, and for step 2 one line per tab.

## Corrected 2026-09-17

The steps used to name a toast. The Workouts screen shows import results in its snackbar, with a Retry action on the unsupported-type refusal (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt`, AR-14), as [[TST-0254-Import-Failure-Toast-Malformed]] and [[TST-0257-Wrong-Tab-File-Filter]] already say. Edwin confirmed the snackbar on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]). The message text is unchanged.

items.name: Workouts opens on the library, and the rider is named in the navigation bar instead of a scorecard
items.text:
## Setup

Any rider with an FTP set, on a phone under 600 dp wide and a tablet at or above it.

## Steps

1. Open Workouts on the phone and read the top of the screen.
2. Read the rider item in the bottom bar in portrait and in landscape, then in the rail on the tablet.
3. Tap the rider item.

## Expect

- Step 1: no rider scorecard or equipment panel above the library; a workout row shows without scrolling.
- Step 2: the rider's bike mark in their colour and their name in the bar's colour, unwrapped, in both orientations and the rail.
- [android] Step 3: the Riders list opens. The current rider's card has a **Profile** button under it.
- [ios] Step 3: the Riders list opens, offering **Switch rider** and **Profile**.

(TST-0421 checks the compact card on the Riders list and TST-0417 checks the full card on Profile. [[TST-0666-TheNavigationContainerCarriesARiderThroughAWholeSession]] tests the rider item across a whole session.)

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.name: Library duration filter narrows the list

items.name: There is no bulk-publish entry point to third-party services
items.text:
## Setup

Strava and intervals.icu both linked for the current rider, and at least one saved ride. On both platforms the connected services are on the rider's Profile: the rider's name in the bottom bar (tab bar on iPhone) or the rail, then **Profile**. On Android, **Profile** is the button under the current rider's card. On iOS it is next to **Switch rider**.

With Strava and intervals.icu linked, sweep the workout library, the route library, the celebration after Save, with its upload chips, and History. On Android, also open the rider profile's Connected section. On iOS, open the rider's Profile: tap the rider's name in the tab bar or rail, then **Profile**, and read its Strava and intervals.icu sections. Verify there is no affordance that sends the whole library, mirrors it, or syncs everything to a third-party service. Per-item send and per-item history are expected and correct. Note before testing this that Android's Strava section carries an **Upload all** button for the pending-upload backlog (TST-0477) — that is a retry of rides already queued, not a library publish; confirm the distinction holds on the build under test before recording a verdict.

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Expect

- Nothing sends, mirrors or syncs the whole library to a third-party service.
- Per-item send and per-item history are there.
- [android] Strava's `Upload all` only retries rides already queued; it does not publish the library.

## Reworded 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] replaced the post-ride summary with a decision dialog and a celebration after Save, whose upload chips offer a Retry for that one ride. The sweep now names the celebration.

items.name: intervals.icu library browses and adds
items.text:
With intervals.icu linked on a PRO or Family seat, open Workout Selection and find the **My intervals.icu Library** section. Test the four things only a rider can see.

## Setup

A PRO or Family rider with intervals.icu linked to an account holding at least one power workout and one HR-zone workout. A trainer connected, and a heart-rate strap for an HR-zone row. The ride modes are picked in the ride-mode strip. The strip sits above the bottom bar on a phone. On a tablet it lies across the top of Workouts on Android, and under Workouts in the rail on iOS.

## Steps

1. **The section loads on a tap, never on its own.** Read the section on first arrival, then tap it. Tap the refresh control in the section header.
2. **The ride mode routes the rows.** The same section appears with **Power** and with **Heart Rate** picked in the ride-mode strip. Find an HR-zone workout in each.
3. **The duration chip filters the rows.** Set the duration filter to a band.
4. **Tapping a row rides it.** Tap a row and ride.

## Expect

- Step 1: first "Tap to load your intervals.icu workouts"; then rows with name, minutes and folder. The header's refresh pulls again.
- Step 2: each mode shows only its own workouts: the HR-zone workout is under Heart Rate, not Power.
- Step 3: intervals.icu rows narrow with the local ones; a row with no moving time stays.
- Step 4: once the gate has trainer, power source and (HR-zone) strap, it rides the workout's durations, targets and order, without a library copy.

## Notes

**There is no search field, no preview step and no add-to-library step on this screen.** The earlier wording asked for all three. Browse, filter and tap-to-ride is the whole flow (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:2030-2125`, `openIntervalsIcuWorkout:620`).

**The two parser assertions this row used to carry have moved to unit tests and should not be tested by hand.** `IntervalsIcuDslParserTest` asserts that an HR-zone token produces an `HR_ZONE` workout (`HR zone token Z2 HR produces an HR_ZONE workout`, and `mixed Z power and Z HR — presence of any HR token flips workoutType`) and that icu Z6 and Z7 clamp to YT Z5 (`Z6 HR token on pull clamps to Z5 with soft notice (FEAT-0090)`, and the Z7 case). Authoring a Z6 workout on intervals.icu by hand to confirm the clamp would show the rider nothing anyway: the clamp notice is deliberately not surfaced, because the policy is fixed and a message on every pull is noise (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:630-634`).

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). What the check asks for is unchanged.

items.name: Workouts and History carry the four destinations and the equipment icons
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies how Workouts and History reach the rest of the app since PHASE-025, which is what [[TST-0596-Chrome-Reachable-From-Every-Pre-Ride]] described before it was split down to its defects. The two screens now share one navigation container and one top bar, on both platforms.

## Setup

Any rider with a trainer bound and switched off at the start. A phone under 600 dp wide and a tablet at or above it. Test on both platforms.

## Steps

1. Open Workouts on the phone and read the bottom bar and the top bar.
2. Tap **History** in the bottom bar, then **Workouts**, then **History** again. Press Back.
3. From History, tap the rider item in the bottom bar, then **Profile**. On Android, **Profile** is the button under the current rider's card. On iOS it is next to **Switch rider**. Then tap **Settings** in the bottom bar.
4. Switch the trainer on and watch the top bar. Then switch it off again.
5. Repeat steps 1 to 3 on the tablet.

## Expect

- Step 1: bar order: rider (mark in rider's colour, name in bar colour), Workouts, History, Settings. Top bar: no gear or rider chip; four equipment icons last.
- Step 2: each tap swaps the screen in place. Back lands on the Riders list, not back through Workouts and History.
- Step 3: the current rider's profile opens. Settings opens as its own destination.
- Step 4: on connect the trainer icon turns the bar's text colour, no slash. On drop it turns faint grey and slashed, on both screens.
- Step 5: the same four destinations sit in a left rail, Settings at its foot.

## Not this check

- The whole session across the container, including the ride-mode strip and reduced motion: [[TST-0666-TheNavigationContainerCarriesARiderThroughAWholeSession]].
- What the equipment icons and the attention bar do around a ride: [[TST-0667-FromAFinishedRideToTheNextStart]].
- That Settings, the profile and the Riders list stay reachable at all, whatever the layout: [[TST-0596-Chrome-Reachable-From-Every-Pre-Ride]].

## Provenance

Step 4 was rewritten on 2026-09-30 by [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]] for FEAT-0132: a trainer that is not connected is drawn faint grey with a slash, not plain grey ([[REQ-0235-ADeviceThatIsNotConnectedIsDrawnWithASlashInTheTopBarAndEveryHubRow]]).

Step 4 was rewritten on 2026-09-28 for FEAT-0130: a connected icon is drawn in the bar's text colour, no longer green ([[REQ-0224-TheTopBarDrawsAllFourEquipmentIconsAndOnlyAFailureIsInColour]]).

Split out of [[TST-0596-Chrome-Reachable-From-Every-Pre-Ride]] on 2026-09-22 (tools/instructions/TESTING.md, "When to invalidate"): the regression test kept the defects' assertion, and this check took the description of the current screens.

items.name: Trainer Pairing
items.text:
## Setup

A trainer to connect, or the fake trainer from Developer Options, with no trainer set up yet. Open the Equipment Hub from the equipment icons in the top bar.

## Steps

Tap Connect on the Smart Trainer row and choose a smart trainer (FTMS) in the sheet that opens. Start a ride, then discard it.

## Expect

- Power and Speed show data.

## What is automated

*(Partially automated: `DevicePickerSheetTest` covers the picker sheet and the device tap; `EquipmentSlotTest` covers the row's state after connecting; the Bluetooth and FTMS link stays hardware-dependent.)*

## Where to find the rows, and who checks their layout

The devices are rows in the **Equipment Hub** on both platforms. Open it by tapping any of the equipment icons at the end of the top bar: a screen on Android, a sheet on iOS. The Workouts screen carries no equipment panel, and iOS Settings has no Equipment Hub row. That is all this check needs. It is here so the check can be tested, and TASK-0853 added its first version after Edwin marked this row `question` on 2026-09-08 with *"I don't see a third slot on the equipment screen"*. He was right: the slot was on a screen nothing navigated to ([[ISS-0417-TheEquipmentHubIsUnreachable]]).

**The Hub's contents and layout are [[TST-0657]]'s and [[TST-0674-TheEquipmentHubListSetsUpInspectsAndForgetsADevice]]'s, not this check's.** Since FEAT-0130 the Hub is one list on both platforms: a YOUR BIKE card with Smart Trainer, and Power and Cadence indented beneath it, then a YOU card with Heart Rate (`EquipmentList.kt`, `EquipmentHubView.swift`). Keeping a second description here would only give the checks a chance to disagree.

The empty-slot decision survives the redesign and is worth reading before testing: **the Power row is always there**, even with nothing bound to it. With a trainer set up it reads *From the trainer*; with no trainer it reads *Not set up* with a Connect button. Edwin settled that on 2026-09-08 ([[ISS-0416-ThePowerSlotAlwaysShowsAndItsCommentSaysItDoesNot]]): a rider who owns pedals has to be able to find the row without being told it exists.

items.name: A trainer that refuses control is recognised, written to no more, described once, and listed in its own bucket
items.text:
Test on **both platforms**. No Schwinn 800IC is needed and none is available: the fake trainer with its capability override set to "Refuses control" reproduces the bike's behaviour, and the KICKR leg proves nothing changed for a trainer that works.

## Setup

Developer Options on Android: under "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)", turn on "Fake a connected trainer", then fully quit and reopen the app. Set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to "Refuses control — every target write answered Control Not Permitted". It acts on writes, so it applies at once. This is the whole data-only state; no bike is needed.

On Android, do not use "Failure mode:" for this. That list only reaches the compatibility test's own mock (the "Run this test against a mock trainer (no hardware; ~15 s, not remembered)" checkbox), not the fake trainer the rest of the app connects to.

**Both platforms can now test every step.** Steps 8 and 10 used to say Android had no whole-app control for *refuses once* or *feature read timeout*, and told the tester to record `question` against [[ISS-0441-TheFakeTrainerCannotRefuseOnceOrTimeOutItsFeatureRead]]. That issue is **fixed as of 2026-09-17** ([[TASK-0924-AndroidDebugControlsForTheOwedChecks]]): both values are in "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)", beside the three that were already there. Test them and expect a verdict.

Step 8 is this check's own negative test for the three-strike latch — the case that must end `drivable` — so the version of this check that forbade testing it on Android was withholding the most valuable step it has.

On iOS, turn on Use mock trainer in Settings → Developer · Trainer and restart. Set Mock trainer capability to Off and Mock failure mode to Refuses control, then restart and connect the mock for the main leg. For step 8, choose Refuses once in Mock failure mode; for step 10, choose Feature read timeout in Mock trainer capability and set Mock failure mode to None. Each change needs a full app restart and a new mock connection. The iOS controls drive the whole-app mock, not the compatibility test's private mock.

A KICKR, or another trainer that accepts control, for the KICKR leg (steps 12 to 15). Android's capability override affects the KICKR too, so set it to Off before each KICKR connection. On iOS, turn Use mock trainer off and restart before connecting the real KICKR.

A heart-rate strap, or the mock HRM, for step 5.

A `data_only` entry in the trainer compatibility list, for step 7. On Android, turn on **Use the bundled test list** in Developer Options → Compatibility List Source (Debug); its Nautilus Schwinn 800IC entry is data-only ([[TASK-0924-AndroidDebugControlsForTheOwedChecks]]). iOS has no bundled test list, so step 7 there depends on the published list carrying a data-only entry.

The iOS build on a second device. Every step is tested on both platforms.

## Steps

### The mock leg — a bike that says no

1. Connect the fake trainer with the override set to "Refuses control", and start a Power workout so the app writes a target.
2. On both platforms, open the Equipment Hub by tapping any of the equipment icons at the end of the top bar, and read the Smart Trainer row. Tap the row and read its Resistance row. Then read both again in one non-English locale.
3. Open Bluetooth diagnostics and read the log.
4. Start a Power workout, then read the log again.
5. With a heart-rate strap or the mock HRM connected, start an HR-Zone workout and look at the delta pill. Without a monitor the start gate holds an HR-Zone ride at Connect or Cancel. Take a screenshot to compare with the same screen on a KICKR.
6. Run the in-app compatibility test and read its scorecard.
7. Open Settings, trainer compatibility check, against a list with a `data_only` entry. On Android, Developer Options → Compatibility List Source (Debug) → Use the bundled test list supplies one. iOS has no test list, so it reads the published list, which must carry a `data_only` entry (Edwin, 2026-09-25).

### The latch guard — one refusal is not a verdict

8. A trainer that refuses once, during a Power workout. On Android set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to **Refuses once — first target write refused, the rest succeed**; it acts on writes, so it needs no reconnect. On iOS, select Mock failure mode **Refuses once** and restart before connecting the mock.
9. Back on the fake trainer with the override still "Refuses control", disconnect and reconnect.

### The unknown states

10. Connect a trainer whose feature read times out. On Android set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to **Feature read timeout — 0x2ACC never answers, capability stays unknown**, then disconnect and reconnect, because it acts on the read. On iOS, select Mock trainer capability **Feature read timeout** and restart before connecting the mock.
11. Set the override to "No Control Point — 0x2AD9 treated as absent". Disconnect and reconnect the fake trainer.

### The KICKR leg — nothing changed for a trainer that works

12. Set the capability override to Off, disconnect the fake trainer, connect a KICKR on each platform and look at the cockpit. Compare the HR-Zone screen with the screenshot from step 5.
13. Run the compatibility test once on the KICKR and read its dispatch rows.
14. On iOS, read the Bluetooth log.
15. On Android, set the override back to "Refuses control", reconnect the fake trainer and start a Power workout until it latches `data-only`. Switch the override to Off before disconnecting the fake trainer and connecting the KICKR. On iOS, set Mock trainer capability Off and Mock failure mode Refuses control, restart and latch the mock; then turn Use mock trainer off and restart before connecting the KICKR. Confirm the KICKR is driven. Disconnect it, restore the normal mock and reconnect to check that the verdict is derived again.

## Expect

- Step 1: the Power workout starts on the refusing fake trainer.
- Step 2: the row shows the hand mark and *Resistance by hand* **once**; its Resistance row reads *Set by hand*. Both read correctly translated.
- Step 3: the log shows `Control capability: unknown → data-only` with its source, after two refusal votes, each followed by a re-issued Request Control.
- Step 4: **no control write appears in the log after the latch**, and exactly one line says writes are suppressed.
- Step 5: the row reads `TARGET n W` with the arrow and delta beside it, and never pulses. No `SUGGEST` pill. It looks different from a KICKR's.
- Step 6: the ERG, Simulation and resistance rows read N/A with a reason. The verdict does not blame the bike, and no control write is attempted.
- Step 7: the entry renders as its own bucket, not as *not listed*.
- Step 8: the capability never leaves `drivable`, and control writes continue after the one refusal.
- Step 9: the capability starts at `unknown` again.
- Step 10: the capability stays `unknown`, writes continue, and the trainer row carries no hand mark.
- Step 11: the capability is `data-only` immediately, before any write.
- Step 12: no manual-resistance line, no data-only `TARGET` readout, and the gear and slope-mode controls are present.
- Step 13: nothing in the scorecard has changed for a trainer that works.
- Step 14: the log carries a Control Point response line and a Start/Resume.
- Step 15: the KICKR is driven: gear and slope-mode controls are back, and no manual-resistance line. The reconnected fake trainer's verdict is derived again, not remembered.

## Not this check

- What the cockpit shows a data-only rider instead of the controls it removed: [[TST-0649-RidingByHandInEveryMode]].
- The fields the parser reads: [[TST-0650-IndoorBikeDataFieldsAndASurvivingLog]].
- The gear calibration rows TST-0143 to TST-0158. A compatibility-test run is **not** evidence for them. It writes an ERG target, a slope or a resistance level straight at the trainer and never consults the gear table. Those rows are the gear sweep, [[TST-0658-TheGearSweepRidesTheGearTable]], and separate rides.
- Whether a data-only scorecard earns the Pro grant, or can be submitted: [[TST-0656-DataOnlyScorecardEarnsNoProGrant]].

## What a failure means

Step 8 is the only step that catches the critical defect the design review found: a capability that latches on the first refusal. Without that guard, a KICKR that briefly loses control would be silenced for the rest of the ride. A `SUGGEST` pill on a KICKR means the gate is inverted. A missing line in step 3, with correct behaviour everywhere else, means the diagnostics are lying. That is the class of defect this whole phase exists to close.

## History of this check

- **Step 2** was untestable as first written. TASK-0853 moved the manual-resistance line onto the equipment panel on the Workouts screen. It had shipped onto an Equipment Hub screen that nothing navigated to ([[ISS-0417-TheEquipmentHubIsUnreachable]]). Edwin's `question` mark on TST-0028 is what found that. Since PHASE-025 (2026-09-22) the line is in the Equipment Hub on both platforms, opened from the equipment icons in the top bar.
- **Step 10**: four different failures produce no feature bits, and none of them is evidence that the bike cannot be driven. That is why `no read` must leave the capability `unknown`.
- **Step 15** was added by TASK-0850's sweep. TST-0451 asserts the same reset for the SIM-capability flag, and TASK-0823 extended that reset to carry this capability too. But TST-0451 is a regression test, so nothing reopens it. The risk is real and belongs in a check that is actually owed, which is this one.
- **Step 13** was corrected on 2026-09-13 by [[TASK-0896-SetupStepsExpectOnTheOwedChecks]]. It used to say "this one run is the evidence for TST-0143 to TST-0158". FEAT-0117 showed that the compatibility test never reaches the gear table, and five of those rows were retired into TST-0658.
- **Steps 2 and 10 were rewritten on 2026-09-28** for FEAT-0130. The manual-resistance line under the trainer's name became the hand mark and *Resistance by hand* on the trainer's row in the Hub list, and the details sheet opened from that row gained a Resistance row reading *Set by hand: this bike does not let the app change it* ([[REQ-0225-TheEquipmentHubIsAListGroupedByBikeAndRider]], [[REQ-0226-ARowOpensTheDevicePickerOrTheDevicesDetailsAsASheet]]). What the steps assert is unchanged: the app says it once, in the rider's language.
- **The Expect lines were shortened on 2026-09-27** ([[TASK-0977-ShortenTheExpectLinesOfTheOwedChecks]]) so the release test prints one short line per step. Step 1 gained a line that asserts nothing, so the lines pair with the steps. Step 4 lost its explanation: one log line per write is the ISS-0409 defect returning. Steps 5 and 12 lost their history: the `SUGGEST` pill is gone on both platforms ([[TASK-0877-TheHrZonePillDropsTheWord]], [[TASK-0935-TheIosHrZoneRowGetsTheSharedReadout]]), an earlier version of step 5 expected it, and in step 12 the data-only row that must be absent on the KICKR is the shared readout that replaced the pill.

items.name: Power meter pedals supply real wattage, and adding a power slot does not un-pair the rider's trainer
items.text:
Nobody on the project owns power meter pedals. On Android, **a physical KICKR in Power Source with the fake trainer in Smart Trainer** exercises the Cycling Power connection, parser, slot rules and source preference. On iOS, **Mock Power Meter in Power Source with Mock Wahoo KICKR in Smart Trainer** exercises the parser and source behavior in the isolated debug app. The iOS mock replaces the whole Bluetooth provider, so it cannot connect the physical KICKR at the same time. Record the iOS result as simulated source behavior; it is not proof of a physical Bluetooth connection. The dual-sided pairing rule still needs real pedals and carries an acceptance exception until a pair is available.

## Setup

Developer Options: "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)" on, as the trainer.

On Android, an awake KICKR, which advertises both FTMS and Cycling Power, stands in for pedals. On iOS, enable **Use mock trainer** and fully restart; its Mock Power Meter supplies Cycling Power packets beside the Mock Wahoo KICKR trainer. The mock trainer advertises both FTMS and Cycling Power for the unplaced-device rule, but a mock cannot prove the physical KICKR's advertisement.

A Cycling-Power-only device, or a stored preference for one, for step 5.

A heart-rate strap on Android, or Mock HRM Strap in iOS mock mode, so all three slots can be filled in step 7.

Garmin Connect signed in on a browser, for step 9.

A ride saved before this release, for step 10.

On both platforms the devices are rows in the **Equipment Hub**. Open it by tapping any of the equipment icons at the end of the top bar: a screen on Android, a sheet on iOS. The power slot is the row titled **Power**, beneath Smart Trainer. Tapping a row with a device of its own opens its details sheet, which holds Change device and Forget; tapping an empty row, or one that reads *From the trainer*, opens the device picker. While a ride runs, rows open nothing and only Reconnect works.

## Steps

### The parser

1. Connect the platform's fake or mock trainer. Tap the **Power** row and choose its separate power source. Look at the cockpit's power.
2. With both the power-slot device and trainer reporting cadence, read the cadence tile. Then stop the power-slot device's cadence and watch the tile. On Android, stop pedalling the KICKR in the power slot; the fake trainer keeps sending its own cadence. On iOS, turn on **Stop the Mock Power Meter's cadence** in Settings → Developer · Trainer ([[TASK-0925-IosDebugControlsForTheOwedChecks]]); its power keeps arriving and the Mock Wahoo KICKR's cadence is untouched.

### The slot rules

3. Connect the dual-service KICKR on Android, or Mock Wahoo KICKR on iOS, with no explicit placement.
4. With the platform's separate power source in the Power row, look at the Smart Trainer row and at the fake or mock trainer's control.
5. Store a preference for a Cycling-Power-only device, then present that device where it no longer satisfies the trainer slot.
6. In the Equipment Hub, open the device picker for Smart Trainer, then Power, then Heart Rate: tap the row, and on a row with a device tap Change device. Swipe each picker away before opening the next.
7. Fill all three rows. Tap each one to open its details sheet. On Power, tap Forget this power source and confirm, then relaunch the app.

### The choice, and the record

8. End the ride. With both still connected, tap the Hub's Power row, then Change device, and choose the trainer. Start a ride and watch the cockpit's power for a minute. End it, choose the separate power source again in the Power row, and start another ride.
9. Save that second ride. Open its session detail. Export the FIT file and import it into Garmin Connect.
10. Open a ride saved before this release.

### What needs real pedals

11. Dual-sided pedals connecting as one device, and left-right behaviour. **Do not test this step on the KICKR.** Record the acceptance exception instead of a pass.

## Expect

- Step 1: live watts, not zero.
- Step 2: the power source's cadence wins. The tile does not flicker when it stops.
- [android] Step 3: the KICKR goes to Smart Trainer only, not also to Power Source.
- [ios] Step 3: the mock KICKR goes to Smart Trainer only. This covers slot choice, not the real KICKR.
- [android] Step 4: Smart Trainer still holds the fake trainer, and it is still driven.
- [ios] Step 4: Smart Trainer still holds the mock KICKR, and it is still driven.
- Step 5: the rider sees a message. The preference is not cleared in silence.
- Step 6: each picker lists only its own kind of device.
- Step 7: each details sheet offers Change device and Forget. After the relaunch, Power reads *From the trainer*.
- Step 8: the watts follow the chosen source and never switch mid-ride.
- Step 9: the ride names its power source. Garmin Connect accepts the file.
- Step 10: the power source reads `unknown`.
- Step 11: left and right pedal power behave correctly.

## Not this check

- Whether the power source stays with the tablet across riders: [[TST-0654-PacerAndPowerSourceBelongToTheRider]].
- What History and personal bests show about where power was measured: [[TST-0655-WherePowerCameFromInHistoryAndPersonalBests]].
- A dedicated cadence sensor in the fourth slot: [[TST-0657-ACadenceSensorFillsTheFourthSlot]].

## What a failure means

Step 4 failing, with the fake trainer losing the trainer slot when the KICKR joins the power slot, is the un-pairing hazard the design review found. It is the reason this feature reopens five pairing checks.

## Notes

- Step 2: crank cadence is measured at the crank, which is why the power source's cadence wins. The precedence is a first value, and Edwin can change it.
- FEAT-0110's priority is open and is Edwin's call. This check is written so it is ready when he schedules it.

## History of this check

- **Step 2** was sharpened by TASK-0851. It used to read "does not fight the mock trainer's own cadence", which does not say which one wins.
- **Step 6a** was added by TASK-0850's sweep. TST-0633 asserts inline Change and Forget on a connected slot. TASK-0826 added a line to that slot and TASK-0848 added a third slot, but TST-0633 is a regression test, so nothing reopens it. A third slot is exactly the kind of change that pushes a control behind an overflow menu, so the assertion belongs in a check that is owed.
- On 2026-09-17, step 8 stopped asking for a power-source change during a ride. Android's ride screen has no route to Power Source, and Edwin decided not to add one ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]). The source is now chosen in the Equipment Hub before each ride starts; the expectation is unchanged.
- On 2026-09-28, steps 1, 4 and 6 to 8 were rewritten for FEAT-0130. The Hub is a list, the scanners are picker sheets, and Change device and Forget moved from each slot's ⋮ or ellipsis menu into the details sheet a row opens ([[REQ-0226-ARowOpensTheDevicePickerOrTheDevicesDetailsAsASheet]]). Step 7's two platform lines became one, because both platforms now draw the same sheet. An unbound power row reads *From the trainer*, which is what "stays empty" meant.
- On 2026-09-16, the old step 6a became numeric step 7 so the release test can give it an independent mark. The former steps 7–10 are now steps 8–11; this changes no expected behavior or ledger verdict.

items.name: The six-screen data-only test on the mock trainer: every screen a knob rider meets, in one pass
items.text:
The three feature checks each test one feature deeply. This one tests the **rider's path** end to end on a bike the app cannot drive, in a single session. It is the check that catches a phase that works feature by feature and does not hang together.

## Setup

Developer Options on Android: under "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)", turn on "Fake a connected trainer", then fully quit and reopen the app. Set "Trainer Capability Override (Debug)" to "Data-only — feature word reports no target bits"; it applies on the next connect.

On Android, do not use "Failure mode:" for this. That list only reaches the compatibility test's own mock (the "Run this test against a mock trainer (no hardware; ~15 s, not remembered)" checkbox), not the fake trainer the rest of the app connects to.

On iOS, turn on Use mock trainer in Settings → Developer · Trainer, set Mock trainer capability to Data-only and Mock failure mode to None, fully close and reopen the app, then connect the mock. The iOS mock capability picker changes the feature word the whole-app mock reports; it is separate from Mock failure mode.

A rider with an FTP and a weight set, and an LTHR that is not a round fraction of Max HR.

A heart-rate strap, or the mock HRM, for step 3. An HR-Zone ride does not start without one.

The iOS build on a second device, for step 8. Screenshots of every screen from both platforms.

The gallery keys from TASK-0843, where a parity difference is recorded.

## Steps

### The six screens

1. **The Equipment Hub.** Connect the fake trainer, open the Equipment Hub by tapping any of the equipment icons at the end of the top bar, and read the Smart Trainer row. It is the same list on both platforms: a screen on Android, a sheet on iOS.
2. **Power cockpit.** Start a structured Power workout and read the control row.
3. **HR-Zone cockpit.** With a heart-rate strap or the mock HRM connected, start an HR-Zone workout and read the large number, the suggestion and the pill.
4. **Route cockpit, terrain primary.** Start a route with the terrain view primary and read the whole cockpit.
5. **Route cockpit, map primary.** Switch the map to primary.
6. **Free-ride SIM cockpit.** Start a free ride in SIM.

### Then, in the same session

7. **Diagnostics.** Export the Bluetooth log.

### Both platforms, side by side

8. Repeat steps 1 to 7 on the other platform. Read the two sets of screenshots together.

## Expect

- Step 1: the trainer connects, and its row shows the hand mark and *Resistance by hand*, once, in neutral colour, not amber.
- Step 2: `TARGET N W`, with a cue where the intensity percentage was.
- Step 3: the row reads `TARGET n W` with the arrow and delta beside it, in the deviation band's colour. No `SUGGEST` pill.
- Step 4: grade shown; no gear control or slope chip. Pacer on, not dismissible. Row: segment line, `TARGET N W`. Profile: next-segment marker. Cadence: `AIM 75`.
- Step 5: the pacer draws on the map too, and the control row reads as it did with the terrain primary.
- Step 6: SLOPE ± is present, the gear control is gone, the row reads `TARGET N W`, and the pacer gap line is on the growing profile.
- Step 7: the log carries the capability transition, the suppressed-writes line once, and the flags word.
- Step 8: both platforms match in wording, position and presence. On every cockpit the target sits in one place and is never called `PACER`.

## Not this check

- Each feature in depth: detection in [[TST-0648-DataOnlyDetectionOnAMockRefusingTrainer]], the cockpit in [[TST-0649-RidingByHandInEveryMode]], the pacer in [[TST-0651-PacerGhostOnAndOff]].

## Why this check exists

A rider who reaches screen 4 and finds the target in a different place than on screen 2 has been given two instruments to learn instead of one. A rider whose HR-Zone screen says `SUGGEST` and whose Route screen says `PACER`, on the same bike, is being told that the same number means two things. Consistency across the six screens is the claim here, and no single-feature check makes it.

## History of this check

- Step 1 was rewritten on 2026-09-28 for FEAT-0130. The manual-resistance line under the trainer's name became the hand mark and *Resistance by hand* on the trainer's row, and both platforms now draw the same list, so the old advice to compare facts rather than layout was dropped ([[REQ-0225-TheEquipmentHubIsAListGroupedByBikeAndRider]]).

- The Expect lines were shortened on 2026-09-27 ([[TASK-0977-ShortenTheExpectLinesOfTheOwedChecks]]). The line "Across steps 2 to 6" joined step 8, so the lines pair with the steps. Step 8 still means that any difference between the platforms is a parity defect, recorded against the TASK-0843 gallery keys. Step 3 lost its history: [[TASK-0877-TheHrZonePillDropsTheWord]] replaced the `SUGGEST` pill with the shared readout on Android, [[TASK-0935-TheIosHrZoneRowGetsTheSharedReadout]] brought iOS to match, and an earlier version of the line expected the pill.

items.name: A cadence sensor fills the fourth slot, its rpm wins, and a rider with no sensor sees exactly what they saw before
items.text:
Nobody on the project owns a cadence sensor, so **the fake cadence sensor plays one**. It emits a crank stream rather than an rpm, as a real sensor does. That is enough for every step below except the last. Run every step on **both platforms**: the whole feature landed on both in one release, so a verdict from one is half a verdict.

## Setup

A trainer connected: the fake trainer ("Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)") or a KICKR. The fake trainer also offers **Mock Cadence Sensor** in the cadence scan.

A power source that reports cadence, for steps 8 and 9. Both debug builds now offer a separate Mock Power Meter; a pedalled KICKR or another live Cycling Power source can also provide this reading.

A heart-rate strap nearby, for step 13.

Two riders, for step 14.

A tablet, the same tablet in split-screen mode, and a phone, for the widths in step 2.

The iOS build on a second device.

## Steps

### The row

1. With a trainer connected and no cadence sensor bound, open the Equipment Hub by tapping any of the equipment icons at the end of the top bar and read the Cadence row.
2. On Android, open the Equipment Hub at three widths: a full tablet, the tablet in split-screen, and a phone. On iOS, open the Hub sheet at tablet and phone widths.
3. At each width, read every row's title and status line, scrolling where needed.
4. Tap the Smart Trainer row and read the details sheet's actions. Repeat on a data-only trainer.
5. Read all four row titles in English, then in every other language.

### The sensor

6. Tap the Cadence row, read the title of the sheet that opens, choose **Mock Cadence Sensor**, and look at the cockpit and the row.
7. Watch the rpm for a minute.
8. Bind the sensor and a power source at once, and read the cadence tile.
9. Forget the sensor from its details sheet. Then forget the power source the same way.
10. With no power override, choose Mock Power Meter directly in the Cadence row. Read its rpm and the trainer's watts, then forget it.

### The things that must not have changed

11. With no sensor bound, ride with the trainer alone. Include a cadence jump of more than 30 rpm from the bike.
12. During a ride with Mock Cadence Sensor bound, pause the ride and tap the equipment icons in the cockpit's top bar. In the Equipment Hub, tap the Cadence row, then Change device, and choose the connected trainer. Return to the cockpit, resume, and watch the clock and cadence tile. Bind the sensor again before leaving the ride.
13. Open the Cadence row's picker with a heart-rate strap nearby. Close it without selecting anything, then open the Smart Trainer row's picker and select the mock trainer.
14. Switch riders. On Android, tap the rider's name in the bottom bar or rail, then the other rider's card. On iOS, tap the rider's name, then **Switch rider**, and pick the other rider. Read the Cadence row in the Equipment Hub and the cadence tile.

### What still needs real hardware

15. Bind a real Bluetooth cadence sensor (CSC). **Nobody owns one.** Record the acceptance exception instead of a pass until one is bought or a rider tests it.

## Expect

- Step 1: *From the trainer*, indented under Smart Trainer. Order: Smart Trainer, Power, Cadence under YOUR BIKE, then Heart Rate under YOU.
- Step 2: one list at every width: YOUR BIKE with its three rows, then YOU with Heart Rate. No tiles.
- Step 3: no title or status line is cut off, and every row can be reached.
- Step 4: the sheet offers Change device, Run the compatibility test and Forget this trainer. Data-only: the row carries the hand mark and *Resistance by hand*.
- Step 5: English reads Smart Trainer, Power, Cadence, Heart Rate. Each language capitalises all four alike.
- Step 6: the sheet reads *Choose a cadence source*. The row shows the sensor's name and *Connected*. The cockpit shows about 90 rpm.
- Step 7: no spikes, no drop to zero, and it never disappears.
- Step 8: the sensor's rpm is shown.
- Step 9: cadence falls back to the power source, then to the trainer, and the Cadence row says which.
- Step 10: about 60 rpm, and the trainer's watts unchanged. After Forget: the trainer's cadence.
- Step 11: the jump is rejected.
- Step 12: the ride stays paused and resumes. The Cadence row reads *From the trainer*. Rebinding brings the sensor's rpm back.
- Step 13: the strap is not in the cadence picker. The trainer goes to Smart Trainer.
- Step 14: rider 2's Cadence row names the same sensor, still *Connected*, and the cadence tile keeps its reading.
- Step 15: a real sensor connects and its rpm is shown.

## Not this check

- Power meter pedals, or a KICKR, in the power slot: [[TST-0652-PedalsInThePowerSlot]].
- Whether the power source stays with the tablet across a rider switch and a restart: [[TST-0654-PacerAndPowerSourceBelongToTheRider]].

## Notes

- Rewritten on 2026-09-28 for FEAT-0130. The Hub is one grouped list on both platforms, so steps 2 and 3 no longer differ by platform. The kebab menu and Device info are gone: step 4 now reads the details sheet a row opens ([[REQ-0226-ARowOpensTheDevicePickerOrTheDevicesDetailsAsASheet]]). The power row is titled *Power*, the cadence scan is a picker sheet titled *Choose a cadence source*, and a row with its own device reads its name and *Connected* rather than *From the sensor*. The dated observations below describe the Hub before this change; no verdict is carried over from them.
- On 2026-09-16 the former step 9a became numeric step 10 so the release test counts its direct meter observation. Former steps 10–14 are now 11–15. The dated observations below retain their original step labels; no verdict changed with the renumbering.
- Partial run on 2026-09-16, Android SM-X910, isolated `com.yourtrainer.debug` build: the full-width panel placed Smart Trainer, Power Source and Cadence together, with Heart Rate beneath. The cadence scan listed Mock Cadence Sensor. Selecting it showed its name and Connected state in the cadence card; Forget restored the trainer name and From the trainer. With Mock Wahoo KICKR selected as trainer and Mock Cadence Sensor selected as cadence source, the unstarted Quick Ride cockpit showed 60 rpm before and after the mock's crank event clock wrap, while the trainer alone had shown a different cadence. This covers observed parts of steps 1, 2, 6, 7 and 9. A full one-minute ride, an independent power source override, the iOS release test and a real CSC sensor were not checked in this run, so the test remains todo.
- Partial Android width run on 2026-09-16, same tablet and debug build: at the original full width, the panel showed the three bike cards across and heart rate below. Temporary 1600×1100 and 1200×800 display sizes produced panel widths about 374dp and 203dp. At the middle width, trainer sat above paired power and cadence cards, with heart rate below. At the narrow width, all four cards stacked. The panel and rider card had matching top and bottom edges at both widths. The narrow cadence card retained its Bluetooth badge, and its kebab menu offered Forget device, Change device and Device info. The original display size was restored. This covers the Android layout parts of steps 2–4, but not the data-only hand mark or the iOS layout, and does not produce a full verdict.
- Partial Android data-only run on 2026-09-16, same tablet and debug build: with the capability override set to Data-only and the mock trainer reconnected, the narrow trainer card displayed its hand mark beside the Bluetooth badge. The four cards remained stacked within the rider card's height. The override was reset to Off and the tablet's original display size was confirmed. Device info's full explanation was not opened in this run, and step 4 still needs its complete manual check on both platforms.
- Android step 4 follow-up on 2026-09-16, same isolated debug tablet: after setting the trainer capability override to Data-only and restarting the app to reconnect Mock Wahoo KICKR, the trainer card's Device info dialog showed its name, address, Connected state and this explanation: "This trainer sends power and cadence but its resistance is set by hand. Targets are shown; match them yourself." The override was reset to Off, the debug app was restarted, and Edwin's trainer and Mock Cadence Sensor were both confirmed Connected with Power Source *From the trainer*. This completes the available Android Device info explanation check; the compact presentation was checked separately above. The release app was untouched.
- Partial Android ride and rider run on 2026-09-16, same tablet and debug build: with Edwin's Mock Cadence Sensor bound, switching to Test2 showed Mock Wahoo KICKR and *From the trainer* in Test2's cadence slot. Test2's active mock ride displayed the trainer's changing cadence, including 78 rpm with a later average of 89 rpm and maximum of 98 rpm; the ride was discarded. On returning to Edwin, his cadence slot still named Mock Cadence Sensor. A separate active mock ride for Edwin showed 60 rpm at 00:16, 00:52 and 01:18; at 01:18 the cadence average and maximum were both 60 rpm. That ride was discarded too. These observations support the Android parts of steps 7 and 13, including multiple mock crank-clock wraps, but the full cross-platform route still has no verdict.
- Android tablet failure on 2026-09-16: the cadence scanner title was Cadence, not Select Cadence Source. Choosing the already connected Mock Wahoo KICKR from it was rejected with "That device is already in use" and "It does not report power, so it cannot be a power source." Edwin's sensor binding remained. This blocks the Android parts of steps 6 and 11 and gives the wrong rejection for step 12; [[ISS-0450-AndroidCadenceScannerRejectsItsTrainerAndMisnamesErrors]] and [[TASK-0914-AndroidCadenceScannerNamesAndAcceptsItsSource]] track the correction.
- Android tablet retest on 2026-09-16 after TASK-0914: the updated isolated debug build showed Select Cadence Source. Choosing the connected Mock Wahoo KICKR changed the cadence card to Mock Wahoo KICKR and *From the trainer*, while the Smart Trainer card stayed Connected. Choosing Mock Cadence Sensor again restored its name and Connected state. Closing a later cadence scan kept the sensor binding. The normal cadence scan filtered out the HRM mock, so no incompatible-device error was tapped on the tablet; the Android code now maps a cadence service rejection to cadence-specific text and the focused unit test checks that a mock HRM strap is rejected from the cadence role. These are Android partial results for steps 6, 11 and 12, not a full TST-0657 verdict.
- Android step 8 setup on 2026-09-16: the isolated debug app accepted a nearby physical KICKR CORE address in the Power Source slot while Mock Wahoo KICKR remained the trainer and Mock Cadence Sensor remained the cadence source. All three cards showed Connected, and a 31-second active ride showed sensor cadence at 90 rpm with average and maximum also 90; the ride was discarded. This confirms the Android sensor wins while all three slots are bound. The KICKR CORE connection used real Bluetooth despite the fake-trainer option, and it was stationary. After forgetting the sensor, the Cadence card named the power source but the unstarted cockpit showed the trainer's changing cadence, so this does not prove power-source fallback. This attempt led to the separate mock power meter tracked by [[ISS-0451-MockSensorAndPowerSourceReportTheSameCadence]] and [[TASK-0915-MockCadenceSourcesHaveDistinctReadings]].
- Android steps 8 and 9 retest on 2026-09-16, SM-X910 isolated `com.yourtrainer.debug`: after adding the separate Mock Power Meter, Smart Trainer, Power Source and Cadence each showed Connected with Mock Wahoo KICKR, Mock Power Meter and Mock Cadence Sensor respectively. The unstarted cockpit showed 90 rpm cadence and 161 W power. At 00:08 of an active ride, it showed 90 rpm with average and maximum both 90, while power was 191 W; that ride was discarded. Forgetting the sensor changed the Cadence card to Mock Power Meter and *From the power source*. The unstarted cockpit showed 60 rpm and 176 W. At 00:08 of another active ride, cadence was 60 rpm with average and maximum both 60, while power was 187 W; that ride was discarded. Forgetting the power meter changed the Power Source and Cadence cards to Mock Wahoo KICKR and *From the trainer*. The unstarted cockpit then showed the trainer's changing cadence, sampled at 62 and 75 rpm. The mock sensor was rebound, the power override was cleared, and both cards' final states were checked. This completes the Android mock parts of steps 8 and 9. iOS and real hardware still need their own checks.
- iOS testability finding on 2026-09-16 before TASK-0916: `MockBluetoothProvider` had a mock trainer and cadence sensor but no separate power meter, so the iOS parts of steps 8 and 9 required a live physical power source. The ride view model also received trainer watts but no selected Cycling Power watts. [[ISS-0452-IosPowerSourceCannotProveCadenceFallbackWithTheMock]] and [[TASK-0916-IosMockPowerMeterShowsSourceFallback]] corrected both paths.
- iOS steps 8 and 9 simulator retest on 2026-09-16: the focused CadenceSourceFallbackTests and CadenceScannerUITests passed on the iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) simulator. The UI test connected Mock Wahoo KICKR and a separate Mock Power Meter, then saw *From the power source*, 60 rpm and 210 W. Binding Mock Cadence Sensor changed the source line to *From the sensor* and the live reading to 90 rpm. Forgetting the sensor restored *From the power source* and 60 rpm. Forgetting the meter restored *From the trainer* and removed the 210 W meter reading. The unit test also confirmed the trainer and meter timers both continued, and that a selected Cycling Power watt reading survived the trainer's next packet before falling back to trainer watts when forgotten. This completes the simulated iOS parts of steps 8 and 9; a physical power source and real CSC sensor remain hardware checks, and the full TST-0657 route is still todo.
- Cross-platform service audit on 2026-09-16: both Cadence scanners offer Cycling Power and FTMS devices, but a separately selected device was read only through CSC on Android; iOS ignored Cycling Power packets outside the power slot, treated a separate FTMS bike's Indoor Bike Data as trainer data, and omitted CSC from connected-device discovery. [[ISS-0453-AcceptedCadenceSourcesCanRemainUnread]] and [[TASK-0917-ReadEveryAcceptedCadenceService]] added step 9a and corrected these paths.
