- Android step 9a on 2026-09-16, SM-X910 isolated `com.yourtrainer.debug`: with Power Source set to Mock Wahoo KICKR *From the trainer*, Mock Power Meter was chosen directly in Cadence. Its cadence card showed Mock Power Meter and Connected. The unstarted cockpit showed 60 rpm and 158 W. In a 25-second active Quick Ride, cadence stayed 60 rpm with average and maximum both 60; trainer power varied, with observed live readings of 161 W and 198 W and a 171 W ride average. The ride was discarded. The meter was forgotten, and Mock Cadence Sensor was rebound; the final debug cards showed trainer and sensor Connected, Power Source *From the trainer*, and Cadence Mock Cadence Sensor Connected. The release app was untouched.
- iOS step 9a on 2026-09-16, iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) simulator: `CadenceScannerUITests.testMockSensorPowerMeterAndTrainerShowEachCadenceFallback` passed all assertions, including Mock Power Meter chosen directly for Cadence, *From the sensor*, 60 rpm, trainer watts rather than the meter's 210 W, and *From the trainer* after Forget. Xcodebuild stalled after the passing UI suite and was terminated, so the command ended interrupted. The complete iOS unit suite passed separately: 815 tests, 2 skipped, 0 failures. The new unit cases cover connected CSC discovery, preference for one cadence stream, and direct Cycling Power and FTMS cadence packets without a watt override. These simulated checks complete step 9a's available mock route; physical devices and the rest of TST-0657 are still owed.
- iOS phone-width retest on 2026-09-16: both `CadenceScannerUITests` cases passed cleanly on the iPhone 17 simulator, including the scanner target, trainer and sensor source line, sensor → power meter → trainer fallback, and direct meter choice in Cadence. A visual capture of the Equipment Hub on that phone and the iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) simulator shows one native Form column with Smart Trainer, Power Source, Cadence and Heart Rate in that order, all four visible at the tested widths. This covers the visible iOS layout parts of steps 2 and 3; the entire cross-platform route and physical CSC exception are still open.
- Android step 12 follow-up on 2026-09-16, same isolated debug tablet: with Mock Cadence Sensor bound, Select Cadence Source listed KICKR CORE C489, Mock Wahoo KICKR, Mock Power Meter and Mock Cadence Sensor. It did not list the nearby Google Fitbit Air or either mock heart-rate device. Closing it kept Mock Cadence Sensor Connected. The trainer card's Change device action then opened Select Trainer; choosing Mock Wahoo KICKR left Smart Trainer Connected, Power Source *From the trainer* and Mock Cadence Sensor Connected. This covers the available Android scanner boundary without selecting an incompatible device.
- Android step 11 failure on 2026-09-16, same isolated debug tablet: a Quick Ride with Mock Cadence Sensor bound showed 90 rpm average and maximum while active. Back opened the ride summary and paused the ride. Settings → Hardware offered trainer status and said to change it on Workouts, with no Cadence slot. The cockpit had no route to the Workouts equipment panel, so the source could not be changed while the ride remained active. The ride was discarded and Edwin's original debug bindings remained. [[ISS-0454-A-RiderCannotChangeCadenceDuringARide]] and [[TASK-0918-ChangeCadenceWithoutEndingTheRide]] track the correction and an in-ride retest.
- Android step 11 retest on 2026-09-16, SM-X910 isolated `com.yourtrainer.debug`, using Sarah's mock trainer and cadence sensor: a running Free Ride showed 90 rpm at 00:09. The in-ride Cadence action opened the scanner over the cockpit. Choosing the connected Mock Wahoo KICKR changed the live tile to 71 rpm at 01:36, with Pause and Finish still available. Reopening and cancelling the picker kept trainer cadence at 77 rpm and the clock at 02:17. Rebinding Mock Cadence Sensor during the same ride restored 90 rpm at 03:45. The ride was discarded, and the final Workouts equipment card again named Mock Cadence Sensor. The first implementation had kept the old sensor monitor feeding 90 rpm after changing source; [[TASK-0918-ChangeCadenceWithoutEndingTheRide]] now stops that monitor before switching. Android `:app:check :app:assembleDebug` passed, including a focused monitor handoff test. This completes the available Android mock path for step 11, without closing the full TST-0657 route.
- iOS step 11 simulator retest on 2026-09-16, iPhone 17: `CadenceScannerUITests.testCadenceCanSwitchToTrainerWhileRideKeepsRunning` connected Mock Wahoo KICKR and Mock Cadence Sensor, started the ride, cancelled a Cadence search without changing its source, then chose the connected trainer. The Equipment Hub returned to the same active ride, the trainer remained Connected, the source line became *From the trainer*, and the clock advanced. The first test found that the mock trainer received a new UUID on each scan and advertised no services, so cadence selection did not recognise it as the bound trainer. Stable mock identity and FTMS/Cycling Power services corrected the simulated path. The full iOS unit suite passed 815 tests with two skipped. This completes the simulator path for step 11; the full manual route and physical CSC step 14 remain outstanding.
- Step 5 catalog audit on 2026-09-16: Android has explicit Power Source translations in all eight non-English resource sets. The iOS Equipment Hub asks for `Power Source`, but `Localizable.xcstrings` has no such key, so the title remains English. The iOS Spanish, Italian and Brazilian Portuguese Heart Rate abbreviations also capitalize their second word while Android's corrected titles use sentence case. [[ISS-0455-IosEquipmentTitlesMissTheirLanguageRules]] and [[TASK-0919-LocalizeTheIosEquipmentTitles]] track the iOS correction. This is a finding, not a step 5 pass.
- Step 5 iOS build finding on 2026-09-16: after the missing catalog values were added, an iPhone simulator launched with German still showed Smart Trainer, Power Source, Cadence and Heart Rate in English. The built app had no compiled language resource folders. The Xcode project refers to `ios/Localizable.xcstrings`, but the file is at `ios/YourTrainer/Localizable.xcstrings`. The failed `testEquipmentTitlesFollowEachSupportedLanguage` assertion expected *Leistungsquelle* and found no such Equipment Hub row. [[ISS-0455-IosEquipmentTitlesMissTheirLanguageRules]] also tracks this resource-path correction; step 5 remains open.
- Step 5 iOS retest on 2026-09-16: after correcting the string-catalog resource path and making the Smart Trainer and Heart Rate rows request localized values, the built app contained compiled language resources. `CadenceScannerUITests.testEquipmentTitlesFollowEachSupportedLanguage` checked all four titles in English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Dutch, Brazilian Portuguese and Traditional Chinese on iPhone 17 and iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) simulators; both test suites reported one pass and zero failures. The iPhone command exited successfully. Xcode stayed open after the passing iPad suite, so its runner was stopped. Visual captures show the longer French Power Source title fits the phone row and the German titles fit the iPad Form. The full iOS unit suite passed 815 tests, with two skipped and no failures. This covers the iOS title part of step 5; the complete TST-0657 test still needs a verdict for its other steps and the real CSC exception.
- iOS step 7 simulator follow-up on 2026-09-16: `CadenceScannerUITests.testMockCadenceSensorHoldsItsRpmThroughOneMinuteOfCrankWraps` passed cleanly on iPhone 17. In an active mock ride it found 90 rpm when the sensor began reporting, again after 32 seconds and again after the ride clock advanced at least 60 seconds from its starting value; Pause remained available. The snapshot seed starts the clock at 12:34, so an initial test assertion expecting `01:xx` was corrected to compare elapsed values. The CSC parser's wrap arithmetic is also covered by unit tests. This is repeatable simulator evidence for step 7; it does not replace the full manual acceptance test.
- Rider and trainer-spike follow-up on 2026-09-16: the new iOS `CadenceSourceFallbackTests.testRiderSwitchClearsThePreviousSensorAndItsLiveCadence` passed. It changed from a rider with a named sensor and 90 rpm to a rider without one, found the trainer name in the Cadence slot and zero cached rpm, then accepted that rider's 80 rpm trainer reading; restoring the first rider's binding did not resurrect a stale live value. The new Android `ScanViewModelCadenceFallbackTest` trainer-only case passed with 80 rpm, a rejected 125 rpm jump and an accepted 85 rpm next packet. The existing iOS `BluetoothParsingTests.testCadenceSanityRejectsImplausibleSpike` and ride-value fallback test passed in the full iOS unit suite. These automated checks support steps 10 and 13; the iOS rider switch and bike jump still need the manual route.
- iOS step 12 simulator follow-up on 2026-09-16: the focused `CadenceScannerUITests.testClosingCadenceSearchLeavesTheNextTrainerSelectionInTrainer` passed after asserting that Mock Cadence Sensor appeared but Mock HRM Strap did not appear in Select Cadence Source. Closing that search and selecting Mock Wahoo KICKR in Select Trainer left Cadence *From the trainer*. The iOS slot validation unit test also rejects a heart-rate binding offered to Cadence. A nearby physical strap was not present in the simulator; the real-radio part of step 12 remains for the release test.

- Step 3 failed before, when the four slots shared a 320 dp panel with the rider card. The Hub is a scrolling list now, so the question is truncation rather than height.
- Step 4: every row with a device opens the same details sheet, so a narrow screen cannot quietly lose Forget or Change device. The data-only fact is the hand mark on the row and the Resistance row in the sheet.
- Step 7: the crank event clock wraps at 16 bits. That is about every 64 seconds on real hardware and within ten seconds on the fake sensor, so the wrap happens on its own rather than needing to be arranged. This is the single most likely thing to have been got wrong.
- Step 8: both devices measure the crank, and the rider's explicit choice of sensor breaks the tie.
- Step 10: the ISS-0117 spike filter now compares against the bike's own last reading rather than the published one, so it must still reject a jump from the *bike*.
- Step 11: choosing the trainer clears the override rather than storing it.
- Step 14: the **Garmin Speed and Cadence Sensor 2** is two sensors in one package, and only one of them transmits over Bluetooth at a time. That is a device limit the app inherits, not a defect it causes. See [[FEAT-0112-CadenceIsASourceLikeTheOthers]].
- The title capitalisation came from TASK-0866. The grouped list on both platforms came from FEAT-0130 (TASK-0986, TASK-0990).
- Rewritten 2026-09-30: step 14 used to expect each rider to have their own sensor or none. The cadence source is now saved for the tablet beside the trainer ([[ISS-0532-ThePowerPedalsAndCadenceSensorAreSavedPerRiderButBelongToTheBike]], built by [[TASK-1022]] and [[TASK-1023]]). The 2026-09-16 run notes in this file describe the per-rider behaviour as it was then.

items.name: From a finished ride to the next start, the chrome says what is waiting and the Hub does the rest
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies the equipment flow DES-0002 sections 2 to 4 describe as one sequence: the indicators, the attention bar, the connecting state, the gate, the Hub in both modes, and the teardown. [[TST-0666-TheNavigationContainerCarriesARiderThroughAWholeSession]] tests the navigation joins and touches equipment only in passing; this check is where the equipment claims are asserted.

## Setup

A phone under 600 dp wide on the release candidate, then a tablet for steps 4 to 9. Four slots filled, with a power source that can be powered down for steps 7 and 8. A mock device cannot be powered down. On Android, turn on **Fake a connected trainer** in Developer Options and restart, keep Mock Wahoo KICKR in Smart Trainer, bind the physical KICKR in Power Source and as the Cadence source, and a real strap or Mock HRM Strap in Heart Rate. On iOS, Use mock trainer with Mock Wahoo KICKR, Mock Power Meter as power and cadence source and Mock HRM Strap fills the four slots for steps 1 to 6 and 9, but no bench device gives a droppable power source there, so steps 7 and 8 wait for one. One rider.

## Steps

1. Open Workout Selection with all four devices bound and connected. Read the top bar.
2. Tap the heart-rate indicator.
3. In the Hub, tap the Cadence row and read its sheet. Close it, then tap the Smart Trainer row.
4. Back on Workout Selection, start a structured Power workout, let it run one minute, then discard it.
5. Read Workout Selection: the indicators and what sits beneath them.
6. Tap **Reconnect**.
7. Power the power meter down. Pick a structured Power workout.
8. Tap **Cancel**, then power the power meter up and pick the workout again.
9. In the cockpit, tap the cadence indicator; then pause the ride and tap it again.

## Expect

- Step 1: four indicators at the end, in the bar's text colour, none green. No rider chip, gear or kebab. The sparkle shows only on FREE.
- Step 2: the Hub opens directly: Smart Trainer, Power, Cadence, Heart Rate, each naming its device and reading Connected.
- Step 3: each opens a sheet with Sends, Change device and Forget. The trainer's adds Resistance and Run the compatibility test.
- Step 4: the workout starts once every device it needs is connected. Discarding it returns to Workout Selection.
- Step 5: every bound indicator is faint grey with a slash, and no dot. Beneath: equipment not connected, with one action, Reconnect. No row reads Connected.
- Step 6: all four indicators turn the app accent, then the bar's text colour, with no further tap.
- Step 7: a Connecting state beneath the indicators names the power source. The cockpit does not open.
- Step 8: after Cancel, the library with nothing selected. On the second pick the cockpit opens once the power source connects.
- Step 9: running, a sheet with no chevrons where only Reconnect and cadence's Change source respond, and the timer counts. Paused: the full Hub.

## Not this check

- The bar, rail and destinations: [[TST-0666-TheNavigationContainerCarriesARiderThroughAWholeSession]].
- The cadence sensor's own binding rules and its mid-ride switch: [[TST-0657-ACadenceSensorFillsTheFourthSlot]], whose step 12 now tests the paused path.
- Whether watts change source when the power meter drops, which is the open question on ISS-0493.
- The heart-rate prompt's fate on Power and Route, which is REQ-0216's open decision; test whichever Edwin chose.
- Each row and sheet of the Hub in depth: [[TST-0674-TheEquipmentHubListSetsUpInspectsAndForgetsADevice]].

## Provenance

- 2026-09-30, [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]]: step 5 expects every bound indicator slashed, because a device that is not connected is now drawn faint grey with a slash ([[REQ-0235-ADeviceThatIsNotConnectedIsDrawnWithASlashInTheTopBarAndEveryHubRow]]). Step 6 still holds: the accent while connecting, then the bar's text colour.
- 2026-09-28: Steps 1, 3, 6 and 9 used to expect green and amber indicators, the cadence slot's overflow menu with Device info, and a reconnect-only Hub drawn full-screen. Step 3 now opens the details sheets that replaced the overflow and Device info, and step 9 the sheet the running ride gets. Since FEAT-0130 the Hub is a list of rows, a connected device's icon is drawn in the bar's text colour rather than green, connecting is the app accent, and only a failed connect is red with a dot ([[REQ-0224-TheTopBarDrawsAllFourEquipmentIconsAndOnlyAFailureIsInColour]], [[REQ-0225-TheEquipmentHubIsAListGroupedByBikeAndRider]]).

items.name: A remembered device reconnects from its Equipment Hub row
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies how a remembered trainer and heart-rate strap come back after a relaunch since PHASE-025: through the Equipment Hub and the equipment icons in the top bar. [[TST-0593-Remembered-Device-Survives-Relaunch-ISS-0364]] described this on the Workouts-page panel before it was split down to its defect.

## Setup

A rider with a trainer and a heart-rate strap bound, both switched on. Test on both platforms.

## Steps

1. Force-quit the app, relaunch it and pick the rider. Watch the equipment icons at the end of the top bar.
2. Switch the trainer off and on again so it drops. Open the Equipment Hub by tapping any equipment icon, and read the Smart Trainer row.
3. Tap Reconnect on the row.
4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 with the heart-rate strap.

## Expect

- Step 1: the trainer and heart-rate icons turn from faint grey with a slash to the bar's text colour without a tap. No picker opens.
- Step 2: the row names the remembered trainer, reads *Disconnected*, and carries a Reconnect button.
- Step 3: it connects without a picker, the row reads *Connected*, and the trainer icon is back in the bar's text colour with no slash.
- Step 4: the same holds for the strap.

## Not this check

- That the device is remembered at all across a relaunch: [[TST-0593-Remembered-Device-Survives-Relaunch-ISS-0364]].
- Restoring every device after a ride with one Reconnect: [[TST-0667-FromAFinishedRideToTheNextStart]].

## Provenance

Steps 1 and 3 were rewritten on 2026-09-30 by [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]] for FEAT-0132: a device that is not connected is drawn faint grey with a slash, in the top bar and in its row ([[REQ-0235-ADeviceThatIsNotConnectedIsDrawnWithASlashInTheTopBarAndEveryHubRow]]).

Rewritten on 2026-09-28 for FEAT-0130: a dropped device's row reads *Disconnected* with a Reconnect button instead of *Tap to reconnect*, and a connected icon is no longer green ([[REQ-0225-TheEquipmentHubIsAListGroupedByBikeAndRider]]).

Split out of [[TST-0593-Remembered-Device-Survives-Relaunch-ISS-0364]] on 2026-09-22 (tools/instructions/TESTING.md, "When to invalidate").

items.name: A failed connect reads as a failure in the Hub row, the equipment icon and the attention bar
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies the words and marks a failed connect produces since PHASE-025, in the three places that now report it. [[TST-0595-Connect-Failure-Visible-ISS-0366]] quoted the old panel's words before it was split down to its defect.

## Setup

A rider with a trainer bound, switched on and not yet connected. Test on both platforms; since FEAT-0130 both show the same words.

## Steps

1. Open the Equipment Hub by tapping any equipment icon at the end of the top bar. Tap Reconnect on the Smart Trainer row, then power the trainer off before it connects. Watch the row and the trainer icon until the attempt gives up.
2. Close the Hub. With the trainer still off, pick a structured Power workout on Workouts and wait.
3. Tap **Retry** with the trainer still off, then **Cancel**.

## Expect

- Step 1: *Connecting…* with a spinner, then *Couldn't connect* in red with a Reconnect button. The trainer icon turns red with a dot.
- Step 2: the bar on Workouts reads *Connecting…* naming the trainer, then *Couldn't connect* with **Retry** and **Cancel**. The cockpit does not open.
- Step 3: Retry starts another attempt. Cancel clears the bar and leaves nothing selected.

## Not this check

- That a failed connect is visible at all: [[TST-0595-Connect-Failure-Visible-ISS-0366]].
- The post-ride *Equipment is not connected* bar and its one Reconnect: [[TST-0667-FromAFinishedRideToTheNextStart]].

## Provenance

Rewritten on 2026-09-28 for FEAT-0130. The slot's words used to differ by platform: *Couldn't connect — tap to try again* on Android and *Connection error* on iOS. Both now read *Couldn't connect* with a Reconnect button on the row, and the icon is red with a filled dot ([[REQ-0224-TheTopBarDrawsAllFourEquipmentIconsAndOnlyAFailureIsInColour]], [[REQ-0225-TheEquipmentHubIsAListGroupedByBikeAndRider]]).

Split out of [[TST-0595-Connect-Failure-Visible-ISS-0366]] on 2026-09-22 (tools/instructions/TESTING.md, "When to invalidate").

items.name: From the Hub's list a rider sets up a strap, reads the trainer's details and forgets a device
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies that the Equipment Hub is a list on both platforms, that a row opens the device picker or the device's details as a sheet, and that signal strength is shown as bars. [[TST-0675-TheTopBarIconsFromFirstRunToAFailedConnect]] covers the top bar's icons.

## Setup

A phone under 600 dp wide and a tablet, both on the release candidate. One rider.

- On Android, turn on **Fake a connected trainer** in Developer Options and restart, so Mock Wahoo KICKR is in Smart Trainer. Mock HRM Strap nearby, not set up.
- On iOS, turn on **Use mock trainer** in Settings → Developer · Trainer and restart, so Mock Wahoo KICKR is in Smart Trainer. Mock HRM Strap nearby, not set up.
- For step 8, a trainer that relays heart rate, that is, one that also advertises the heart-rate service. No mock does, so this step needs such a trainer on the bench.
- For steps 13 to 15, a real heart-rate strap you can switch off, because a mock device cannot be powered down ([[TASK-0962-IosDebugControlsForTheFirstIosReleaseWalk]]). On iOS the mock replaces all of Bluetooth, so turn Use mock trainer off, restart, and use the real KICKR for these steps.
- For steps 16 and 17, a data-only trainer: on Android, Trainer Capability Override set to Data-only; on iOS, Mock trainer capability set to Data-only. Restart and reconnect after changing it, and set it back to Off afterwards.

## Steps

1. Tap the equipment icons in the top bar to open the Equipment Hub. Read the YOUR BIKE card.
2. Read the caption under the YOUR BIKE card.
3. Read the YOU card and its caption.
4. Read the strip below the cards.
5. Look at the Smart Trainer row's icon and status text.
6. Long-press a row, and look for a ⋮ or ellipsis button on each row.
7. Tap Connect on the Heart Rate row. Read the sheet that opens.
8. With a trainer that relays heart rate in Smart Trainer, find it in that sheet and tap it.
9. Tap the heart-rate strap.
10. Tap the Smart Trainer row. Read the sheet that opens.
11. Turn on TalkBack or VoiceOver and read the Signal row.
12. Read the sheet's actions, then close it.
13. Switch the strap off and wait for its row to change.
14. Tap Reconnect on the Heart Rate row with the strap still off, and wait.
15. Switch the strap on and tap Reconnect again.
16. With a data-only trainer in Smart Trainer, read its row.
17. Tap the Smart Trainer row and read its Resistance row.
18. Open the strap's details, tap Forget this heart-rate monitor, and confirm.
19. Start a ride. While it runs, open the Hub from the top bar and try to tap each row.
20. Close the Hub and watch the ride.

## Expect

- Step 1: Smart Trainer, with Power and Cadence indented beneath it on a connecting line, each reading *From the trainer*.
- Step 2: the caption begins *The trainer is all you need to ride* and ends *to use power pedals or a cadence sensor instead*.
- Step 3: Heart Rate reads *Not set up*, with a slashed icon on a dashed tile and a Connect button. Under it, *Needed for HR-Zone rides only.*
- Step 4: LIVE READINGS shows power, cadence and a dash for heart rate. No large tiles.
- Step 5: the trainer's icon is plain, in the text colour, on a neutral tile, not the app accent. Its status text is grey. Nothing is green.
- Step 6: a long-press does nothing, and no row has a ⋮ or ellipsis button.
- Step 7: *Choose a heart-rate monitor*: nearby devices with three signal bars each, no dBm number, and Cancel.
- Step 8: the trainer is greyed and reads *In use as Smart Trainer*. Tapping it does nothing.
- Step 9: the sheet closes. Heart Rate reads *Connecting…* with a spinner, then *Connected*.
- Step 10: a sheet naming Smart Trainer, the device and *Connected*, with Resistance, Sends and Signal rows. No MAC address.
- Step 11: Signal shows bars and no word. The screen reader reads Strong, Fair or Weak signal.
- Step 12: Change device, Run the compatibility test and Forget this trainer. No separate info dialog.
- Step 13: the row's icon turns faint grey with a slash, the row reads *Disconnected*, and a Reconnect button sits on the row itself.
- Step 14: the row's status text and icon tile turn red, it reads *Couldn't connect*, and Reconnect stays.
- Step 15: the row reads *Connected*.
- Step 16: the hand mark and *Resistance by hand*, in the row's normal colour, not amber.
- Step 17: *Set by hand: this bike does not let the app change it*.
- Step 18: the app asks once. Afterwards Heart Rate reads *Not set up* with Connect.
- Step 19: a sheet with no chevrons. Only Reconnect, and Change source on the Cadence row, respond.
- Step 20: the ride timer kept counting and the trainer kept its resistance.

## Not this check

- The top bar's icons and their colours: [[TST-0675-TheTopBarIconsFromFirstRunToAFailedConnect]].
- What the compatibility test does once opened: TST-0353 and its siblings.
- The start gate and the one-tap reconnect after a ride: [[TST-0667-FromAFinishedRideToTheNextStart]].

## Provenance

Rewritten on 2026-09-30 by [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]] for FEAT-0132. A connected trainer's icon tile is no longer lit in the app accent, and a device that is not connected, or not set up, is drawn faint grey with a slash ([[REQ-0235-ADeviceThatIsNotConnectedIsDrawnWithASlashInTheTopBarAndEveryHubRow]]). Steps 3, 5 and 13 say so; step 14's red tile and text still hold.

Rewritten on 2026-09-28 by [[TASK-0995-TheChecksTheNewHubReopens]] against what FEAT-0130 built. Each step now has exactly one expected line, so a release test procedure can cite each step on its own (`tools/instructions/TESTING.md`, "The release test", rule 9). The long-press and ellipsis lines, which differed by platform, became one step. The failed reconnect is its own step instead of an "if it fails instead" line.

Promoted on 2026-09-28 by [[TASK-0995-TheChecksTheNewHubReopens]] to `level: acceptance`, `status: active`, once FEAT-0130 was built on both platforms. The equipment panel section of the release test now cites each step.

items.name: The top bar draws four equipment icons from first run, and only a failed connect is red with a dot
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies the top bar's four equipment icons in every state DES-0002 § 2 draws: always present, plain when connected, faint grey with a slash when not connected or not set up, and red with a dot only on failure.

## Setup

A phone under 600 dp wide on the release candidate, in dark theme. Clear app data (Android) or delete and reinstall (iOS) so nothing is set up, and create one rider. Mock Wahoo KICKR and Mock HRM Strap available: on Android through **Fake a connected trainer** in Developer Options, on iOS through **Use mock trainer** in Settings → Developer · Trainer. For step 8, a real heart-rate strap that is set up and can be switched off, because a mock device cannot be powered down; on iOS that means the mock off and the real KICKR in Smart Trainer.

## Steps

1. With nothing set up, read the top bar on Workouts, History, the rider screen and Settings.
2. Read the icons' colour, then tap them.
3. Switch the phone to light theme and read the icons again. Switch back to dark.
4. Set up Mock Wahoo KICKR as Smart Trainer only. Read the top bar while it connects.
5. Read the top bar once it is connected.
6. Set up Mock HRM Strap as Heart Rate. Read the top bar.
7. Start a ride and discard it. Read the top bar before tapping anything.
8. Switch the strap off and tap Reconnect on its Hub row. Wait for the connect to fail, then read the top bar.

## Expect

- Step 1: four icons on every screen. Trainer, power and cadence share one shaded background; heart rate stands apart.
- Step 2: all four are faint grey with a diagonal slash, still easy to see, and no dot. Tapping them opens the Equipment Hub.
- Step 3: the faint grey icons and their slashes are still easy to see.
- Step 4: while connecting, the trainer, power and cadence icons are in the app accent.
- Step 5: all three are in the bar's text colour, with no slash. Heart rate stays faint grey and slashed.
- Step 6: all four icons are in the bar's text colour. None is green.
- Step 7: the set-up devices' icons are faint grey with a slash, the same as not set up, with no dot.
- Step 8: the heart-rate icon is red with a small filled dot. The other three are unchanged.

## Not this check

- The Hub's rows and sheets: [[TST-0674-TheEquipmentHubListSetsUpInspectsAndForgetsADevice]].
- Whether the cluster fits a 360 dp phone: REQ-0214's measurement, re-taken by TASK-0988.

## Provenance

Rewritten on 2026-09-30 by [[TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar]] for FEAT-0132. A device that is not connected and one that is not set up are both drawn faint grey with a slash, so they now look the same in the top bar ([[REQ-0235-ADeviceThatIsNotConnectedIsDrawnWithASlashInTheTopBarAndEveryHubRow]]). Steps 2, 3, 5 and 7 say so; steps 4, 6 and 8 still hold.

Rewritten on 2026-09-28 by [[TASK-0995-TheChecksTheNewHubReopens]] against what FEAT-0130 built. Each step now has exactly one expected line, so a release test procedure can cite each step on its own (`tools/instructions/TESTING.md`, "The release test", rule 9). The light-theme reading and the connected reading became steps of their own.

Promoted on 2026-09-28 by [[TASK-0995-TheChecksTheNewHubReopens]] to `level: acceptance`, `status: active`, once FEAT-0130 was built on both platforms. The equipment panel section of the release test now cites each step.

items.name: HRM Prompt — Connect
items.text:
Tap "Connect" on the HRM prompt, then select an HRM device.

## Steps

1. Tap "Connect" on the HRM prompt.
2. Select an HRM device.

## Expect

- Step 1: the HRM scanner opens.
- Step 2: the workout proceeds automatically after connection.

## What is automated

*(partially automated: HrmPromptTest.connectCallbackFired — full flow requires BLE)*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: HRM Prompt — Dismiss Scanner
items.text:
## Setup

A rider with a trainer connected and no heart-rate monitor connected. Pick a Power workout so the prompt offers Connect and Skip.

## Steps

1. On a Power workout, tap "Connect" on the prompt, then dismiss the HRM scanner without selecting a device.
2. Tap Skip on the "Connect Heart Rate Monitor?" prompt.

## Expect

- Step 1: the workout starts without an HRM, as it does after Skip. The prompt does not come back.
- Step 2: tapping Skip starts the workout without an HRM.

## Not this check

On an HR-Zone workout the prompt has no Skip, so dismissing the scanner leaves the ride waiting; [[TST-0179-HR-Zone-Start-Requires-HRM]] tests that.

## Corrected to the apps, 2026-09-25

Step 1 now asserts what both apps do: closing the heart-rate scanner on a Power, Route or free ride without choosing a device starts the ride without the strap, the same as Skip. On Android, `EquipmentBinderHost.onDismissed` in `WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt` calls `skipHeartRateAndContinue`; on iOS, `scannerDismissed` in `WorkoutSelectionView.swift` does the same. Both carry the comment "goes on without the strap where Skip was allowed, as it always has".

PHASE-025 had rewritten this step on 2026-09-22 to say the prompt comes back. Edwin chose the apps' behaviour on 2026-09-25 (decision 6 in [[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit]], applied by [[TASK-0961-ApplyEdwins20260925DecisionsToTheWalk]]). REQ-0216's open question, whether the strap keeps its Connect or Skip prompt on Power and Route rides at all, is separate and unchanged by this correction. The steps were numbered on 2026-09-24 so the two results take separate marks (FEAT-0122, A7).

items.name: Import summary dialog — Save writes the route, Cancel writes nothing
items.text:
Trigger the import summary dialog twice from the same file and take a different exit each time.

## Steps

1. **Save.** Edit the name, tap Save. The workout appears in the Route library under the edited name, and a **snackbar** reads "Imported: \<edited name\>". The feedback is the scaffold's snackbar, not a toast (`WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:961-968`); a toast appears only on a screen with no scaffold snackbar host.
2. **Cancel writes nothing.** Trigger the dialog again and tap Cancel. No workout is saved.
3. **Cancel says nothing either.** No import feedback appears on the Cancel path — no snackbar, no toast. This is the negative the merge keeps as its own step, because a Cancel that silently saves and a Cancel that silently confirms are different defects.

## Expect

- Step 1: the route is in the Route library under the edited name, and a snackbar, not a toast, reads "Imported: \<edited name\>".
- Step 2: no workout is saved.
- Step 3: no snackbar and no toast.

## What it absorbed, and what one tick no longer separates

| Absorbed | Step | What a single tick no longer distinguishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TST-0245` | 2, 3 | A Cancel that saves the route anyway now fails the same tick as a Save that writes the wrong name. |

*(partially automated: `RouteImportSummaryDialogTest.save_fires_onConfirm_with_edited_name` and `.cancel_fires_onCancel_not_onConfirm` cover the dialog's two exits; library persistence and the snackbar copy stay manual.)*

items.name: Auto Backup Does Not Carry Credentials
items.text:
On a device with Auto Backup enabled and Strava connected, uninstall and reinstall. After Auto Backup restores, verify the app shows Strava as disconnected and the BYOK key slot is empty. (Credentials must not ride through Auto Backup either.) *(partially automated: `BackupCredentialExclusionTest` guards the Strava-token + API-key exclusion at the serialisation layer — which is the same scrubbing path Auto Backup uses via `android:allowBackup` attribute rules; uninstall/reinstall round-trip stays manual.)*

The iOS release test must not treat its reinstall or iCloud backup path as this Android Auto Backup result without a separate expectation and scope decision.

## Expect

- After Auto Backup restores, Strava shows as disconnected and the bring-your-own AI key slot is empty.

## Test this fifth, in the destructive backup sequence

**These four rows do not merge; the saving is in running them in order.** Each needs a different install state, and two of them destroy the state the others need, so the order is the whole economy of this group.

1. Fresh install → [[TST-0291-Export-Button-Gating]]
2. Create a rider
3. [[TST-0293-Export-Round-Trip]] — export, producing the file the rest consume
4. [[TST-0298-Merge-Vs-Overwrite-Prompt]] — import over existing data
5. **[[TST-0437-Auto-Backup-Does-Not-Carry-Credentials]] — this row.** The uninstall is destructive, so it comes after every row that needs the populated install, and before the Clear Data row. Strava must be connected when the uninstall happens, or the check has nothing to prove.
6. [[TST-0295-Import-After-Wipe]] — Clear Data

**Anything that needs the pre-wipe state must finish before step 6.** TST-0295 clears app data, and nothing before it can be re-tested without rebuilding the install from step 1.

items.name: Garmin Connect accepts an exported FIT (ISS-0387)
items.text:
Complete a ride, export the session as FIT, and upload the file to Garmin Connect at <https://connect.garmin.com/modern/import-data>. The import must succeed and the activity must open as an indoor cycling ride with power, heart rate and cadence present.

The defect this guards is a file missing its `lap` and `activity` messages, which Garmin rejected outright with *"This file is not supported for the .fit format"* while Strava and intervals.icu accepted the same file. Run the same upload from an iOS export as well — the two encoders are separate implementations and only a real upload distinguishes them.

[[TST-0643]] asserts the messages are in the file on every build. It cannot assert Garmin's importer is happy with them, which is why this check exists and has to be discharged by hand once. Neither can the Garmin SDK: it decodes the *pre-fix* file cleanly and reports `checkFileIntegrity: OK`, so a green decode says the file is well-formed and says nothing about whether the service will take it.

## Expect

- Garmin Connect accepts the file, and it opens as an indoor cycling ride with power, heart rate and cadence present.

## Partial evidence already in hand, 2026-09-02

The rider's own ride, re-encoded through the fixed encoder, **was accepted by Garmin Connect**. The same bytes before the fix were refused twice — once on type without an extension, once on validation with one. So the encoder half of the fix is proven on real rider data, and the `DEVELOPMENT` manufacturer is proven acceptable to Garmin.

**This check is still open**, because that file was built by a test harness and uploaded from a desktop. What remains is the rider's actual path: finish a ride on a device with the new build, tap **Export FIT**, share it, **check the filename that lands** (it must end `.fit`), then upload. The share half — `EXTRA_TITLE` on `ACTION_SEND` — is not a documented contract and has only unit coverage, so it is exactly the half a real device pass is needed for.

**A ready-made pair sits in `docs/issues/evidence/`** — the same synthetic ten-minute ride through the old and the new Android encoder:

- `ISS-0387-android-export-after-fix-2026-09-02.fit` — **upload this one first.** It is the post-fix encoder's output with a correct extension and the full message set. Accepted means the rider is unblocked by the next release; refused means something beyond the two known defects is at work.
- `ISS-0387-android-export-before-fix-2026-09-02.fit` — the same ride through the old encoder, for contrast.

**Do not read the error text as a diagnosis.** Garmin returns *"We don't support the file type you tried to import"* for validation failures as well as for genuinely unsupported types — its own forums show it on files that plainly carry a `.fit` extension. The message tells you it failed, not why.

If the after-fix file is refused, the next suspect is the `manufacturer` field: the encoder writes `DEVELOPMENT` (255) with serial `12345`, and Garmin's developer forum carries recurring (unconfirmed) reports that Connect rejects FIT without a registered manufacturer.

Uploading both is the whole check, and it is also the experiment: a refusal of the first is what proves the diagnosis rather than merely being consistent with it. **If the before-file imports fine, the diagnosis is wrong and ISS-0387 should be reopened** — the fix would still be correct, but it would not be the fix for this rider's problem.

## The share half was run on 2026-09-05, and it failed

Edwin exported a ride on the tablet (build 2.1.8 / versionCode 182, which contains the TASK-0802 fix) and saved it to Google Drive. The file landed as `Your Trainer Ride <date>_<time>` — **no `.fit`**. Exactly the half this check warned was untested.

Cause and fix are [[ISS-0393-DriveNamesTheSharedFitFromTheSubject]] and [[TASK-0805-ShareSubjectIsTheFilename]]: Drive names the saved file from `EXTRA_SUBJECT` and ignores the `EXTRA_TITLE` TASK-0802 relied on. The subject is now the filename.

**This check stays open, and its device leg has to be re-run on a build containing TASK-0805.** The sequence is unchanged: finish or open a ride, tap **Export FIT**, **Save to Drive**, confirm the saved name ends `.fit`, then upload it at <https://connect.garmin.com/app/import-data>.

Worth capturing on the same run: which apps the share sheet offers. The declared type narrowed to `application/vnd.ant.fit` in TASK-0802 and nobody has looked at a real share sheet since.

## The rider ran the whole path on 2026-09-08 and Garmin took the file

> "I tested the FIT file export and it imported into Garmin without any issues." — Paul Evans, 2026-09-08

This is the leg the check has been open for: a real ride, exported from a device on a released build, uploaded by the rider to the real service, accepted. Every pass before it was a synthetic file, a desktop upload, or both.

**The file itself is in the repo** at `docs/issues/evidence/ISS-0387-rider-export-accepted-by-garmin-2026-09-08.fit`, and decoding it confirms it is this app's output rather than something Garmin re-exported: `manufacturer` 255 (`DEVELOPMENT`), `serial_number` 12345, 1800 record messages over a 30-minute ride, `sport` 2 / `sub_sport` 6, and **one `lap` and one `activity` message present** — the two the defect was the absence of. The filename Paul's export produced was `Ride_20260907_1755.fit`, which answers the share-half question this note asked separately: the extension survived.

**One question stands before the mark moves.** Nobody has established which app version he exported from. v2.1.8 (versionCode 185) is the build carrying both the missing-messages fix and TASK-0805's filename fix, and it reached Play on 2026-09-06 — two days before the mail, which is tight enough to be worth asking rather than assuming. His 2026-09-02 report of the same export failing makes the inference a strong one, and it is still an inference. **Ask him the version; on 2.1.8 or later this check is discharged.**

Decoding the file also turned up a defect nobody had reported — the session's work field carries kilojoules where FIT defines joules, and iOS omits the field entirely ([[ISS-0420-TotalWorkIsWrittenInKilojoulesIntoAJoulesField]]). It does not affect this check: Garmin accepted the file, and Garmin derives work from the power stream rather than that field.

items.name: Family tier resolves for a cold-started, never-used rider
items.text:
**Two preconditions in one run, because one rider can satisfy both:** a FAMILY licence on the device, and a rider who was created and has never ridden and is not the primary rider.

1. **Cold start.** Force-quit the app. Reopen it and immediately select that rider, before anything else has had a chance to resolve the tier.
2. **Ride.** Complete a workout as that rider, and tap Save ride.
3. **Premium features are there.** Tap Done on the celebration, and open the ride's menu in History.

*(partially automated: `LicensingManagerTest` covers device-wide tier resolution and the billing-priority logic, `UserRepositoryTest.multiple_riders_sorted_or_not_still_each_retrievable` the multi-rider path; the Play Billing purchase, the cold-start timing and the screens after Save stay manual.)*

## Expect

- The celebration opens with no paywall, and the ride's menu offers Export FIT without a lock.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0367]], which asked for the same completion overlay under a different precondition: a rider who had never been used, rather than a cold start. ISS-0108 was one defect that both preconditions exposed, and a rider who is both new and selected straight after a force-quit exercises them together in one workout.

One tick no longer separates "the tier resolves too late after a cold start" from "the tier resolves wrongly for a rider with no history". If it fails, run it again with the app already warm to tell the two apart.

## Expect rewritten 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] removed the summary's FIT export and Strava upload buttons: a ride now uploads by itself to each connected account, and Export FIT is in History. The check still asks whether FAMILY has resolved for this rider, read from the PRO-gated Export FIT. It states how the product behaves now as well as the fixed defect, so it carries `kind: feature` (`TESTING.md`, "When to invalidate").

items.name: compatibility.json live and reachable (TASK-0525 — post-deploy sanity)
items.text:
From a browser on any network, navigate to `https://your-applications.com/your-trainer/compatibility.json`. Verify HTTP 200, `content-type: application/json`, and that the body parses as JSON with `schema_version: 1` + a `trainers[]` array containing at least the three verified entries (KICKR, KICKR CORE, Direto). *(Re-run only when the list is updated.)*

## Expect

- HTTP 200 and `content-type: application/json`.
- JSON with `schema_version: 1` and `trainers[]` listing at least KICKR, KICKR CORE and Direto.

items.name: TODAY ghost lifecycle — VM combine + course-switch reset
items.text:
— VM combine flow drops the PB when stored ghosts is empty; `loadGhostsForCourse` nulls `_sessionBestGhost` on course switch. Replaces §1.19 "TODAY Ghost On First-Ever Ride" + "TODAY Ghost Cleared Between Rides" rows.

## Expect

- The first-ever ride of a course shows no TODAY ghost.
- Switching course clears the previous course's TODAY ghost.

## Left owed 2026-08-19 — the one coverage claim that names nothing runnable

Its 66 siblings from the same changelog section were given a `command:` naming the test that took them over. This one could not be: the body names `loadGhostsForCourse` and describes a "VM combine flow", both of which are **production** symbols, not a test. There is no class here to run.

That is exactly the unrunnable claim [[ISS-0198]] refused to let `covered_by:` carry, and the honest response is to owe the release test rather than assume the coverage. It stays `active` and `manual`, so it is asked for, until someone either names the covering test — `GhostRepositorySessionBestTest` is the likely candidate but was **not** verified to cover these two assertions — or tests it.

items.name: Rider-facing copy says connect, never pair
items.text:
Technical identifiers in logs and diagnostics may keep pair; only rider-facing copy is in scope. (TST-0032, TST-0033 and TST-0498 check individual strings; nothing sweeps the vocabulary.)

## Steps

1. Sweep every rider-facing string on the connection path: the Equipment Hub's rows and captions, the device picker sheet, the device details sheet and its Forget question, the HRM prompt, mid-ride reconnect, connection error dialogs, and any notification.
2. Read every place the surface is named.

## Expect

- Step 1: each reads connect, connected or disconnected, and never pair or paired.
- Step 2: the surface is named **Equipment Hub** wherever it is named.

## Where this check came from

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Rewritten 2026-09-28

Step 1's list named the scanner and the slot states. Since FEAT-0130 the Hub is a list whose rows open a picker sheet or a details sheet, each with new words, so the list names those instead. The expected results are unchanged.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: New screens carry no stray English in a Tier-1 locale
items.text:
Set the device to each Tier-1 non-English locale in turn — de, fr, es, it, ja, zh-Hant, pt-BR, nl — and test the screens added or changed since the last release. Verify every rider-facing label, button, dialog body, empty state and toast is translated, with no stray English. Brand nouns that are deliberately untranslated — intervals.icu, Strava, Your Trainer, FTMS — are expected to stay in English. Record any untranslated string with its screen and locale. (TST-0110 and TST-0497 each cover one surface; nothing sweeps the new ones.)

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Expect

- Every rider-facing label, button, dialog body, empty state and toast is translated, with no stray English.
- Brand nouns stay in English: intervals.icu, Strava, Your Trainer, FTMS.

items.name: Rider-facing copy holds the product-as-subject register
items.text:
Read the rider-facing copy on the paywall, About, the onboarding and empty states, and any integration or upgrade prompt. Sign-offs on correspondence are outside this check and are fine as they are.

## Steps

1. Read the copy for who its subject is.
2. Read the copy for how it opens and how it addresses the rider.
3. Read the copy for its English cadence.

## Expect

- Step 1: it is written with the product as the subject, not the developer — no *I built*, no *I'll send*.
- Step 2: there are no motivational-imperative openers and no second-person stacking.
- Step 3: British-English cadence — *household* rather than *whole family*, *one-time purchase* rather than *buy once*.

## Where this check came from

*Split out of [[TST-0013-IosParityAcceptance]] on 2026-08-20. That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: No Upload When Not Linked
items.text:
Complete a workout with Strava unlinked. Verify no upload errors.

## Expect

- The ride saves with Strava unlinked, and no upload error appears.

items.name: Two riders upload to their own Strava accounts, and the uploaded data is right
items.text:
Two rides on one device, two Strava accounts, then one visit to strava.com to read both.

## Procedure

1. **Each rider's ride goes to their own account.** Rider A completes a workout — it uploads to A's Strava. Rider B completes a workout — it uploads to B's Strava. Neither appears on the other's account.
2. **The uploaded activities carry the right data.** Open strava.com for both riders. Each activity has the correct name, duration, power and HR data.

*(Partially automated: `WorkoutSessionRepositoryTest` covers the per-user session scoping that drives dispatch; the Strava upload and everything read on strava.com stay manual.)*

## Expect

- Step 1: each ride is on its own rider's Strava account, and not on the other's.
- Step 2: each activity is titled with the ride's workout or route name, and has the right duration, power and heart rate.

## Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

| Retired | What it asked for | Taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [[TST-0107-Upload-Verification]] | name, duration, power and HR correct on strava.com for both riders | step 2 |

## What one tick no longer distinguishes

- **TST-0107** — routing and content are separate failures: an activity can land on the right account with the wrong power data, and that now records as the same verdict as it landing on the wrong account entirely.

## Evidence (fill after running)

- Which account each activity landed on, and the four fields read off each.

## Step 2 reworded 2026-10-10

[[FEAT-0134-WhenARideEndsOneScreenCelebratesItSavesItAndSharesItAsAPicture]] sends a title and a description with each upload. Before, Strava named the activity itself, such as "Evening Ride". The title and description in full are [[TST-0688-EachUploadIsTitledWithTheRidesNameAndDescribedByItsHeadline]].

items.name: Coming back to the app checks a connected rider's Strava ride links
items.text:
With a rider who connected Strava, background Your Trainer (Recents → swipe to another app, or Home), wait at least 30 s, then bring it back to the front and watch logcat for about 30 s. Do not tap anything. *([[TASK-0973-StravaRideLinksAreCheckedAgainForAConnectedRider|TASK-0973]])*

## Expect

- Within about 5 s, with no tap, the log shows `StravaUpload: reconcile`: `N session(s) need activityId resolution` or `done, matched=0 / 0`.

## Rewritten 2026-09-26

This check expects the automatic ride-link check again. Connecting Strava is the rider's standing consent for automatic reads of their own data (`tools/instructions/AGENT_RULES.md`, "No silent network calls", as Edwin corrected it on 2026-09-26), so the check that TASK-0400 added is allowed, and Edwin asked for it back. For one day, 2026-09-25 to 2026-09-26, this check expected the opposite: [[TASK-0964-StravaIsCalledOnlyWhenTheRiderAsks|TASK-0964]] had removed the check under the earlier wording, which said every request needed a tap.

A rider who has not connected Strava gets no check. That is pinned by `StravaRideLinksAreCheckedForAConnectedRiderTest`, not tested here, because the PRO test that carries this check has one rider.

On iOS the check is not built yet. iOS checks ride links only from the Settings tap, and the gap is a MISSING row in `PARITY_MATRIX.md` B.1.

items.name: Post-restore reconciliation (ISS-0142)
items.text:
Restore a rider backup that contains uploaded sessions, with Strava connected. Pick the rider and watch logcat. Do not tap Refresh. *(ISS-0142, [[TASK-0973-StravaRideLinksAreCheckedAgainForAConnectedRider|TASK-0973]])*

## Expect

- With no tap, the log shows `StravaUpload: reconcile — N session(s) need activityId resolution`, then `matched sessionId=… → activityId=…` lines.
- Those rides' History rows change from `Open in Strava` to `View on Strava`.

## Rewritten 2026-09-26

Picking a rider who connected Strava checks their ride links again. Edwin corrected the network rule on 2026-09-26: a connected account is standing consent for automatic reads of the rider's own data. For one day this check reconciled from the Refresh tap instead, because [[TASK-0964-StravaIsCalledOnlyWhenTheRiderAsks|TASK-0964]] had removed the rider-select check; TASK-0973 restored it. On iOS the check is not built yet: iOS reconciles only from the Settings tap, and the gap is a MISSING row in `PARITY_MATRIX.md` B.1.

items.name: Deletion detection (ISS-0125)
items.text:
Delete an activity on Strava's web UI for a session your device has uploaded. Tap Refresh in the Strava section of the rider's Profile. Picking the rider no longer reconciles ([[TASK-0964-StravaIsCalledOnlyWhenTheRiderAsks|TASK-0964]]). Verify logcat emits `reconcile — detected deletion of sessionId=…` and the corresponding history row flips from `View on Strava` back to the white `[☁] Strava` upload pill. *(ISS-0125)*

On iOS, tap **Refresh Strava status** in the Strava section of the rider's Profile. iOS writes no such log line; the deleted ride's History row shows the **Upload to Strava** pill instead (`StravaService.reconcileDeletions`). Edwin accepted this as the iOS equivalent on 2026-09-25 ([[TASK-0960-FinishTheWalkProcedureStateReadinessAndPlatformAudit|TASK-0960]], decision 19).

## Expect

- [android] The log shows `reconcile — detected deletion of sessionId=…`, and that ride's pill turns from `View on Strava` back to the white `[☁] Strava`.
- [ios] That ride's History row shows the `Upload to Strava` pill instead of `View on Strava`.

items.name: The celebration shows how each connected account's upload is going, and nothing for an account that is not connected
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies the upload chips in the celebration's bottom bar (DES-0005, "Upload chips") on both platforms, and that iOS now uploads a saved ride to each connected account by itself ([[ISS-0534-OniOSASavedRideIsNotUploadedToAConnectedAccount]]).

## Setup

PRO, so the Strava upload is not gated. The rider has Strava and intervals.icu connected: Android Profile → Connected, iOS the rider's Profile. A trainer that accepts control, or the fake trainer. Airplane mode off.

## Steps

1. Save a ride, and watch the bottom bar of the celebration.
2. Tap View on Strava.
3. Return to the app, and tap Open on the intervals.icu chip.
4. Turn airplane mode on. Save another ride, and read the chips.
5. Turn airplane mode off, and watch the chips without tapping.
6. Tap Retry on a chip that reads Upload failed.
7. Disconnect intervals.icu. Save a ride, and read the bottom bar.
8. Disconnect Strava too. Save a ride, and read the bottom bar.

## Expect

- Step 1: one chip for Strava and one for intervals.icu, each reading Uploading…, then Uploaded with a green tick.
- Step 2: Strava opens on this ride's activity.
- Step 3: intervals.icu opens on this ride's activity.
- [android] Step 4: the Strava chip reads Waiting for the network; the intervals.icu chip reads Upload failed, with Retry.
- [ios] Step 4: both chips read Waiting for the network.
- [android] Step 5: the Strava chip turns to Uploaded by itself; the intervals.icu chip still reads Upload failed.
- [ios] Step 5: both chips turn to Uploaded by themselves.
- Step 6: the chip reads Uploading…, then Uploaded.
- Step 7: only the Strava chip shows.
- Step 8: no upload chip shows; the bottom bar holds only its buttons.

## Not this check

- What the upload is called on Strava and intervals.icu: [[TST-0688-EachUploadIsTitledWithTheRidesNameAndDescribedByItsHeadline]].
- History's upload pills and Retry: [[TST-0102-Auto-Upload-After-Workout]].
- Which rider's account a ride goes to: [[TST-0106-Auto-Upload-Per-User]].
- A FREE rider's Strava gate: the Strava checks in the PRO Route section.

## Platform readiness

On iOS an upload made offline waits for the network instead of failing, and nothing on the iOS debug menu makes an upload fail. So step 6 has no failed chip to retry on iOS unless the account's access is revoked; the release test marks it.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the built chips: Android `UploadStatusChip` (`UPLOAD_CHIP_STRAVA_TAG`, `UPLOAD_CHIP_INTERVALS_ICU_TAG`, `UPLOAD_CHIP_RETRY_TAG`) with uploads from `RideUploads` (Strava queued by WorkManager until the network returns; intervals.icu sent at once), and iOS `UploadChip` (`celebration.uploadRetry`) with uploads from `RideUploader`, which keeps an offline ride pending until `NWPathMonitor` sees the network. On iOS a failed chip also names a short reason, `Upload failed · <reason>`.

items.name: Each upload to Strava and intervals.icu is titled with the ride's name and described by its headline
items.text:
## Purpose

Verifies DES-0005 section 5 on both platforms: what a saved ride is called on Strava and intervals.icu, and that the place where the rider connects each account says so.

## Setup

PRO. The rider has Strava and intervals.icu connected, and a browser signed in to both accounts. A workout ride saved on this build has uploaded to both, such as the first ride of [[TST-0687-TheCelebrationShowsEachConnectedAccountsUploadAndOnlyThose]].

## Steps

1. On strava.com, open that ride's activity and read its title.
2. Read the activity's description.
3. On intervals.icu, open the same ride and read its name and description.
4. Save a Quick Ride, and open it on strava.com.
5. In the app, read the Strava and intervals.icu lines where the accounts are connected.

## Expect

- Step 1: the title is the workout's name, with no app name in front.
- Step 2: `<headline>: <large number>, <comparison>. Ridden indoors with Your Trainer.`, such as `First time on Sweet Spot Base: 1:00:00, the time to beat next time.`
- Step 3: the same title and the same description as on Strava.
- Step 4: the title is Quick Ride, not Strava's own name such as Evening Ride.
- Step 5: each line says Connected, then `finished rides upload automatically, with their name and a short description`.

## Not this check

- The chips on the celebration while the upload runs: [[TST-0687-TheCelebrationShowsEachConnectedAccountsUploadAndOnlyThose]].
- That the activity's duration, power and heart rate are right, and on the right rider's account: [[TST-0106-Auto-Upload-Per-User]].
- The description in another language. It follows the app's language, and the unit tests `UploadTextTest` (Android) and `UploadTextTests` (iOS) cover German.

## Provenance

Written on 2026-10-10 by [[TASK-1041-TheChecksParityRowsGalleriesAndReleasePaperworkForTheCelebration]] from the built text: Android `UploadText.forSession` and iOS `UploadText`, used by every upload path. Strava receives `name`, `description` and `trainer = 1`; intervals.icu receives `name` and `description`. On intervals.icu the connected line keeps the athlete's name when it is known: `Connected as <name> — finished rides upload automatically, with their name and a short description`.

items.name: Resistance edge — gear 1 / 0 % floors at 5 % level
items.text:
## Steps

In Resistance mode at gear 1 and 0 %, ride the floor and report the feel.

## Expect

- A very light spin, not "chain dropped".

## Original wording

In Resistance mode at gear 1 / 0 %, ride the floor and report the feel: it should be a very light spin, not "chain dropped". [1.11]

## Narrowed 2026-09-12 — the number moved to a note CI runs

[[TST-0664]] asserts the dispatched level is 5 at gear 1 on flat ground, for a 75 kg and a 95 kg rider, on every build via `PhysicsUtilsLinearSnapshotTest`. The floor exists because SIM physics says 0 W there and 0 % feels like a dropped chain on some hardware — whether the 5 % floor actually avoids that feel is the question this row still asks, and only a rider on a trainer can answer it.

The row keeps `automation: manual` and no `command:` so that question stays in the release gate (`tools/instructions/TESTING.md` § "Release gating").

items.name: Resistance edge — descent floors at 5 % level
items.text:
## Steps

In Resistance mode, coast down descents: gear 1 at −15 %, gear 9 at −3 % and gear 13 at −5 %.

## Expect

- The trainer does not go to genuine free-spin: a little torque stays under the pedals.

## Original wording

Resistance mode, on a descent the rider is actually coasting down. Verify the trainer does not go to genuine free-spin — a little torque stays under the pedals. Ride gear 1 at −15 %, gear 9 at −3 % and gear 13 at −5 %. [1.11]

## Narrowed 2026-09-12 — one point of the claim moved to a note CI runs, the rest did not

[[TST-0664]] asserts gear 1 at −15 % dispatches level 5, on every build via `PhysicsUtilsLinearSnapshotTest`. That is one point, and this row claims the floor holds at *any* gear on *any* slope at or below −3 %. Nothing in the source asserts the wider claim, so the sampling above is not optional — it is the only check the wider claim gets. Two more `assertEquals` in `PhysicsUtilsLinearSnapshotTest` would automate it, and TASK-0882 wrote no code.

The feel half stays here too: a floor of 5 % is meant to keep a little torque under the pedals on a descent, and only a rider can say whether it does. The row keeps `automation: manual` and no `command:` so both stay in the release gate.

## Corrected 2026-09-12 — "any gear" was never true, and now a test says so

This row read *"any gear, slope at or below −3 %"*. That is not what the code does, and it should not be. A high gear trims the grade **upward**, so gear 26 on a −3 % descent reaches the trainer as `−3 × 0.5 + 3.0 = +1.5 %` — a real climb that ought to cost real watts. Flooring it would mean a rider who shifts up on a descent feels nothing change.

What floors is the **effective** grade, not the slope the rider sees. `simulationResistance_does_not_floor_a_high_gear_on_a_shallow_descent` in `PhysicsUtilsLinearSnapshotTest` now pins that boundary, so nobody "completes" the floor to cover every gear.

The three gears named above are the ones that do floor, and [[TST-0664]] now asserts all three on every build ([[TASK-0888-AssertTheTwoNarrowedGearClaims]]). What is left here is the feel: whether a 5 % floor reads as a light spin rather than a dropped chain. Only a rider can say, so the row keeps `automation: manual` and no `command:`.

items.name: Resistance edge — gear 26 / 5 % near-saturation
items.text:
## Steps

In Resistance mode, ride gear 26 at 5 % and report the effort.

## Expect

- Sustainable-hard: around 530 W for the reference rider, roughly 2.5 × FTP.

## Original wording

Top gear on a moderate climb in Resistance mode — gear 26 at 5 %. Ride it and report the effort: sustainable-hard, around 530 W for the reference rider, roughly 2.5 × FTP. [1.11]

## Narrowed 2026-09-12 — the level moved to a note CI runs

[[TST-0665]] asserts the dispatched level is 80 at gear 26 on a 5 % climb, and that only a 20 % climb saturates at 100. It runs `PhysicsUtilsLinearSnapshotTest` on every build, so both the "~80 %" figure and the "does not saturate" claim are machine-checked.

What stays here is the watts a rider actually produces at that level, which no unit test can assert. This row is also a one-off rather than something [[TST-0658]] absorbs: gear 26 sits above the gear sweep's derived ceiling, so the sweep never rides it. The row keeps `automation: manual` and no `command:` so the reading stays in the release gate.

items.name: The parser keeps what the bike sends, and a 40-minute ride still exports its connect-time block
items.text:
Test on **both platforms**. The fake trainer supplies the packets. The KICKR leg confirms nothing changed on real hardware.

## Setup

Developer Options on Android: "Fake Trainer — no hardware needed (Debug)" on. The repeated-status mode is **Send a Machine Status every second**, under "Fake Trainer — what it puts on the wire (Debug)" ([[TASK-0924-AndroidDebugControlsForTheOwedChecks]]).

One **forty-minute** ride on the fake trainer. This is not a spot check: the defect only appears once the 500-line log has wrapped round several times.

The packets steps 5 to 9 name come from the packet menu in the same section: "Heart rate relayed — bit 9" for steps 5 and 6, "Heart rate zero — bit 9 set, value 0" for step 7, "Bits 7, 8 and 9 — average power, energy, heart rate" for step 8, and "Speed, total distance, resistance level" for step 9. Both controls apply within a second, with no reconnect. Set the packet back to Default and the repeated status off when done.

**iOS has neither control.** Settings → Developer · Trainer offers no repeated-status mode and no choice of packet, so steps 1 to 9 cannot be produced on iOS. Edwin decided on 2026-09-25 to build both, mirroring Android, in [[TASK-0962-IosDebugControlsForTheFirstIosReleaseWalk|TASK-0962]], deferred to the first iOS release.

A heart-rate strap, for step 6.

A KICKR, or another trainer that accepts control, for step 10.

The iOS build on a second device.

## Steps

### The log

1. Connect the fake trainer in the repeated-status mode.
2. Ride for forty minutes.
3. Open Settings, Equipment, Bluetooth Diagnostics, and share the log. Read the export.
4. Disconnect and reconnect mid-ride, then export the log again.

### The fields

5. With **no heart-rate strap connected**, feed a packet carrying a non-zero heart rate in bit 9. Look at the cockpit.
6. Connect a strap and watch the heart-rate tile across several notifications.
7. Disconnect the strap. Feed a bit-9 heart rate of zero.
8. Feed a flags word with bits 7 and 8 set as well as bit 9.
9. Feed a packet with speed, total distance and resistance level present. Read the log, then look at every screen.

### The KICKR leg

10. Ride a KICKR for ten minutes and export the log.

## Expect

- Step 1: the export's connect-time block is at the top and complete: characteristic table, 0x2ACC feature and target bits, Request Control and Start/Resume responses.
- Step 2: **a repeated line appears once, with a count**, such as `[FTMS] Status notification: [4] (x2400)`, not hundreds of times.
- Step 3: the Indoor Bike Data flags word appears exactly once, with its field names decoded. MAC addresses still read `device_1`, `device_2`.
- Step 4: the pinned block describes the current connection, and the counts start again.
- Step 5: the cockpit shows the bike's heart rate.
- Step 6: **the strap's value wins** at every notification, and the bike's is ignored.
- Step 7: no heart rate is shown. Zero means no strap on the console, not a stopped heart.
- Step 8: the heart rate is still correct.
- Step 9: the log shows all three fields were read, and **nothing new appears on any screen**.
- Step 10: cadence, power and the displayed speed are exactly what they were. The export's format for a line that is not repeated is unchanged.

## Not this check

- Where the trainer's own speed should be shown. That is ADR-0011 and ISS-0388, and this phase deliberately leaves it untouched.
- How the app decides a trainer cannot be driven: [[TST-0648-DataOnlyDetectionOnAMockRefusingTrainer]].

## What a failure means

An export in step 3 whose earliest line is minutes old means the pinned block is not protected from being pushed out of the log. A heart rate in step 6 that flickers between two values means the strap-wins rule is a preference rather than a gate, and the bike is still writing into the same place.

## Notes

- Step 8 proves the parser walks the offsets field by field rather than reading heart rate from a hard-coded position.
- Step 9: this phase supplies the fields and does not decide where they are displayed.
- On 2026-09-27 the four Expect lines that step 3 carried were given to steps 1, 2 and 3, so the lines pair with the steps ([[TASK-0977-ShortenTheExpectLinesOfTheOwedChecks]]). All four are still read in the export at step 3; the connect-time block comes from connecting, and the repeated line from the ride.

items.name: No Dead Gears
items.text:
## Steps

In simulation mode on the LINEAR preset, shift through all gears, 1 to 26.

## Expect

- Each gear change produces a perceptible resistance change.

## Original wording

In simulation mode on the LINEAR preset, shift through all gears 1–26. Verify each gear change produces a perceptible resistance change.

## Corrected 2026-09-12 — the range is 1–26, not 1–22

LINEAR has had 26 gears since TASK-0459, which widened the table from 22 gears at 5–72 % to 26 at 5–82 % (`VirtualGearPreset.kt`, `LINEAR_RESISTANCE`). The row was still asking for a test that stopped four gears early, which left the top of the table — where the steps are 3 % apart and a dead gear is most likely to hide — untested.

## Narrowed 2026-09-12 — the table is machine-checked, the perception is the sweep's

That the values differ from gear to gear is asserted on every build: `ResistanceForGearTest` walks gears 2..26 twice, once in `every gear shift produces a noticeable change` and once in `resistance increases monotonically with gear`, and the second is the stronger claim — strictly increasing, not merely different. Run it with `cd android && ./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests com.yourtrainer.ui.viewmodels.ResistanceForGearTest`.

No command is written into this row's frontmatter, because a distinct number in a table is not a *perceptible* change on a trainer, and perception is the whole of what this row asks. [[TST-0658]] measures it directly: the sweep rides each gear in turn, records average watts, and flags a gear whose watts did not move. It stops at a derived ceiling rather than at gear 26, so the top gears still need this row's hand test.

items.name: Gear 1 Light
items.text:
## Steps

Ride gear 1 on flat (0 % slope) at 80 rpm.

## Expect

- A very easy spin, about 30 W at 80 rpm.

## Original wording

Verify gear 1 on flat (0 % slope) feels like a very easy spin (~30 W at 80 RPM).

## Narrowed 2026-09-12 — the 30 W is a floor CI asserts, the "easy spin" is the sweep's

The ~30 W figure is not an estimate, it is the ERG floor. `PhysicsUtils.routeErgTargetPower` coerces its result into 30..1000 W, and gear 1 on the flat sits below the floor because its effective grade is −3 %, where the physics says the rider is coasting. `PhysicsUtilsTest` asserts the exact value in `FEAT-0068 — gear sweep produces monotonic target range`, which does `assertEquals(30, flatLow)` for gear 1 at 0 %. Run it with `cd android && ./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests com.yourtrainer.utils.PhysicsUtilsTest`.

No command is written into this row's frontmatter, because "feels like a very easy spin" is the claim and it is subjective. [[TST-0658]] rides gear 1 as the first step of its climb and records what the rider actually produced there, so the sweep's scorecard is the evidence this row reads.

items.name: History shows a real workout name, never "Unknown Workout"
items.text:
Both cases read off one History list in one go.

## Steps

1. **Free Ride.** Complete a Free Ride session.
2. **A deleted custom workout.** Delete a custom workout that has past sessions.

## Expect

- Step 1: it appears in History as "Free Ride", not "Unknown Workout".
- Step 2: those sessions show a formatted name, for example "My Custom 1", not "Unknown Workout".

## Background

Neither may read "Unknown Workout" — that string is the defect ISS-0116 fixed.

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0385]] (step 2). Both are the same fallback in the same list, reached by two different missing-name paths.

One tick no longer says whether the Free Ride name or the deleted-workout name is the one that fell through to "Unknown Workout". The two take different branches, so write down which row in History was wrong.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were a numbered list with no `## Steps` heading, so the release test read them as one part and could give the whole check only one mark. They now sit under `## Steps`, with one expectation each under `## Expect`, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: No Mid-Ride Mode Toggle
items.text:
Start a ride from any tab (Quick Ride / Free Ride / Zone Ride). Verify there is NO MODE button in the cockpit — mode is fixed for the session. To change modes, return to Workout Selection and pick a different tab. *(partially automated: `WorkoutViewModelDispatchTest.startFreeRide_*` — mode is set once at dispatch and only re-routed through `selectWorkout` / `startFreeRide`, so no in-cockpit mode cycle exists on the VM surface; cockpit-absence of the button stays visual.)*

## Expect

- There is no MODE button in the cockpit. The mode is fixed for the session.

## Also covers ISS-0130 from 2026-09-12

[[TST-0429-No-Resistance-Mode]] was retired on 2026-09-12 and its `covers: [[ISS-0130]]` moved here. That row asked a rider to read the mode toggle's label; this row asks for the toggle's absence, which is the stronger claim and the one the code supports. A rider who confirms there is no MODE button has confirmed there is no "RESISTANCE MODE" label on it either.
