items.name: A purchased PRO is never shown as FREE
items.text:
Three questions about one rider: does their PRO survive the Play Store being unreachable, does the app wait for Play instead of guessing during the first seconds after launch, and does a new PRO device avoid asking which rider holds the seat.

Manual because every failure here is environmental — Play reachability, cache state, cold-start timing. None of it can be produced from inside the app.

## Setup

- A device holding a **real PRO purchase** on the signed-in Play account. The debug tier override does not exercise this check: it bypasses billing entirely, and billing is the thing under test.
- Know how to reach **Settings → About**, which is where the tier is displayed.
- For the fresh-install cases, be ready to uninstall and reinstall. Riders on the device will be lost, so export anything you want to keep first.

## Case A — PRO survives an unreachable Play Store

The stated market is basement tablets on intermittent Wi-Fi. A paying rider reading as FREE is the most serious failure this check guards.

1. Aeroplane mode on → force-stop the app → cold start.
2. **Expect:** the tier still reads PRO. PRO surfaces stay unlocked.
3. Aeroplane mode off. Clear the **Play Store** app's cache (Android Settings → Apps → Google Play Store → Storage → Clear cache) → force-stop Your Trainer → cold start.
4. **Expect:** still PRO.
5. Disable the Play Store app entirely (Android Settings → Apps → Google Play Store → Disable) → cold start Your Trainer.
6. **Expect:** still PRO. Re-enable the Play Store afterwards.

All three must hold. Any one of them reading FREE is a fail.

## Case B — the app waits for Play rather than guessing

`BillingManager.retryConnection` reconnects every 2 s with **no cap**, so on a device Play never answers it would retry forever. `startResolutionTimeout` bounds that at 8 s and then releases the gate on whatever the cache holds. Both halves are tested here: the waiting, and the bound on the waiting.

1. Uninstall, reinstall, and launch on the PRO account with no backup to restore.
2. From the first frame, go for rider creation as fast as you can tap.
3. **Expect:** no rider cap and no seat write is applied before Play answers. In practice: you are never told you have reached a rider limit, and no seat chooser appears because the app decided you were FREE for a moment.
4. Now the bound. Uninstall, reinstall, put the device in aeroplane mode **before** first launch, so nothing can answer and nothing is cached.
5. **Expect:** the app becomes usable within about 8 seconds rather than hanging. It reads FREE — correctly, since nothing has ever said otherwise — and it does not sit waiting forever.

## Case C — a new PRO device does not ask which rider gets the seat

1. Clean install on the PRO account, no backup restored. Complete ordinary onboarding.
2. **Expect:** no seat-selection screen at any point. The rider you create becomes the seat.
3. Restore a backup made **after** FEAT-0104 shipped.
4. **Expect:** no seat-selection screen. The seat resolves from the restored database.
5. Restore a backup made **before** FEAT-0104, holding more than one rider, onto the PRO device.
6. **Expect:** the seat-selection screen **does** appear, naming the riders that will become inaccessible.

Step 6 is the only case in this check where the chooser is correct, and the only path to it that does not involve a purchase.

## On iOS

iOS bills through the App Store, so the Play Store actions have App Store equivalents. The rule under test is the same: a paying rider never reads as FREE.

- **Setup:** a sandbox account holding a real PRO purchase, signed in under Settings → App Store → Sandbox Account.
- **Case A:** test the aeroplane-mode cold start only. iOS has no store app whose cache can be cleared or which can be disabled, so steps 3 to 6 do not apply.
- **Case B:** test it as written, with the App Store as the store that must answer.
- **Case C:** test steps 1 to 4 as written. Steps 5 and 6 need the seat-selection screen, which no iOS path opens yet ([[ISS-0430-IosProSeatIsNeverEnforced]]). Leave that part unresolved until it does.

## Expect

- [android] Case A: after each cold start (aeroplane mode, Play Store cache cleared, Play Store disabled) the tier reads PRO and PRO stays unlocked.
- [ios] Case A: after the aeroplane-mode cold start the tier reads PRO and PRO stays unlocked.
- Case B, the wait: no rider-limit message and no seat chooser before the store answers.
- Case B, the bound: usable within about 8 seconds, reading FREE, never waiting forever.
- Case C, clean install: no seat-selection screen. The rider you create holds the seat.
- Case C, a backup from after FEAT-0104: no seat-selection screen.
- Case C, a backup from before FEAT-0104 with several riders: the seat-selection screen **does** appear, naming the riders who become inaccessible.

## Not this check

- Which rider the seat resolves to, and the arrival-state table — that logic is [[TST-0016-SeatResolutionAndArrivalStates]] and runs as unit tests.
- Whether the purchase itself completes: [[TST-0074-Purchase-Flow]].
- Recovering an entitlement after a reinstall by tapping Restore: [[TST-0641-Restore-Purchases]]. This check is about what happens when nobody taps anything.

## Provenance

Covers the two billing defects PHASE-020 repaired: [[ISS-0374-EntitlementNotCachedOffline]] (Case A) and [[ISS-0373-EntitlementRaceOnColdStart]] (Case B).

Re-levelled 2026-08-19 from `system` to `acceptance` (ISS-0213 / TASK-0507): the note describes a person verifying rider-facing behaviour, so `level:` was wrong. `status:` returned to `active` in the same edit, because an acceptance check rests there and its verdict is a ledger event, not a field (ADR-0031, later ADR-0037). Safe to re-level because this note is one procedure over one subject, which is the shape ADR-0030 requires — unlike TST-0011, TST-0012 and TST-0013, which were 18, 15 and 107 rows each and were left alone.

Rewritten 2026-09-06 into the Setup / Steps / Expect shape. The previous title advertised "the unbounded retry" and the body never mentioned a retry, so the mechanism and the observable were never connected; Case B now names both.

items.name: Device-Wide License
items.text:
**The entitlement is device-wide; the PRO seat is per-rider. Both are true at once, and this check exists to hold them apart.**

There is no such thing as a rider holding a licence. The purchase belongs to the Play account on the device, and `currentUserTier` resolves it from `BillingManager`'s purchases with no reference to which rider is selected — so switching riders can never change the tier. What `FEAT-0104` added is not a per-rider licence but a per-rider **seat**: under PRO exactly one rider may use the app, named by `license_state.licensedRiderId`, and the rest are hidden.

## Steps

1. **The tier does not vary by rider.** With any tier, switch between riders and read the tier shown in Settings → About, the paywall's current-plan marker and the lock inventory for each.
2. **Under FAMILY.** Look at every rider.
3. **Under PRO.** Look at which riders are usable and read the tier. `TST-0080` tests the hiding; this check only asserts the tier itself is the same wherever you look.
4. **Purchasing while rider B is selected.** Purchase while rider B is selected, then see how the PRO seat is chosen.
5. **The tier survives a relaunch.** On a FAMILY licence, force-quit the app and reopen it. Select each rider in turn and read Settings → About.

## Expect

- Step 1: the tier in Settings → About, the paywall's current-plan marker and the lock inventory are identical for every rider.
- Step 2: all riders stay visible and usable. There is no seat.
- Step 3: one rider is usable and the others are hidden. The tier itself is the same everywhere: one licence admitting one rider.
- Step 4: the purchase entitles the device, not rider B. The PRO seat is then chosen explicitly, never taken from who was on screen.
- Step 5: Settings → About reads "FAMILY", not "FREE", even on the first screen after launch.

## What is automated

*(partially automated: `LicensingManagerTest` covers tier resolution, billing priority in `getEffectiveTier` and the read-through on construction; `LicenseSeatResolverTest` covers seat resolution and visibility. The Play Billing purchase flow and the app-restart timing stay manual.)*

## Absorbed 2026-09-12 — what one tick no longer distinguishes

This row absorbed [[TST-0368]], which is step 5. Both rows test the same thing: select each rider in turn and read the tier back. TST-0368 added the force-quit before the release test, which is the only part that was not already here.

One tick no longer separates a tier that varies by rider from a tier that is simply late after a relaunch. If the tick fails, note whether the app had just been launched, because that is the difference between the two.

## Release test history

**2026-08-30 — `question`.** *"This is unclear what these profiles mean, if these are the profiles in the app, they cannot have different gates, since the actual license is for the application, not per profile."*

The objection was right and the check was wrong. It read *"Purchase Pro/Family on one profile. Switch profiles and verify all profiles are now upgraded"* — which frames the licence as something a profile can hold and then acquire, a model the app has never implemented. Rewritten to assert what is actually true, and to name the thing that genuinely is per-rider so the two are not confused again.

## Numbered 2026-09-17

The results were one part, so the release test could give the whole check only one mark. They are now numbered steps with one expectation each, so a failure in one no longer fails the others (FEAT-0122, criterion A7; [[TASK-0922-CorrectTheWalkCorpus]]). The wording is otherwise unchanged.

items.name: Retry Uploads to Correct Account
items.text:
As Rider B (Strava linked, has failed upload), tap Retry. Verify the upload goes to Rider B's Strava account.

**Producing the failed upload.** On strava.com, signed in as rider B's Strava account, open Settings → My Apps and revoke Your Trainer. As rider B, ride and save a short ride: Strava refuses the upload and the ride reads failed with a Retry action. Then connect rider B to the same Strava account again (Profile — Connected on Android, Settings → Integrations on iOS) before tapping Retry. Airplane mode does not produce a failure: the upload waits for a network instead. *(partially automated: `WorkoutSessionRepositoryTest.updateStravaUploadStatus_flips_status_in_place` + `SessionItemTest.showsRetryWhenFailedAndLinked` cover the retry button + status transitions; actual upload goes to external Strava.)*

The check never said how to get a failed upload. Revoking the app's access makes Strava refuse the upload with a 4xx response, which marks the ride failed at once (`StravaUploadWorker`: a 4xx response goes to `failWithStatus`). Edwin agreed to this route on 2026-09-17 ([[ISS-0444-CheckNotesTheV220ProceduresFoundStaleOrUnwalkable]]). It has not yet been tried on a device.

items.name: A duplicate rejection links the session to the original (ISS-0179)

Verify the app parses the `duplicate of /activities/<id>` form out of the rejection, stores that activity id against the session, and that the session's pill becomes **View on Strava** deep-linking the original activity — not a failed-upload state and not a retry loop. (TST-0474 covers the unknown-id pill, which is the case where no id was recovered.)

That note was a 107-row iOS parity test; an audit against the 579-check acceptance corpus found 63 of its rows already covered by existing checks and 44 not. This is one of the 44. It is written platform-neutral because the behaviour is unverified on both platforms, not only on iOS.*

## Expect

- The app keeps the id from `duplicate of /activities/<id>`: the pill reads **View on Strava** and opens the original activity.
- It is not a failed upload and not a retry loop.

items.name: Every History filter chip fits and is tappable on a phone (ISS-0390)
items.text:
**The defect's assertion, and the only claim this row makes:** on a 360 dp phone, all five History filters — All, Power, Route, Heart Rate and PBs — are on screen and readable, and none is clipped off the right edge. ISS-0390 was the trailing **PBs** chip falling outside a 360 dp phone, where it could not be tapped at all.

The case that holds it is `HistoryFiltersSitInHistoryTest.on_a_phone_the_filters_are_under_past_sessions_and_nothing_is_docked_above_the_bar`. It opens History at a pinned 360 dp and asserts that each of the five filters has its label and lies inside the filter row, which fails for a chip pushed off the row's edge. It does not tap the chips on saved rides; those taps are tested by hand in [[TST-0190-Session-Type-Labeling]] and [[TST-0321-History-Trophy-Filter]].

How the filters look is not this row's claim. On Android the chips are a row in History, under the Past Sessions heading (TASK-1068, 2026-10-11). They keep their labels on a phone rather than collapsing to icons; [[TST-0552-Filter-Chips-Render-Dispatch]] carries that. On iOS the chips are still a strip docked to the History destination until TASK-1066, and this command does not run there.

**The width is pinned, not taken from the device.** A check that relied on the device's own width would pass on a tablet with the defect present, which is how this shipped. Pinning 360 dp makes the guard independent of whatever hardware runs it.

## History of this row

Until 2026-09-22 the command ran `HistoryTypeFilterRowTest`, nine cases over the in-page `HistoryTypeFilterRow`. The one that pinned the defect was `all_five_chips_fit_within_a_small_phone_width`, a geometry check on the PBs chip's right edge; two more pinned the icon-only collapse under 600 dp, which the new strip no longer does. That class was deleted with the in-page row. The earlier fix had turned `assertExists` into `assertIsDisplayed` and a synthetic `OnClick` into a real `performClick`; the new case keeps the first. Verified 2026-09-02 on an SM-X910 under the old class.

From 2026-09-22 to 2026-10-11 the command ran `NavigationContainerTest`, whose case `history_filters_keep_their_labels_on_a_360dp_phone` laid the docked strip out at 360 dp. TASK-1068 moved the filters into History and deleted that case with the strip.

items.name: First-Transition Reset
items.text:
An HR-Zone workout whose first interval is shorter than 60 seconds opens its lookahead window before the ride starts. The controller must hand over to the next zone on that first transition without stalling: the effective target zone is already the *next* zone at tick 0, so the flip never happens at a boundary the rider can see. `HrZoneLookahead` clamps the lead to half the interval for exactly this case, and the controller's status machine picks up the new target on the next `tick()`.

## The observation method this row had is gone; the assertion is not

The row used to say "watch the `auto · converging` status banner at tick 0 vs. tick 1". That banner does not render. ISS-0166 and ISS-0167 replaced it with the delta pill and the heartbeat progress bar under the watts row (`ActiveWorkoutScreen.kt:1680-1690`), and `hrZoneAlgorithmStatus` now drives only one visible thing: the watts number greys out when the HRM is lost (`ActiveWorkoutScreen.kt:1725`). There is no tick-0-vs-tick-1 status text to read off the screen any more.

The reset itself also moved. `WorkoutViewModel.kt:1734-1740` records the decision: an effective-zone change no longer resets the controller, because resetting there restarted the rate window and cost up to 20 seconds of dead time in the middle of the pre-ramp. The controller's `tick()` just receives the new `targetZone` and its status machine recovers on its own.

What is left is arithmetic and a state machine, and both run under unit test. `HrZoneLookaheadTest` pins the lookahead-already-open case (`short interval clamps lead to half the duration`, `very short interval still pre-ramps in its second half`); `HrZoneLockControllerTest` pins the status machine and `reset()`. The `command:` below runs both classes and was verified to run.

No status is stamped here — that belongs to `tools/scripts/run-tests.py`, from an exit code, never to a hand (ADR-0010).

items.name: A PRO rider can import their own history, and it lands on the rider they can see (ISS-0392)
items.text:
Fifteen unit cases over `RiderImportPlanner`, plus three instrumentation cases that cover the wiring a pure function cannot.

**The case that pins the defect is `PRO with an unmatched name lands on the seat instead of the add path that always fails`.** Before the fix, a file whose profile name did not exactly match the rider's produced `ImportConflict.None`, whose dialog offers only "add as a new rider" — and `Tier.riderCap(PRO)` is 1, so that action was refused every time. The rider could not import their own history at all.

**The guard against the second defect is `a name match on a hidden rider never reaches the dialog`** and its overlap twin. Both detection queries read the whole rider table, so under PRO the dialog could name a rider the tier does not show, and merging landed the data back out of sight — ISS-0386's symptom arriving through the door ISS-0386 declared safe.

`no outcome under PRO with riders can ever be the add path` sweeps the reachable inputs rather than asserting one of them. That is the invariant the fix actually establishes, and asserting it directly is what stops a later branch quietly re-opening the dead end.

The FREE and FAMILY cases are not padding. The change filters detection through `LicenseSeatResolver.visibleRiders`, which returns every rider off PRO — so those cases are what prove the filter is a no-op where it should be, and that the four existing dialogs still reach their existing outcomes.

**Red-then-green, verified 2026-09-04.** Both defects were re-introduced into `RiderImportPlanner` — the PRO stage deleted and the two visibility filters removed — and 7 of the 15 unit cases failed. The 8 FREE/FAMILY cases stayed green throughout, which is the evidence they are not over-constrained. Restored, all 15 pass.

Instrumentation verified 2026-09-04 on an SM-X910 (Android 16): 48 tests in `com.yourtrainer.data.backup`, all green. That run includes `merge_keeps_the_target_riders_profile_and_never_takes_the_files`, which pins Edwin's second decision — the target rider's FTP, weight, max HR and LTHR survive an import that carries different ones.

**Not covered here:** the rider-facing half. Whether the confirmation copy actually tells a rider where their rides are going is a judgement about understanding, not something these assert. That belongs with the FEAT-0104 acceptance rows.
items.verdict_reason: Both halves of the check's command. Android: RiderImportPlannerTest 15 unit tests, plus the com.yourtrainer.data.backup instrumentation package (BackupRoomDbTest 23, PerRiderRestoreTest 9, RiderImportConflictDetectionTest 16) on Test_Phone_API_35. iOS: the full YourTrainerTests suite, 578 tests. 0 failures anywhere.

items.name: HRM prompt dialog + Skip dispatch
items.text:
— `HrmPromptTest` covers the dialog appearance with Connect / Skip actions and the Skip-callback dispatch. **It tests a private copy of the dialog** declared inside the test file (`HrmPromptTest.kt:29`), not the dialog Workouts shows, so a change to the production prompt does not reach it. **The gap since 2026-09-22:** the production prompt now has a second, required variant for HR-Zone rides — *"HR-Zone rides are steered by heart rate, so they need a heart-rate monitor."* with Connect and Cancel and no Skip (`ws_hrm_required_body`, REQ-0216). Nothing automated asserts that variant, or that Power and Route rides still get Skip; [[TST-0179-HR-Zone-Start-Requires-HRM]] and [[TST-0032-HRM-Prompt-Connect]] test them by hand. Replaces §1.2 "HRM Connect Prompt (Workout)" + "HRM Connect Prompt (Free Ride)" + "HRM Prompt — Skip" rows. The Connect-then-scan handoff and the dismiss-scanner-without-pick path stay manual (require BLE).

items.text:
On rider A, set preset to `MTB (12)`. Profile → Data → Export My Data. On a fresh device or after clearing rider A, import the file. Verify rider A's preset is restored to `MTB (12)` (not the default LINEAR). *(automated: `RiderFileSerializationTest.virtualGearPreset round-trips through serialization` + `… older rider file without virtualGearPreset deserialises as LINEAR` cover the round-trip + backwards-compat fallback.)*

items.name: Exported FIT carries every message the Activity file definition requires (ISS-0387)
items.text:
Decodes a file straight out of `FitEncoder` and asserts the global message numbers present include `file_id`, `record`, `lap`, `session` and `activity` — the five the FIT Activity file definition requires. Also asserts the lap's totals match the session's, and that `activity` is the last message in the file.

The encoder shipped for months without `lap` or `activity` because the two tests that existed checked file length and per-record sample fidelity, and neither looked at which message types were written. This check is the one that would have caught it.

items.name: ERG mode at 0 % / gear 9
items.text:
Free Ride, slope-mode = `ERG` (Settings → Hardware), slope = 0 %, gear 9. **Verify target reads ~77 W within ±10 W**, matching the SIM rider effort row above. [1.11]

## Declared automated 2026-09-12 — the number this row exists to check is asserted on every build

`PhysicsUtilsTest` asserts `routeErgTargetPower(0 %, gear 9, LINEAR, FTP 200, 80 kg)` lands in 70..90 W, in the test named `FEAT-0068 — 0pct slope cruise gear matches SIM ~80 W`. That is the same rider, the same corner and the same tolerance the row asks a person to read off the cockpit. Today the function returns 76 W.

The row used to open with "Cockpit shows target wattage", and that sentence was removed here. It is a rendering claim, not an arithmetic one, and [[TST-0037-ERG-Free-Ride-Watts]] already tests it — ERG free ride must show watts rather than a percentage. Nothing leaves the release test that another row was not already asking for.

No status is written here. `tools/scripts/run-tests.py` runs the command and CI is the verdict (ADR-0010 / ADR-0025).

## Also measured on hardware by the gear sweep — 2026-09-12

The `command:` above proves the app computes the right ERG target for this point on every build. It says nothing about whether a trainer *holds* it, which is what a rider used to set this point up to find out.

[[TST-0658-TheGearSweepRidesTheGearTable]] now visits two derived gears at 0 % in ERG mode as part of its cross-mode leg, and records what the rider actually produced beside what was predicted. Test the sweep rather than staging this point on its own.

The predicted figure is a reference the scorecard prints, never a threshold. It comes from one constant fitted to one rider on one trainer (`V_REF_FTP_FRACTION`), and the rider is the actuator. Edwin, 2026-09-12: *"it needs to have some correlation with the original measurements but I don't think we can be very precise?"*

items.name: Slope + Gears Together
items.text:
In simulation mode, set slope to 5% and shift gears. Verify both controls independently affect resistance — slope sets the hill, gears adjust effort within it.

## Declared automated 2026-09-12 — both halves of the claim are asserted on every build

`PhysicsUtilsLinearSnapshotTest` asserts each half separately. `effectiveGrade_5pct_slope_adds_2_5pct_to_each_gear` shows the slope adding a flat 2.5 % on top of whatever grade offset the gear carries: gear 1 moves from −3.00 to −0.50, gear 13 from −0.12 to 2.38, gear 26 from 3.00 to 5.50. `simulationResistance_5pct_slope_75kg_rider` shows the gear still moving the dispatched level while that slope is held: 32, 55 and 80 at gears 1, 11 and 26. Set beside `simulationResistance_flat_road_75kg_rider` (5, 31, 63 at the same gears) the pair is exactly the row's claim — each control moves resistance on its own.

This row carries no cockpit or layout claim and no `invalidated_by`, so nothing is left for a rider once the arithmetic is machine-checked. The sibling row [[TST-0120-Slope-Gears]] makes the same arithmetic claim and does carry a layout remainder, so it stays manual and its arithmetic half is [[TST-0663]].

No status is written here. `tools/scripts/run-tests.py` runs the command and CI is the verdict (ADR-0010 / ADR-0025).

items.name: Each preset counts its own gears — 26 for Linear, 22 for Road, 12 for MTB — and a rider who never chose one gets Linear
items.text:
The number a rider reads in the cockpit's `GEAR N of M` label, and the number printed on each chip in Profile → Preferences, both come from `VirtualGearTables.gearCount(preset)`. This check asserts that function returns 26 for LINEAR, 22 for ROAD_COMPACT and 12 for MTB_1X, and that the resistance and grade tables behind each preset hold that many entries.

`VirtualGearTablesTest` asserts it in `linear_has_26_gears`, `road_compact_has_22_gears` and `mtb_1x_has_12_gears`. Each of the three checks the count function and both tables together, so a table edited without its count, or a count changed without its table, fails the build.

The same class also asserts that a rider who never picked a preset still gets Linear. `fromString_null_resolves_to_LINEAR` and `fromString_unknown_resolves_to_LINEAR` cover the stored-preference path, and `resistanceForGear_default_arg_returns_LINEAR` and `gradeForGear_default_arg_returns_LINEAR` walk all 26 gears to show that a call site which passes no preset produces LINEAR values unchanged.

## Why this note exists separately

Three acceptance rows made this arithmetic claim inside a larger claim a rider has to test. Splitting the arithmetic out lets each of those rows keep `automation: manual` and stay in the release gate for the half a person still performs, which a `command:` on the original row would have silently removed (`tools/instructions/TESTING.md` § "Release gating"). The three rows are [[TST-0036-Simulation-Gear-Shifting]] (the buttons sit below the slope controls and the label renders), [[TST-0118-Gear-Shifting]] (the buttons appear in simulation mode and a shift is felt) and [[TST-0127-Virtual-Gear-Presets-Picker-Visibility-TASK]] (the three chips render in Profile → Preferences and an existing rider defaults to Linear).

No status is written here. `tools/scripts/run-tests.py` runs the command and CI is the verdict (ADR-0010 / ADR-0025).

items.name: Shifting up never gets easier, and every preset's table ends where its preset says it does
items.text:
On all three presets, resistance must never fall as the gear number rises, and the grade offset must never fall either. `VirtualGearTablesTest` asserts both across every entry of every table, in `all_resistance_tables_are_non_decreasing` and `all_grade_tables_are_non_decreasing`.

**Non-decreasing, not strictly increasing, and that is deliberate.** `ROAD_COMPACT_RESISTANCE` holds 45 at both gear 13 and gear 14. That pair is a real 2×11 cassette overlap where two adjacent chainring-and-cog combinations resolve to the same ratio, and the test's comment names it. A rider shifting 13 → 14 on Road feels nothing change, by design. LINEAR is the preset where every shift does change resistance, and [[TST-0425-No-Dead-Gears]] is the row that asks a person to feel it.

The endpoints are asserted in the same class. `all_resistance_tables_anchor_to_5_at_bottom` puts every preset's gear 1 at 5 %, the shared warm-up floor. `resistance_top_anchors_per_preset` puts LINEAR's top gear at 82 % and both cassette presets at 72 %. `all_grade_tables_anchor_to_neg3_at_bottom` and `all_grade_tables_anchor_to_pos3_at_top` hold every preset's grade band at −3.00 to +3.00, which is what keeps the slope extremes feeling the same whichever preset a rider picks.

One more assertion belongs to the same claim: `resistanceForGear_returns_different_values_for_different_presets` compares gear 6 across the three tables and fails if two of them agree. The regression it guards is Road or MTB silently resolving to the LINEAR table, which would make the preset picker decorative.

## Why this note exists separately

The three rows that made this claim each also ask a rider for something a machine cannot supply, so they keep `automation: manual` and stay in the release gate: [[TST-0118-Gear-Shifting]] (a shift is felt in simulation mode), [[TST-0130-Virtual-Gear-Presets-ROAD-COMPACT-Cassette]] (the low gears step further apart than the high ones) and [[TST-0131-Virtual-Gear-Presets-MTB-1X-Wider]] (gear 1 light, gear 12 heavy, and the cockpit buttons clamping at the ends).

No status is written here. `tools/scripts/run-tests.py` runs the command and CI is the verdict (ADR-0010 / ADR-0025).

items.name: Every preset starts the rider on its own cruise gear, and all three land near the same 30 % effort
items.text:
Switching preset resets the rider to that preset's cruise gear rather than carrying the old gear number across. A gear number means a different effort in each table, so carrying it over would change the rider's effort silently. `VirtualGearTables.defaultGear(preset)` is the function that decides, and it returns 9 for LINEAR, 7 for ROAD_COMPACT and 5 for MTB_1X.

`VirtualGearTablesTest` asserts LINEAR exactly: `linear_default_gear_is_9` checks both that the function returns 9 and that `LINEAR_RESISTANCE[8]` is 30 %, which is the historical cruise feel TASK-0459 had to preserve when it moved that feel from gear 10 of 22 to gear 9 of 26.

The two cassette presets are asserted as effort rather than as a gear number. `road_compact_default_gear_resists_close_to_30pct` requires the default gear's resistance to sit in 25..35 %, and `mtb_1x_default_gear_resists_close_to_30pct` requires 25..40 % — a wider window because MTB steps are bigger and no gear hits 30 % exactly. Today those resolve to gear 7 at 31 % and gear 5 at 35 %.

**The gap this note used to name is closed.** The two cassette assertions pinned the *effort*, not the *gear number*, so a re-tune that moved ROAD_COMPACT's cruise gear from 7 to 8 while keeping it inside 25..35 % would have passed while the cockpit read `GEAR 8 of 22`. `every_preset_starts_on_the_cruise_gear_the_cockpit_prints` now asserts 9, 7 and 5 as numbers, and `every_preset_cruise_gear_is_inside_its_own_table` checks each one falls inside its own table ([[TASK-0888-AssertTheTwoNarrowedGearClaims]]).

What still needs a person is the screen, not the number: [[TST-0132-Virtual-Gear-Presets-Preset-Switch-Resets]] asks someone to navigate Profile → Preferences and read `GEAR 7 of 22` and `GEAR 5 of 12` off the cockpit. A test can prove the function returns 7; only a rider can prove the label shows it.

## Why this note exists separately

Three rows made this claim alongside something a rider has to do: [[TST-0132-Virtual-Gear-Presets-Preset-Switch-Resets]] (navigate Profile → Preferences and back, and read the cockpit label), [[TST-0130-Virtual-Gear-Presets-ROAD-COMPACT-Cassette]] and [[TST-0131-Virtual-Gear-Presets-MTB-1X-Wider]] (the feel of the steps). All three keep `automation: manual` so their remainders stay in the release gate.

No status is written here. `tools/scripts/run-tests.py` runs the command and CI is the verdict (ADR-0010 / ADR-0025).

items.name: Slope and gear each move resistance on their own — the slope adds half its value on top of whatever the gear already asks for
items.text:
Setting a slope does not replace the gear's contribution, it adds to it. `PhysicsUtils.effectiveGrade` halves the rider's slope — the Zwift-style 50 % trainer-difficulty scaling — and adds the gear's own grade offset on top.

`PhysicsUtilsLinearSnapshotTest` asserts the addition at three slopes. `effectiveGrade_flat_road_returns_pure_gear_offset` shows that at 0 % the result collapses to the gear offset alone: −3.00 at gear 1, −0.12 at gear 13, 3.00 at gear 26. `effectiveGrade_5pct_slope_adds_2_5pct_to_each_gear` shows the same three gears moving to −0.50, 2.38 and 5.50, each exactly 2.5 higher. `effectiveGrade_10pct_slope_adds_5pct_to_each_gear` and `effectiveGrade_negative_slope_descends` repeat it at 10 % and at −5 %.

The dispatched level follows. `simulationResistance_flat_road_75kg_rider` gives 5, 31 and 63 at gears 1, 11 and 26 on the flat; `simulationResistance_5pct_slope_75kg_rider` gives 32, 55 and 80 at the same three gears on a 5 % climb. Read across, the slope moved every gear; read down, the gear still moves the level while the slope is held. That pair is the row's claim that the two controls act independently.

## Why this note exists separately

[[TST-0120-Slope-Gears]] made this claim and also carries an `invalidated_by` from TASK-0460: the Free Ride cockpit's slope Row moved inside a Column, and someone has to confirm the tap targets still work and the gear Row still sits beneath as a sibling. That is a layout check, so TST-0120 keeps `automation: manual` and stays in the release gate for it.

[[TST-0430-Slope-Gears-Together]] makes the same arithmetic claim under [[ISS-0130]] and carries no layout remainder, so it took this command directly and reads `automation: full`. The two notes run the same class on purpose: one records the claim for the feature, the other records it for the defect, and they are cross-linked so a future edit to either finds the other.

No status is written here. `tools/scripts/run-tests.py` runs the command and CI is the verdict (ADR-0010 / ADR-0025).

items.name: The trainer is never told to free-spin — gear 1 on the flat and a steep descent both floor at level 5
items.text:
SIM physics says a rider in the lowest gear on flat or falling ground needs 0 W, and 0 % dispatched to the trainer feels like a dropped chain on some hardware. `PhysicsUtils.simulationResistance` therefore coerces its output to a 5 % floor, and this check asserts the floor holds at both edges.

`PhysicsUtilsLinearSnapshotTest` asserts the flat edge in `simulationResistance_flat_road_75kg_rider`: gear 1 at 0 % returns 5, and the same call for a 95 kg rider also returns 5, so the floor is not an accident of one rider weight. It asserts the descent edge in `simulationResistance_descent_floors_at_5pct_level`: gear 1 at −15 % returns 5.

**Widened 2026-09-12, and one claim corrected.** The descent assertion covered a single point, gear 1 at −15 %. `simulationResistance_descent_floors_in_the_gears_TST_0157_samples` now adds gear 9 at −3 % and gear 13 at −5 %, at two rider weights each — the gears [[TST-0157-Resistance-Edge-Descent-Floors-At-5]] asks a rider to sample.

`TST-0157` used to claim the floor held for *any* gear at or below −3 %. It does not, and should not: a high gear trims the grade upward, so gear 26 on a −3 % descent arrives as +1.5 % and is a climb. `simulationResistance_does_not_floor_a_high_gear_on_a_shallow_descent` pins that boundary so the floor is not later "completed" to swallow it. See [[TASK-0888-AssertTheTwoNarrowedGearClaims]].

## Why this note exists separately

Two rows made this claim and each also asks for something only a rider on a trainer can report. [[TST-0156-Resistance-Edge-Gear-1-0-Floors]] asks whether the floor feels like a very light spin rather than a dropped chain, and [[TST-0157-Resistance-Edge-Descent-Floors-At-5]] asks whether the trainer stays out of genuine free-spin on the road. Both keep `automation: manual` so those remainders stay in the release gate.

No status is written here. `tools/scripts/run-tests.py` runs the command and CI is the verdict (ADR-0010 / ADR-0025).

items.name: Top gear on a 5 % climb dispatches level 80, leaving headroom — only an impossible climb saturates at 100
items.text:
The hardest gear on a 5 % climb has to stay below the trainer's ceiling, otherwise there is nothing left for a steeper climb and every hard effort feels identical. `PhysicsUtilsLinearSnapshotTest` asserts the number in `simulationResistance_5pct_slope_75kg_rider`: gear 26 at 5 % for a 75 kg rider dispatches level 80, which is both the "~80 %" figure the acceptance row quotes and its "does not saturate at 100 %" claim.

The ceiling is asserted too, so the headroom is a real gap rather than a missing clamp. `simulationResistance_steep_climb_caps_at_100` puts a 95 kg rider in gear 26 on a 20 % climb and gets 100. `simulationResistance_10pct_slope_75kg_rider` fills in the middle at 56, 73 and 95 for gears 1, 11 and 26.

## Why this note exists separately

[[TST-0158-Resistance-Edge-Gear-26-5-Near]] also claims the rider's own effort there lands around 530 W, roughly 2.5 × FTP for the reference rider, and no unit test can assert what a person produced. That row keeps `automation: manual`. It is also a one-off rather than something [[TST-0658]] absorbs: gear 26 sits above the gear sweep's derived ceiling, so the sweep never rides it.

No status is written here. `tools/scripts/run-tests.py` runs the command and CI is the verdict (ADR-0010 / ADR-0025).

tests.title: A failed connect reads as a failure in the Hub row, the equipment icon and the attention bar

frontmatter.title: A failed connect reads as a failure in the Hub row, the equipment icon and the attention bar

tests.html:
A failed connect reads as a failure in the Hub row, the equipment icon and the attention bar

Purpose

Verifies the words and marks a failed connect produces since PHASE-025, in the three places that now report it. TST-0595-Connect-Failure-Visible-ISS-0366 quoted the old panel's words before it was split down to its defect.

Setup

A rider with a trainer bound, switched on and not yet connected. Test on both platforms; since FEAT-0130 both show the same words.

Steps

  1. Open the Equipment Hub by tapping any equipment icon at the end of the top bar. Tap Reconnect on the Smart Trainer row, then power the trainer off before it connects. Watch the row and the trainer icon until the attempt gives up.
  2. Close the Hub. With the trainer still off, pick a structured Power workout on Workouts and wait.
  3. Tap Retry with the trainer still off, then Cancel.

Expect

  • Step 1: Connecting… with a spinner, then Couldn't connect in red with a Reconnect button. The trainer icon turns red with a dot.
  • Step 2: the bar on Workouts reads Connecting… naming the trainer, then Couldn't connect with Retry and Cancel. The cockpit does not open.
  • Step 3: Retry starts another attempt. Cancel clears the bar and leaves nothing selected.

Not this check

  • That a failed connect is visible at all: TST-0595-Connect-Failure-Visible-ISS-0366.
  • The post-ride Equipment is not connected bar and its one Reconnect: TST-0667-FromAFinishedRideToTheNextStart.

Provenance

Rewritten on 2026-09-28 for FEAT-0130. The slot's words used to differ by platform: Couldn't connect — tap to try again on Android and Connection error on iOS. Both now read Couldn't connect with a Reconnect button on the row, and the icon is red with a filled dot (REQ-0224-TheTopBarDrawsAllFourEquipmentIconsAndOnlyAFailureIsInColour, REQ-0225-TheEquipmentHubIsAListGroupedByBikeAndRider).

Split out of TST-0595-Connect-Failure-Visible-ISS-0366 on 2026-09-22 (tools/instructions/TESTING.md, "When to invalidate").

tests.title: Not-connected devices are slashed, and the cockpit's bottom bar shows the rider and the actions

frontmatter.title: Not-connected devices are slashed, and the cockpit's bottom bar shows the rider and the actions

tests.html:
Not connected is slashed, and the cockpit's bottom bar carries the rider and the actions

Purpose

Verifies FEAT-0132 on a phone in dark theme, where connected and not-connected icons were hardest to tell apart. The top bar and the Hub rows must use one drawing, and the cockpit must end in a bar with the rider in every ride state.

Setup

A phone under 600 dp wide on the release candidate, in dark theme, with one rider. No heart-rate strap set up. A bundled Power workout and Free Ride.

  • On Android, turn on Fake a connected trainer in Developer Options and restart, with Mock Wahoo KICKR as the Smart Trainer. Discarding a ride disconnects every device, which step 6 uses.
  • On iOS, use the real KICKR as the Smart Trainer, with Use mock trainer off in Settings → Developer · Trainer. A mock device cannot be switched off, and iOS keeps its devices connected after a ride, so step 6 switches the KICKR off instead.

Steps

  1. With the trainer connected, read the four icons in the top bar on Workouts.
  2. Open the Equipment Hub from the icons and read each row's icon. Close it.
  3. Open the Power workout and read the bottom of the cockpit before START.
  4. Tap START and read the bottom bar while riding.
  5. Tap PAUSE and read the bottom bar.
  6. Tap FINISH, then Discard. On iOS, also switch the trainer off. Read the top bar, then open the Hub and read it.
  7. Switch the trainer back on if it is off. Tap Reconnect on its row and watch its icon and row until it is connected.
  8. Open Free Ride, tap START and read the bottom bar.
  9. Tap the rider in the bottom bar.

Expect

  • Step 1: trainer, power and cadence are plain, in the bar's text colour. Heart rate is faint grey with a diagonal slash.
  • Step 2: row icons match the top bar; no tile is in the accent colour. Heart rate: slashed, on a dashed tile, Not set up.
  • Step 3: a full-width bar like the Workouts navigation bar. Left: the rider's mark in their colour, name under it. Middle: START. Right: empty.
  • Step 4: the rider, then PAUSE and FINISH, each an icon in a tinted pill with its label under it.
  • Step 5: the rider, RESUME and FINISH.
  • Step 6: trainer, power and cadence are faint grey and slashed, in the top bar and in their rows. The trainer row reads Disconnected.
  • Step 7: while connecting, the icon is in the accent colour with no slash, and the row shows a spinner. Then it is plain.
  • Step 8: the rider stays on the left while Free Ride runs, beside PAUSE and FINISH.
  • Step 9: nothing happens. The rider is not a button.

Not this check

  • Every state of the top bar from first run to a failed connect: TST-0675-TheTopBarIconsFromFirstRunToAFailedConnect.
  • Setting up, inspecting and forgetting a device in the Hub: TST-0674-TheEquipmentHubListSetsUpInspectsAndForgetsADevice.
  • The rider's colour on the terrain: TST-0668-TheRiderIsIdentifiableInEveryCockpit.
  • The cockpit fitting the smallest phone: TST-0676-OnTheSmallestPhoneEveryCockpitShowsItsTerrainAndWholeNumbers and the layout grids.

Provenance

Written on 2026-09-30 with FEAT-0132's planning, and held at level: system until the feature was built, the way TST-0676 was held for FEAT-0131.

  • 2026-09-30, TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar: checked against the build, given level: acceptance and moved to active, so the v2.2.0 release test owes it. Three things were corrected. A paused ride shows FINISH beside RESUME on both platforms, not an empty right slot. The details sheet has no Disconnect action, so step 6 reaches Disconnected by discarding a ride on Android and by switching the real trainer off on iOS. "Tapping the rider does nothing" became step 9, so each step has one expected line.

tests.html:
Coming back to the app checks a connected rider's Strava ride links

With a rider who connected Strava, background Your Trainer (Recents → swipe to another app, or Home), wait at least 30 s, then bring it back to the front and watch logcat for about 30 s. Do not tap anything. (TASK-0973)

Rewritten 2026-09-26

This check expects the automatic ride-link check again. Connecting Strava is the rider's standing consent for automatic reads of their own data (tools/instructions/AGENT_RULES.md, "No silent network calls", as Edwin corrected it on 2026-09-26), so the check that TASK-0400 added is allowed, and Edwin asked for it back. For one day, 2026-09-25 to 2026-09-26, this check expected the opposite: TASK-0964 had removed the check under the earlier wording, which said every request needed a tap.

A rider who has not connected Strava gets no check. That is pinned by StravaRideLinksAreCheckedForAConnectedRiderTest, not tested here, because the PRO test that carries this check has one rider.

On iOS the check is not built yet. iOS checks ride links only from the Settings tap, and the gap is a MISSING row in PARITY_MATRIX.md B.1.

tests.title: The discard dialog — when it fires, when it must not, and its Dutch wording on two screens

frontmatter.title: The discard dialog — when it fires, when it must not, and its Dutch wording on two screens

ios.reason: The iOS editor's Cancel closes it at once, with no Discard or Keep editing dialog (WorkoutEditorView), so steps that choose in that dialog cannot be performed. Edwin's 2026-09-17 rule makes a missing iOS feature a PHASE-019 parity gap: leave it owed on iOS and record no Pass; it is tracked as ISS-0507.

tests.html:
The discard dialog — when it fires, when it must not, and its Dutch wording on two screens

Steps 1–3 are done in one go in the Workout Editor. Steps 4 and 5 repeat the wording check on a Dutch device, and step 5 is a different screen from the rest of this row.

Procedure

  1. Dirty back raises it. Edit a workout, then tap the top-bar back or the system back. The dialog reads Discard changes? with Discard and Keep editing.
  2. Never-saved back raises it too. From a bundled workout's Edit action, the editor opens showing (Copy). Tap back without typing anything — the dialog still fires, because the copy is an unsaved change.
  3. A freshly loaded workout must not raise it. Open a saved workout, do nothing at all, tap back — it returns to the picker silently. Before the fix, loadSnapshot was not reactive, so loadWorkout's flow updates were compared against a stale snapshot and reported dirty.
  4. Dutch wording, editor dialog. Repeat step 1 on a Dutch device. The dialog reads Wijzigingen verwerpen? with Verwerpen and Doorgaan met bewerken. cta_discard in NL used to read Verwijder, which means delete; it was corrected to Verwerpen.
  5. Dutch wording, rider-setup cancel dialog. This is a different screen. Start creating a new rider and cancel out of the setup flow. Its confirmation reads Nieuwe rider verwerpen? — the same Verwerpen correction, applied where a rider is being discarded rather than an edit.

Expect

  • Step 1: "Discard changes?" appears, with Discard and Keep editing.
  • Step 2: the dialog still appears on the untouched (Copy).
  • Step 3: back returns to the picker silently, with no dialog.
  • Step 4: the dialog reads "Wijzigingen verwerpen?" with Verwerpen and Doorgaan met bewerken, never Verwijder.
  • Step 5: the rider-setup dialog reads "Nieuwe rider verwerpen?", with Verwerpen, never Verwijder.

Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

Retired What it asked for Taken at
TST-0504-Discard-Dialog-Never-Saved-Back the dialog fires on a never-saved bundled copy step 2
TST-0505-No-False-Positive-Discard-Freshly-Loaded the dialog does not fire on a freshly loaded workout step 3
TST-0506-Dutch-Discard-Wording the Dutch button wording, in the editor and in rider setup steps 4 and 5

What one tick no longer distinguishes

  • TST-0504 — a dialog that has stopped firing at all still passes step 1's opposite, so the two dirty paths are tested separately even though they share a verdict.
  • TST-0505 — this is the negative case, and a false-positive dialog is a nuisance rather than data loss, so it is the one most likely to be tolerated when the row is failed for another step. It keeps its own named step for that reason.
  • TST-0506 — the rider-setup dialog is a different screen from the rest of this row, so its wording is step 5 rather than a clause inside step 4; a regression there would otherwise be invisible.

Evidence (fill after running)

  • The exact dialog title and button labels seen in each locale, and which screen each came from.

tests.html:
Bulk translate — the run, and cancelling it mid-flight

Both steps start from Settings → Language with at least five user-created workouts missing the rider's locale. Run the cancel first if you want the second run to have something left to do.

Procedure

  1. The run. A "Translate all my workouts" row appears with a count badge. Tap it → a confirmation dialog → Continue → a progress dialog with a per-workout counter (Translating workout 3 of 7…). On completion the dialog reads 7 of 7 workouts translated to Français. Open any of those workouts — it renders in French.
  2. Cancel mid-flight. Start a bulk translate with at least five pending workouts. While the progress dialog is showing, tap Cancel. The workout currently in flight finishes and is saved; the ones after it are skipped. Re-running the bulk action picks up the remaining ones.

Expected results

  • Step 1: the count badge, the per-workout counter and the completion line all agree with what translated. A translated workout opens in the new language.
  • Step 2: Cancel stops the queue without discarding the in-flight result, and the action is resumable.

Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

Retired What it asked for Taken at
TST-0343-Bulk-Action-Cancel-Mid-Flight Cancel keeps the in-flight result and leaves the rest resumable step 2

What one tick no longer distinguishes

  • TST-0343 — a Cancel that throws away a paid translation already in flight now records as the same failure as a bulk action that will not start, and the wasted API call is invisible in the verdict.

frontmatter.title: AI error messages are actionable and dismissable, on both providers

ios.reason: On iOS the provider is chosen in Settings → AI Coach, not in the builder, and the builder shows an error as plain red text with no Close (×) button (AIWorkoutBuilderView), so step 3 cannot be performed. Edwin's 2026-09-17 rule makes a missing iOS feature a PHASE-019 parity gap: leave it owed on iOS and record no Pass; it is tracked as ISS-0507.

tests.html:
AI error messages are actionable and dismissable, on both providers

Two deliberately invalid keys, two error lines, one container. The two provider message strings differ and each keeps its own tick; the widget they render in is the same and is checked once.

Procedure

  1. Claude's message. Enter an invalid Anthropic key (e.g. sk-ant-invalid) and tap Generate. The error line reads "Claude Error 401 at https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages: authentication_error — invalid x-api-key" or close to it, not an opaque generic exception. This is ClaudePartner mirroring OpenAiPartner's error-body parsing.
  2. Gemini's message. Switch to Gemini, enter an invalid key (e.g. AIzaSy-invalid), tap Generate. The error reads "Gemini Error 400: INVALID_ARGUMENT — API key not valid…" or a similarly short message. Before the fix Gemini dumped its whole multi-kB response body, echoed system prompt included, into the editor.
  3. The container, checked once. On either provider the error is not a toast. It is an inline Text in the AI builder card, in the error colour, capped at four lines with an ellipsis, with a Close (×) icon button to its right and a troubleshooting link below (WorkoutEditorScreen.kt:1922-1948, ISS-0203 / TASK-0432). It stays on screen until the rider taps Close, so the copy can be read at leisure rather than caught in a three-second window. Tap the × — the error disappears immediately and the input is usable again.

Expect

  • Step 1: the error reads close to "Claude Error 401 … authentication_error — invalid x-api-key", not a generic exception.
  • Step 2: the error reads close to "Gemini Error 400: INVALID_ARGUMENT — API key not valid…", in one short line.
  • Step 3: the error stays inline, at most four lines, never a toast, until Close (×) removes it.

Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

Retired What it asked for Taken at
TST-0055-AI-Gemini-Error-Messages-Are-Actionable the Gemini error string, the four-line clip and the Close icon steps 2 and 3

What one tick no longer distinguishes

  • TST-0055 — a Gemini message that regresses while Claude's stays correct now fails the same row as a broken error container, so step 2 keeps its own wording and its own tick to make the difference writable.

Evidence (fill after running)

  • The two error lines as they rendered, and a note of whether the × dismissed them.

tests.title: The locale picker end to end, the feedback row below it, and a Japanese pass for CJK rendering

frontmatter.title: The locale picker end to end, the feedback row below it, and a Japanese pass for CJK rendering

ios.reason: iOS Settings → Language has a picker that applies after a restart but no language-feedback row, so step 3 and the email body in step 4 cannot be checked (SettingsView). Steps 1, 2 and 5 can be tested after restarting the app. Edwin's 2026-09-17 rule makes a missing iOS feature a PHASE-019 parity gap: leave it owed on iOS and record no Pass; it is tracked as ISS-0508, deferred to the first iOS release.

tests.html:
The locale picker end to end, the feedback row below it, and a Japanese pass for CJK rendering

One pass through Settings → Language, with two locale switches: German for steps 1–3, then Japanese for step 4.

Procedure

  1. The picker and the switch. Settings → Language. The row shows the current effective locale on its right. Tap it — a picker dialog opens with System default and the eight Tier-1 locales. Pick Deutsch: the activity recreates and the Settings panel re-renders in German, titles, subtitles and buttons alike.
  2. The rest of the app follows. Tap back and visit Profile, Workouts, History and the Active Workout screen. All are localised too.
  3. The language-feedback row. Still on Settings → Language, directly below the auto-translate toggle and the bulk-translate row, a row reads "Spotted a translation issue?" with a Report it TextButton on the right — no → arrow, matching the Export and Import rows above it. Tap it: the device email composer opens with support@your-applications.com in To: and the subject prefilled Your Trainer — Language feedback (<locale>) — v<version>. The body is hybrid: the rider-facing prompts (What I saw:, What I expected:, Where in the app:) render in the rider's language so they can be filled in naturally, while the trailing Locale: … and Version: … diagnostics stay English so the support reader does not have to translate them. In German the row prompt reads Übersetzungsfehler entdeckt? with Melden, and the body prompts are German while the diagnostics stay English.
  4. The Japanese CJK pass. Switch the device to Japanese and repeat step 3. The row prompt, the picker and the email body prompts all render in Japanese, with no missing glyphs, no tofu boxes and no clipped characters. This is the only step that exercises a non-Latin script, so it keeps its own tick — a font or measurement regression shows in Japanese and in nothing else.
  5. System default returns the device locale. Reopen the picker and choose System default. The UI returns to the device's own language.

Expected results

  • [android] Step 1: the picker lists System default and eight languages. Picking Deutsch redraws Settings in German: titles, subtitles and buttons.
  • [ios] Step 1: the picker lists System Default and eight languages. After the restart Settings is in German: titles, subtitles and buttons.
  • Step 2: Profile, Workouts, History and the Active Workout screen are in German too.
  • Step 3: Übersetzungsfehler entdeckt? with Melden, no arrow. The email to support@your-applications.com: German prompts, English Locale and Version lines, subject Your Trainer — Language feedback (<locale>) — v<version>.
  • Step 4: Japanese renders everywhere the German pass touched, with no missing glyphs, tofu boxes or clipped characters.
  • Step 5: the app returns to the device's own language, English.

Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

Retired What it asked for Taken at
TST-0334-Language-Feedback-Row-TASK-0461-Relocated the feedback row's placement, styling and hybrid email body, plus a Japanese CJK check steps 3 and 4

What one tick no longer distinguishes

  • TST-0334 — the feedback row is the rider's only route for reporting a bad translation, and a broken mail intent now records the same as a picker that will not switch; the CJK pass is split out as step 4 because it fails for reasons unrelated to either.

Evidence (fill after running)

  • The email composer's subject and body as generated in German and in Japanese.

Everything the AI builder card does around a generation, in one go at the card. Steps 1 and 2 share a single generation; step 3 needs three short ones.

Procedure

  1. The counter and the rotating status. Tap Generate on a long prompt. Within 1–2 s the card replaces the empty input with a "Generating… Ns · <status>" line where N ticks each second. The status rotates every 5 s through "Drafting intervals…", "Choosing power targets…", "Adding coaching cues…", "Almost there…". A Cancel TextButton sits to the right of the status.
  2. Cancel mid-flight. Five to ten seconds in, tap Cancel. The card returns to the idle textbox immediately, with no error toast, and the elapsed counter resets to 0. Tap Generate again with a fresh prompt — it works normally, with no stuck state.
  3. The recent-prompt strip. Generate three different prompts in succession. After each, a Recent label and a horizontal chip strip appear below the input, newest first, capped at 10 and ellipsised when long. Tap a chip — the textbox refills with that prompt. Re-submit an existing prompt — it moves to the front with no duplicate. Cancel out of the editor or navigate away and back — the strip is empty, because it is per-session memory only.

Expected results

  • The elapsed counter ticks and the status rotates on the five-second cadence.
  • Cancel returns the card to idle with no residue, and a second generation still works.
  • The chip strip is newest-first, de-duplicating, tappable, and gone after leaving the editor.

Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

Retired What it asked for Taken at
TST-0057-AI-Generation-Cancel-Mid-Flight-TASK Cancel returns the card to idle and leaves no stuck state step 2
TST-0058-AI-Builder-Recent-Prompts-Chip-Strip the recent-prompt chip strip and its per-session lifetime step 3

What one tick no longer distinguishes

  • TST-0057 — a Cancel that leaves the card stuck now records as the same failure as a counter that never appears.
  • TST-0058 — a broken chip strip and a broken progress line share one verdict, even though they are different code and different screens' worth of state.

Evidence (fill after running)

  • Which of the three steps failed, if any, and what the card showed.

tests.html:
One rider, one session, and the chrome at every step

Purpose

Verifies that the navigation container, the four equipment indicators and the rider token hold together across a whole session rather than screen by screen. The screen-by-screen assertions belong to the checks this change invalidates; this one tests the joins between them, which is where a container change fails.

Setup

A phone under 600 dp wide and a tablet at or above it, both on the release candidate. Four slots filled, with a cadence source that can be powered down for step 8. A mock device cannot be powered down. On Android, turn on Fake a connected trainer in Developer Options and restart, keep Mock Wahoo KICKR in Smart Trainer, and bind the physical KICKR in Power Source and as the Cadence source; switching the KICKR off drops the cadence source. On iOS the mock replaces the whole Bluetooth provider, so no bench device gives a droppable cadence source beside a trainer; step 8 waits for one. Two riders in the household with different colours. Test every step on the phone first, then repeat steps 2 to 6 on the tablet.

Steps

  1. Open the app on the household list. Pick the second rider.
  2. Read the navigation container.
  3. Change the ride mode twice from the Workouts destination.
  4. Open History from the container, and filter it.
  5. Open the Equipment Hub from the chrome, then open the current rider's profile from the rider destination.
  6. Turn the system reduced-motion setting on and re-enter Workouts.
  7. Start any workout and let it run for a minute.
  8. Power down the cadence source mid-ride.
  9. Finish or discard the ride, land back on Workout Selection, and restore the equipment.

Expect

  • Step 1: Workouts opens, with at least one workout row showing unscrolled. The first destination shows the rider's name and bike mark in their colour.
  • Step 2: four destinations: rider, Workouts, History, Settings. A bottom bar on phones, a left rail on tablets. No gear or kebab up top.
  • Step 3: the three ride modes form one group on Workouts. Changing mode changes the library below without leaving Workouts.
  • Step 4: History shows All, Power, Route, HR-Zone and the personal-bests toggle, each with a readable label, not an icon alone.
  • Step 5: the Hub opens from the chrome, not through Settings, with four device rows. Profile opens for the current rider, and for the other after switching.
  • Step 6: the mode strip appears without animating.
  • [android] Step 7: before START, four equipment icons up top; the rider's mark and name in the bar's left slot. The terrain bike is the mode's colour.
  • [ios] Step 7: before START, four equipment icons up top; the rider's mark and name in the bar's left slot. The terrain glyph wears their colour.
  • Step 8: the cadence indicator turns faint grey with a slash, and no dot, and the ride carries on.
  • Step 9: restoring the ride's equipment is one action, not one per device.

Not this check

  • Whether each moved screen still does its own job: that is the roughly 142 checks this change invalidates, tested from their own notes.
  • The equipment flow in depth, the Hub's two modes, the gate and the teardown: TST-0667-FromAFinishedRideToTheNextStart. The steps here that touch equipment assert only that the joins hold.
  • The token on the terrain, against ghosts and grade bands, and in the free-ride cockpits: TST-0668-TheRiderIsIdentifiableInEveryCockpit.
  • The cockpit's per-device controls: the cadence-source button is gone from the top bar (ISS-0494-CadenceIsChangedFromTheTopBarWhileEveryOtherDeviceIsHandledOnItsTile), and the Hub's modes are TST-0667-FromAFinishedRideToTheNextStart.
  • Where the watts come from when a power meter drops, answered on ISS-0493-TheChromeReportsTwoOfTheFourEquipmentSlots and fixed in ISS-0501-WithPedalsConnectedTheTrainersWattsStillFeedTheDisplayedPower.

Provenance

  • 2026-09-30, TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar: step 7 reads the rider from the cockpit's bottom bar, which replaced the Riding as chip, and step 8 expects the cadence icon slashed (REQ-0235-ADeviceThatIsNotConnectedIsDrawnWithASlashInTheTopBarAndEveryHubRow, REQ-0236-TheCockpitsActionsAndTheRiderSitInABottomBarShapedLikeTheNavigationBar).
  • 2026-09-29: step 7 read the rider's colour and glyph on the cockpit's title line. TASK-1010-TheCockpitBarLosesTheCadenceButtonAndTheRiderMovesBesideStart moved the rider to a Riding as chip left of START, and TASK-1011-EdwinsAnswersTheLapLineWrapsAndTheRidingAsLabelMovesLeft moved the chip to the row's left edge (CHG-20260929-The-Cockpit-Fits-Every-Screen-And-The-Terrain-Keeps-Its-Share).
  • 2026-09-28: steps 5 and 8 used to read four slots and a cadence indicator "turned to disconnected". Since FEAT-0130 the Hub is a list of rows, a connected device's icon is drawn in the bar's text colour rather than green, connecting is the app accent, and only a failed connect is red with a dot (REQ-0224-TheTopBarDrawsAllFourEquipmentIconsAndOnlyAFailureIsInColour, REQ-0225-TheEquipmentHubIsAListGroupedByBikeAndRider).

tests.html:
The top bar's icons from first run to a failed connect

Purpose

Verifies the top bar's four equipment icons in every state DES-0002 § 2 draws: always present, plain when connected, faint grey with a slash when not connected or not set up, and red with a dot only on failure.

Setup

A phone under 600 dp wide on the release candidate, in dark theme. Clear app data (Android) or delete and reinstall (iOS) so nothing is set up, and create one rider. Mock Wahoo KICKR and Mock HRM Strap available: on Android through Fake a connected trainer in Developer Options, on iOS through Use mock trainer in Settings → Developer · Trainer. For step 8, a real heart-rate strap that is set up and can be switched off, because a mock device cannot be powered down; on iOS that means the mock off and the real KICKR in Smart Trainer.

Steps

  1. With nothing set up, read the top bar on Workouts, History, the rider screen and Settings.
  2. Read the icons' colour, then tap them.
  3. Switch the phone to light theme and read the icons again. Switch back to dark.
  4. Set up Mock Wahoo KICKR as Smart Trainer only. Read the top bar while it connects.
  5. Read the top bar once it is connected.
  6. Set up Mock HRM Strap as Heart Rate. Read the top bar.
  7. Start a ride and discard it. Read the top bar before tapping anything.
  8. Switch the strap off and tap Reconnect on its Hub row. Wait for the connect to fail, then read the top bar.

Expect

  • Step 1: four icons on every screen. Trainer, power and cadence share one shaded background; heart rate stands apart.
  • Step 2: all four are faint grey with a diagonal slash, still easy to see, and no dot. Tapping them opens the Equipment Hub.
  • Step 3: the faint grey icons and their slashes are still easy to see.
  • Step 4: while connecting, the trainer, power and cadence icons are in the app accent.
  • Step 5: all three are in the bar's text colour, with no slash. Heart rate stays faint grey and slashed.
  • Step 6: all four icons are in the bar's text colour. None is green.
  • Step 7: the set-up devices' icons are faint grey with a slash, the same as not set up, with no dot.
  • Step 8: the heart-rate icon is red with a small filled dot. The other three are unchanged.

Not this check

  • The Hub's rows and sheets: TST-0674-TheEquipmentHubListSetsUpInspectsAndForgetsADevice.
  • Whether the cluster fits a 360 dp phone: REQ-0214's measurement, re-taken by TASK-0988.

A device that is not connected and one that is not set up are both drawn faint grey with a slash, so they now look the same in the top bar (REQ-0235-ADeviceThatIsNotConnectedIsDrawnWithASlashInTheTopBarAndEveryHubRow). Steps 2, 3, 5 and 7 say so; steps 4, 6 and 8 still hold.

Each step now has exactly one expected line, so a release test procedure can cite each step on its own (tools/instructions/TESTING.md, "The release test", rule 9). Steps 2, 3 and 5 cannot be completed on iOS. tests.html:
The manual links — the About card, the locale segment, the stub redirect, and the four contextual links

Every link out of the app to the manual, tested in one pass. Steps 1–3 and 5 are in the app; step 4 is in a desktop browser with the app closed.

Procedure

  1. The Manual & Guides card. Settings → About. The Manual & Guides card uses the same shape as the Privacy Policy and Email Support cards above and below it: a surface-variant Card with a title, a subtitle paragraph, and a final tappable inline TextButton line that renders the URL itself in primary tint — no "Open" word, no OutlinedButton. Tap it, and the system browser opens https://www.your-applications.com/your-trainer/manual.html, whose page carries the four sub-page links (workouts / ai-skills / workout-schema / troubleshooting).
  2. German URLs carry the locale segment. Switch the device language to German and tap the same card. The browser opens https://www.your-applications.com/your-trainer/de/manual.html, and the DE stub auto-redirects — meta-refresh with a JS fallback — to the EN page. Repeat for each contextual link from step 5: all four URLs include /de/.
  3. English URLs drop it again. Switch back to English. The URLs go back to bare paths (…/manual.html), with no locale segment.
  4. The stub redirects on its own, in a desktop browser. Separately from the app, open https://www.your-applications.com/your-trainer/de/manual.html directly in a desktop browser. It lands on the EN page. This is the only step that tests the hosted stub rather than the app, so it keeps its own tick.
  5. The four contextual learn-more links. Each opens the right URL via Intent.ACTION_VIEW. (a) Workout Editor → AI builder card, on both the Power and HR-Zone start screens → "Prompt tips →" → …/ai-skills.html. (b) History → AI Coach card, expanded → same link, same URL. (c) Workout Editor → start screen, Power and HR-Zone → "Workout schema docs →" below the preset list → …/workout-schema.html. (d) Workout Editor → AI builder card with a corrupted API key → "Troubleshoot →" below the error text → …/troubleshooting.html. In cases (a) and (b) the "Prompt tips →" link sits right-aligned directly under the multi-line goal-input field, flush with the field's right edge, not under the Generate button. None of these links appear on Settings → AI Coach, on the main Workout Selection screen, or in the active workout cockpit.

Expected results

  • Step 1: the card is shaped like Privacy Policy and Email Support, and opens https://www.your-applications.com/your-trainer/manual.html, linking four sub-pages.
  • Step 2: the manual opens …/de/manual.html, which redirects to the English page, and all four contextual URLs include /de/.
  • Step 3: every URL is a bare path such as …/manual.html, with no locale segment.
  • Step 4: the DE stub redirects to EN from a plain browser.
  • Step 5: Prompt tips, right-aligned under the goal field, opens …/ai-skills.html, schema docs …/workout-schema.html, Troubleshoot …/troubleshooting.html. Not on AI Coach, Workout Selection or the ride screen.

Rows this row absorbed — 2026-09-12

Retired What it asked for Taken at
TST-0331-Manual-Guides-Link-TASK-0463-Privacy the Manual & Guides card's shape and its tap target step 1
TST-0332-Contextual-Learn-More-Links-TASK-0463 the four contextual links, their URLs and their placement step 5

What one tick no longer distinguishes

  • TST-0331 — a card that has reverted to the OutlinedButton style still opens the right URL, so a styling regression and a broken link now share one verdict.
  • TST-0332 — four separate links collapse into one step, so a single dead link, or one that has drifted back under the Generate button, records as "step 5 failed" and must be named in the evidence.

Evidence (fill after running)

  • The URL opened by each of the five link paths, in both languages, and whether the desktop stub redirected.

tests.title: `YourTrainerTopBar` — Pro-upgrade gate + four equipment indicators
tests.html:
YourTrainerTopBar — Pro-upgrade gate + four equipment indicators

— YourTrainerTopBarTest, rewritten on 2026-09-22 for FEAT-0125 (10 tests). The title renders. The upgrade sparkle shows on FREE only, is hidden on PRO and on FAMILY, and tapping it fires onGoPro. The bar carries no Settings gear and no rider chip. With nothing bound it shows no equipment indicators; once anything is bound it shows all four (trainer, power source, cadence, heart rate). A screen reader reads every slot's name and state. Tapping any indicator opens the Equipment Hub. Pairs with the §1.6 FREE-tier lock rows that still require full-screen navigation.

Automated 2026-08-19 — it left the release test because a test took it over, not because it stopped being verified

This was never a check anyone tests by hand. The pre-migration ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.md carried a section titled "Moved from Tier 1 / Tier 2 — Fully Automated" — a changelog of rows already removed from the release test when tests replaced them — and the migration read that section as live rows, turning a record of 60 removals into 60 active obligations.

It was briefly set to retired earlier today, and that was wrong in a way worth stating: retired reads as no longer verified, and the truth is the opposite. This behaviour is verified on every CI run rather than once per release by a person.

command: is how that is said (STATUSES.md § [[test]], level: acceptance: "Adding a command: is how it becomes automated, and from that moment the runner owns its status like any other executable test"). The status below is written by tools/scripts/run-tests.py from an exit code, never by hand (ADR-0010) — so if the covering test is renamed or deleted, this stops passing instead of quietly claiming coverage it no longer has.

frontmatter.title: From the Hub's list a rider sets up a strap, reads the trainer's details and forgets a device

tests.html:
The Equipment Hub's list sets up, inspects and forgets a device

Purpose

Verifies that the Equipment Hub is a list on both platforms, that a row opens the device picker or the device's details as a sheet, and that signal strength is shown as bars. TST-0675-TheTopBarIconsFromFirstRunToAFailedConnect covers the top bar's icons.

Setup

A phone under 600 dp wide and a tablet, both on the release candidate. One rider.

  • On Android, turn on Fake a connected trainer in Developer Options and restart, so Mock Wahoo KICKR is in Smart Trainer. Mock HRM Strap nearby, not set up.
  • On iOS, turn on Use mock trainer in Settings → Developer · Trainer and restart, so Mock Wahoo KICKR is in Smart Trainer. Mock HRM Strap nearby, not set up.
  • For step 8, a trainer that relays heart rate, that is, one that also advertises the heart-rate service. No mock does, so this step needs such a trainer on the bench.
  • For steps 13 to 15, a real heart-rate strap you can switch off, because a mock device cannot be powered down (TASK-0962-IosDebugControlsForTheFirstIosReleaseWalk). On iOS the mock replaces all of Bluetooth, so turn Use mock trainer off, restart, and use the real KICKR for these steps.
  • For steps 16 and 17, a data-only trainer: on Android, Trainer Capability Override set to Data-only; on iOS, Mock trainer capability set to Data-only. Restart and reconnect after changing it, and set it back to Off afterwards.

Steps

  1. Tap the equipment icons in the top bar to open the Equipment Hub. Read the YOUR BIKE card.
  2. Read the caption under the YOUR BIKE card.
  3. Read the YOU card and its caption.
  4. Read the strip below the cards.
  5. Look at the Smart Trainer row's icon and status text.
  6. Long-press a row, and look for a ⋮ or ellipsis button on each row.
  7. Tap Connect on the Heart Rate row. Read the sheet that opens.
  8. With a trainer that relays heart rate in Smart Trainer, find it in that sheet and tap it.
  9. Tap the heart-rate strap.
  10. Tap the Smart Trainer row. Read the sheet that opens.
  11. Turn on TalkBack or VoiceOver and read the Signal row.
  12. Read the sheet's actions, then close it.
  13. Switch the strap off and wait for its row to change.
  14. Tap Reconnect on the Heart Rate row with the strap still off, and wait.
  15. Switch the strap on and tap Reconnect again.
  16. With a data-only trainer in Smart Trainer, read its row.
  17. Tap the Smart Trainer row and read its Resistance row.
  18. Open the strap's details, tap Forget this heart-rate monitor, and confirm.
  19. Start a ride. While it runs, open the Hub from the top bar and try to tap each row.
  20. Close the Hub and watch the ride.

Expect

  • Step 1: Smart Trainer, with Power and Cadence indented beneath it on a connecting line, each reading From the trainer.
  • Step 2: the caption begins The trainer is all you need to ride and ends to use power pedals or a cadence sensor instead.
  • Step 3: Heart Rate reads Not set up, with a slashed icon on a dashed tile and a Connect button. Under it, Needed for HR-Zone rides only.
  • Step 4: LIVE READINGS shows power, cadence and a dash for heart rate. No large tiles.
  • Step 5: the trainer's icon is plain, in the text colour, on a neutral tile, not the app accent. Its status text is grey. Nothing is green.
  • Step 6: a long-press does nothing, and no row has a ⋮ or ellipsis button.
  • Step 7: Choose a heart-rate monitor: nearby devices with three signal bars each, no dBm number, and Cancel.
  • Step 8: the trainer is greyed and reads In use as Smart Trainer. Tapping it does nothing.
  • Step 9: the sheet closes. Heart Rate reads Connecting… with a spinner, then Connected.
  • Step 10: a sheet naming Smart Trainer, the device and Connected, with Resistance, Sends and Signal rows. No MAC address.
  • Step 11: Signal shows bars and no word. The screen reader reads Strong, Fair or Weak signal.
  • Step 12: Change device, Run the compatibility test and Forget this trainer. No separate info dialog.
  • Step 13: the row's icon turns faint grey with a slash, the row reads Disconnected, and a Reconnect button sits on the row itself.
  • Step 14: the row's status text and icon tile turn red, it reads Couldn't connect, and Reconnect stays.
  • Step 15: the row reads Connected.
  • Step 16: the hand mark and Resistance by hand, in the row's normal colour, not amber.
  • Step 17: Set by hand: this bike does not let the app change it.
  • Step 18: the app asks once. Afterwards Heart Rate reads Not set up with Connect.
  • Step 19: a sheet with no chevrons. Only Reconnect, and Change source on the Cadence row, respond.
  • Step 20: the ride timer kept counting and the trainer kept its resistance.

Not this check

  • The top bar's icons and their colours: TST-0675-TheTopBarIconsFromFirstRunToAFailedConnect.
  • What the compatibility test does once opened: TST-0353 and its siblings.
  • The start gate and the one-tap reconnect after a ride: TST-0667-FromAFinishedRideToTheNextStart.

Provenance

Rewritten on 2026-09-30 by TASK-1018-TheChecksParityMatrixGlossaryAndGalleriesForTheSlashAndTheBottomBar for FEAT-0132. A connected trainer's icon tile is no longer lit in the app accent, and a device that is not connected, or not set up, is drawn faint grey with a slash (REQ-0235-ADeviceThatIsNotConnectedIsDrawnWithASlashInTheTopBarAndEveryHubRow). Steps 3, 5 and 13 say so; step 14's red tile and text still hold.

Rewritten on 2026-09-28 by TASK-0995-TheChecksTheNewHubReopens against what FEAT-0130 built. Each step now has exactly one expected line, so a release test procedure can cite each step on its own (tools/instructions/TESTING.md, "The release test", rule 9). The long-press and ellipsis lines, which differed by platform, became one step. The failed reconnect is its own step instead of an "if it fails instead" line.

Promoted on 2026-09-28 by TASK-0995-TheChecksTheNewHubReopens to level: acceptance, status: active, once FEAT-0130 was built on both platforms. The equipment panel section of the release test now cites each step.
